**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 9, Verse 1 (Part 1 of 4)**

**Surah At-Tawbah: An Overview**

This is a Madani surah. Even if it is not called the last surah of the Quran, its connection is certainly to the very last period of the Quran's revelation, because the widely accepted reports state that Surah An-Nasr is the last surah. Accordingly, the laws and regulations in it concerning the relations between the Muslim ummah and the other nations living on the earth are final and definitive laws. In this surah, the standing of the various groups within the Muslim society itself is also determined, and the circumstances of each are described. Here, "tabaqat" (classes or categories) does not mean the classes that the word is commonly used for today, but rather the groups that, according to Islamic concepts, have been classified as distinct groups, such as the Ansar, the Muhajirun, the People of Badr, the People of the Pledge of Ridwan, those who spent their wealth in the way of Islam before the Conquest of Makkah, those who spent their wealth after the Conquest of Makkah, those who stayed behind at home instead of going out for jihad, and then those who remained hypocrites (munafiqun). In short, in this surah the daily life of the Islamic society and the circumstances of all the classes and groups within it are described with great detail and clarity.

The importance of this surah lies in the fact that it describes the various stages and measures of the Islamic movement. This is especially so when its final commands are compared with the commands of the immediately preceding surah, which were temporary. This comparative study will show how firm and decisive this method of interpretation is. If this method of study is not adopted, the very form of the laws and regulations changes. For example, someone may take those verses that were specific to a particular stage, declare them to be the final and definitive commands, and then begin to interpret the verses that contain the final and definitive guidance so that these final guidances harmonise with the temporary verses. This is especially so with regard to Islamic jihad and the subject of international relations between the Muslim society and other societies. It is hoped that we shall be able to clarify some of these subjects in the course of explaining the verses and in this introduction to Surah At-Tawbah.

**When was this surah revealed?**

From the study of the subjects of this surah, the reports and hadith about it, the narrations concerning the occasions of revelation, and the study of the historical circumstances and events, it becomes clear that this surah was revealed entirely in the ninth year after the Hijrah. However, it was not revealed all at once. We cannot say with certainty when the different parts of this surah were revealed, but it can be said that the surah was revealed in three stages. The first part was revealed in the ninth year of the Hijrah, in the month of Rajab, before the Battle of Tabuk. The second part was revealed during the period of preparations for that campaign and during the campaign itself. The third part was revealed after the Muslims returned from that expedition. However, the initial part of the surah, namely verses 1 to 28, was revealed at the end of the ninth year after the Hijrah, that is, before the Hajj, in Dhu al-Qa'dah or Dhu al-Hijjah. Only this much can be said in general, and it is what the heart finds satisfactory.

....

In the first part of this surah, namely verses 1 to 28, the final regulation of the relations between the polytheists living in the Arabian Peninsula and the Muslims is set out. The practical and actual reasons for this regulation, its historical causes, and its ideological foundations are also mentioned. All of this is presented in the Quran with an allusive style, an effective manner of expression, and a decisive and clear form of statement. It would be appropriate to place a few examples before you for reflection.

﴿A declaration of disassociation from Allah and His Messenger, toward those polytheists with whom you made a treaty.﴾ (9:1)

﴿So travel freely in the land for four months, and know that you cannot escape Allah, and that Allah will disgrace the disbelievers.﴾ (9:2)

﴿And an announcement from Allah and His Messenger to the people on the day of the greater pilgrimage that Allah and His Messenger are free of obligation to the polytheists. So if you repent, it is better for you; but if you turn away, then know that you cannot escape Allah. And give tidings of a painful punishment to those who disbelieve.﴾ (9:3)

﴿Except those among the polytheists with whom you made a treaty and who have not failed you in anything nor supported anyone against you. Fulfil their treaty until its term. Indeed, Allah loves the righteous.﴾ (9:4)

﴿And when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists wherever you find them, capture them, besiege them, and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush. But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakah, then let them go their way. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (9:5)

﴿And if any of the polytheists seeks your protection, then grant him protection so that he may hear the words of Allah, and then deliver him to his place of safety. That is because they are a people who do not know.﴾ (9:6)

﴿How can there be a treaty for the polytheists with Allah and with His Messenger, except those with whom you made a treaty at al-Masjid al-Haram? So long as they remain true to you, be true to them. Indeed, Allah loves the righteous.﴾ (9:7)

﴿How (can there be a treaty) when, if they gain the upper hand over you, they would not observe regard for kinship or pledge toward you? They satisfy you with their mouths, but their hearts refuse, and most of them are defiantly disobedient.﴾ (9:8)

﴿They have exchanged the verses of Allah for a small price and averted others from His way. Evil is what they have been doing.﴾ (9:9)

﴿They do not observe regard for kinship or pledge toward a believer, and those are the transgressors.﴾ (9:10)

﴿But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakah, then they are your brothers in religion. And We detail the verses for a people who know.﴾ (9:11)

﴿It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah while bearing witness against themselves with disbelief. Those, their deeds are worthless, and in the Fire they will abide eternally.﴾ (9:17)

﴿The mosques of Allah are maintained only by those who believe in Allah and the Last Day, establish prayer, give zakah, and fear none but Allah. It is expected that those will be among the guided.﴾ (9:18)

﴿Those who believed, emigrated, and strove in the way of Allah with their wealth and their lives are greater in rank in the sight of Allah, and it is they who are the triumphant.﴾ (9:20)

And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.﴾ (9:24)

﴿Allah had already given you victory on many occasions, and (also) on the day of Hunayn, when your large numbers pleased you but they did not avail you at all, and the earth was confining for you in spite of its vastness, and you turned back in retreat.﴾ (9:25)

﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquillity upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down soldiers you did not see, and He punished those who disbelieved. And that is the recompense of the disbelievers.﴾ (9:26)

**Translation:** A declaration of disassociation from Allah and His Messenger to those polytheists with whom you made a treaty. So travel freely in the land for four months, and know that you cannot escape Allah and that Allah will disgrace the disbelievers. And an announcement from Allah and His Messenger to the people on the day of the greater Hajj that Allah and His Messenger are free of obligation to the polytheists. If you repent, it is better for you; but if you turn away, know that you cannot escape Allah. And give tidings of painful punishment to the disbelievers. Except for those polytheists with whom you made a treaty, who have since not failed you in anything nor supported anyone against you; fulfil their treaty until its term, for Allah loves the righteous. Then when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists wherever you find them, capture them, besiege them, and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush. But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakah, then let them go their way, for Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. And if any of the polytheists seeks your protection, grant him protection so that he may hear the words of Allah, and then deliver him to his place of safety. That is because they are a people who do not know.

How can there be a treaty for the polytheists with Allah and with His Messenger, except those with whom you made a treaty at al-Masjid al-Haram? So long as they remain true to you, be true to them, for Allah loves the righteous. How (can there be a treaty) when, if they gain the upper hand over you, they would not observe regard for kinship or pledge? They satisfy you with their mouths, but their hearts refuse, and most of them are defiantly disobedient. They have exchanged the verses of Allah for a small price and averted others from His way. Evil is what they have been doing. They do not observe regard for kinship or pledge toward a believer, and those are the transgressors. But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakah, then they are your brothers in religion, and We detail the verses for a people who know. And if they break their oaths after their covenant and defame your religion, then fight the leaders of disbelief, for indeed, they have no oaths, so that they may cease. Will you not fight a people who broke their oaths and determined to expel the Messenger, while they initiated hostilities against you the first time? Do you fear them? Allah has more right that you fear Him, if you are believers. Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands, disgrace them, give you victory over them, and satisfy the hearts of a believing people. And He will remove the rage within their hearts. And Allah turns in forgiveness to whom He wills, and Allah is Knowing and Wise.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 9, verse 1 (part 2 of 4):

O believers, do you think you will be left alone while Allah has not yet made evident those of you who strove and took no intimate friends other than Allah, His Messenger and the believers? And Allah is well aware of what you do. It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah while they bear witness against themselves to disbelief. Those, their deeds have become worthless, and in the Fire they will abide eternally. The mosques of Allah are maintained only by those who believe in Allah and the Last Day, establish prayer, give zakah, and fear none but Allah. It is expected that those will be among the guided. Have you made the providing of water to the pilgrims and the maintaining of al-Masjid al-Haram equal to one who believes in Allah and the Last Day and strives in the way of Allah? They are not equal in the sight of Allah, and Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people. Those who believed, emigrated, and strove with their wealth and their lives in the way of Allah are greater in rank in the sight of Allah, and it is they who are the attainers. Their Lord gives them good tidings of mercy from Him and approval and gardens for them in which is enduring pleasure. They will abide therein forever. Indeed, with Allah is a great reward. O you who believe, do not take your fathers and your brothers as allies if they prefer disbelief over faith. And whoever of you takes them as allies, then it is those who are the wrongdoers. Say, [O Muhammad], "If your fathers and your sons and your brothers and your spouses and your kindred and wealth which you have acquired and commerce in which you fear decline and dwellings with which you are pleased are more beloved to you than Allah and His Messenger and jihad in His cause, then wait until Allah executes His command. And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people." O believers, Allah has already given you victory on many battlefields, and [particularly] on the day of Hunayn, when your large number pleased you, but it did not avail you at all, and the earth, with all its vastness, was confining to you; then you turned back in retreat. Then Allah sent down His tranquillity upon His Messenger and upon the believers and sent down armies you did not see and punished those who disbelieved. And that is the recompense of the disbelievers. Then Allah turns in forgiveness after that to whom He wills. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. O you who believe, indeed the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this year of theirs. And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Wise.

Through the verses quoted above, and through all the other verses of this lesson, strong and emphatic stress is laid on taking decisive steps against the polytheists of Arabia, and the believers are urged to boycott the polytheists and to begin military action against them throughout the whole Arabian Peninsula. Such insistence shows that at that time the Muslim community, or some of its individuals, had a feeling that starting such an action against the polytheists throughout the Arabian Peninsula at one time was not an appropriate matter, or that such decisive action appeared frightening to them, and they were not of one mind about it. There were also some reasons for this, about which we will speak shortly, in the commentary and then in the explanation of the verses, Allah willing.

In the second part of this surah, the boundaries of relations between the Islamic society and the People of the Book are defined, and the commands given therein are final. The ideological, historical and practical reasons for these decisions, for which Islam has laid down such a regulation of these relations, are also explained. In this part, Islam and the permanent reality of Islam are also described, and it is also shown that the People of the Book have deviated from their true religion both ideologically and practically. Therefore, they no longer practically adhere to the religion that Allah sent to them, and because of which they were called People of the Book. For example, consider the following verses:

Fight those who do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day and who do not consider unlawful what Allah and His Messenger have made unlawful and who do not adopt the religion of truth from among those who were given the Scripture, until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled. (29): Fight against those among the People of the Book who do not believe in Allah and the Last Day, who do not forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, and who do not adopt the religion of truth as their religion. (Fight them) until they pay the jizyah with their own hand, while they are subdued.

The Jews say, "Ezra is the son of Allah," and the Christians say, "The Messiah is the son of Allah." That is their statement from their mouths; they imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before them. May Allah destroy them; how deluded they are! (30) They have taken their scholars and monks as lords besides Allah, and [also] the Messiah, the son of Mary. And they were not commanded except to worship one God; there is no deity except Him. Exalted is He above whatever they associate with Him. (31): The Jews say that Ezra is the son of Allah, and the Christians say that the Messiah is the son of Allah. These are baseless words which they utter with their tongues. They imitate the disbelievers who were before them. May the curse of God be upon them; from where are they being deceived? They have taken their scholars and their ascetics as lords besides Allah, and likewise the Messiah son of Mary, although they were commanded to worship none but one God, besides whom there is no one worthy of worship. Glorified is He above what they associate.

They wish to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah refuses except to perfect His light, although the disbelievers dislike it. (32) It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all religion, although the polytheists dislike it. (33): They wish to extinguish the light of Allah by blowing with their mouths, but Allah will not accept except to complete His light, even if the disbelievers are averse. He it is who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion, even if the polytheists are averse.

O you who have believed, indeed many of the scholars and monks consume the wealth of people unjustly and avert [people] from the way of Allah. And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah - give them tidings of a painful punishment. (34) On the Day when it will be heated in the fire of Hell and their foreheads, their sides, and their backs will be branded with it, [and it will be said], "This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard." (35): O believers! The condition of many of the scholars and monks of the People of the Book is that they devour the wealth of people by false means and bar them from the way of Allah. Give tidings of a painful punishment to those who collect gold and silver and do not spend them in the way of Allah. A day will come when that gold and silver will be heated in the fire of Hell, and their foreheads, their sides and their backs will be branded with it. This is the treasure that you collected for yourselves; now taste your hoarded wealth.

The style of address in this part shows that these verses were revealed to remove the anxiety that people felt about taking some severe action against the People of the Book, or that this hesitation and fear was found in the hearts of the great majority of them, as to how they should begin relations with the People of the Book according to the first verse. In reality, however, the address in these verses was directed towards the Romans, with whom the Christians of Syria and Arabia had allied relations. This hesitation and fear regarding the Romans was also justified, because the people of the Arabian Peninsula had a historical reputation of the Romans. Although the words of the verse are general to all the People of the Book, and the attributes mentioned in the verse all apply to them, as we will explain at the time of the commentary on the verse.

The third part of this surah mentions the lazy and sluggish people who, when called to jihad, make themselves heavy and fall to the ground, and show laziness in the general call to arms. Not all of these who were lazy were hypocrites, as will become clear later; rather, since this expedition was arduous, some people had become slack because of the difficulties of the way.

O you who have believed, what is [wrong] with you that when you are told, "Go forth in the cause of Allah," you adhere heavily to the earth? Are you satisfied with the life of this world rather than the Hereafter? But the enjoyment of worldly life, compared to the Hereafter, is little. (38) If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment and will replace you with another people, and you will not harm Him at all, and Allah is over all things competent. (39) If you do not aid him, Allah has already aided him when those who disbelieved expelled him, the second of two; when they were in the cave, when he said to his companion, "Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us." So Allah sent down His tranquillity upon him and supported him with soldiers you did not see, and made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, while the word of Allah is the highest; and Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise. (40) Go forth, whether light or heavy, and strive with your wealth and your lives in the cause of Allah. That is best for you, if you only knew. (41): O believers, what has happened to you that when you were told to go forth in the way of Allah, you clung to the earth? Have you preferred the life of this world over the Hereafter? If that is so, know that all the provision of worldly life will turn out to be very little in the Hereafter. If you do not go forth, Allah will punish you with a painful punishment and will bring in another people in your place, and you will not harm Him at all. He has power over everything. If you do not help the Prophet, it does not matter; Allah had already helped him when the disbelievers expelled him, when he was the second of two, when they were both in the cave, when he said to his companion, "Do not grieve, Allah is with us." Then Allah sent down His tranquillity upon him and supported him with armies you did not see, and brought the word of the disbelievers low, while the word of Allah is exalted. Allah is Mighty and Wise. Go forth, whether light or heavy, and strive with your wealth and your lives in the way of Allah; that is better for you, if you knew.

Here, emphasis, warning and rebuke are repeatedly expressed. It is said that as far as the help of the Messenger of Allah is concerned, Allah helped him even without the participation of any human being. Recall the time when the disbelievers of Makkah expelled him; no army was with him, yet he succeeded. Then the emphasis that whether you are heavy or light, you must go forth in this expedition, all these matters show that this expedition was very hard, and that among the people there was laziness and hesitation, even fear. Therefore, here the most severe words are used to stress that you must definitely go forth in this expedition.

After this comes the fourth part of this surah, which is quite long; it constitutes about half of this surah. In it, the hypocrites and their intrigues against the Islamic society are described in detail. The psychological state of the hypocrites and their practical bewilderment in the period of the Battle of Tabuk, before and after it, are taken up. Their intentions, their excuses and pretexts, and their deceptive reasons are ridiculed, and it is shown how they stayed behind from that jihad, how they continued spreading weakness, division and unrest in the Muslim ranks, and how they continued to harass the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the sincere believers. Alongside this, the sincere believers are warned about their intrigues. Accordingly, regarding relations with them, it is recommended that the sincere ones should keep away from them. This part is the fundamental part of the surah and its essential core. From this part it becomes clear how hypocrisy, which had nearly disappeared after the Conquest of Makkah, spread again, and in the next paragraph you will see what the causes of the spread of this hypocrisy were. Here we cannot reproduce that entire part, but by way of example, a few sentences may be observed.

Had it been immediate gain and a moderate journey, they would have followed you, but the distance was too difficult for them. They will swear by Allah, "If we were able, we would have gone out with you." They destroy themselves, and Allah knows that they are liars. (42): O Prophet, if the gain had been easily attainable and the journey light, they would certainly have been ready to follow you, but this path has become too difficult for them. Now they will swear by Allah that if they had been able, they would surely have gone with you. They are throwing themselves into destruction, and Allah knows well that they are liars.

﴿If they had truly intended to set out, they would have made some preparation for it, but God disliked their being sent forth, so He held them back, and it was said: "Sit with those who sit (at home)." (46) Had they gone out with you, they would have added nothing to you but corruption. They would have hurried about among you, seeking to stir up dissension, and some among you would have listened to them. God knows the wrongdoers well.﴾ (47) ﴿They had already sought to cause dissension before, and they turned affairs over in their minds against you, until the truth came and the command of God prevailed, while they were averse.﴾ (48)

Some of them hurt the Prophet with their words and say, "He is all ears." Say: "He is all ears for your good. He believes in God, trusts the believers, and is a mercy to those of you who believe. But those who hurt the Messenger of God will have a painful punishment." (61)

Among them is one who says, "Grant me leave and do not put me to trial." Behold, they have already fallen into trial, and Hell surrounds the disbelievers. (49) If good befalls you, it grieves them; if a misfortune befalls you, they say, "We had already taken our precaution," and they turn away rejoicing. (50)

They swear by God that they are truly of you, but they are not of you; they are a people who are afraid. (56) If they could find a refuge, or caves, or a hole to enter, they would flee to it at full speed. (57)

Among them are those who find fault with you concerning the alms. If they are given some of it, they are pleased; if they are not given, they become angry at once. (58) If only they had been content with what God and His Messenger gave them, and had said, "God is sufficient for us; God and His Messenger will give us of His bounty; to God alone we turn with longing." (59)

Among them are those who hurt the Prophet and say, "He is all ears." Say: "He is all ears for your good. He believes in God, trusts the believers, and is a mercy to those of you who believe. But those who hurt the Messenger of God will have a painful punishment." (61)

They swear to you by God in order to please you, but God and His Messenger have more right to be pleased, if they are believers. (62) Do they not know that whoever opposes God and His Messenger, for him is the fire of Hell, to abide therein forever? That is the great disgrace. (63)

The hypocrites fear that a surah may be sent down against them, telling them what is in their hearts. Say: "Mock on! Surely God will bring out what you fear." (64) If you question them, they will surely say, "We were only chatting and playing." Say: "Was it God, His signs, and His Messenger that you were mocking?" (65) Make no excuses; you have disbelieved after your belief. If We pardon one group of you, We will punish another group, because they are guilty. (66)

The hypocrite men and hypocrite women are all alike. They enjoin what is evil, forbid what is good, and withhold their hands (from giving). They forgot God, so He forgot them. Surely the hypocrites are the defiantly disobedient. (67) God has promised the hypocrite men, the hypocrite women, and the disbelievers the fire of Hell, to abide therein forever. It is enough for them. God has cursed them, and theirs is a lasting punishment. (68)

O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be stern with them. Their refuge is Hell, and what a wretched destination it is. (73) They swear by God that they said nothing, yet they did say the word of disbelief and became disbelievers after their submission. They planned what they could not achieve, and they resented only that God and His Messenger had enriched them by His bounty. If they repent, it will be better for them; but if they turn away, God will punish them with a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no protector or helper on earth. (74)

Among them is one who made a covenant with God, saying, "If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity and be among the righteous." (75) But when He gave them of His bounty, they became miserly with it and turned away, averse. (76) So He caused hypocrisy to take root in their hearts, to last until the day they meet Him, because they broke their promise to God and because they lied. (77)

Those who find fault with the believers who give freely of their wealth in charity, and with those who have nothing but their own effort, and mock them, God will mock them, and theirs is a painful punishment. (79) Whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not, even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, God will not forgive them, because they disbelieved in God and His Messenger. God does not guide the defiantly disobedient people. (80)

Those who were left behind rejoiced at sitting idle, contrary to the Messenger of God, and they disliked striving with their wealth and their lives in the way of God. They said, "Do not march in this heat." Say: "The fire of Hell is far hotter, if only they understood." (81) So let them laugh little and weep much, as recompense for what they have earned. (82) If God brings you back to a group of them and they ask your permission to go out, say: "You will never go out with me, nor will you fight an enemy with me. You were content to sit idle the first time, so sit with those who remain behind." (83) Never pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave. They disbelieved in God and His Messenger, and they died in a state of defiant disobedience. (84) Let not their wealth and children impress you. God only intends to punish them by these in this world, and that their souls should depart while they are disbelievers. (85)

This lengthy criticism, containing countless revelations, demonstrates that at that time the hypocrites (munafiqun) were constantly and day and night striving to harm the Islamic community. These hypocrites kept trying to turn the Muslims away from their objective through various kinds of conspiracies, sowing discord and spreading false propaganda.

Moreover, from this critical address it is also evident that at that time there was a lack of harmony and complete unity in the Islamic ranks, and the organic completion of the Muslim community was still incomplete. This has also been pointed out through this phrase: ﴿وَفِيكُمْ سَمَّاعُونَ لَهُمْ﴾ "And among you are those who listen to them."

Furthermore, the strict prohibition against praying for such people and the emphasis on not performing the funeral prayer for them also show that at that time sentiments of sympathy for such people existed within the Islamic ranks. This situation arose because after the Conquest of Makkah, people entered Islam in large groups, and faith had not yet firmly taken root in their hearts, nor had they yet been fully colored in the Islamic hue. We will give the details of this in the verses of this surah in which the constituent elements of the Islamic community, from which the community was formed at that time, are discussed.

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 9, verse 2 (part 1 of 3):**

(Surah Bara'ah / Tawbah: A Look at It, Second Part)

﴿O you who believe! Remember the favour of Allah upon you when hosts came against you, and We sent against them a wind and hosts you did not see. And Allah is ever Seeing of what you do.﴾ (9)

﴿When they came at you from above you and from below you, and when the eyes shifted and the hearts reached the throats, and you assumed about Allah assumptions.﴾ (10)

﴿There the believers were tested and shaken with a severe shaking.﴾ (11)

﴿And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease said, "Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion."﴾ (12)

﴿And when a faction of them said, "O people of Yathrib, there is no place for you, so return," and a group of them asked permission of the Prophet, saying, "Indeed our houses are exposed," while they were not exposed. They only intended to flee.﴾ (13)

﴿And if they had been entered from its surroundings and then they were asked to commit sedition, they would have given it, and they would not have delayed in it except briefly.﴾ (14)

O you who believe! Remember the favour of Allah upon you, when armies came upon you, and We sent upon them a wind and hosts you did not see. And Allah was watching what you were doing. When they came upon you from above you and from below you, and when the eyes became dazed, and the hearts reached the throats, and you assumed about Allah assumptions. There the believers were tested and shaken with a severe shaking. And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease said, "Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion." And when a group among them said, "O people of Yathrib, there is no place for you to stay, so return to your homes." A party of them sought permission from the Prophet, saying, "Our homes are unprotected," while they were not unprotected. They only wanted to flee from the battle. Had they been entered from its sides, and then they were asked to commit sedition, they would have accepted it and would not have delayed in it.

﴿O you who believe! Take your precaution, then go forth in separate groups or go forth all together.﴾ (71)

﴿And indeed among you is one who will certainly lag behind. So if a misfortune strikes you, he says, "Allah has blessed me, for I was not present with them as a witness."﴾ (72)

﴿But if a bounty from Allah reaches you, he will surely say, as if there had never been between you and him any affection, "Oh, I wish I had been with them, so I could have achieved a great success."﴾ (73)

O you who believe! Remain engaged in your protection and preparation. Then go forth in separate groups or all together. Certainly among you is one who delays. So if a misfortune befalls you, he says, "Allah has favoured me greatly in that I was not with them." And if a bounty from Allah comes to you, he says, as if there had been no bond of affection between you and him, "Would that I had been with them, so that I might have attained a great success."

﴿Have you not seen those who were told, "Restrain your hands, establish prayer, and give zakah"? But when fighting was prescribed for them, behold, a group of them feared people as they fear Allah, or with even greater fear. And they said, "Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us? If only You had delayed us to a near term." Say, "The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah, and you will not be wronged even a speck."﴾ (77)

﴿Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you were in towers built high.﴾ (78)

Have you not seen those who were told to restrain your hands, establish prayer and pay zakah? Then when fighting was enjoined upon them, a group of them began to fear people as they fear Allah, or with even greater fear. They say, "Our Lord, why have You enjoined fighting upon us? If only You had given us respite for a short term." Say, "The provision of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for one who fears Allah, and you will not be wronged in the least." Wherever you are, death will overtake you, even if you were in fortified towers. And if good befalls them, they say, "This is from Allah," and if bad befalls them, they say, "This is from you." Say, "All is from Allah." So what is the matter with these people that they hardly understand any statement?

﴿The life of this world is nothing but amusement and diversion. And if you believe and fear Allah, He will give you your rewards, and He will not ask you for your wealth.﴾ (36)

﴿If He should ask it of you and press you, you would be stingy, and He would bring out your resentments.﴾ (37)

﴿Here you are, those invited to spend in the cause of Allah, but among you are some who withhold. And whoever withholds, he withholds only from himself. And Allah is the Free of need, while you are the needy. And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people, and they will not be like you.﴾ (38)

The life of this world is nothing but play and amusement. If you believe and fear Allah, He will give you your rewards, and He will not ask you for your wealth. If He were to ask it of you and press you, you would be miserly, and He would bring out your rancour. Here you are, invited to spend in the way of Allah, yet among you are some who are miserly. Whoever is miserly is miserly only towards himself. Allah is free of need, and you are the needy. And if you turn away, He will bring in another people in your place, and they will not be like you.

﴿Have you not seen those who befriended a people with whom Allah is angry? They are neither of you nor of them, and they swear by falsehood while they know.﴾ (14)

﴿Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment. Indeed, evil is what they have been doing.﴾ (15)

﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield, and they hinder [others] from the way of Allah, so for them is a humiliating punishment.﴾ (16)

﴿Neither their wealth nor their children will avail them anything against Allah. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.﴾ (17)

﴿On the Day Allah will resurrect them all, and they will swear to Him as they swear to you, and they think that they are upon something. Unquestionably, it is they who are the liars.﴾ (18)

﴿Satan has overcome them and made them forget the remembrance of Allah. Those are the party of Satan. Unquestionably, the party of Satan are the losers.﴾ (19)

﴿Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger are among the most humiliated.﴾ (20)

﴿Allah has decreed, "I will surely prevail, I and My messengers." Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.﴾ (21)

﴿You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers, their sons, their brothers, or their clan. Those, He has written faith upon their hearts and supported them with a spirit from Himself, and He will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. Those are the party of Allah. Unquestionably, the party of Allah are the successful.﴾ (22)

Have you not seen those who made friends with a people upon whom Allah is angry? They are neither of you nor of them, and they swear falsely while they know. Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment; indeed, evil is what they have been doing. They have made their oaths a shield, and they bar others from the path of Allah, so for them is a humiliating punishment. Neither their wealth nor their children will avail them against Allah at all. They are the companions of the Fire, and they will abide in it forever. On the day Allah resurrects them all, they will swear to Him as they swear to you, and they think they stand on something. Beware, they are the liars. Satan has overcome them and made them forget the remembrance of Allah. They are the party of Satan. Beware, the party of Satan are the losers. Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger are among the most humiliated. Allah has decreed, "I and My messengers will surely prevail." Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might. You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers, their sons, their brothers, or their kindred. Those, He has written faith upon their hearts and supported them with a spirit from Himself, and He will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. Those are the party of Allah. Unquestionably, the party of Allah are the successful.

﴿O you who believe! Do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies; they are allies of one another. And whoever among you allies with them is indeed one of them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ (51)

﴿So you see those in whose hearts is a disease hastening toward them, saying, "We fear that a misfortune may befall us." But perhaps Allah will bring a conquest or a decision from Him, and they will become, over what they had kept secret within themselves, regretful.﴾ (52)

﴿And those who believe will say, "Are these the ones who swore by Allah with their most emphatic oaths that they were with you?" Their deeds have become worthless, and they have become losers.﴾ (53)

O you who believe! Do not take the Jews and Christians as allies; they are allies of one another. Whoever among you takes them as allies is indeed one of them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people. You see those in whose hearts is a disease rushing towards them, saying, "We fear a misfortune may befall us." Perhaps Allah will bring victory or a command from Himself, and they will then regret what they concealed within themselves. And those who believe will say, "Are these the ones who swore by Allah with their strongest oaths that they were with you?" Their deeds have become void, and they have become losers.

﴿O you who believe! Do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies, showing them affection, while they have disbelieved in the truth that has come to you. They expel the Messenger and you because you believe in Allah, your Lord. If you have gone out for jihad in My cause and seeking My approval, [then do not] confide to them with affection, for I know best what you conceal and what you declare. And whoever does this among you has strayed from the right way.﴾ (1)

﴿If they overcome you, they will be enemies to you and extend their hands and tongues against you with evil, and they wish that you would disbelieve.﴾ (2)

﴿Your relatives and your children will not benefit you on the Day of Resurrection. He will separate between you, and Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾ (3)

﴿There has already been for you an excellent example in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, "Indeed, we are free of you and of what you worship other than Allah. We have rejected you, and there has appeared between us and you enmity and hatred forever until you believe in Allah alone," except for the statement of Abraham to his father, "I will surely ask forgiveness for you, though I have no power to do anything for you against Allah. Our Lord, upon You we have relied, and to You we have turned, and to You is the final return."﴾ (4)

O you who believe! If you have gone out to strive in My cause and seek My pleasure, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies, showing them affection, when they have rejected the truth that has come to you. They expel the Messenger and you simply because you believe in your Lord. You secretly send them messages of affection, while I know what you conceal and what you disclose. Whoever of you does this has strayed from the straight path. If they overcome you, they will be your enemies, and they will stretch out their hands and tongues against you with evil, and they wish that you would disbelieve. Your relatives and your children will not benefit you on the Day of Resurrection; He will separate you, and Allah sees what you do. There has been for you an excellent example in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, "We are free of you and of what you worship besides Allah. We have rejected you, and enmity and hatred have appeared between us and you forever until you believe in Allah alone." But [there was an exception:] the statement of Abraham to his father, "I will surely seek forgiveness for you, though I have no power to obtain anything for you from Allah. Our Lord, upon You we have relied, and to You we have turned, and to You is the final return."

These verses are not translated in this section; I will translate the passage as given.

Within these various surahs, these ten pieces of evidence are sufficient for our purpose: that in the Islamic society there sometimes occurred such temporary conditions, and they occurred because a sudden flood of new people had entered the Islamic society, bringing with them their old habits. And these habits could only be removed through continuous training and purification, and this required sustained educational struggle.

However, the basic structure of the Muslim society in Madinah Tayyibah was sound, because within that structure the primary importance belonged only to those among the Muhajirun and Ansar who were the foremost early believers (al-Sabiqun al-Awwalun), and who were extremely firm people. Moreover, in the building and training of that society there was such unity and harmony, and in its structure such solidity, that it had overcome those weaknesses, afflictions and disorder; and the elements which were affected by fear and anxiety, and who had not yet been fully trained, and had not yet blended into this new society, and in whom complete harmony had not yet arisen, were also supported by the collective social system.

Nevertheless, gradually these new elements were being trained. They were adapting to this society, their purification was continuously taking place, and they kept joining the true strength of the Islamic society. And the number of the weak-hearted, the disobedient and those of wavering certainty was decreasing day by day. Those who feared worldly interests, and those people in whose hearts the Islamic worldview had not yet fully settled, so that they would also establish their social relations on the foundation of that worldview.

Thus, before the Conquest of Makkah, the state of affairs had become such that the Islamic society had come close to the level of perfection in its education, training and outward form, and most of the Muhajirun and Ansar had followed in the footsteps of the foremost early believers. And this society had become so pure and trained that it was closer to the standard required by the Islamic system of life.

It is true that by then such values had developed in that society that were directly connected with Islamic principles. Because of these values, some people within the movement were more distinguished, more steadfast, and ahead of others in the ranks of the movement. For example, the foremost early believers among the Muhajirun and Ansar, the people of Badr, and those who gave the Bay'at al-Ridwan at Hudaybiyyah. Then, those who took part in jihad, spending (in charity) and fighting before the Conquest of Makkah, and those who did so afterwards. From the texts of the Book of Allah, the Prophetic Hadith, and some practical measures of the movement, this difference in ranks and values is evident. These Islamic values and distinctions were determined from the perspective of advancing the Islamic worldview.

The explicit statement of the Qur'an:

﴿And the foremost early ones among the Muhajirun and the Ansar, and those who followed them in goodness — Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. And He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great achievement.﴾ (At-Tawbah 9:100)

Those Muhajirun and Ansar who were the first to respond to the call of faith by taking the lead, and also those who came after them with sincerity and followed them. Allah was pleased with them, and they were pleased with Him. Allah has prepared for them such gardens beneath which rivers flow, and they will abide therein forever. This is the supreme success.

In the words of a Hadith, it is also stated: "Perhaps Allah has informed the people of Badr: do whatever you wish, for indeed Paradise has become obligatory for you." This is a part of a Hadith of Bukhari. In these words, he rejected the proposal of Hadrat Umar, in which he had sought permission to cut off the neck of Hadrat Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah, a Companion of Badr, who had shown the weakness of informing the Quraysh about the preparations for the Conquest of Makkah, and this had been intercepted.

﴿Certainly Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree, and He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquility upon them and rewarded them with a near victory (18) and abundant spoils which they will take. And Allah is ever Exalted in Might and Wise.﴾ (Al-Fath 48:18–19)

Allah was pleased with the believers when they were pledging allegiance to you under the tree, and Allah knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquility upon them, and gave them a victory and many spoils which they are taking. And Allah is Mighty and Wise.

﴿Not equal among you are those who spent and fought before the victory. Those are greater in rank than those who spent and fought afterwards. But to each Allah has promised the best. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ (Al-Hadid 57:10)

Among you, those who spent and fought before the victory hold a greater rank than those who spent and fought afterwards, although Allah has made good promises to both. And Allah is well aware of what you do.

"Khalid, be gentle, leave my companions alone. By Allah, if you had gold equal to Uhud and you spent it in the way of Allah, you could not attain the reward that they attained by taking part in jihad morning and evening." This Hadith is cited by Ibn al-Qayyim in Zad al-Ma'ad. These words were said by the Prophet ﷺ admonishing Hadrat Khalid when he had a harsh exchange with Hadrat Abdur Rahman ibn Awf. Khalid, although he was "Sayf Allah," Ibn Awf was among the foremost early believers. "Leave my companions alone" — the purpose of the Prophet ﷺ was that in the Islamic society there is this distinguished class.

The faith which the Islamic movement produced in the hearts of these personalities, and the virtues which arose in them as a result, their ranks were also different according to their differences. But before the Conquest of Makkah this disparity had greatly diminished, the Islamic society was fully harmonious, and its irregularities were completely concealed. Most of their weaknesses had been removed, and miserliness regarding life and property had been removed from their characters. Their beliefs had become clear, and hypocrisy had been completely removed from their lives. Before the Conquest of Makkah, the condition of the Madinan society was such that it had become a complete Islamic society which was the foundation of the Islamic revolution.

But when in the eighth year of Hijrah Makkah was conquered, and after that, as a result of the Battle of Hunayn, Hawazin, Thaqif and other tribes were conquered — these two tribes were, after the Quraysh, the distinguished powers of Arabia — then a flood of people entered the Islamic society. In terms of faith and morals, these were people of different levels. Among these people there was also a large number of hypocrites, who disliked Islam in their hearts. Among them were also those who had been swept along upon seeing the might of Islam. Among them were also those whose hearts were to be reconciled (Mu'allafat al-Qulub), and these groups were such that they had not yet blended into the Islamic mold, nor had they been fully trained. These new people were unacquainted with the true spirit of Islam.

In the path of the spread of Islam in the Arabian Peninsula, the Quraysh stood like a wall and a dam, because in religious and worldly affairs the Quraysh held a great position. Moreover, in literary, cultural, intellectual and economic respects too, they were worthy of imitation for the other Arabs. For this reason, their setting themselves against it and blocking the way of this religion caused all Arabia to turn away from this religion, and not to enter Islam; or, if they did not ignore it, at least this was the situation that people remained in doubt, and decided to wait, so that the struggle between the Muslims and the Quraysh would reach a decision. When after the Conquest of Makkah the Quraysh were subdued, Hawazin and Thaqif also were subdued. The strength of the powerful Jewish tribes of Madinah had already been broken before this. Banu Qaynuqa and Banu Nadir were exiled toward Syria. Banu Qurayzah also were finished, and the matter of Khaybar was also settled; Khaybar was conquered. As a result of these events, Islam then spread throughout the whole Arabian Peninsula, and people began to enter the religion of Islam in droves, and within just one year, people entered the religion of Islam.

Because the graph of Islam rose horizontally, those weaknesses entered the Islamic ranks which had come in because of the astonishing victory of the Battle of Badr. Now these weaknesses were on a very large scale. The weak elements which had entered the Islamic ranks after Badr al-Kubra were purified through education and training to such an extent that in the seven years from Badr al-Kubra to the Conquest of Makkah, it was nearly the case that the Madinan society became free of all weaknesses, and the people of Madinah became a strong base and a firm foundation for the Islamic revolution. Here a gathering of the foremost early ones, the Muhajirun and Ansar, was prepared such that it was always a trustee for the Islamic system. Had this gathering not existed, it would have been difficult to manage that great revolution. But after Badr al-Kubra, that gathering, composed of the foremost early believers among the Muhajirun and Ansar, continuously guarded that great revolutionary trust. In those seven years, Allah the Exalted prepared and trained this gathering of Madinah Tayyibah for this task, so that these people would be able to control the flood of people entering Islam after the great victory. Allah knew very well to whom to entrust the protection of His message and this revolutionary message.

The first appearance of these weaknesses occurred on the Day of Hunayn. Its mention in Surat al-Tawbah is in these words:

﴿Allah had already given you victory on many occasions, and on the Day of Hunayn, when your large number pleased you, but it did not avail you at all, and the earth, vast as it was, became confining for you, then you turned back retreating (25). Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down hosts you did not see, and punished those who disbelieved; and that is the recompense of the disbelievers.﴾ (At-Tawbah 9:25–26)

"Allah had already helped you on many occasions. Just recently, on the day of the Battle of Hunayn, when you were conceited about your great numbers, but that was of no use to you at all, and the earth, despite its vastness, became too narrow for you, and you turned back fleeing. Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down hosts that you did not see, and punished the disbelievers; and that is the reward of those who deny the truth."

In this battle, the first cause of the initial defeat was that among the ten thousand Islamic army, two thousand Tulaqa' were present... These had believed on the day of the Conquest of Makkah and had gone out with the Islamic army for jihad. Thus the very presence of these two thousand individuals within the Islamic army became the cause of this disorder. The second cause was that Hawazin attacked suddenly, and the army of Islam, since it was not composed solely of the truly trained army of Madinah Tayyibah, whose training had been completed over the previous seven years and who were the real foundation and treasure of this movement, disorder arose.

The weaknesses which appeared in the Battle of Hunayn were due to the sudden vertical rise in the numerical strength of Islam. New people entered Islam in droves, who were people of different ranks in faith and sincerity, among whom there was a difference of ranks. And in Surat al-Tawbah these weaknesses are discussed, and then criticized severely from various angles and aspects, the detailed excerpts of which we have already presented earlier.

For the study of the history of the formation and training of the Islamic society, it is necessary that we look at the events of history exactly two years after the Conquest of Makkah. Exactly two years later, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed away, the whole of the Arabian Peninsula apostatized once. Only the Islamic society trained in Madinah remained steadfast in its place, and as we have said, this was the firm foundation of the Islamic society. Therefore, if these circumstances are kept in view, the appearance of those weaknesses can be understood, because after the Conquest of Makkah, in only two years, it was not possible to complete the work of moral training and purification of character for the people entering Islam, since the level of faith of those who came varied. After the Prophet ﷺ's death, the condition was that the whole of the Arabian Peninsula was suffering from intellectual disorder and turmoil, while the base of Madinah Tayyibah remained firmly fixed on its position. Through its strength and firmness, and through its unity and harmony, this society stood firm against that disorder and flood, and by stopping the flood of people from its wrong course, it turned its current back toward Islam.

After viewing these realities from this angle, we clearly understand that the difficulties and trials to which the Islamic call was subjected in Makkah were, under Allah's constructive wisdom, a purposeful matter, so that this society, which was the foundation of Islam, would emerge from these difficulties refined like pure gold. We see how much the polytheists in Makkah tormented the Muslims, subjected them to trials, shed their blood, and what they did to them.

Allah knew that this was the method of training for the establishment of a strong Islamic movement, so that the foundation of the community would be strong, because without that strength, it would be difficult to bear the weight of whatever structure stands upon it. For the beginning of a movement, such strength, sincerity, insistence on the goal, and the capacity to endure difficulties such as hardship in the way of Allah, exile, hunger and poverty, scarcity of numbers and shortage of material resources were necessary. For the beginning of the movement, this same standard of firmness was necessary.

When this first group reached Madinah, the foremost early ones from the Ansar joined them. It was the wisdom of Allah that these people should become the foundation for the Islamic movement and be able to manage those who came after Badr al-Kubra, whose full training had not been completed.

The Mecca-conquest period and the Companions

By the time Makkah was conquered, the society of Madinah had reached such a state that the majority of its inhabitants had already attained the high stages of perfection and training. It was this trained group of Companions who took charge of the armies that came after the conquest of Makkah, and who then confronted the flood of apostasy after the passing of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

From this it becomes clear why Allah, throughout the entire Makkan period, subjected the Islamic movement to the most severe hardships, and why, right up to the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, He kept the movement in a state of difficulty, warfare and fear. What was the true wisdom behind this? From the movement's process we can derive the principle of what the method of the Islamic movement should be in our own age.

In the initial stages, all Islamic movements need to devote their greater attention to strengthening the foundations of the Islamic movement. They should focus on the training and moral purification of the initial group, so that the edifice of the movement is raised upon firm foundations. Faith should be planted deep within them, so that they become steadfast, hold a true attachment to the movement, and have a clear awareness of their objective. And until the initial group within the movement has been properly trained, the work of expanding the call should not be begun, because if a movement is extended before its core group is well prepared, the result will be that disorder begins at that very outset. Whoever acts in this way will be acting against the divine method of training and against the Sunnah and the practice of the Prophet (ﷺ).

The success of this call is guaranteed by Allah. When Allah wills that a movement be raised upon firm foundations, He afflicts the initial contingents of the movement with overwhelming hardships and thereby bestows upon them maturity of character. In this way Allah makes them wait a long time for success. Their number is small, people keep away from them, but when it becomes known that these people are now patient, that they are steadfast, that they have completed their preparation and developed the capacity, then Allah makes them the means through which this great task may begin, and they become its trustees and standard-bearers. Then Allah advances them step by step. Allah is dominant over His affairs, but most people do not know.

After these discussions, we now turn to giving a brief summary of the themes of this surah here: its major topics and, in particular, the rulings in which the future relations of the Islamic state with the polytheists and disbelievers are regulated, because the rulings that came on this subject are the final rulings, and therefore they draw the highest movement-related lines.

In the introduction to Surah al-Anfal in Part Nine, we quoted about the final ordinance concerning the disbelievers and polytheists. I think a summary of it should be restated here. Although the passage from Imam Ibn al-Qayyim will recur here, despite this repetition a few of its sentences will be most appropriate here and in keeping with the context, and they will lend vitality to the discussion.

Imam Ibn al-Qayyim Jawziyyah, in his well-known book Zad al-Ma'ad, established a heading concerning the struggling life of the Prophet (ﷺ): "His conduct towards the disbelievers and hypocrites from his commission until his death." Under this heading he writes:

Allah first revealed to him the revelation, "Read in the name of your Lord." Thus began his prophethood. At that time he was commanded to read within his own heart; he had not yet been given the command to convey. After some time this verse was revealed: "O you who are wrapped up, arise and warn." By "Iqra'" he received prophethood, and by "Ya ayyuhal-muddaththir" he was granted the station of messengership, and he was commanded to warn his relatives. After his relatives, he warned his people of the evil end. After his people, he conveyed the message to the tribes spread around Makkah. After this, the message was made known throughout the whole Arab world, and finally this call was made an international call.

After beginning the work of the Islamic call, the Prophet (ﷺ) spent several years only in preaching and conveying, and did not use force. Rather, he was commanded to act with patience and forgiveness, and not to repay a brick with a stone. After a period he was permitted to migrate, and at the same time he was permitted to fight the enemies, but this permission was limited to fighting only those people who came out onto the battlefield to fight, and not to fight others. Finally it was commanded that war be continued against the disbelievers and polytheists until the religion becomes exclusively for Allah (liyakun al-din kulluhu lillah). At the time the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to wage jihad, there were only three forms of relations between the Prophet and the disbelievers: the people of treaty (ahl al-sulh), the people of war (ahl al-harb), and the people of protection (ahl al-dhimmah). Concerning the people of treaty, meaning those with whom peace agreements had been made, the command was that the covenant be kept to its end, but only on the condition that the other party remained bound by its agreement; and if they broke the covenant and acted treacherously, then he too should throw the agreement back in their faces. However, war was not to be actually initiated against such people until they were formally informed that the agreement had ended. When Surah Bara'ah was revealed, all these categories of rulings were explained separately. Allah commanded the Prophet (ﷺ) to fight the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) until they either pay the jizyah or enter Islam, and jihad was also commanded against the polytheists and hypocrites. Moreover, he was commanded to be stricter with the hypocrites. Jihad against the disbelievers took the form of armed war, and against the hypocrites it was waged with tongue and argument.

In Surah Bara'ah it was also commanded that all treaties made with the disbelievers be terminated, and that disavowal of them be declared openly. After this proclamation, the people of covenant were classified into three categories. Those against whom war was commanded were the ones who had broken their covenant and had not remained faithful to it; the Prophet fought these people and gained victory over them. The second category was those with whom there was a covenant and who kept it; he was commanded to keep their agreement intact for its stipulated term and to observe its conditions. The third category consisted of people with whom there was no treaty, but who had not joined in any war against him, or with whom an agreement had been concluded without a fixed term. Concerning such people it was commanded that they be given four months' respite, and be told that after this no agreement would be made with them: either they should become Muslims, or they should prepare to fight.

(This ruling applies only to the polytheists of Arabia; they were not permitted to live under the protection of the Islamic state as dhimmis by paying jizyah. This is because after the full disclosure of the truth, no excuse remained for their deviation. They knew well that the Prophet (ﷺ) was a prophet, and since the Qur'an was revealed in their own language, they knew well that it was the speech of Allah. They were refusing out of sheer obstinacy, and therefore they did not deserve any indulgence. For the People of the Book among the Arabs and for non-Arab polytheists and People of the Book, this concession was made: if they wished, they could live as honoured citizens under the Islamic government by paying a ransom for the protection of life and property, or jizyah.)

Accordingly, in keeping with these instructions, the Prophet (ﷺ) fought the covenant-breakers, granted four months to those with whom there was no covenant, fulfilled his covenant with the upright treaty partners, and all such people became part of the believers and Muslims before the term of their agreements had ended, while jizyah was imposed on the people of protection.

As has been said, after the revelation of Surah Bara'ah, the Prophet's relations with the disbelievers became of three kinds: those at war, the people of protection, and the people of covenant. Since the people of covenant all entered Islam, only the people of protection and the people of war remained. The condition of the people of war was that during the Prophet's lifetime they always lived in fear of him.

Thus, in the final period of the Prophet's life, the nature of his relations with all people was only this: some of them were Muslims and believers, some were secure and at peace, and some were fearful of him and at war with him.

As for the Prophet's conduct towards the hypocrites: Allah had commanded him to accept their declaration of Islam, to leave their inner state to Allah, to use only the weapons of knowledge and argument against them, to adopt a cold attitude towards them, to be stern with them, and, keeping their psychological condition in mind, to strive to reform them through his lofty words. He was not to attend their funeral prayers, nor to stand at their graves to pray; and even if he sought forgiveness for them, Allah would certainly not forgive them. This was the brief account of the Prophet's conduct towards his disbelieving and hypocritical enemies.

Allamah Ibn al-Qayyim has presented this excellent summary of the various stages of Islamic jihad, and from it the lasting and deep foundations of the movement-oriented aspect of the true religion become clear, and they deserve to be pondered carefully for some time. In this brief discussion we will limit ourselves to a few indications only.

1. From this "biography section" of Ibn al-Qayyim, the first foundation of Islamic jihad that emerges is this: the true religion, in its method of action, is thoroughly realistic. This method is in fact the movement that confronts any human society existing on earth, and it confronts it by all those means which can be effective against the actual existence of society.

It attacks the intellectual sphere of jahiliyyah on which a living system of life is actually established, a system which the power of the age sustains by material force.

The Islamic movement, in actual fact, confronts this real situation, employing all the means and resources which this jahiliyyah employs. It confronts this jahiliyyah with explanation and speech, so that the beliefs and ideas of society may be reformed; and it also uses force with the utmost effort, so that the system and authority of jahiliyyah may be utterly crushed.

That authority, which stands as an obstacle in the work of reforming the masses and shaping ideas, which is imposed upon them by compulsion, which keeps them in darkness, and which makes them servants of others in place of the Lord Most High—this is a movement which does not end with mere declaration, just as in this movement there is no intention of gaining material dominance and forcing its message upon people. It does not even believe in compulsion in acceptance or rejection; "There is no compulsion in religion." In the method of the true religion, these two things are not present. It is a movement that has been established so that people may be freed from servitude to other servants and enter into the worship of Allah, the One, without partner.

(Because of its great length, the complete commentary on this verse could not be included. We apologise for this. Please read the remainder of the commentary on this verse in Fi Zilal al-Quran, volume ...)

(Continuation of Lesson 87)

Having also forbidden every kind of compulsion and coercion in matters of religion, as we have explained in detail under the verse (2:256, p. 26–40, vol. 3), the polytheists opposed the Messenger, subjected the Muslims to trials and torture, and sought to prevent them from the path of Allah. They also forcibly prevented the Messenger ﷺ from conveying the message. The situation became such that none of his followers was safe; everyone faced persecution and the threat to life, unless one was under someone's protection or was an ally of someone. Therefore the Muslims migrated several times. After this, their harassment and torment increased further. They secretly decided that he should be confined permanently, or expelled from the land, or killed; and they announced this proposal openly in the Dar al-Nadwa. But their final decision was that he should be killed. Then Allah commanded him to migrate, as we have given its details in the commentary on the verse (8:30), "And [remember] when those who disbelieved plotted against you..." (vol. 9, p. 650). So the Messenger ﷺ migrated, and the other people for whom this honour had been written also migrated. In Madinah they found the Ansar, in whose hearts the love of the Messenger of Allah and of the emigrants was firmly established. These people displayed unparalleled self-sacrifice. Between the emigrants and the Messenger of Allah on one side and the disbelievers of Makkah on the other, there was a state of war in accordance with the custom of that time. The People of the Book who lived around Madinah made a treaty of peace with him, but they did not fulfil that treaty; they practised treachery and betrayal, and in collusion with the polytheists of Arabia they always supported the forces against the Messenger of Allah and the Muslims. Details of this we have given in Surah al-Anfal. See the pages of this same volume (pp. 53 to 68).

Before this, the Prophet ﷺ had made a ten-year treaty with the polytheists at Hudaybiyyah, and he made this treaty not out of weakness, but despite his strength and dominance, on the conditions of the polytheists, merely because he loved peace and security, and wished to spread his religion through argument and proof.

(This statement is correct to the extent that the propagation of Islam in a movement-oriented manner is also through argument and proof. But if it means that jihad in Islam is only for defence, then this is not correct. Apart from defence, jihad is also obligatory upon the Muslims.)

The Banu Khuza'ah made a covenant with him, and the Banu Bakr made a covenant with the Quraysh. Then the Quraysh, supporting the Banu Bakr, attacked Khuza'ah, and thus they became deserving of the penalty for breaking the covenant. Because of this breach of covenant, the state of war returned between the Muslims and the polytheists of Makkah. As a result, Makkah was conquered, by which the glory of Islam was established and the polytheists were humiliated. But despite this, whenever it was possible, these people continued to betray the Messenger ﷺ. And experience proved that whether they were strong or weak, treachery against the Muslims was settled in their hearts, and they never kept a covenant. As will come in the explanation of the verse of this same surah, they were always ready to break covenants.

"How can there be a covenant for the polytheists with Allah..." up to verse 12, "Then fight the leaders of disbelief, for indeed they have no oaths, that they may desist."

That is, understand about them that they have no intention of fulfilling any covenant. That is, there is no possibility of the Muslims living together with these people through a treaty, in such a way that each party is safe and secure from the mischief and sedition of the other, the polytheists remain upon their beliefs, their law does not prevail, and both parties can live together in this manner. Because of their past treacheries and deceits, it has been proven that this is not possible, although, given their circumstances, as People of the Book they should have kept their covenants.

(It is surprising that the author has reached this profound truth which is the real cause of these measures, and that the outcome of these treaties proved that there is no possibility of mutual peace between the Islamic front and the polytheistic front, unless there is some brief interval. Yet despite this, the author believes in treaties between the Islamic system and the polytheistic system, by which both systems could live together within the Dar al-Islam. According to him this is always possible, and if anything has happened contrary to it, that is an exception. Unless the matter is specific to the polytheists of Makkah. (To some extent it is correct that this ruling is limited to the polytheists of Makkah, but how could the condition of other polytheists differ from the polytheists of the Arabian Peninsula? We shall give the details further on.)

This is the true legal principle according to which the rulings for the abrogation of general treaties came down, and for those who had not broken their treaty, the instruction came to fulfil the treaties until their term. The wisdom of these rulings was that shirk should be uprooted from the Arabian Peninsula and the Arabian Peninsula should be reserved for the Muslims. But the earlier principles were kept in place; for example, in 2:190 it is said, "And fight in the way of Allah those who fight you" (i.e., fight in the cause of Allah against those who fight you), and in another place, "And if they incline to peace, then incline to it too" (i.e., if they incline towards peace and security, then you too incline towards them). As far as possible, this has been the policy. Although the opinion of the majority of scholars is that these earlier verses have been abrogated by the verse of the sword in this surah, and that all covenants with the people of polytheism are abrogated.

From this excerpt and the concluding commentary upon it, and from the other explanations of Tafsir al-Manar, it appears that although the author has indeed reached the real causes of the abrogation of treaties and of the beginning of war by the polytheists and People of the Book against the Muslims, he has not reached the true roots of this cause, nor does he wish to extend this cause and make it a general policy. Therefore in this matter he cannot reach the reality of the religion and its movement-oriented character, and he has also not been able to reach the point that there is a fundamental and real contradiction between the Islamic system of life and the systems of life devised by humans, and that the two cannot live together in one place.

Apart from Tafsir al-Manar, the statements of Ustadh Muhammad Izzah on this issue also deserve consideration. In his tafsir "al-Tafsir wal-Hadith," what he says is far from this great truth, and he has been unable to grasp the real causes of these events and rulings. Ustadh Muhammad Izzah, like other writers of the present age, day and night seeks to prove that Islam is a religion of peace and harmony and looks for arguments for this. When these people today look at the bad days of the generations whose forefathers were Muslims, and then compare them with today's irreligious, atheistic and so-called People of the Book who are at the peak of material prosperity, they sit day and night trying to prove that Islam is a most sheep-like religion, one that stays huddled within its own boundaries, and that whenever anyone speaks to it about peace and security, it accepts.

These people hold that the cause of revelation of the verses of Surah al-Tawbah is solely that some people had broken their covenant with the Messenger ﷺ, so this action was taken against them; and as for those who had not broken their covenant, whether their treaties were temporary or permanent, this surah maintains them. And even if someone had broken a covenant, this surah permits that a fresh covenant be made with those people. These people regard the verses of the early stages as the fundamental principle and consider these last verses of this surah to be of secondary benefit.

Therefore this author interprets verses 4 and 5 of Surah al-Tawbah as follows:

"Except those of the polytheists with whom you made a covenant, who have not failed you in anything and have not backed anyone against you; so fulfil to them their covenant until their term. Indeed, Allah loves the righteous. And when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists wherever you find them, and capture them, besiege them, and sit in wait for them at every place of ambush. But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakah, then let them go their way. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."

In these two verses and in the verses before them, there is a colour of the final days of the Prophet's ﷺ Madinan period. They show that there were some treaties between the Muslims and the polytheists, made either before or after the conquest of Makkah. Some of the polytheists were such that they kept their treaties, while others broke their covenants, continued to support the forces rising against the Muslims, and committed treachery and breach of covenant.

We have said earlier that the exegetes and interpreters call the second of the two verses under commentary the Verse of the Sword. They hold that this verse abrogates all verses which contain indications or rulings of leniency, tolerance, overlooking and disregard concerning the polytheists. Rather, according to this verse, their killing is obligatory absolutely. Some exegetes have said only that those with whom there is a treaty are exempt from its ruling for the duration of their treaty term, while some do not exempt even them, and accept nothing from them except conversion to Islam.
