We have already warned that there is exaggeration in this opinion, and that it contradicts the explicit rulings of the Qur'an, in which it is clearly stated that no one except the enemies should be killed, and that those who offer friendship and make covenants should be dealt with justly. The exegetes have repeatedly transmitted their statements and reports on this matter from the early people of tafsir and ta'wil. Allama Ibn Kathir has narrated from Hadrat Ibn Abbas that in this verse Allah commanded the Prophet ﷺ to place the sword upon the necks of all those with whom treaties had been made, until they entered Islam, and that the treaties made with them were to be cancelled.

This author himself quotes a strange statement of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, who established harmony between this verse, the surah, and other verses in other surahs in which there is no command to fight the polytheists, by saying that these verses are "three swords," and that the Messenger ﷺ sent these three verses with Hadrat Ali ibn Abi Talib on the Day of the Greater Hajj. Among them is this verse, which he called the sword for the Arab polytheists; one sword is for the People of the Book, and that is verse 29 of Surah al-Tawbah, namely: "Fight those who do not believe in Allah or the Last Day and do not forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, and do not adopt the religion of truth from those who were given the Scripture, until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled" (9:29). One sword is for the hypocrites, and that is verse 73 of Surah al-Tawbah: "O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh upon them. Their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination" (9:73). And one sword is against rebels, and that is verse 9 of Surah al-Hujurat: "And if two groups among the believers fight, then make peace between them. But if one of them oppresses the other, then fight the one that oppresses until it returns to the command of Allah" (49:9).

And more surprising is that Imam al-Tabari went to the view that this verse applies to both those with treaties and those without, with no distinction between them, although in his commentary on verse 8 of Surah al-Mumtahanah he held that this verse is muhkam. The verse is: "Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you over religion and do not expel you from your homes, from being righteous toward them and acting justly toward them. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly" (60:8). Therefore Allah does not forbid the Muslims from acting with kindness and justice towards whoever remains neutral in their affairs and makes a covenant of peace and security, whatever religion or community he may belong to. It may be that such people are not even treaty-holders.

These are all the proofs and the context of this verse make clear that this command applies only to those who were under treaty and broke their covenant. Apart from them, there is no permission for unrestricted fighting against any other group. Therefore, to say that this verse is the *Ayat al-Sayf* (the verse of the sword) and applies generally to every polytheist is a claim that this verse cannot bear, and the context of the discourse does not support it. Nor is it correct to say that this verse abrogates (*naskh*) several verses, especially those whose content is fundamental and general, such as *Lā ikrāha fī al-dīn* (﴿There is no compulsion in religion﴾), or the verses calling to wisdom and to good preaching, or to debate in the best manner, or the verses enjoining goodness and justice. This is especially so because subsequent verses on the same theme state that the treaty with those you made near the Sacred Mosque must be honoured as long as they remain faithful to it. We will discuss this in detail later.

"Two questions arise regarding the commands in these verses. The first is this: the exception in the first verse extends until the term of the treaty expires. Will the polytheists who made a treaty then be outside the protection of Allah and His Messenger when that term ends, so that fighting them becomes obligatory? The statements of the exegetes (*mufassirūn*) indicate that they answer this question in the affirmative. However, we have found no reliable narration from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on this matter. Our view is that if the meaning of the first verse is taken in an absolute sense, then the meaning the exegetes have derived is correct. It nonetheless requires further clarification. Therefore, we must examine what the position of those who made the treaty was before the treaty. Either they were enemies before the treaty, and fighting and combat had taken place with them, and then the Muslims made a treaty with them, as the Messenger ﷺ made peace with the Quraysh at Hudaybiyyah. Or they were people who entered into a pact of peace and friendship with the Muslims without any war, fighting or combat. The verse of Surat al-Nisa (90) refers to these people: ﴿Except those who join a people between whom and you there is a treaty, or who come to you with hearts constricted from fighting you or fighting their own people. Had Allah willed, He would have given them power over you, and they would have fought you. So if they keep away from you and do not fight you, and offer you peace, then Allah has not given you any way against them.﴾ Thus the ruling for such people is mentioned in this verse as an event. Some incidents from the Sirah also contain examples of such people. Ibn Ishaq reported that the Messenger ﷺ made a covenant with Banu Sakhr, a branch of Kinanah, that he would not attack them, and they would not attack Madinah, nor would they increase the number of any people against him, nor assist his enemy. In this regard, he also made a written agreement with them. Furthermore, there is nothing in this verse to prevent a covenant from being renewed with anyone, or the term of a treaty with a people who have neither broken their promise nor committed treachery from being extended. The Muslims also have no authority to do so, because they were commanded to fight those who fight them or who aggress against them in any form, especially in the verse that is coming soon, which clearly says: ﴿Fulfil your covenant with the polytheists as long as they fulfil theirs.﴾ This verse also contains an indication supporting what you are saying. In shā' Allāh."

"The second issue is that at the end of the second verse it is said: if they establish prayer and give zakat, then let them go and end the fighting against them."

"What comes to mind regarding this question is this: those polytheists who broke their covenant and waged war against the Muslims no longer deserve to have a new treaty made with them. Therefore it became obligatory on the Muslims to impose conditions on them which would guarantee peace and security in the region. Those conditions can only be that they repent of shirk, enter Islam, perform Islamic worship and fulfil their financial obligations. Such measures will not be considered compulsion in religion, regardless of the fact that the system of shirk they are caught in drags humanity down to a most degrading level, gives people beliefs and practices that are extremely feeble and contrary to reason and logic, and, as a result of these ideas, establishes a jahili system that is extremely oppressive, in which the most abominable and evil deeds are committed, and people fall victim to strange prejudices. By contrast, the Islamic system into which Islam requires them to enter guarantees them freedom, intellectual progress and practical perfection. The Islamic system gives them good forms of worship, the highest standard of morality, and a logical system of thought and vision. Nevertheless, we do not hold that there is no room for a new agreement with those who break covenants, if the interests of both parties lie in it. Sometimes it may happen that the Muslims are unable to fight, or do not have the power to subdue such people through war. Allah knows best."

From the passages of the author's commentary that we have selected above, it appears that the author and others like him do not grant Islam the right to rise and liberate human beings across the whole world from the slavery of their fellow humans and bring them into the slavery of Allah, wherever and whenever this is possible for Islam, regardless of whether the Muslims have been wronged or not, and whether that wrong was done to them within or outside their territorial boundaries. Such people reject this very principle, although the Islamic system of jihad is built upon it, and apart from this principle, Islam has no right to remove all the material obstacles from its path. If this principle is denied, then the Islamic system cannot confront humanity with realism and seriousness, on equal resources and positions, nor can it adopt a strategy suited to different circumstances and stages. Islam would then be left with only the path of relying on preaching and exhortation in the face of material forces. This is a weak position which Allah certainly does not want for His religion.

(For details, see Maulana Abul A'la Mawdudi's book *al-Jihad fi al-Islam*, and the excerpts from this book that we presented in the ninth part of this exegesis.)

These excerpts also show that the author's thought and outlook do not include the activist methodology of the revival of Islam, which requires that at every occasion weapons equal to those of the enemy be used. The approach the author has adopted in this exegesis is to treat the verses of the earlier stages of the Islamic movement as final, and then restrict the verses revealed in the last period by them. They do not consider that the verses revealed in earlier periods were meant for earlier stages and circumstances. We too say that these commands are not in fact abrogated, in the sense that if circumstances similar to those of the earlier verses confront anyone anywhere today, the rulings of those verses will be applied, and the final verses of Surat al-Tawbah will be taken as the guide. The earlier verses also remain in force, but these verses do not oblige the Muslims that, even when they have entered circumstances like those of the final verses of Surat al-Tawbah, they must refrain from taking appropriate measures and must not implement the verses under discussion.

This subject demands great breadth of heart and deep reflection, and to do it justice it is necessary to understand, in the revival of Islam, the nature of Islam and its activist methodology, as we have said above.

Now I think we should cast one more look at the lines with which we began our commentary on this lesson:

"Those who carefully study the events and circumstances of the Sirah of the Prophet will clearly know what the activist methodology of the revival of Islam is: its nature and character, what the stages are for the various measures in this process, and what its ultimate goals are. Furthermore, they can easily discover that the final lines drawn in this surah for relations between the Islamic front and the polytheists and People of the Book in the various camps of the Arabian Peninsula were perfectly timely. The ground had been prepared for them, the circumstances were favourable, and these lines and measures were decisive, and they were meant to occur at their appointed time."

Through repeated experience, the principle and law was being established: what the ultimate nature of relations would be between a society in which sovereignty and supreme authority belong exclusively to Allah, and whose laws are made by Allah, and a jahili society in which all these matters are reserved for other than Allah, or in which some other than Allah is associated with Allah. The ultimate principle of these relations is the perpetual struggle that takes place at all times between an Islamic society and any jahili society, which is mentioned in this verse of Surat al-Hajj:

﴿Those who have been expelled from their homes without right, only because they say: "Our Lord is Allah." And had Allah not repelled some people by means of others, monasteries, churches, synagogues and mosques, in which the name of Allah is much mentioned, would surely have been demolished. Allah will surely help those who help Him. Indeed, Allah is Strong and Mighty.﴾ (22:40)

The effects of this final and decisive law appeared in two ways.

The first is that Islam kept advancing step by step. One battle followed another, one stage came after another, and Islam spread into the surrounding regions. The word of Allah spread from one region to another, and from one tribe to another. In this way the call of Islam was carried to the whole earth, and all the obstacles in the path of this preaching and propagation were removed, so that this call could reach all the people of the world without any material obstruction. At the end of these stages, the Muslims conquered Makkah, the great obstacle in the path of Islam's spread was removed, and Hawazin and Thaqif, which were powerful tribes after the Quraysh, also accepted the supremacy of Islam. In this stage, Islam became a force that the enemies of Islam began to fear, and thus the way was paved for the final and decisive action in the Arabian Peninsula. And this matter was not confined to the Arabian Peninsula; this was indeed the policy, so that no fitnah would remain anywhere in the world and the entire religion would belong to Allah.

The second manifestation is that the jahili camp repeatedly broke the treaties it made with the Islamic front, and whenever it had the opportunity it broke its covenant. Whenever the people of jahiliyyah sensed that the Islamic front was in danger and in a struggle of life and death, or at least when the polytheists and People of the Book who broke their covenants were assured that their future was secure. Whatever treaties those people made, the motive behind them was not a genuine desire for peace and harmony with the Muslims. Rather, they made them under extreme compulsion and for a suitable time. They would make these treaties, but when they saw that Islam existed and was progressing, they became helpless and broke those treaties. This is because Islam, by its very existence, was contrary to their existence, and in the small and great affairs of life it was contrary to their ways. Since truth, life, movement and expansion were deeply ingrained in Islam, it was a threat to their existence, because the sole aim of Islam was to bring all people into the slavery of Allah.

This final manifestation, and the principle that produced this pattern, Allah has indicated in several verses. ﴿And they will continue to fight you until they turn you back from your religion, if they are able.﴾ (2:217) This is what was said about the polytheists and about the People of the Book. ﴿Many of the People of the Book wish they could turn you back into disbelief after your belief, out of envy from themselves, after the truth has become clear to them.﴾ (2:109) And elsewhere: ﴿The Jews and the Christians will never be pleased with you until you follow their religion.﴾ (2:120) Through these definitive texts, Allah Himself informs us of the activities of all fronts against Islam: that they are united against Islam, that their position is not temporary but permanent, a universal position, and is not bound by any time or place.

Sayyid Qutb's commentary (Fi Zilal al-Quran), Urdu translation, on Surah 9, verse 3 (part 3 of 4):

It is impossible to understand the Islamic doctrine of jihad at all without grasping the final and definitive law and principle of Islam regarding the relations between the Islamic society and its state on the one hand, and jahili systems and governments on the other; without reflecting on the historical manifestations of that law and principle; and without understanding the positions of both fronts in Islamic history. One cannot understand that long and dark conflict which has existed between the Islamic camp and the camps of jahiliyyah for the past hundred years. Nor can one understand why the mujahid group of the Companions (ṣaḥābah kirām) undertook these operations; nor can the Islamic conquests of later periods be understood; nor the war between idol-worship and Islam; nor the long struggle between Islam and the Crusader wars, which lasted fourteen hundred years, and which today continue against the descendants of Muslims, although, due to misfortune, those descendants have for some time now renounced the reality of Islam, and for them only the name and title of Islam remain. This Crusader war against the descendants of Muslims continues today in Russian territories and in Christian Crusader territories. In Russia, in China, in Yugoslavia, in Japan, in India and Kashmir—in short, everywhere—this war continues. In Habasha (Abyssinia), Zanzibar, Kenya, South Africa and America, everywhere the Crusader war against Islam continues. Then, wherever Islamic movements arise, they are not allowed to raise their heads. Within the Islamic world itself, or in those regions which were once Islamic, movements for the revival of Islam arise, and they are not allowed to raise their heads; the movements for the revival of Islam are not merely ended, but crushed. And in this matter, the idolaters, the Crusaders of the West and the Communists of the East are in complete agreement and unity. And those governments which carry out this duty are given such aid that they are sustained in all their needs; and then these rulers who oppress the Islamic leaders are met with complete silence by these so-called developed countries and proponents of fundamental rights. Yet the people who work for the revival of Islam are most honourable citizens.

This Islamic law regarding relations between states had become clear shortly before the revelation of Surah Tawbah, and after the conquest of Makkah it became manifest in the two forms described above. Therefore, whatever measures were taken concerning the polytheists in the Arabian Peninsula, or whatever attitude was adopted toward the People of the Book, their details are given in this part of Surah Tawbah.

The Islamic leadership had complete conviction in this law and these measures, but at that time the various groups within the Islamic community—especially those who had only recently believed, or who were among the mu'allafat al-qulub (those whose hearts were to be won over), or weak-faithed Muslims, or hypocrites—did not understand the Islamic doctrine of jihad or this policy in the Arabian Peninsula.

Within the Islamic society there were people—and perhaps they were among the most honoured, far-sighted and wise people among the Muslims—who wondered why the treaties made with all the polytheists were being terminated. That is, those who had broken their covenant were given four months' respite; but those whose treaty had no fixed term, or those who had no treaty and had not fought the Muslims, or those whose treaties were for less than four months, or those who had temporary treaties but had not violated them and did not take part in campaigns against the Muslims—these groups of Muslims, although they understood the order to terminate treaties with those who broke their covenant or from whom treachery was feared, as already mentioned in Surah al-Anfal:

"And if you fear treachery from a people, then throw back to them [their treaty] openly and evenly. Indeed, Allah does not love the treacherous." (Qur'an 8:58)

—nevertheless could not grasp why the treaties of others were to be ended after four months, or ended after their stated term, because they were accustomed to such rulings from the days of jahiliyyah, when, so long as both parties honoured the covenant, or maintained friendship, or lived in peace and safety, such people were not treated in this way. But Allah's plan was far-reaching beyond that customary plan, and the stage reached by the upheaval among the Arabs was its natural stage and measure.

Again, among the Islamic ranks there were people—and it is possible that among the prominent and important people too there were such—who thought it not appropriate to begin fighting and war against all the polytheists of the peninsula, especially to continue this war until these people submit to Islam, when Islam had already become victorious and dominant in the Arabian Peninsula. Only a few scattered, distant regions remained which were not under Islamic rule, and these regions posed no threat to Islam; and it was also expected that these regions too would accept Islam. Especially in peaceful circumstances, such people considered it improper to fight even their relatives, tribesmen, and groups and people with whom they had social and economic ties, since they believed that the path for these people to enter Islam had been paved even without such harsh action. But Allah's will was that among the people of the Abode of Islam, mutual relations should rest solely upon the foundation of the Islamic way of life; all other ties should be severed; the Arabian Peninsula should be purified for Islam and become a secure centre of Islam. And Allah knew that the Romans were preparing to attack Islam from the direction of Syria.

Within the Islamic society there were also some people—perhaps among the honourable and esteemed ones—who thought that in this way the markets of Makkah and Madinah would fall into recession, and the economic and commercial relations of the Arabian Peninsula would be disrupted, because now there would be war and bloodshed everywhere between Muslims and polytheists. The pilgrimage season in particular would be affected, while the proclamation also contained the statement that polytheists and naked persons would not perform Hajj. And now the polytheists would no longer have a share in the construction of mosques, while in the opinion of such people there was no military necessity for this measure, and this aim could be achieved by gradual and peaceful means. But Allah's will was that collective affairs and relations should rest only upon principles, and that in the hearts of believers the importance of creed and principle should be superior to all other aims and objectives, whether these relations were of kinship, or of charity and commercial profit. Accordingly, Allah said that He is the Provider, and that the means of sustenance are in His power, and Allah turns them as He wills.

Then, within the Islamic society at that time there were also the weak in faith, the hesitant, the mu'allafat al-qulub, the hypocrites, and other neutral, comfort-seeking people; they had entered the religion of Islam in droves, but had not been fully coloured by Islam. These people feared the general declaration of war against the polytheists—especially the commercial recession, the disruption of communications and the closing of trade routes in a state of war, and above all, the bearing of the hardships of jihad, while they did not find in themselves the strength for it, since a vast crowd of common people had entered Islam seeing its dominance, for it was a profitable bargain. Yet this general proclamation was not even in the periphery of their thinking, because these people had only newly entered Islam and were not yet aware of the difficulties of that path. And Allah wished to purify the Islamic ranks; this was His decree:

"Or do you think that you will be left alone while Allah has not yet known those among you who strove and did not take as intimates other than Allah, His Messenger, and the believers? And Allah is Acquainted with what you do." (Qur'an 9:16)

In short, in that mixed Islamic society after the conquest of Makkah there were people of diverse purposes. Therefore, in this part of Surah Tawbah, instructions were given and indications made in such a detailed and varied style, so that the weaknesses or wrong notions that remained in people's hearts could be removed, and that restlessness, disorder and doubts arising from thoughts within the Islamic ranks could be purged—those doubts that were present even in the hearts of some of the most sincere people.

Thus, in such circumstances, the Surah begins with the clear proclamation that Allah and His Messenger are now free of obligation toward the polytheists. And after one verse, the proclamation repeats this matter again and again, in very forceful words, so that no Muslim should maintain any kind of relationship with those from whom Allah and His Messenger have declared disassociation.

"A declaration of disassociation from Allah and His Messenger to those polytheists with whom you made covenants." (Qur'an 9:1)

And, in order to reassure the Muslims and to warn the disbelievers, it was necessary to also announce that Allah is the one who disgraces the deniers of truth, and that those who turn away will not escape the punishment of Allah.

"And an announcement from Allah and His Messenger to the people on the day of the greatest Hajj: that Allah is free of obligation to the polytheists, and so is His Messenger." (Qur'an 9:3)

"So travel freely in the land for four months, and know that you cannot escape Allah, and that Allah will disgrace the disbelievers." (Qur'an 9:2)

"So if you repent, it is better for you; but if you turn away, then know that you cannot escape Allah. And give the disbelievers the good news of a painful punishment." (Qur'an 9:3)

Strong displeasure was expressed at the question of how there could be any covenant between Allah and His Messenger and these polytheists, except for those who made a covenant and then remained steadfast in it—for that covenant would continue until its term. But at the same time the Muslims were warned that these polytheists, whenever they gain power, will not respect any covenant or pledge, and do not regard any action against the Muslims as blameworthy, provided they are able to do it. Thus their disbelief was portrayed, and it was said that these people are great liars.

"How can there be a covenant with the polytheists in the sight of Allah and His Messenger, except those with whom you made a covenant at al-Masjid al-Haram? So long as they are upright toward you, be upright toward them; indeed, Allah loves the righteous. How [can there be a covenant], when if they gain the upper hand over you, they will not observe toward you any tie of kinship or covenant? They satisfy you with their mouths, but their hearts refuse, and most of them are defiantly disobedient. They have exchanged the signs of Allah for a small price and have averted [others] from His way. Indeed, evil is what they have been doing. They do not observe toward a believer any tie of kinship or covenant; and it is those who are the transgressors." (Qur'an 9:7–10)

The bitter memories in the hearts of the Muslims, and the burning rage for vengeance in their awareness and emotions, the circumstances required that this be somewhat stirred up, so that by crushing the enemies of Allah, the enemies of Allah's religion and the enemies of the Muslims themselves, hearts might be cooled.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 9, verse 3 (part 4 of 4):

"Will you not fight against a people who broke their oaths, and who intended to expel the Messenger, and who began the aggression against you the first time? Do you fear them? Yet Allah has more right that you should fear Him, if you are believers. Fight them, and Allah will punish them by your hands, and will disgrace them, and will help you against them, and will heal the breasts of a believing people, and will remove the rage of their hearts. And Allah turns in forgiveness to whom He wills, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise."

The circumstances demanded that there be a complete separation on the basis of principles, that personal interests and feelings of kinship be confronted, and that they not be allowed to become obstacles in the path of Allah, His Messenger, and jihad in the way of Allah. Thus the Muslims are placed between two paths, so that they must decide about one of them.

(Due to its great length, the complete commentary on this verse could not be included. We apologize for this. Please read the remainder of the commentary on this verse in the volume of Fi Zilal al-Quran.)

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 9, verse 4:

Having explained the general principle, we now come to the temporary exceptional situation. That is, this exceptional situation too is to come to an end and return to the principled situation mentioned in the first verse.

﴿Except those of the polytheists with whom you made a treaty, then they have not failed you in anything, nor have they supported anyone against you. So fulfil their treaty to them until their term. Indeed, Allah loves the God-fearing.﴾ Concerning whom did this exceptional clause come? The authentic reports say that it concerns a branch of Banu Bakr, namely Banu Khuzaymah ibn Amir, who were a branch of Bakr ibn Kinanah. At Hudaybiyah, the treaty made with Quraysh and their allies was upheld by them, and this group did not take part with Banu Bakr in the military campaign against Khuza'ah, whereas Quraysh had supported Banu Bakr, and it was through their support that they attacked Khuza'ah. Thus Banu Bakr and Quraysh broke the Treaty of Hudaybiyah, and Makkah was conquered two years after that treaty, although that treaty was for ten years. This group, Banu Bakr, namely Banu Khuzaymah ibn Amir, kept the covenant and remained upon polytheism. Accordingly, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered that the covenant with them be fulfilled for its term. Our view is also supported by the narration of Muhammad ibn Abbad ibn Ja'far. Al-Suddi says: "They were Banu Damrah and Banu Mudlij, two tribes of Banu Kinanah." Mujahid says: "The covenant was with Banu Mudlij and Khuza'ah, and it was concerning them that Allah said: fa-atimmu ilayhim 'ahdahum ila muddatihim (so fulfil their treaty to them until their term)." However, it should also be noted that after the conquest of Makkah, Khuza'ah accepted Islam. Therefore, this statement applies to those polytheists who remained upon polytheism. This is also confirmed by the following verse:

﴿How can there be a covenant for the polytheists with Allah and with His Messenger, except those with whom you made a treaty at al-Masjid al-Haram? So long as they remain upright toward you, be upright toward them. Indeed, Allah loves the God-fearing.﴾

These were the two tribes of Banu Kinanah who made a covenant with the Messenger of Allah at al-Masjid al-Haram on the day of Hudaybiyah, did not fail in their covenant, and did not support any enemy against the Messenger of Allah. Thus, this exceptional clause refers only to these people, and all the commentators have accepted this view. Ustadh Rashid Rida adopted this same view, but Ustadh Azzah Darwazah, in his commentary, took those referred to as "the others" in the first exception to mean other people than those mentioned. He adopted this view because he holds that treaties with polytheists may be permanent. He based his opinion on the phrase: fa-ma istaqamu lakum fa-istaqimu lahum (So long as they remain upright toward you, be upright toward them). He argues that a treaty with polytheists can be permanent. In truth, this is a far-fetched view, and it is contrary to these verses, to the real position of the Islamic system, and to the very temperament of this religion, as we have said repeatedly.

Islam established this exceptional clause so that loyalty would be shown to those who were loyal to the Islamic movement. Therefore, Islam did not limit their respite to four months, as had been fixed for other people; rather, they were given respite until the term of the treaty, because they had not broken their covenant and had not aided enemies. The requirement of this loyalty was that loyalty be shown to them, and this long term was granted despite the policy that Allah wished to purify the Arabian Peninsula of polytheists and make it a secure center of Islam. Because other enemies adjacent to the borders of the Arabian Peninsula had regarded Islam as a great threat, and, as will be discussed in the details of the Battle of Tabuk, they had begun preparations to confront this new power. Before that, the incident of Mu'tah had taken place, and it had opened eyes to how busily the Romans were preparing. Furthermore, these polytheists in southern Yemen sympathized with the Persians and intended, with Persian support, to attack the new religion.

Allamah Ibn al-Qayyim mentioned that those who were excluded by this verse and ordered to be given loyalty of covenant had become Muslims before the term of the covenant expired. Rather, the other people who had committed breach of covenant and had been given four months' respite, so that they could travel for four months, instead of travelling and going into exile, accepted Islam.

Allah had complete knowledge, and Allah was advancing the Islamic movement with His own power. He knew that the time had come to uproot shirk and kufr from the Arabian Peninsula. Circumstances had become ready for this final blow, the right time had arrived, and this step was taken at the right and appropriate time, in exact accordance with real events and circumstances, and in accordance with Allah's law of divine decree and destiny.

The command of Allah to keep the covenant is worthy of reflection here: that loyalty should be shown to those who are loyal. Fa-atimmu ilayhim 'ahdahum ila muddatihim; inna Allaha yuhibbu al-muttaqin (So fulfil their treaty to them until their term; indeed, Allah loves the God-fearing). Here, the fulfilment of covenant is linked with the fear of God, awe, and the love of Allah. That is, Allah loves the God-fearing. Therefore, fulfilling covenant is also a kind of worship and piety, and Allah loves piety. This is Islam's moral perspective. In the legal and moral system of Islam, expediency and interests have no importance, and there is no room in it for customs and traditions, because customs and traditions also keep changing. The foundation of the Islamic moral system is laid upon the servitude of Allah and the fear of God. The essential duty of a Muslim is to act upon those matters which his Lord loves. Thus Islamic morals are established upon the fear of God and the pleasure of Allah. This is why morals in the Islamic system possess strong power; they receive strength from this real and intuitive consciousness. Along with this consciousness, Islamic morals in practice are also beneficial for people, and their benefit is hidden within them. As a result, a collective society and community comes into being in which the conflict of mutual interests is minimized. In this system, human personality becomes elevated, and it becomes connected with the higher world in the face of the impurities of the earth.

After the announcement of disavowal by Allah and His Messenger concerning the polytheists, whether they are treaty-bound or not, the exception applies only to those who did not break their covenant and did not aid anyone against the Muslims.

Now the question is posed: what measures will the Muslims take at the end of this period?

On the meaning of the phrase "al-Ashhur al-Haram" (the sacred months), there are several opinions as to which months are meant. The commonly known sacred months are Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah and Muharram, and then Rajab. So the "four months" would mean three months plus the remaining twenty days of Dhu al-Hijjah, which makes fifty days, counted from the announcement. Alternatively, the period of four months is said to begin on the tenth of Dhu al-Hijjah and end on the tenth of Rabi' al-Akhir. Or it is said that the first period applies to those who broke their covenant, and the second period to those with whom there had been no prior covenant at all. These are the various opinions.

In my view, the four months mentioned here are not the technical "Ashhur Hurum" (sacred months). These four months are called "Ashhur Hurum" (sacred months) because fighting and bloodshed were declared forbidden in them, so that the polytheists could move about freely during that time. That was the general term. However, for those whose treaties had a fixed term, and for whom a respite was granted up to that term, since Allah had given them four months' freedom of choice, the start of this period should be counted from the announcement. Given the nature of that declaration, the preferred view is that this period should be reckoned as four months from the day of the announcement.

Allah commanded the Muslims that after this period expires, wherever they find a polytheist they should kill him or take him captive, and sit in every passage and ambush so that none of them can escape, except those who are exempted by a specific stipulation. They cannot treat them in any other way. Since the polytheists had been warned of an evil end for a long time and given respite, this action against them is neither sudden nor unjust, and since their agreements have been terminated, nothing should come as unexpected to them now.

However, this action against the polytheists was not intended to annihilate them, but so that they would accept Islam.

﴿فَاِنْ تَابُوْا وَاَقَامُوا الصَّلٰوةَ وَاٰتَوُا الزَّكٰوةَ فَخَــلُّوْا سَـبِيْلَهُمْ ۭاِنَّ اللّٰهَ غَفُوْرٌ رَّحِيْمٌ﴾: "But if they repent, establish prayer and give zakah, then let them go their way. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."

Before this, the Islamic movement had spent twelve years with them, and during that time the duty of da'wah and preaching had been fulfilled. In that period they inflicted immense suffering upon the Muslims. They launched armies against the Muslims and sought to overthrow their government. Yet the gentle attitude that Islam adopted towards them, and the noble conduct of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ towards them, is a long history. Despite this, the doors of Islam remain open to them, and Allah commands the Muslims who were tormented, fought against, expelled from their homeland and killed, and commands the Prophet ﷺ, that if these polytheists repent, then withhold your hand from them, if they sincerely accept Islam and embrace its symbols, through which it is evident that they have truly become Muslims, because Allah does not disappoint anyone who returns with sincere repentance. ﴿ان اللّٰه غفور رحيم﴾ "Indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." We do not enter into the jurisprudential debates that scholars have conducted about this verse, namely ﴿فان تابوا واقاموا الصلوة واتوا الزكوة﴾ "if they repent, establish prayer and give zakah." The jurists have debated whether performing prayer and paying zakah are among the conditions of Islam, whether one who abandons them is to be called a disbeliever, and when he would become one, and whether prayer and zakah alone are to be taken as the sign of repentance or whether other pillars of Islam are also to be required of them.

I believe that this verse was not revealed to resolve any of these questions. This text was revealed concerning the actual circumstances of the polytheists of Arabia at that time, and at that time there was no notion that someone who repented would act only upon prayer and zakah while neglecting other deeds. Whoever repented entered the whole of Islam. Although this verse mentions these two matters, it is because those who entered Islam at that time entered it with all its conditions, and the first of these conditions was that they would establish Allah's religion throughout their lives, and believe in the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ. Therefore, the debates that jurists and exegetes have conducted were not in view of this verse; rather, it was guidance concerning a practical course of action.

It should also be kept in mind that even after the four-month period, Islam does not abandon tolerance, seriousness and realism. As we have said, this struggle of Islam is not for genocide; rather it is a campaign of guidance. Those polytheists who are not organised into a jahili society, but exist as individuals, and who do not obstruct the path of Islam, have their rights to complete peace and security preserved within the Dar al-Islam. Allah commands the Messenger of Allah and the Muslims to grant them protection, so that they may hear the Word of Allah and understand it, and then convey them to a place where they may be safe.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 9, verse 6:

This shows that Islam has an intense desire that every person should be guided and come onto the right path. And if a person among the polytheists seeks refuge in the Abode of Islam (Dar al-Islam), it is an obligation of the Abode of Islam to grant him refuge, because when the polytheists become refugees in the Abode of Islam, then they will not be able to wage war against the Abode of Islam. Therefore, giving them refuge and making them acquainted with the Quran and the principles of the religion of Islam is beneficial. It is possible that in this way their hearts will open, they will be guided and accept. If they do not accept even then, Allah has made it obligatory upon the people of the Abode of Islam to protect them and deliver them to a country where they can live in peace and security.

This refuge of the Abode of Islam (Dar al-Islam) for the polytheists was in fact one of the high stations of Islam. And beyond this, in Islam, beyond one lofty peak, other lofty peaks and heights are visible, and among them this is an extremely exalted station: that a Muslim is the protector of a polytheist. He is the protector of an enemy of Islam and of Muslims, one who has inflicted severe torments upon Muslims and Islam and put them into difficulties, and yet protection is provided to him until he reaches some place outside the Abode of Islam. This is an extremely exalted station of tolerance.

It becomes clear that Islam is a system of guidance and that it is not a system of genocide. Its purpose is only that it should arrange an extremely secure and protected centre for Islam.

Those who raise objections against the doctrine of jihad in the Islamic system, claiming that through it people are forced to accept Islamic beliefs, and then those Muslims who read the accusations of the Orientalists become apprehensive and adopt a defensive stance in response to these accusations, and then take the position that Islam fights only in defence, and that it defends only within its own state boundaries — both of these groups, namely those who level accusations and those who defend against them, should rise to this exalted station of Islam, cast a glance over the world, and then read this verse again and reflect. They will find the entire history of humanity low, and found empty-handed.

﴿And if any one of the polytheists seeks your protection, then grant him protection so that he may hear the Word of Allah; then deliver him to his place of safety. That is because they are a people who do not know.﴾ Thus this religion is a warning for those who do not know. And this religion is a place of refuge for those who seek refuge. Indeed, it is also for those enemies who took up the sword against it, waged war against it and held enmity towards it. Islam raises the banner of jihad at the time when material powers stand between the Islamic call and the common people, and obstruct the call from reaching their ears, and become obstacles in the path of the Word of Allah, blocking the way of guidance. Moreover, these material powers stand in the way of freeing people from the servitude and worship of humans, and compel people to continue worshipping other than Allah. And when these powers are broken and these obstacles are removed from the path of the Islamic call, then all individuals become free, "free in their own opinion." Islam then only teaches them; it neither compels them, nor kills anyone needlessly, but rather conveys them, protects them, and then grants them refuge up to their place of safety. This treatment is given despite their conduct of denying the Islamic system.

In the present world there are systems and ways of life that have been fashioned by humans themselves. If anyone opposes these man-made systems and ways of life, his life is not secure, nor is his property secure, nor is his honour secure, nor are his other human rights secure. Some people see such a situation in the world with their own eyes in practice, and yet in response to these baseless accusations and calumnies against Islam they make excuses and "shuf shuf" (hesitant murmuring), and in response they resort to a defeated mentality, a weak position, and, against the sword and the cannon, mere apology and the pen, and then [there is] our modern age.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 9, verse 7:

In the preceding verses, the final form of relations between the Islamic state and the other communities of the Arabian Peninsula, and the polytheists of the Arabian Peninsula, was regulated. The purpose of that measure was that the state of treaty and peace between the Islamic state and those other groups should come to an end. Some of them were given a respite of four months, and some were given a respite until the end of the term of their treaty. After these terms expired, only two forms of relations would remain: either they accept Islam, establish prayer and pay zakat, that is, accept Islam and become bound by all its obligations; or they must be prepared for fighting, captivity and siege.

When the situation has become such, then in the following verses, in the form of a rhetorical question, a denial and a warning in strong words are issued: it is neither appropriate nor should it be that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ make any covenant with a polytheist; that is, in principle, it should not happen at all. This matter is fundamentally contrary to the temperament of Islam.

﴿How can there be a covenant for the polytheists with Allah and with His Messenger?﴾ Through this rhetorical question of denial in the present verses, it could have been understood that the respite granted in the earlier verses to those whose treaties had a fixed term, who had kept their treaties and had not been hostile to the Muslims, might perhaps have been withdrawn by the present verse and command. Therefore it is repeated here that the respite of such people remains.

﴿Except those with whom you made a covenant at al-Masjid al-Haram. So long as they remain straight with you, be straight with them. Indeed, Allah loves the righteous.﴾ However, an addition has come in this renewed emphasis. In the earlier command, it was stated that respite had been granted to them because they had not broken their covenant in the past. Here a condition is imposed: that from the revelation of this verse until the end of the term of the treaty, they too must remain bound to keep the covenant. This shows that the Holy Qur'an has employed great precision in regulating international affairs. Instead of mere allusions and inference, it was considered necessary to bring an explicit text.

In light of what we have said in the introduction to this surah and to this section, and of the circumstances and phenomena existing within the Muslim society at the time the surah was revealed, it becomes well understood why this decisive step was taken. Now, in the verses that follow, while consoling the Muslims and removing the doubts, hesitations and anxieties that arose in their hearts, they are made aware of the reality of the thoughts and intentions of these very polytheists regarding the Muslims and the Islamic system: they do not keep any regard for any covenant made with the Muslims. In this matter they consider every action lawful, and they are always ready to break these treaties. They never fulfil them; they never bind themselves to their covenant; and whenever they gain power, they are always ready to attack the Muslims. Therefore there is no need to create a state of security and peace with them, nor can any trust be placed in them in this regard, unless they enter Islam.

﴿How can there be a covenant for the polytheists with Allah and with His Messenger?﴾ Polytheists do not serve only one Allah. They also do not acknowledge the prophethood of Muhammad. How then can there be for them a covenant with the Messenger of Allah? Their condition is that they cannot deny the status of creatures like themselves, nor can they deny the systems made by humans; but on the other hand they deny their Creator and true Provider. They are hostile to Allah and His Messenger, so how can there be for them a covenant with Allah and His Messenger?

In this rhetorical question the matter is raised, and this matter is so important that in principle it rejects the very idea that there could be any covenant at all between a Muslim, or Allah and His Messenger, and a polytheist, apart from the existing treaties.

Here the question arises: at the time this verse was revealed, treaties with the polytheists were in practice in force, and regarding some of these treaties Allah Himself commanded that they be fulfilled until their term; and with the establishment of the Islamic state in Medina, treaties were concluded with the unbelievers. Treaties were made with the Jews, treaties were made with the polytheists; in the sixth year of Hijrah the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah took place, and the earlier verses also permit such treaties, though those verses also command that if there is a fear of treachery, these treaties may be annulled. If the verse under discussion regards in principle the very idea of a covenant with the polytheists as far-fetched, then why were such treaties permitted, why were they concluded, and why then does this rhetorical denial come upon them?

If the methodology of the Islamic movement is understood in the manner we have tried to explain in the previous pages, then this difficulty does not arise at all, in the beginning of this surah and at the beginning of Surah al-Anfal. In reality these treaties were concluded at a specified time, because of certain practical circumstances, and they were appropriate means of war for the appropriate moment. They were for an interim period. The final, ultimate and definitive guidance, however, is that there should be no covenant with the polytheists, and that no covenant should henceforth exist for the polytheists with Allah and His Messenger. The ultimate goal of the Islamic movement was that there should be no system other than the Islamic system, and that no partner of Allah should exist on the face of the earth; but the treaties were made for the interim period. As far as the ultimate goal of Islam is concerned, it was declared from the very first day. The demand of the initial and interim period was that those polytheists who did not fight the Muslims should be left to their own condition, and that those who fought should be dealt with. And that those who in any phase of the movement desired friendship should be befriended; treaties should be made with those who wished to make treaties; and those who wished to remain neutral should be left to remain so. But the ultimate goal was nonetheless that the workers of the movement never ceased to aim, at any time, at the elimination of shirk from the whole earth and especially from the Arabian Peninsula. It should also be kept in view that the treaties which the polytheists themselves made with the people of Islam were also for a fixed time, and it was inevitable that after the term expired they could attack. How could they keep faith with the Prophet, when they knew well what his objectives were? They established a state of peace with him so that during that time they could make preparations against him. And Allah had given the Muslims a permanent guidance, which was not restricted to any time or place.

﴿And they will not cease to fight you until they turn you back from your religion, if they are able.﴾ This is a permanent statement, a permanent admonition, not restricted to any age, any society, or any era.

In principle, alongside the denial of all treaties, Allah kept the treaties of those people in force until the end of their term, who neither broke their covenant nor took part in any action against the Muslims, provided that they continue this same conduct in future; this condition is newly imposed here.

﴿Except those with whom you made a covenant at al-Masjid al-Haram. So long as they remain straight with you, be straight with them. Indeed, Allah loves the righteous.﴾

Those people to whom this verse alludes, who made a covenant with you at al-Masjid al-Haram, are the same as those already mentioned.

﴿Except those with whom you made a covenant at al-Masjid al-Haram. So long as they remain straight with you, be straight with them. Indeed, Allah loves the righteous.﴾

In this verse no one other than them is meant, as some exegetes have understood. They are the same people mentioned in verse four as an exception to the general disavowal, and they are mentioned a second time because Allah, by "How can there be," negated in principle any covenant with every polytheist. So an exception was made again, lest this principled verse be taken to abrogate the earlier exception. Here too taqwa is mentioned, and it is stated that Allah loves the righteous, and there too a similar statement was made; the purpose of the allusion was that the subject is one and the subject of the verse is the same, while in the second verse the exception adds that just as in the past they kept their conduct upright, so in the future too they must keep their conduct upright. As we have said, this is an extremely precise legal formulation, a proviso, and reading the two verses together it follows that just as they kept faith in the past, so the respite will continue only while they remain upright in future too, that is, during the period of the respite.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran), Urdu translation, on Surah 9, verses 8–9:

Now it is explained why, in principle, treaties with the polytheists have been prohibited. The historical reasons are listed here. The practical necessity is being stated, and attention is drawn to the ideological and faith-based separations and contradictions between the two sides.

...

How can there be a covenant of Allah and His Messenger with the polytheists? They make covenants only when they are unable to face you. If they overpower you and gain the upper hand, they will do to you things that you cannot even imagine. Then they will not respect any treaty, nor keep any sense of their obligations. They will not hesitate to commit disgraceful acts against you, because by nature they have no regard for any covenant or any ties of kinship, and they cross all limits in oppression and injustice. In your case, they do not even consider those disgraceful acts to be disgraceful, which they generally regard as very shameful in their own society and do not commit. The hatred against you in their hearts is so great that they are ready to inflict every kind of cruelty upon you, provided they gain power, even when treaties are in place. It is not that they refrain from taking action against you merely because of treaties; rather, they simply do not have the power. Today, while you are strong, they speak to you gently in outward appearance and show loyalty, but their hearts are boiling with enmity towards you, and they have no motive to remain faithful to a covenant, because in them there is neither fidelity nor love. Their condition is this: ﴿And most of them are defiant transgressors﴾ [9:8]. ﴿They have sold the signs of Allah for a small price, and they have barred others from His way. Evil indeed is what they have been doing﴾ [9:9]. Their hearts are full of envy and resentment towards you, and this is the real reason. For this reason they are not faithful in the treaties agreed upon with you. And whenever they feel they have strength, they rise up to take revenge against you. In this matter they feel no hesitation or reluctance. Because of these qualities they are described as defiant and are considered to be outside the guidance of Allah. The signs of Allah came to them, and they cast them behind their backs in exchange for a few coins. The world in which they live is so dear to them that they preferred its interests over the signs of Allah. They feared that the reformist system of Islam would harm their interests or that they would have to make some additional payments. Therefore, they used to prevent others from coming to Islam, and they themselves would not come to it. In this way, these people became leaders of disbelief. Hence Allah described their conduct as the root of evil, or of evils. ﴿Evil indeed is what they have been doing﴾. The hatred and rancour found in the hearts of these people is not limited to you, and their malicious plan is not confined to you alone. They have concealed this envy for all the believers. They treat every Muslim with the same malicious behaviour. In fact, their treatment is directed at your quality, that is, the quality of faith and Islam, and the quality of faith and Islam. Those in Islamic history in whom this quality was found were treated in exactly this way. This was expressed by those believing sorcerers who fell victim to Pharaoh's desire for revenge and wrath. They said: ﴿And you are taking revenge on us only because we believed in the signs of our Lord when they came to us﴾ [7:126]. And the Messenger of Allah, in accordance with the guidance of his Lord, said the same to the People of the Book: ﴿Say: "O People of the Book, do you resent us only because we believe in Allah?"﴾ [5:59]. And Allah said the same about the People of the Trench, when they were burned: ﴿They tormented them only because they believed in Allah, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾ [85:8]. In short, the reason for the vengeance of the polytheists was nothing other than the quality of faith. This is why the enemies of Islam have held enmity towards every believer solely because of faith, and in this matter they have paid no regard to any covenant, pact, or ties of kinship.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 9, verse 11–12 (part 1 of 2):

11–12: Now it is explained in detail how the believers should conduct themselves towards the polytheists in these circumstances.
...
The Muslims face enemies who are always lying in wait, and they hold back from launching a merciless attack on the Muslims only because they lack the strength to attack from within. This is not because they observe any covenant or pact, nor because they feel any sense of responsibility, nor because they are affected by the blame and censure of any critic, nor do they respect any ties of kinship or relationship. The struggle between religion and irreligion has a long history, and this history has continued along this same path. If there has been any deviation from this highway, it has been only due to temporary causes, and quickly history returns to the line that has been fixed and marked out.
On the one hand, we have before us this practical history; on the other hand, the nature of the goals of the Islamic system of life is that, in view of them, people are to be delivered from servitude to human beings and given over to servitude to Allah alone, whereas the goals of all the jahili systems of life, in contrast to the Islamic system of life, are that people remain slaves of people. In such circumstances, the movement of the Islamic system of life addresses the world in this manner:
فَاِنْ تَابُوْا وَاَقَامُوا الصَّلٰوةَ وَاٰتَوُا الزَّكٰوةَ فَاِخْوَانُكُمْ فِي الدِّيْنِ ۭوَنُفَصِّلُ الْاٰيٰتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَّعْلَمُوْنَ: "So if they repent, establish prayer and give zakah, then they are your brothers in religion. And We detail the verses for a people who know."
وَاِنْ نَّكَثُوْٓا اَيْمَانَهُمْ مِّنْۢ بَعْدِ عَهْدِهِمْ وَطَعَنُوْا فِيْ دِيْنِكُمْ فَقَاتِلُوْٓا اَىِٕمَّةَ الْكُفْرِ ۙ اِنَّهُمْ لَآ اَيْمَانَ لَهُمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَنْتَهُوْنَ: "And if they break their oaths after their covenant and attack your religion, then fight the leaders of disbelief, for indeed they have no oaths, that perhaps they may cease." (Meaning: perhaps, by the power of the sword, they will desist.)
Then the situation will be that either they will enter the religion that the Muslims have entered, repent of their previous sins, and abandon polytheism and oppression. Then the Muslims will overlook their polytheism and oppression, a doctrinal bond will be established between them, these new Muslims will become brothers of the earlier Muslims, and all their past will be forgotten, both from history and from hearts. And it is said: وَنُفَصِّلُ الْاٰيٰتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَّعْلَمُوْنَ, that is, only those people can understand these rulings, and only those who are people of knowledge can reach their wisdom. Or else the situation will be that they turn away from the religion of Islam even though they had given a covenant to it, and they keep finding fault with the religion of Islam; then they will be the leaders of disbelief. Their hearts will have no faith, and their covenants and pacts will have no value. Then for us there will be no option except to begin war against them, and there will be no other way. Perhaps through the force of the sword they will desist. Earlier we have said that the strength of the Islamic camp and its military dominance sometimes inclines people to become ready to accept the truth. They see that the truth prevails, so they accept it, and their reasoning is that since this system prevails, it is true, and that behind it stands divine power, and that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said that in the end Allah and His messengers will certainly prevail. In this way, these people, having been convinced in their minds, accept guidance and repent. It will not happen that their religion is changed by force because of war. Rather, they will become content in this way, because the religion of Islam will be moving before them in a successful form, and sometimes the practical experience of a matter produces such results.
----
Now we consider it necessary to clarify the point of what the scope of this policy is. In which period of history was this policy in practice, in which dynasty and in which society was it implemented? Was this policy specific to the people of the Arabian Peninsula at the beginning of Islam, or has its scope and field of application extended in history and in any other time and place?
At the beginning, when these verses were revealed, their implementation was in the final phase of the struggle between Islam and polytheism in the Arabian Peninsula, and there is no doubt that these rulings were first applied to that situation. And in these verses, the polytheists referred to are those very polytheists with whom the Messenger ﷺ had to deal.
It is entirely true that the historical background was this, but the question is: is this the final scope of these verses, and are these verses limited to this alone?
Here it is appropriate for us to review historically the stance and conduct of the polytheists towards the Muslims, so that we may know what the aims, purposes and limits of the policy declared in these verses are, and how far its scope extends. We should turn the pages of history and look briefly.
As far as the Arabian Peninsula is concerned, there is ample material on this in this very section of Fi Zilal al-Quran. The events of the Seerah are well known: how the polytheists treated the religion of Islam in Makkah, and then what they continued to do against the Islamic state in Madinah. The oppression they inflicted on those who believed, the detailed account of which has been fully given within those texts.
It is also an undeniable reality that the struggle between Islam and polytheism has not been as long and intense as the struggle between Islam and the People of the Book, Jews and Christians. But it remains the case that the polytheists also always adopted the same stance against Islam that is depicted in these verses:
كَيْفَ وَاِنْ يَّظْهَرُوْا عَلَيْكُمْ لَا يَرْقُبُوْا فِيْكُمْ اِلًّا وَّلَا ذِمَّةً ۭ يُرْضُوْنَكُمْ بِاَفْوَاهِهِمْ وَتَاْبٰي قُلُوْبُهُمْ ۚ وَاَكْثَرُهُمْ فٰسِقُوْنَ. اِشْتَرَوْا بِاٰيٰتِ اللّٰهِ ثَـمَنًا قَلِيْلًا فَصَدُّوْا عَنْ سَبِيْلِهٖ ۭاِنَّهُمْ سَاۗءَ مَا كَانُوْا يَعْمَلُوْنَ. لَا يَرْقُبُوْنَ فِيْ مُؤْمِنٍ اِلًّا وَّلَا ذِمَّةً ۭ وَاُولٰۗىِٕكَ هُمُ الْمُعْتَدُوْنَ: "How (can there be a covenant with them) when, if they gain the upper hand over you, they would not observe regarding you any tie of kinship or pact? They satisfy you with their mouths, but their hearts refuse, and most of them are defiantly disobedient. They have exchanged the verses of Allah for a small price and averted [people] from His way. Evil is what they have been doing. They do not observe regarding a believer any tie of kinship or pact, and it is those who are the transgressors."
The stance of the polytheists and the People of the Book towards the Muslims has been a permanent and settled one. The treatment that the People of the Book meted out to the Muslims will be mentioned in the context of the second lesson of this surah, and as far as the polytheists are concerned, throughout the entire Islamic history they remained on this same policy against the Muslims.
If we reflect on the fact that Islam did not begin with the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ, but rather the Islamic call concluded with him, and that throughout human history the stance of the polytheists against the religion of the Lord of the worlds has remained one and the same, then the whole of Islamic history will join together as one continuous thread. In this way this stance will be well understood, and it will be established as a reality just as it is described in these texts, and the entire Islamic and human history will bear witness to it.
What the polytheists did against Prophets Nuh, Hud, Salih, Ibrahim, Shu'ayb, Musa and Isa (peace be upon them), and how they treated the nations of those prophets in their respective eras, and finally what they did to Muhammad ﷺ, and after him what treatment they meted out to the believers: the truth is that they paid no regard to any ties of kinship or any covenant concerning the Muslims. Whenever they got the opportunity, and whenever they gained strength, they attacked the sanctuary of the religion of the Lord of the worlds.
The polytheists launched a second attack against the Muslims in the form of the Tatars. Keep the events of that in mind, and consider what they have not been doing against the Muslims even after fourteen hundred years, and in what part of the earth they are not doing it. The truth is that they show no regard for any ties of kinship or any covenant concerning the Muslims. And these divine verses unveil an eternal reality.
When the idol-worshippers gained dominance over Baghdad, the tragedy that occurred then has some glimpses recorded in the history books. We give some glimpses from Tarikh Abu al-Fida. Abu al-Fida, in al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, under the events of the year 656 AH, wrote:
"They fell upon this city (Baghdad), and they killed as many children, women, men, the elderly and the aged as they could kill. Many people hid out of fear in wells, took refuge in thickets, and in filthy ponds. These people remained hidden in those places for a long time and did not appear. Some people locked themselves in shops, closed the doors; the Tatars would break the doors or set them on fire and enter. These people would climb onto roofs, and so on the surface of the houses they would kill them, and their blood would flow through the gutters and into the streets. Innâ lillâhi wa innâ ilayhi râji'ûn. The killing of people continued in mosques, madrasas and caravanserais, and except for the dhimmi Jews and Christians, no one else remained alive, or those who remained were those who took refuge with the Tatars, or those who took refuge with the minister Ibn al-Alqami, who was a Rafidi; some merchants also obtained safe-conduct in exchange for heavy bribes. In this way they and their wealth were saved. And after this disaster, Baghdad, which was the crown of cities, became as though it were a wasteland, with only a few people remaining in it, and they too in a state of fear, drowned in hunger, humiliation and poverty."
"Regarding the exact number of Muslims who were put to the sword in Baghdad in this event, there is disagreement. Some said that eight hundred thousand people were killed. Some put this number at one million, and some put it at two million. Innâ lillâhi wa innâ ilayhi râji'ûn. Wa lâ hawla wa lâ quwwata illâ billâhi al-'Aliyyi al-'Azhim. The Tatars entered Baghdad in the last days of Muharram. They continued killing people for a full forty days. The caliph al-Mu'tasim, Amir al-Mu'minin, was killed on Tuesday, 14 Safar. He was sixteen years old. Then his second son Abu al-Fadl 'Abd al-Rahman was killed; he was thirteen years old. His youngest son Mubarak and three daughters, Fatimah, Khadijah and Maryam, were taken captive."
"The teacher of the court, Muhyi al-Din Yusuf ibn Shaykh al-Faraj ibn al-Jawzi, was also killed; he was an opponent of the minister. His three children were also killed, whose names were 'Abd al-Rahman, 'Abd al-Karim and 'Abd Allah. And the leading figures of the government were killed one by one, among them the two chamberlains Sagir, Mujahid al-Din Aybak, Shihab al-Din Sulayman Shah, and the leaders of Ahl al-Sunnah and the notables of the city. Their method of operation was this: they would summon people from the caliphal palace together with their families. Their children and women would also be with them. They would be led towards the Tomb of Khallal, towards al-Manzarah, and there they would be slaughtered in the way a sheep is slaughtered. Whichever of their girls and slave-women they liked, they would take as captives. The courtier and shaykh al-shuyukh of the caliph, Sadr al-Din 'Ali ibn al-Nayyar, was also killed. Preachers, imams and Qur'an memorizers, all were put to death."
"When the ruins had risen and the forty days were complete, Baghdad had been brought to total destruction. In the whole city only a few people could be seen. On the roads there were heaps of corpses. Then it rained, and the bodies of the people swelled. The whole city was drowned in stench and putrefaction. The air changed, a severe plague spread in the region, and a great multitude became the prey of death. The common people of the entire area were seized by plague and famine. They departed to the path of non-existence by the sword and the plague. Innâ lillâhi wa innâ ilayhi râji'ûn."
"And when after forty days a proclamation of safety was made in Baghdad and people emerged from cellars, ambush places and graveyards, they were like the dead rising from their graves. They could not recognize one another, to the point that a father denied his sons, and a brother did not recognize his brother. A severe plague spread among the people, and in this way they too departed on the path on which the slain had gone." etc.

This was a historical situation: when the polytheists gained the upper hand over the Muslims, they paid no regard to ties of kinship, to treaties, or to any obligation, and gave no proof of any responsibility. Do you think this was a remote historical situation, and that only the Tatars among the polytheists committed it, and that it was their particular trait? It is certainly not so. The events of the modern age are no different in their features. When Pakistan was formed and the territories of the Muslims were separated from India, the heart-rending events of that time were in no way less than the events of the destruction of Baghdad. On that occasion eight million Muslims migrated. Attacks were carried out against the Muslims living in various parts of India. For this reason they considered it appropriate to migrate towards Pakistan. Of them, only three million people were able to reach Pakistan, and the remaining five million were put to the sword on the way. These refugees and travellers were attacked by Hindu troops, as is known to the government of India, and these troops carried out this massacre under the supervision of the leaders of the Government of India. Throughout that route of migration, these Muslims were slaughtered like cattle, and their bodies were left for the birds of prey, and after killing them the worst cruelty was inflicted upon them. The oppressions they suffered were in no way less than those of the Tatars. Greater cruelty took place when a train carrying Muslim migrant employees from India to Pakistan was attacked. It was travelling under the Liaquat-Nehru agreement, carrying those employees who had chosen to go to Pakistan. Fifty thousand people were on board that train. When the train reached certain boundaries (the area of the Punjab), experienced Hindu and Sikh troops attacked it, and when it reached Pakistan there was nothing inside it except corpses and severed limbs. How well Allah has said: "كَيْفَ وَاِنْ يَّظْهَرُوْا عَلَيْكُمْ لَا يَرْقُبُوْا فِيْكُمْ اِلًّا وَّلَا ذِمَّةً" — "How can it be? For if they gain the upper hand over you, they do not observe towards you any tie of kinship or any covenant." According to various estimates and in various forms, this massacre has continued to happen. In this era the disturbances in the Punjab were a clear example of it.

After this, see how the successors of the Tatars treated Muslims in Communist Russia and Communist China. In these areas, in just twenty-five years, they annihilated 26 million Muslims. That is to say, they went on killing a million Muslims a year in Russia. And this process is still continuing. Apart from these, there are the events of oppression and cruelty at which one's hair stands on end. In recent days, events of this kind have taken place in China, before which the cruelties of the Tatars pale. A leader of the Muslims was seized and brought forward. A pit was dug on the public highway, and the Muslims were compelled to bring human excrement in baskets. In these areas it is the custom that people are made to gather excrement and refuse for making fertiliser, and in return they are given bread, so that fertiliser can be prepared from it. In short, these people were ordered to throw this filth upon that Muslim leader. This continued for three rounds, until he died in this way.

In Communist Yugoslavia too, the Muslims were treated in the same way, and when the Communist system was established there after the Second World War, several million Muslims were annihilated. To the extent that in some places Muslim men and women were thrown into mincing factories so that bones and flesh emerged from the other side, and this process is still continuing.

What is happening in Yugoslavia, this process is going on day and night against Muslims in all Communist countries. It is still happening, and in this modern age it is occurring. And through this, the saying of the Exalted Lord is confirmed: كَيْفَ وَاِنْ يَّظْهَرُوْا عَلَيْكُمْ لَا يَرْقُبُوْا فِيْكُمْ اِلًّا وَّلَا ذِمَّةً — "How can it be? For if they gain the upper hand over you, they do not observe towards you any tie of kinship or any covenant." This situation in the Arabian Peninsula was neither a temporary circumstance nor a passing one. In Baghdad it was not a sudden incident or state either. It is a permanent and constant pattern of conduct. Whenever the people of polytheism gain control over a believer, one who worships Allah alone, their conduct towards that believer is always this, everywhere and in every age.
