At the beginning, when these verses were revealed, their implementation was in the final phase of the struggle between Islam and polytheism in the Arabian Peninsula, and there is no doubt that these rulings were first applied to that situation. And in these verses, the polytheists referred to are those very polytheists with whom the Messenger ﷺ had to deal.
It is entirely true that the historical background was this, but the question is: is this the final scope of these verses, and are these verses limited to this alone?
Here it is appropriate for us to review historically the stance and conduct of the polytheists towards the Muslims, so that we may know what the aims, purposes and limits of the policy declared in these verses are, and how far its scope extends. We should turn the pages of history and look briefly.
As far as the Arabian Peninsula is concerned, there is ample material on this in this very section of Fi Zilal al-Quran. The events of the Seerah are well known: how the polytheists treated the religion of Islam in Makkah, and then what they continued to do against the Islamic state in Madinah. The oppression they inflicted on those who believed, the detailed account of which has been fully given within those texts.
It is also an undeniable reality that the struggle between Islam and polytheism has not been as long and intense as the struggle between Islam and the People of the Book, Jews and Christians. But it remains the case that the polytheists also always adopted the same stance against Islam that is depicted in these verses:
كَيْفَ وَاِنْ يَّظْهَرُوْا عَلَيْكُمْ لَا يَرْقُبُوْا فِيْكُمْ اِلًّا وَّلَا ذِمَّةً ۭ يُرْضُوْنَكُمْ بِاَفْوَاهِهِمْ وَتَاْبٰي قُلُوْبُهُمْ ۚ وَاَكْثَرُهُمْ فٰسِقُوْنَ. اِشْتَرَوْا بِاٰيٰتِ اللّٰهِ ثَـمَنًا قَلِيْلًا فَصَدُّوْا عَنْ سَبِيْلِهٖ ۭاِنَّهُمْ سَاۗءَ مَا كَانُوْا يَعْمَلُوْنَ. لَا يَرْقُبُوْنَ فِيْ مُؤْمِنٍ اِلًّا وَّلَا ذِمَّةً ۭ وَاُولٰۗىِٕكَ هُمُ الْمُعْتَدُوْنَ: "How (can there be a covenant with them) when, if they gain the upper hand over you, they would not observe regarding you any tie of kinship or pact? They satisfy you with their mouths, but their hearts refuse, and most of them are defiantly disobedient. They have exchanged the verses of Allah for a small price and averted [people] from His way. Evil is what they have been doing. They do not observe regarding a believer any tie of kinship or pact, and it is those who are the transgressors."
The stance of the polytheists and the People of the Book towards the Muslims has been a permanent and settled one. The treatment that the People of the Book meted out to the Muslims will be mentioned in the context of the second lesson of this surah, and as far as the polytheists are concerned, throughout the entire Islamic history they remained on this same policy against the Muslims.
If we reflect on the fact that Islam did not begin with the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ, but rather the Islamic call concluded with him, and that throughout human history the stance of the polytheists against the religion of the Lord of the worlds has remained one and the same, then the whole of Islamic history will join together as one continuous thread. In this way this stance will be well understood, and it will be established as a reality just as it is described in these texts, and the entire Islamic and human history will bear witness to it.
What the polytheists did against Prophets Nuh, Hud, Salih, Ibrahim, Shu'ayb, Musa and Isa (peace be upon them), and how they treated the nations of those prophets in their respective eras, and finally what they did to Muhammad ﷺ, and after him what treatment they meted out to the believers: the truth is that they paid no regard to any ties of kinship or any covenant concerning the Muslims. Whenever they got the opportunity, and whenever they gained strength, they attacked the sanctuary of the religion of the Lord of the worlds.
The polytheists launched a second attack against the Muslims in the form of the Tatars. Keep the events of that in mind, and consider what they have not been doing against the Muslims even after fourteen hundred years, and in what part of the earth they are not doing it. The truth is that they show no regard for any ties of kinship or any covenant concerning the Muslims. And these divine verses unveil an eternal reality.
When the idol-worshippers gained dominance over Baghdad, the tragedy that occurred then has some glimpses recorded in the history books. We give some glimpses from Tarikh Abu al-Fida. Abu al-Fida, in al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, under the events of the year 656 AH, wrote:
"They fell upon this city (Baghdad), and they killed as many children, women, men, the elderly and the aged as they could kill. Many people hid out of fear in wells, took refuge in thickets, and in filthy ponds. These people remained hidden in those places for a long time and did not appear. Some people locked themselves in shops, closed the doors; the Tatars would break the doors or set them on fire and enter. These people would climb onto roofs, and so on the surface of the houses they would kill them, and their blood would flow through the gutters and into the streets. Innâ lillâhi wa innâ ilayhi râji'ûn. The killing of people continued in mosques, madrasas and caravanserais, and except for the dhimmi Jews and Christians, no one else remained alive, or those who remained were those who took refuge with the Tatars, or those who took refuge with the minister Ibn al-Alqami, who was a Rafidi; some merchants also obtained safe-conduct in exchange for heavy bribes. In this way they and their wealth were saved. And after this disaster, Baghdad, which was the crown of cities, became as though it were a wasteland, with only a few people remaining in it, and they too in a state of fear, drowned in hunger, humiliation and poverty."
"Regarding the exact number of Muslims who were put to the sword in Baghdad in this event, there is disagreement. Some said that eight hundred thousand people were killed. Some put this number at one million, and some put it at two million. Innâ lillâhi wa innâ ilayhi râji'ûn. Wa lâ hawla wa lâ quwwata illâ billâhi al-'Aliyyi al-'Azhim. The Tatars entered Baghdad in the last days of Muharram. They continued killing people for a full forty days. The caliph al-Mu'tasim, Amir al-Mu'minin, was killed on Tuesday, 14 Safar. He was sixteen years old. Then his second son Abu al-Fadl 'Abd al-Rahman was killed; he was thirteen years old. His youngest son Mubarak and three daughters, Fatimah, Khadijah and Maryam, were taken captive."
"The teacher of the court, Muhyi al-Din Yusuf ibn Shaykh al-Faraj ibn al-Jawzi, was also killed; he was an opponent of the minister. His three children were also killed, whose names were 'Abd al-Rahman, 'Abd al-Karim and 'Abd Allah. And the leading figures of the government were killed one by one, among them the two chamberlains Sagir, Mujahid al-Din Aybak, Shihab al-Din Sulayman Shah, and the leaders of Ahl al-Sunnah and the notables of the city. Their method of operation was this: they would summon people from the caliphal palace together with their families. Their children and women would also be with them. They would be led towards the Tomb of Khallal, towards al-Manzarah, and there they would be slaughtered in the way a sheep is slaughtered. Whichever of their girls and slave-women they liked, they would take as captives. The courtier and shaykh al-shuyukh of the caliph, Sadr al-Din 'Ali ibn al-Nayyar, was also killed. Preachers, imams and Qur'an memorizers, all were put to death."
"When the ruins had risen and the forty days were complete, Baghdad had been brought to total destruction. In the whole city only a few people could be seen. On the roads there were heaps of corpses. Then it rained, and the bodies of the people swelled. The whole city was drowned in stench and putrefaction. The air changed, a severe plague spread in the region, and a great multitude became the prey of death. The common people of the entire area were seized by plague and famine. They departed to the path of non-existence by the sword and the plague. Innâ lillâhi wa innâ ilayhi râji'ûn."
"And when after forty days a proclamation of safety was made in Baghdad and people emerged from cellars, ambush places and graveyards, they were like the dead rising from their graves. They could not recognize one another, to the point that a father denied his sons, and a brother did not recognize his brother. A severe plague spread among the people, and in this way they too departed on the path on which the slain had gone." etc.

This was a historical situation: when the polytheists gained the upper hand over the Muslims, they paid no regard to ties of kinship, to treaties, or to any obligation, and gave no proof of any responsibility. Do you think this was a remote historical situation, and that only the Tatars among the polytheists committed it, and that it was their particular trait? It is certainly not so. The events of the modern age are no different in their features. When Pakistan was formed and the territories of the Muslims were separated from India, the heart-rending events of that time were in no way less than the events of the destruction of Baghdad. On that occasion eight million Muslims migrated. Attacks were carried out against the Muslims living in various parts of India. For this reason they considered it appropriate to migrate towards Pakistan. Of them, only three million people were able to reach Pakistan, and the remaining five million were put to the sword on the way. These refugees and travellers were attacked by Hindu troops, as is known to the government of India, and these troops carried out this massacre under the supervision of the leaders of the Government of India. Throughout that route of migration, these Muslims were slaughtered like cattle, and their bodies were left for the birds of prey, and after killing them the worst cruelty was inflicted upon them. The oppressions they suffered were in no way less than those of the Tatars. Greater cruelty took place when a train carrying Muslim migrant employees from India to Pakistan was attacked. It was travelling under the Liaquat-Nehru agreement, carrying those employees who had chosen to go to Pakistan. Fifty thousand people were on board that train. When the train reached certain boundaries (the area of the Punjab), experienced Hindu and Sikh troops attacked it, and when it reached Pakistan there was nothing inside it except corpses and severed limbs. How well Allah has said: "كَيْفَ وَاِنْ يَّظْهَرُوْا عَلَيْكُمْ لَا يَرْقُبُوْا فِيْكُمْ اِلًّا وَّلَا ذِمَّةً" — "How can it be? For if they gain the upper hand over you, they do not observe towards you any tie of kinship or any covenant." According to various estimates and in various forms, this massacre has continued to happen. In this era the disturbances in the Punjab were a clear example of it.

After this, see how the successors of the Tatars treated Muslims in Communist Russia and Communist China. In these areas, in just twenty-five years, they annihilated 26 million Muslims. That is to say, they went on killing a million Muslims a year in Russia. And this process is still continuing. Apart from these, there are the events of oppression and cruelty at which one's hair stands on end. In recent days, events of this kind have taken place in China, before which the cruelties of the Tatars pale. A leader of the Muslims was seized and brought forward. A pit was dug on the public highway, and the Muslims were compelled to bring human excrement in baskets. In these areas it is the custom that people are made to gather excrement and refuse for making fertiliser, and in return they are given bread, so that fertiliser can be prepared from it. In short, these people were ordered to throw this filth upon that Muslim leader. This continued for three rounds, until he died in this way.

In Communist Yugoslavia too, the Muslims were treated in the same way, and when the Communist system was established there after the Second World War, several million Muslims were annihilated. To the extent that in some places Muslim men and women were thrown into mincing factories so that bones and flesh emerged from the other side, and this process is still continuing.

What is happening in Yugoslavia, this process is going on day and night against Muslims in all Communist countries. It is still happening, and in this modern age it is occurring. And through this, the saying of the Exalted Lord is confirmed: كَيْفَ وَاِنْ يَّظْهَرُوْا عَلَيْكُمْ لَا يَرْقُبُوْا فِيْكُمْ اِلًّا وَّلَا ذِمَّةً — "How can it be? For if they gain the upper hand over you, they do not observe towards you any tie of kinship or any covenant." This situation in the Arabian Peninsula was neither a temporary circumstance nor a passing one. In Baghdad it was not a sudden incident or state either. It is a permanent and constant pattern of conduct. Whenever the people of polytheism gain control over a believer, one who worships Allah alone, their conduct towards that believer is always this, everywhere and in every age.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 9, verses 13–16:

Tafsir of verses 13 to 16:

This paragraph has come because, at that time, there were people of different levels in Islamic society, and in the hearts of some there was a doubt as to why such a decisive and harsh measure should be taken. We have already discussed this point in detail earlier. Such people had the desire, and they also hoped, that perhaps the remaining polytheists would accept Islam, and that perhaps fighting and severity would not be necessary. Apart from this, other considerations would also have been before them, and they thought, "Why not adopt the easier path?"

In these verses, these very notions, apprehensions and reasons are being addressed. By bringing forward events of the recent and distant past, the matter is clarified, the hearts of the Muslims are purified, and they are made to understand what the outcome was when treaties were made with the polytheists, how truthful the oaths they used to swear were, and then with what cruelty they expelled the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from his homeland. The Prophet (ﷺ) was compelled to leave Makkah. Then it was they who first attacked Madinah. After this, they are shamed, their sense of honour is roused, and they are asked whether they fear these people. "If you are believers, fear only Allah." After this, they are urged to fight them: "Perhaps Allah wills that He punish them at your hands." Thus you will have the honour of becoming the instrument of the Divine decree. Through you, Allah will humiliate His enemies, and they will become deserving of disgrace and the wrath of Allah. And the hearts of the believers who were tormented in the path of Allah will be gladdened. After this, the wishes of those who thought that perhaps these people would enter the religion of Islam without fighting are shown to be mistaken. It is explained that Allah's policy is to bring them into Islam by defeating and humiliating them. In the case of defeat, whoever is destined to repent will repent and submit before the dominant Islam. Finally, Allah draws attention to His sunnah that He continually places the righteous communities of His servants in such trials, and that there is no change in the Divine sunnah.

﴿أَلَا تُقَاتِلُونَ قَوْمًا نَّكَثُوا أَيْمَانَهُمْ وَهَمُّوا بِإِخْرَاجِ الرَّسُولِ وَهُم بَدَءُوكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ ۚ أَتَخْشَوْنَهُمْ ۚ فَاللَّهُ أَحَقُّ أَن تَخْشَوْهُ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ﴾: Will you not fight a people who broke their oaths, and who intended to expel the Messenger, and who began the aggression against you first? Do you fear them? If you are believers, Allah has more right that you fear Him.

In the history of relations between the Muslims and the polytheists, two matters hold great significance: turning away from faith, and breaking of covenants. The closest example at the time of these verses was the breach of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. The Prophet (ﷺ), under Divine inspiration and guidance, accepted that treaty according to the conditions of the polytheists, and some eminent Companions of the Messenger of Allah considered those conditions to be extremely humiliating. In it, the harsh conditions imposed by the polytheists were strictly observed by the Prophet (ﷺ), and he adopted a most noble course of conduct. But they themselves opposed that treaty, and after only two years they tore it to shreds. Again, it was the polytheists who expelled the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from their city, and before the Hijrah, in Makkah, they decided to kill him, and they made this decision in the Sacred House, where even a murderer would find refuge, and where the blood and property of a killer were also safe. This law was so respected that a man would find the killer of his father and brother in the Sacred House, yet he would not inflict any harm upon him. What was the crime of the Messenger of Allah? He invited people to faith, calling them to worship Allah alone, yet they showed no respect even for the House of Allah. They sought to drive the Messenger of Allah out of it, then plotted his murder, and they committed this act boldly and without any hesitation. Then they waged war against the Muslims in Madinah and made plans to destroy the Muslims. Under the leadership of Abu Jahl, they decided that they would certainly fight the Messenger of Allah even though their caravan had escaped safely. Then in the Battle of Uhud and the Battle of the Trench they were clearly the aggressors, and then at Hunayn too they were fully prepared for war. At the time of the revelation of these verses, all these were recent events that formed part of their hostilities, and all these events confirmed the attitude that the Qur'an describes: ﴿وَلَا يَزَالُونَ يُقَاتِلُونَكُمْ حَتَّىٰ يَرُدُّوكُمْ عَن دِينِكُمْ إِنِ اسْتَطَاعُوا﴾ "And they will not cease fighting you until they turn you back from your religion, if they are able." This also shows what the nature of relations has always been between the front that serves Allah alone and the one that associates partners with Allah and worships many other gods besides Him.

After presenting this catalogue of events and bitter memories in a very concise, swift and highly effective manner, Allah addresses them at the end: ﴿أَتَخْشَوْنَهُمْ﴾ "Do you fear them?" Clearly, if you do not begin jihad and fighting against the polytheists, your sitting idle cannot be without fear or some reason. Then the answer to this interrogative clause is given by Allah Himself, which is highly encouraging for the Muslims: ﴿فَاللَّهُ أَحَقُّ أَن تَخْشَوْهُ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ﴾ "Whereas Allah is more deserving that you fear Him, if you are believers." Being a believer means one who does not fear people; therefore the believer is one who fears Allah. So if these people fear the polytheists, they should fear Allah far more. Allah is more deserving that people fear Him, and the fear of anyone other than Allah should not exist, at least in the hearts of the believers.

In short, the Islamic consciousness of the Muslims is being awakened, and by renewing these events and their memories, enthusiasm is created within them. They are reminded that these polytheists are the very people who conspired against the person of the Prophet (ﷺ), then broke every treaty they made with the Prophet (ﷺ), and whenever they found the Muslims heedless or saw a gap in their ranks, they tried to strike. Then they took the initiative in attacking and aggressing against the Muslims. So, for these reasons and causes, the Muslims are urged to take military action against them.

﴿قَاتِلُوهُمْ يُعَذِّبْهُمُ اللَّهُ بِأَيْدِيكُمْ وَيُخْزِهِمْ وَيَنصُرْكُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ وَيَشْفِ صُدُورَ قَوْمٍ مُّؤْمِنِينَ * وَيُذْهِبْ غَيْظَ قُلُوبِهِمْ ۗ وَيَتُوبُ اللَّهُ عَلَىٰ مَن يَشَاءُ ۗ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾

Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands, disgrace them, give you victory over them, and heal the breasts of a believing people, and remove the rage of their hearts. And Allah turns in forgiveness to whom He wills, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.

Fight them. You will become a screen for the Hand of Divine power and a form of the Divine will. Thus Allah will send His punishment upon them through your hands. He will humiliate them by defeat while they consider themselves very strong, but Allah will support you against them, and will heal your hearts, because they had inflicted great torment upon the believers, and the rage against them still existed in the hearts of the Muslims. Thus, by the defeat of the disbelievers and polytheists, their hearts will be lightened, because the polytheists had tormented them and expelled them from their homes. Not only this, but a greater reward awaits them.

﴿وَيُذْهِبْ غَيْظَ قُلُوبِهِمْ ۗ وَيَتُوبُ اللَّهُ عَلَىٰ مَن يَشَاءُ ۗ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾: And will remove the rage of their hearts, and Allah turns in forgiveness to whom He wills. Allah is All-Knowing and All-Wise. As a result of the Muslims' victory, the hearts of many people may incline towards Islam, and their insight may lead them to the conclusion that the future belongs to Islam, because the Muslims are attaining victory, and it becomes evident that above human strength there is another power that supports the Muslims. In practice it also happened that many people became Muslims. Likewise, the mujahidin received a double reward: one reward for their jihad in the way of Allah, and another for the entry of those misguided people into the fold of Islam and their being guided, which came about because of jihad. And through these people Islam's manpower and military strength increased.

It is said that Allah is All-Knowing and All-Wise. He knows well the good outcomes of these measures, and He is All-Wise: the measures He commands are based on profound wisdom.

When Islam appears in a forceful form, it is more attractive, compared with the Islam whose strength is unknown to people or which appears weak and feeble. But when the Islamic community appears with strength and power, and is firmly established in its ideology and practice, half the path of the Islamic movement is traversed by itself.

Allah, who was training and overseeing the Islamic community in Makkah, there promised only Paradise to the community of Muslims, while in Makkah the community was small and had weak people in it, and here the Muslims were given only one guidance: hold firmly to the rope of Allah. When the community showed patience as it should be, and became seekers of Paradise alone, Allah granted it help, and when it became victorious, Allah roused it to political dominance and jihad. This is because that political dominance was not the dominance of the community, but the dominance of Allah's religion, and through it the word of Allah was being exalted.

At that time the situation was such that the Muslims were required to fight all the polytheists, to annul all the treaties of the polytheists, and to stand united against them. This was necessary so that the secret pacts existing against the Muslims would end, that those whose intentions were deceitful would come out openly, that the veils behind which hypocrites stood and plotted against Islam would be removed, and that the ties which some maintained under the guise of kinship and family relations would also be severed. It was necessary to tear down these veils and entirely remove these excuses. Therefore the command was given to end relations with all such people, so that those in whose hearts some corruption lay hidden would be exposed, and those who were taking others as friends besides Allah and His Messenger, and who through these excuses maintained connections with the camp opposed to Islam, would be revealed. The nature of those connections was not clear but doubtful, and therefore this command was given.

﴿أَمْ حَسِبْتُمْ أَن تُتْرَكُوا وَلَمَّا يَعْلَمِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا مِنكُمْ وَلَمْ يَتَّخِذُوا مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ وَلَا رَسُولِهِ وَلَا الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَلِيجَةً ۚ وَاللَّهُ خَبِيرٌ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ﴾: Or do you think that you will be left alone, while Allah has not yet made evident those among you who strove, and who took no one as an intimate friend besides Allah, His Messenger and the believers? Allah is well aware of what you do.

As is generally the case, in the Islamic society too there were people who wavered, who went beyond the limits, who had many excuses, who, without the knowledge and counsel of the community, met its enemies and protected their own interests even though the Islamic movement suffered loss by it. These people benefited from the relations existing between the Muslims and the polytheists, because a complete severing of relations between the Muslims and the polytheists had not yet taken place. But when it was clearly announced that now there would be no relationship with the polytheists of Arabia, and that the ties were now cut, then such people had no excuse left, and their secret intrigues came to light.

It is in the interest of the Islamic community and the Islamic ideology of life that the veils be lifted, that relations be entirely open, and that back doors be closed, so that a clear distinction is made between those who strive sincerely and those who wander about on every side, and the people of both camps become clearly known and recognised, and their reality becomes well understood, although Allah is All-Knowing and All-Aware. He already knows in advance what each person is; but Allah seizes people only when their reality has become clear to all who see. This is the Divine sunnah: Allah distinguishes between the genuine and the counterfeit, and the distinction between genuine and counterfeit is made by subjecting people to trials and hardships.

He invited people to faith, calling them to worship Allah alone, yet they showed no respect even for the House of Allah. Then they waged war against the Muslims in Madinah and made plans to destroy the Muslims. Under the leadership of Abu Jahl, they decided that they would certainly fight the Messenger of Allah even though their caravan had escaped safely. Then in the Battle of Uhud and the Battle of the Trench they were clearly the aggressors, and then at Hunayn too they were fully prepared for war. This also shows what the nature of relations has always been between the front that serves Allah alone and the one that associates partners with Allah and worships many other gods besides Him.

Being a believer means one who does not fear people; therefore the believer is one who fears Allah. So if these people fear the polytheists, they should fear Allah far more. Allah is more deserving that people fear Him, and the fear of anyone other than Allah should not exist, at least in the hearts of the believers.

In short, the Islamic consciousness of the Muslims is being awakened, and by renewing these events and their memories, enthusiasm is created within them. They are reminded that these polytheists are the very people who conspired against the person of the Prophet (ﷺ), then broke every treaty they made with the Prophet (ﷺ), and whenever they found the Muslims heedless or saw a gap in their ranks, they tried to strike. Then they took the initiative in attacking and aggressing against the Muslims. So, for these reasons and causes, the Muslims are urged to take military action against them.

﴿قَاتِلُوهُمْ يُعَذِّبْهُمُ اللَّهُ بِأَيْدِيكُمْ وَيُخْزِهِمْ وَيَنصُرْكُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ وَيَشْفِ صُدُورَ قَوْمٍ مُّؤْمِنِينَ * وَيُذْهِبْ غَيْظَ قُلُوبِهِمْ ۗ وَيَتُوبُ اللَّهُ عَلَىٰ مَن يَشَاءُ ۗ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾

Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands, disgrace them, give you victory over them, and heal the breasts of a believing people, and remove the rage of their hearts. And Allah turns in forgiveness to whom He wills, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.

Fight them. You will become a screen for the Hand of Divine power and a form of the Divine will. Thus Allah will send His punishment upon them through your hands. He will humiliate them by defeat while they consider themselves very strong, but Allah will support you against them, and will heal your hearts, because they had inflicted great torment upon the believers, and the rage against them still existed in the hearts of the Muslims. Thus, by the defeat of the disbelievers and polytheists, their hearts will be lightened, because the polytheists had tormented them and expelled them from their homes. Not only this, but a greater reward awaits them.

﴿وَيُذْهِبْ غَيْظَ قُلُوبِهِمْ ۗ وَيَتُوبُ اللَّهُ عَلَىٰ مَن يَشَاءُ ۗ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾: And will remove the rage of their hearts, and Allah turns in forgiveness to whom He wills. Allah is All-Knowing and All-Wise. As a result of the Muslims' victory, the hearts of many people may incline towards Islam, and their insight may lead them to the conclusion that the future belongs to Islam, because the Muslims are attaining victory, and it becomes evident that above human strength there is another power that supports the Muslims. In practice it also happened that many people became Muslims. Likewise, the mujahidin received a double reward: one reward for their jihad in the way of Allah, and another for the entry of those misguided people into the fold of Islam and their being guided, which came about because of jihad. And through these people Islam's manpower and military strength increased.

It is said that Allah is All-Knowing and All-Wise. He knows well the good outcomes of these measures, and He is All-Wise: the measures He commands are based on profound wisdom.

When Islam appears in a forceful form, it is more attractive, compared with the Islam whose strength is unknown to people or which appears weak and feeble. But when the Islamic community appears with strength and power, and is firmly established in its ideology and practice, half the path of the Islamic movement is traversed by itself.

Allah, who was training and overseeing the Islamic community in Makkah, there promised only Paradise to the community of Muslims, while in Makkah the community was small and had weak people in it, and here the Muslims were given only one guidance: hold firmly to the rope of Allah. When the community showed patience as it should be, and became seekers of Paradise alone, Allah granted it help, and when it became victorious, Allah roused it to political dominance and jihad. This is because that political dominance was not the dominance of the community, but the dominance of Allah's religion, and through it the word of Allah was being exalted.

At that time the situation was such that the Muslims were required to fight all the polytheists, to annul all the treaties of the polytheists, and to stand united against them. This was necessary so that the secret pacts existing against the Muslims would end, that those whose intentions were deceitful would come out openly, that the veils behind which hypocrites stood and plotted against Islam would be removed, and that the ties which some maintained under the guise of kinship and family relations would also be severed. It was necessary to tear down these veils and entirely remove these excuses. Therefore the command was given to end relations with all such people, so that those in whose hearts some corruption lay hidden would be exposed, and those who were taking others as friends besides Allah and His Messenger, and who through these excuses maintained connections with the camp opposed to Islam, would be revealed. The nature of those connections was not clear but doubtful, and therefore this command was given.

﴿أَمْ حَسِبْتُمْ أَن تُتْرَكُوا وَلَمَّا يَعْلَمِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا مِنكُمْ وَلَمْ يَتَّخِذُوا مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ وَلَا رَسُولِهِ وَلَا الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَلِيجَةً ۚ وَاللَّهُ خَبِيرٌ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ﴾: Or do you think that you will be left alone, while Allah has not yet made evident those among you who strove, and who took no one as an intimate friend besides Allah, His Messenger and the believers? Allah is well aware of what you do.

As is generally the case, in the Islamic society too there were people who wavered, who went beyond the limits, who had many excuses, who, without the knowledge and counsel of the community, met its enemies and protected their own interests even though the Islamic movement suffered loss by it. These people benefited from the relations existing between the Muslims and the polytheists, because a complete severing of relations between the Muslims and the polytheists had not yet taken place. But when it was clearly announced that now there would be no relationship with the polytheists of Arabia, and that the ties were now cut, then such people had no excuse left, and their secret intrigues came to light.

It is in the interest of the Islamic community and the Islamic ideology of life that the veils be lifted, that relations be entirely open, and that back doors be closed, so that a clear distinction is made between those who strive sincerely and those who wander about on every side, and the people of both camps become clearly known and recognised, and their reality becomes well understood, although Allah is All-Knowing and All-Aware. He already knows in advance what each person is; but Allah seizes people only when their reality has become clear to all who see. This is the Divine sunnah: Allah distinguishes between the genuine and the counterfeit, and the distinction between genuine and counterfeit is made by subjecting people to trials and hardships.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 9, verse 17:

After the declaration of disavowal (bara'ah), no one has any excuse left for not fighting the polytheists. Nor should people's minds remain troubled by the thought that the polytheists will be deprived of visiting the Haram, unless they are prevented from taking part in the construction of the building of the Masjid al-Haram, in which they used to participate in the days of jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance). This is because the polytheists have no right at all to build mosques. The right to build mosques and to perform the religious obligations within them belongs only to the people of faith. In the days of jahiliyyah they did this work, but the construction of the Masjid al-Haram and the giving of water to the pilgrims cannot now be excluded from this general rule. These verses remove the doubts that were in the hearts of some Muslims, who thought that this principle had stopped people from a good deed.

﴿مَا كَانَ لِلْمُشْرِكِيْنَ أَنْ يَّعْمُرُوْا مَسٰجِدَ اللّٰهِ شٰهِدِيْنَ عَلٰٓي اَنْفُسِهِمْ بِالْكُفْرِ﴾: "It is not for the polytheists to be the caretakers and servants of the mosques of Allah while they bear witness against themselves to disbelief."

This is an exceedingly reprehensible matter and contrary to the principles of human nature: that polytheists should take part in the building of mosques. Mosques exist solely for the remembrance of God, and in them no name other than Allah's is mentioned. How, then, can those take part in building mosques whose hearts hold no tawhid (the affirmation of God's oneness) and who associate others with Allah? Moreover, their very lives are bearing witness to disbelief rather than to the truth, and the practical testimony of one's life is a testimony that no one can deny; one has no choice but to acknowledge it.

﴿أُولٰۗىِٕكَ حَبِطَتْ أَعْمَالُهُمْ ښ وَفِي النَّارِ هُمْ خٰلِدُوْنَ﴾: "Their deeds have come to nothing, and in the Fire they will abide forever."

All their deeds are void. They will receive no reward even for their construction of mosques, because they chose disbelief and shirk instead of accepting the belief in tawhid.

Among acts of worship and deeds, those that are accepted are the ones based upon correct beliefs. If the belief itself is not sound, how can the deeds be sound? Therefore, as long as faith and belief are not correct, the building of the Masjid al-Haram and the performance of the rites of worship in it have no meaning. Hence, deeds must be based upon pure belief in Tawheed (the Oneness of Allah), and these deeds must be exclusively for Allah; only then will they be accepted.

Here there are two conditions: faith in Allah, which is an inner quality, and, along with outward deeds, the condition that a person does not fear anything other than Allah. This is a mandatory condition, not a voluntary one. Therefore, being exclusively for Allah is obligatory. And in a person's consciousness and conduct there should not be even a trace of shirk. Fearing other than Allah is in reality also a shade of hidden shirk (shirk khafi), and here attention has been deliberately drawn to it so that a person becomes completely pure and clean in consciousness, belief, deed and conduct. After this sincerity, the believer becomes entitled to maintain and build the masajid, and it is such people who can hope for guidance.

﴿فَعَسٰٓى اُولٰۗىِٕكَ اَنْ يَّكُوْنُوْا مِنَ الْمُهْتَدِيْنَ﴾: "It is expected of them that they will be among those who are guided." That is, they are expected to walk the straight path. This is because the heart turns in attention, then the limbs act, and all of this can happen only if Allah is pleased; if it is Allah's will, then there will be attention, deeds will be done, and guidance and success will follow.

This is the principle of building the masajid, and this is the real means of the correction of worship and rites.

This passage is from Sayyid Qutb's commentary on Surah At-Tawbah, verse 19.

The principle is set before both the Muslims and the polytheists. Accordingly, those who in the Jahiliyyah (the period of ignorance before Islam) built the Kaaba and gave water to the pilgrims, but whose beliefs were not pure, and who did not take part in good deeds or in jihad in the way of Allah; and those who took part in the building of the House of Allah, whose faith was sound, who on that sound faith also performed good deeds, and who also struggled in the way of Allah, are not equal.

﴿Do you consider the providing of water to the pilgrims and the maintaining of the Sacred Mosque equal to one who believes in Allah and the Last Day and strives in the way of Allah? They are not equal in the sight of Allah.﴾ This is the translation of: "Do you make the giving of water to the pilgrims and the care of the Masjid al-Haram equal to the one who believed in Allah and the Last Day and strove in the way of Allah? They are not equal with Allah."

Indeed they are not equal, because they do not conform to the balance and measures of Allah, and the measures and standards belong only to Allah.

﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ This is the translation of: "And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people." Those polytheists who do not accept the true religion, and who do not purify their beliefs from shirk, are meant here, even if they are the builders of the House of Allah and the servers and attendants of the pilgrims.

This passage concludes the theme that the believers, the emigrants (muhajirin) and the strugglers (mujahidin) are people of elevated rank. The mercy and pleasure of Allah await them, and for them there is everlasting bliss (na'im muqim) in Paradise. Besides this, there is also a great reward.

In this verse, the superlative form is used: a'zam darajah (﴿أَعْظَمُ دَرَجَةً﴾, "greater in degree"). This does not mean that the ranks of other people are lower; rather, it refers to absolute excellence. This is because, in contrast to these people, there are those whose deeds went to waste and who will remain forever in Hell. Therefore, there is no proportion between such people in terms of deeds and ranks. On one side are the disbelievers, and on the other side are the believers, the emigrants and the strugglers, who will be in high ranks and in lasting blessings.

Now, in the following verses, the thoughts, consciousness and mutual relations of the Muslims are purified, so that they become single-minded for the religion of the Lord of the Worlds. Thus, the love of all kinship ties, all kinds of worldly interests, and all human pleasures and joys are placed on one pan of the scale, while Allah, His Messenger, and jihad in the way of Allah are placed on the other pan, and Muslims are given the choice: now choose whatever you wish.

The Islamic way of life also does not tolerate that anyone else should share the heart of the believer with it. Either we shall give place in our heart only to the Islamic way of life, or else we abandon it and give place in our heart to other loves. But what is required here is not that a Muslim should sever relations with his family, his clan, his wife and husband, his children and wealth, his business and goods, and worldly pleasures, and become a monk or one who renounces the world. This is by no means the case. Rather, the demand of the Islamic way of life is that a Muslim hold Islam dear and beloved, and that his heart and his thought be focused upon it. Then such a believer may take part in all the activities of the world, but the criterion is that when the demand of the Islamic revolution arises, he should abandon all his activities and rise up to fulfil that demand.

What is the line that distinguishes these two positions? It is this: whether the ideology dominates your heart, mind and life, or the equipment of the world does. Your first slogan and your first speech is for Islam, or it is for some aim and demand of this world. When a believer is assured that the Islamic way of life has overspread his heart and thought, then no one will hold him to account afterwards. If he enjoys his children, brothers, wife or husband, family, wealth and goods, and takes part in all the affairs of life, he may also adorn himself and eat and drink well, without extravagance and without arrogance. Indeed, in such circumstances and such a conception, the enjoyment and use of these provisions is recommended for him, in the sense that this too is a form of gratitude to God, since Allah bestows His bounties upon His servants in this way, while their belief is that Allah is the Provider, the Bestower of sustenance.

﴿O you who believe! Do not take your fathers and your brothers as allies if they prefer disbelief over faith.﴾ "O you who have believed, do not take your fathers and brothers as friends if they prefer disbelief to faith."

Thus the bonds of pure blood and lineage are cut. If ideological ties are severed among such people, if the kinship of Allah comes to an end, then family ties too come to an end. True friendship belongs to Allah, and in His name the whole of humanity can be gathered; and if there is no ideological unity, then all unity and ties break apart. The rope is cut into pieces.

﴿And whoever among you takes them as allies, it is they who are the wrongdoers.﴾ "Whoever among you makes them his allies, those are the wrongdoers." Here "wrongdoers" (ẓālimūn) means polytheists (mushrikūn). If a people and a clan prefer disbelief to faith, then befriending that people and clan is disbelief and polytheism. Such a situation does not suit the states of faith.

The context here does not simply state the principle. It also gives examples and shades of the love in question. Which ties, which connections and which pleasures would stand against faith are named, so that they may be placed on one side of the scale, and the demands of faith and Islam on the other, in a concrete and vivid way. For instance: fathers, sons, brothers, spouses and the family, meaning the ties of blood and lineage and kinship; wealth from trade, toward which one has a natural inclination; and houses and mansions where one rests and enjoys the pleasures of life. All of these are placed on one side, and the love of God, the love of the Messenger and the zeal for jihad (struggle in the way of Allah) on the other, and a choice is offered.

Jihad here does not have such a simple meaning. Jihad involves hardships and has its own specific demands. It involves difficulties and exhaustion, it involves straitened circumstances and bitterness, it involves sacrifices and deprivations, it involves being wounded, and it involves giving one's life. All of this is contained in the word jihad, and all of it must be done in a state free even of the slightest trace of fame, display and self-promotion, and free even of the slightest trace of pride, arrogance and haughtiness. There must not even be a hint or suggestion of seeking conquest of lands or of seeking positions of power. If the mujahid (one who performs jihad) is afflicted by any of these diseases, he will be deprived of the reward of the Hereafter. Read again carefully:

﴿Say: If your fathers, your sons, your sons, your brothers, your wives, your kinsfolk, the wealth you have earned, the trade whose slump you fear, and the dwellings you are pleased with are dearer to you than Allah and His Messenger and jihad in His cause, then wait until Allah brings His command.﴾

Beware! This is an extremely arduous path, and this is an extremely great responsibility! Yet that is the matter: if you do not fulfil this responsibility, then wait until Allah brings His command before you. ﴿And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.﴾ The demand for such sincerity is not made of an individual alone. It is made of the whole Muslim community (ummah). The Islamic state too must be sincere in this way. Therefore, in an Islamic society, no preference and no aim should be more important than the requirements of the Islamic worldview and of jihad in the cause of Allah.

Is human nature able to reach this standard? Evidently, when Allah demanded such a standard from the people of faith, it is possible to set such a standard, and that is why He demanded it. For Allah does not require of any soul what lies beyond its capacity. It is the great generosity of Allah that He has placed in this weak human being such capacity and strength that he can present such a sincere standard, endure such hardships, and that He has given him, within this awareness and sincerity, such delight that he can bid farewell to all the earthly pleasures for its sake. Union with God and the awareness of attaining nearness to God, the awareness of seeking the pleasure of Allah, elevates a person above human weakness, baseness, and the pleasures of blood, flesh and skin. His gaze is fixed on some lofty station on a distant horizon. Whenever the base pleasures of this world pull at his skirt, he fixes his gaze on a bright aim on the lofty horizon, and in this way he frees himself from their grip.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 9, verses 25–27:

25–27: Now let us glance at the recent memories of the near past. The Muslims had passed through those circumstances only in the very recent period. In those circumstances, the special help of Allah displayed a miracle. This miracle was not due to their strength or their number. On the day of Hunain they were in large numbers and possessed great strength, yet they were defeated. Later, when the help of Allah came, the picture of affairs changed. On that day, the two thousand Tulaqa of the Conquest of Makkah mingled into the Islamic army. For a few moments the Muslims were overtaken by a state in which they became heedless, intoxicated with strength and multitude, merely because of their numbers and equipment. This was a lesson for the people of faith as to what sincerity and jihad purely for the sake of Allah truly mean: that when connection with Allah exists, there is victory even in small numbers; but if one relies upon equipment and a large number of insincere people, then winning the battlefield will be difficult.

---

Allah had given help to the Muslims on countless occasions and days, and the memories of those days were fresh in their minds. The Battle of Hunain took place in Shawwal of the eighth year of Hijrah, after the Conquest of Makkah, when the Messenger (ﷺ) had finished the affairs of the Conquest of Makkah, the matters of Makkah were set right, and the general people of Makkah had become Muslims. The Messenger (ﷺ) pardoned them, and in this way they became famous by the name of "Tulaqa." On this occasion, you (ﷺ) were informed that the tribes of Hawazin were about to take military action against you, and that their leader Malik ibn Awf al-Nadri, along with the tribes of Thaqif ibn Jusham, Banu Sa'd ibn Bakr, some people of Banu Hilal, and some of Banu Amr ibn Amir and Awf ibn Amir, were supporting this. These people had brought along their women, children and livestock too, and they all came out in this army. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out against them with the army of the Conquest of Makkah. This army consisted of ten thousand Ansar and Muhajirun, and several Arab tribes participated in it. Among these people were also those who had embraced Islam in Makkah only the day before, who were called Tulaqa, and their number was two thousand. The Messenger (ﷺ) set out towards the enemy with this army. The two armies met in a valley between Makkah and Ta'if, and this valley was called the Valley of Hunain. This encounter took place at the very beginning of the day, in the dawn darkness. When the Muslims descended into the valley, the Hawazin were lying in ambush ahead. When the Muslims descended into the valley, they came to know that Hawazin had attacked. They rained down arrows, drew their swords, and attacked in the manner that a single person attacks. This was a sudden assault, and its plan had been made by their king. In the first attack the Muslims fled, just as Allah mentioned in the text. The Messenger (ﷺ) was riding the white mule and did not move from his place. The right rein of the Messenger's mule was held by Hadrat Abbas, and on the left side Abu Sufyan was holding the rein. These people were restraining the mule lest it rush quickly into the midst of the enemy. The Messenger (ﷺ) called out to the people by his own name and invited them to return: "O people, come to me, I am the Messenger of Allah," and in such circumstances he recited the rajaz: "I am the Prophet, no lie; I am the son of Abd al-Muttalib." About a hundred persons remained steadfast with him; some have said they were eighty. Among them were Hadrat Abu Bakr, Hadrat Umar, Abbas, Ali, Fadl ibn Abbas, Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith, Ayman ibn Umm Ayman, Usama ibn Zayd and others (may Allah be pleased with them). After this, the Messenger (ﷺ) said to Hadrat Abbas, who had a very loud voice, to call out loudly: "O companions of the tree of the Pledge of Ridwan!" Under that tree the Muslims had pledged that they would not flee from battle. In this way they were also called by this name: "O companions of Samurah, O companions of Surah al-Baqarah." Thus people heard and returned, saying "Here I am, here I am" (labbayk, labbayk). So all the people returned and gathered around the Messenger of Allah. People returned in such a way that if someone's camel did not turn back, he would put on his armour, leap down, leave the camel, and carry himself to the Messenger of Allah. When a group of people had gathered around the Messenger (ﷺ), he ordered them to fight with truthfulness. Thus the disbelievers were defeated and began to flee. The Muslims pursued them, killed and captured them, and the people turned back only when a army of prisoners had assembled before the Messenger of Allah.

This was the battle in which, for the first time, the Muslims had gathered a great number of twelve thousand. This number appeared to them unconquerable. They became heedless because of their earlier victories. Allah afflicted them with defeat at the beginning of that encounter. Thus their heedlessness was removed, and afterwards, when a relatively small number gathered around the Messenger (ﷺ), Allah granted success, because this number stood firm with the Messenger (ﷺ).

The verse recounts some scenes of that encounter and mentions its conscious impressions here.

﴿Certainly Allah has helped you on many occasions, and on the day of Hunain, when your great number pleased you but it availed you nothing, and the earth, spacious as it is, became narrow for you, then you turned back retreating.﴾ Allah has already helped you on many occasions. Just now, on the day of the Battle of Hunain, you have seen the manner of His support. On that day your large number made you proud, yet it did not avail you anything, and the earth, despite its vastness, became constricted upon you, and you turned back fleeing.

The first impression was that we are very numerous. Then came the spiritual defeat, when the earth seems narrow to a person. Then comes that difficult time in which a person feels that there is pressure upon him from every direction. Then comes the physical defeat, that people ran away. After all these impressions, this impression:

﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers﴾: "Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers." As if tranquility is a cloak that descended from the heavens. It strengthened hearts and cooled these temporary impressions.

﴿And sent down hosts you could not see﴾: "And He sent down hosts that you did not see." What these hosts were, their nature and form, we do not know; and only Allah knows the powers and armies of Allah.

﴿And punished those who disbelieved﴾: "And He punished those who denied the truth." They were punished through being killed, plundered and defeated. ﴿And that is the recompense of the disbelievers﴾: "That is the recompense of those who deny the truth."

﴿Then Allah relents after that to whom He wills, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾: "Then (you have also seen that) after punishing in this way, Allah grants repentance to whomever He wills; Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."

Because the door of forgiveness with Allah always remains open, and sinners can return by repenting at whatever time they wish.

Here this glimpse of the Battle of Hunain is presented in order to show what the consequences are for those who become heedless of Allah and begin to rely upon other powers instead of Allah. But from this event there emerges before us another subsidiary truth. And this second truth is indeed: which power is that upon which an ideology may rely? In ideological movements, numerical multitude has no value; rather, a small number of steadfast, sincere people who know the principles holds importance. Sometimes a large number becomes the cause of defeat, because some temporary-minded people enter it, who have not understood the ideology of life well, but have been swept along by the current of circumstances. When difficult times come upon such people, their feet waver. Such people create turmoil in the ranks of the ideology and become the cause of defeat and failure. Then a crowd also becomes a source of deception for the leadership, and the people in a crowd do not have firm mutual bonds or relationships, nor do they have a strong connection with Allah; thus the leadership is deceived into thinking that victory and success are due to numbers, whereas the secret is that victory, help and success come from sincerity and training.

It has always been so that a small pure group of the sincere rises carrying an ideology. The mass of the public, which is like foam upon water, cannot become the bearer of any ideology, and grass and rubbish cannot withstand the storms of difficulties.

When the matter reaches this point, and historical events are fixed in the consciousness of the Muslims, then final words are given to the ultimate policy regarding the polytheists, a policy which will remain until the Day of Resurrection. (See verse 28.)

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 9, verses 25–27:

25–27: Now let us glance at the recent memories of the near past. The Muslims had passed through those circumstances only in the very recent period. In those circumstances, the special help of Allah displayed a miracle. This miracle was not due to their strength or their number. On the day of Hunain they were in large numbers and possessed great strength, yet they were defeated. Later, when the help of Allah came, the picture of affairs changed. On that day, the two thousand Tulaqa of the Conquest of Makkah mingled into the Islamic army. For a few moments the Muslims were overtaken by a state in which they became heedless, intoxicated with strength and multitude, merely because of their numbers and equipment. This was a lesson for the people of faith as to what sincerity and jihad purely for the sake of Allah truly mean: that when connection with Allah exists, there is victory even in small numbers; but if one relies upon equipment and a large number of insincere people, then winning the battlefield will be difficult.

---

Allah had given help to the Muslims on countless occasions and days, and the memories of those days were fresh in their minds. The Battle of Hunain took place in Shawwal of the eighth year of Hijrah, after the Conquest of Makkah, when the Messenger (ﷺ) had finished the affairs of the Conquest of Makkah, the matters of Makkah were set right, and the general people of Makkah had become Muslims. The Messenger (ﷺ) pardoned them, and in this way they became famous by the name of "Tulaqa." On this occasion, you (ﷺ) were informed that the tribes of Hawazin were about to take military action against you, and that their leader Malik ibn Awf al-Nadri, along with the tribes of Thaqif ibn Jusham, Banu Sa'd ibn Bakr, some people of Banu Hilal, and some of Banu Amr ibn Amir and Awf ibn Amir, were supporting this. These people had brought along their women, children and livestock too, and they all came out in this army. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out against them with the army of the Conquest of Makkah. This army consisted of ten thousand Ansar and Muhajirun, and several Arab tribes participated in it. Among these people were also those who had embraced Islam in Makkah only the day before, who were called Tulaqa, and their number was two thousand. The Messenger (ﷺ) set out towards the enemy with this army. The two armies met in a valley between Makkah and Ta'if, and this valley was called the Valley of Hunain. This encounter took place at the very beginning of the day, in the dawn darkness. When the Muslims descended into the valley, the Hawazin were lying in ambush ahead. When the Muslims descended into the valley, they came to know that Hawazin had attacked. They rained down arrows, drew their swords, and attacked in the manner that a single person attacks. This was a sudden assault, and its plan had been made by their king. In the first attack the Muslims fled, just as Allah mentioned in the text. The Messenger (ﷺ) was riding the white mule and did not move from his place. The right rein of the Messenger's mule was held by Hadrat Abbas, and on the left side Abu Sufyan was holding the rein. These people were restraining the mule lest it rush quickly into the midst of the enemy. The Messenger (ﷺ) called out to the people by his own name and invited them to return: "O people, come to me, I am the Messenger of Allah," and in such circumstances he recited the rajaz: "I am the Prophet, no lie; I am the son of Abd al-Muttalib." About a hundred persons remained steadfast with him; some have said they were eighty. Among them were Hadrat Abu Bakr, Hadrat Umar, Abbas, Ali, Fadl ibn Abbas, Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith, Ayman ibn Umm Ayman, Usama ibn Zayd and others (may Allah be pleased with them). After this, the Messenger (ﷺ) said to Hadrat Abbas, who had a very loud voice, to call out loudly: "O companions of the tree of the Pledge of Ridwan!" Under that tree the Muslims had pledged that they would not flee from battle. In this way they were also called by this name: "O companions of Samurah, O companions of Surah al-Baqarah." Thus people heard and returned, saying "Here I am, here I am" (labbayk, labbayk). So all the people returned and gathered around the Messenger of Allah. People returned in such a way that if someone's camel did not turn back, he would put on his armour, leap down, leave the camel, and carry himself to the Messenger of Allah. When a group of people had gathered around the Messenger (ﷺ), he ordered them to fight with truthfulness. Thus the disbelievers were defeated and began to flee. The Muslims pursued them, killed and captured them, and the people turned back only when a army of prisoners had assembled before the Messenger of Allah.

This was the battle in which, for the first time, the Muslims had gathered a great number of twelve thousand. This number appeared to them unconquerable. They became heedless because of their earlier victories. Allah afflicted them with defeat at the beginning of that encounter. Thus their heedlessness was removed, and afterwards, when a relatively small number gathered around the Messenger (ﷺ), Allah granted success, because this number stood firm with the Messenger (ﷺ).

The verse recounts some scenes of that encounter and mentions its conscious impressions here.

﴿Certainly Allah has helped you on many occasions, and on the day of Hunain, when your great number pleased you but it availed you nothing, and the earth, spacious as it is, became narrow for you, then you turned back retreating.﴾ Allah has already helped you on many occasions. Just now, on the day of the Battle of Hunain, you have seen the manner of His support. On that day your large number made you proud, yet it did not avail you anything, and the earth, despite its vastness, became constricted upon you, and you turned back fleeing.

The first impression was that we are very numerous. Then came the spiritual defeat, when the earth seems narrow to a person. Then comes that difficult time in which a person feels that there is pressure upon him from every direction. Then comes the physical defeat, that people ran away. After all these impressions, this impression:

﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers﴾: "Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers." As if tranquility is a cloak that descended from the heavens. It strengthened hearts and cooled these temporary impressions.

﴿And sent down hosts you could not see﴾: "And He sent down hosts that you did not see." What these hosts were, their nature and form, we do not know; and only Allah knows the powers and armies of Allah.

﴿And punished those who disbelieved﴾: "And He punished those who denied the truth." They were punished through being killed, plundered and defeated. ﴿And that is the recompense of the disbelievers﴾: "That is the recompense of those who deny the truth."

﴿Then Allah relents after that to whom He wills, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾: "Then (you have also seen that) after punishing in this way, Allah grants repentance to whomever He wills; Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."

Because the door of forgiveness with Allah always remains open, and sinners can return by repenting at whatever time they wish.

Here this glimpse of the Battle of Hunain is presented in order to show what the consequences are for those who become heedless of Allah and begin to rely upon other powers instead of Allah. But from this event there emerges before us another subsidiary truth. And this second truth is indeed: which power is that upon which an ideology may rely? In ideological movements, numerical multitude has no value; rather, a small number of steadfast, sincere people who know the principles holds importance. Sometimes a large number becomes the cause of defeat, because some temporary-minded people enter it, who have not understood the ideology of life well, but have been swept along by the current of circumstances. When difficult times come upon such people, their feet waver. Such people create turmoil in the ranks of the ideology and become the cause of defeat and failure. Then a crowd also becomes a source of deception for the leadership, and the people in a crowd do not have firm mutual bonds or relationships, nor do they have a strong connection with Allah; thus the leadership is deceived into thinking that victory and success are due to numbers, whereas the secret is that victory, help and success come from sincerity and training.

It has always been so that a small pure group of the sincere rises carrying an ideology. The mass of the public, which is like foam upon water, cannot become the bearer of any ideology, and grass and rubbish cannot withstand the storms of difficulties.

When the matter reaches this point, and historical events are fixed in the consciousness of the Muslims, then final words are given to the ultimate policy regarding the polytheists, a policy which will remain until the Day of Resurrection. (See verse 28.)
