Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 9, verse 28:

The polytheists are ritually impure (najis) in their very essence. Their spirit is so impure that this impurity has penetrated into their blood and flesh. Therefore they are wholly impure. A pure sentiment recoils at the mere thought of them; it feels disgust, and people of pure temperament prefer to keep away from them. This is a moral impurity, which is more intense than physical impurity. That their bodies have not become impure is the very effective mode of expression of the Qur'an, which makes even spiritual matters tangible. Since they are impure, what is the ruling?

﴿O you who believe! The polytheists are indeed impure, so let them not come near al-Masjid al-Haram after this year of theirs.﴾ O people who have believed, the polytheists are impure, so after this year they must not be allowed to come near al-Masjid al-Haram. Since al-Masjid al-Haram is pure and they are impure, they should not be permitted to come near al-Masjid al-Haram. The ruling has been attached to their very persons.

But the economic consequences of this measure were also grave. The season of Hajj and the season of trade were about to arrive, on which their annual budget depended. Most of the people of the Arabian Peninsula used to trade in it, and their summer and winter journeys also depended on this system. This was the summary of their economic life. If the polytheists were suddenly forbidden in this way, the whole of their life was bound to be affected. Then, when war is also declared against the disbelievers and polytheists...

All these events and facts are correct, but this matter is connected with principles. Allah wants you to become sincere to this principle and to become ready for sacrifice. As for provision and commercial interests, no system is their guarantor; Allah is, and Allah brings provision through means that are not habitual and familiar.

﴿And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you of His bounty, if He wills; indeed Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾ (9:28) And if you fear want, it is not unlikely that Allah, if He wills, will make you rich by His bounty; Allah is All-Knowing and All-Wise. When Allah wills, He changes the means: He closes one door and opens other doors. He is All-Knowing and All-Wise; by His knowledge, His wisdom, and His measure and reckoning, He keeps making these arrangements.

...

Thus, the Islamic system was now operating in a society that was victorious, and people of various degrees of faith had joined it. As we have explained throughout this lesson, there were weak points at various places in that society, and the Qur'an was training this community by removing those weaknesses. In this way the Qur'an was continuously striving, in accordance with its own method, to reform the Muslim Ummah so that these weak points would be strengthened.

The Qur'an was striving to raise this Ummah to the highest station and height of purity and sincerity, so that it would become the most sincere Ummah toward this religion and this system. Its loves, its ties and its priorities were to become entirely separated for this system. This could only be achieved by establishing a political system in which people would leave the system of servitude to their fellow humans and enter the Islamic system, in which only the servitude of the Lord, the Possessor of Majesty, prevails. Thus people would be completely divided into two camps, since union between these two camps is not possible.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 9, verse 29 (part 1 of 3):

Lesson No. 88 At a Glance

This is the second lesson of this surah. In this second part, the final form of the international relations between the Islamic state and the People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab) is described, just as in the first part the final nature of the international relations between the Islamic state and the polytheists (mushrikin) of the Arabian Peninsula was defined.

The verses of the first part related to the polytheists of the Arabian Peninsula, and those verses mentioned the qualities found among the polytheists. The events and incidents that actually occurred in the Arabian Peninsula at that time were the subject of discussion in the first lesson, and those verses applied to them directly, whereas the verses of this part relate generally to the People of the Book. The verses of this part are general both in wording and in meaning, whether the People of the Book are in the Arabian Peninsula or in any place outside it.

Through these texts, a fundamental change has been made in the relations that had previously existed between the Muslims and the People of the Book, especially the Christians. A state of war with the Jews had indeed been established on some occasions before this, but there was no state of declared war with the Christians.

What change occurred? It is clearly apparent that the command was given to fight those People of the Book who deny the Divine religion, and to continue this fight until they become humbled and are ready to pay the jizyah. The time has now passed when treaties could be made with them, or when relations of friendship and peace could be established with them. Now it is either war, or submission to them, or their acceptance of the jizyah. For them, the only right that is preserved is that they remain as protected subjects (dhimmis) under the Islamic state, and that peace be established between them and the Muslim subjects. Yes, when they accept the Islamic ideology and fully enter Islam, then they are Muslims like other Muslims.

It is a settled matter that under the Islamic state they may keep their belief freely, and they will not be compelled to embrace Islam, because the firm and settled principle of Islam is: "There is no compulsion in religion" (La ikraha fi al-din) ﴿There is no compulsion in religion﴾. However, they may continue their religion in the Islamic world only so long as they continue to pay the jizyah, and this will be subject to an agreement concluded between them and the Islamic state.

This changed nature of the relationship between the Islamic society and the People of the Book can be understood only when an attempt is made to understand this final form of the relationship between the Islamic system of life and the jahili systems in accordance with the activist temperament of Islam. It should be read with careful understanding and insight, especially from the perspective that the laws of these international relations have passed through several stages to reach this final form, and that in it modification and change have continued to occur due to practical circumstances and new stages.

What is this final form? It is this: the Islamic system of life and the jahili systems of life can live together under certain specific conditions. The first is that this jahili system should not be an obstacle in the way of the goal of the Islamic system, that no person on this earth shall be the slave and servant of other persons. No human being shall serve another human being like himself. And on this earth no system, no government and no society shall exist that stands in the way of Islam. This is because the very temperament of Islam is that it wants to prevail, so that it may bring people out of the slavery of other human beings like themselves and into the slavery of Allah. And this is the general proclamation of Islam, whereas the primary aim of jahili systems of life is that they defend themselves, because this proclamation is a proclamation of death for them, and therefore they want to eliminate every movement of this kind, whereas the demand of Islam is that no jahili system should block the way of Islam.

The temperament of the Islamic system of life and of the Islamic movement is that, in the face of jahiliyyah, it brings such weapons as are equal to the weapons of jahiliyyah or are more effective than those weapons, and that the Islamic system adopts an appropriate attitude and conduct in confrontation with jahiliyyah according to a step-by-step programme. And when the final stage arrives, in that stage it acts upon the definitive rules and laws that Islam has laid down for the final stages.

In this part of the surah, the Holy Qur'an has determined the final and definitive form of relations between the Muslims, the Islamic state and the People of the Book. The final position of the People of the Book has also been described, and it has been said that they adhere to shirk, kufr and falsehood. And the events and causes for which this command has been given have been pointed out, whether the cause is that their beliefs are kufr, just as the beliefs of the other disbelievers were, and there is complete similarity between the two, or their conduct, their dealings and their actual circumstances are such. The following reasons are enumerated here:

1. That these people do not believe in Allah and the Last Day.
2. That they do not consider unlawful what Allah and His Messenger have made unlawful.
3. That they do not submit to the religion of truth (the Islamic system).

Among these People of the Book, the belief of the Jews was that Uzair is the son of Allah, and the belief of the Christians was that Jesus is the son of Allah. In these two statements these People of the Book resembled the other disbelievers and polytheists, whether they were Greek idol-worshippers, Roman idol-worshippers, Hindu idol-worshippers, Pharaonic idol-worshippers, or other people of kufr. (Later we shall explain that the Christian claim of the Trinity and sonship, or the Jewish claim of sonship, is derived from earlier idol-worship; this belief was by no means part of the original Christianity or the original Judaism.)

4. (Note: numbering as in the original.) That these people had made their rabbis and monks lords besides Allah, just as they had made the Messiah a lord. Whereas they had been commanded to remain steadfast on the Tawhid of Allah and to keep religion purely for Allah, otherwise they would be polytheists.

5. That they are at war against the religion of Allah and intend to extinguish this new light with the blowing of their mouths; therefore they are disbelievers.

6. That most of the rabbis and monks consume the property of people by false means and prevent people from the religion of Allah.

Because of these attributes, and because of the position on which the People of the Book stood, the Holy Qur'an determined the above final position regarding the People of the Book. Now, in accordance with this final rule, the international code between the Islamic state, the Islamic society and the People of the Book has been formulated.

Here it becomes clearly evident that, unlike the earlier decisions of the Qur'an, this decision is of a completely different nature. Orientalists and Christian missionaries have indeed said that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perceived that his movement had gained strength, he changed his earlier commands. That is, previously there was a different attitude towards the People of the Book, and after acquiring power these commands came.

We say: consider carefully all the Meccan and Medinan verses concerning the People of the Book. From this it will be well understood that no change has occurred in Islam's standpoint regarding the position and beliefs of the People of the Book. Islam regards them, even at this final stage, as holders of misguided beliefs in the same way as Islam's view of them in the early stages: namely, that these are polytheistic beliefs, and amount to a rejection of the religion of truth, and also oppose the religion of which they themselves claim to be adherents. What has changed is only this: how the Islamic state will deal with them in future as an international community; and international relations are a subject for which the rules and policy are determined according to the circumstances existing at any given time, and circumstances, as is obvious, keep changing. As for the beliefs held by the People of the Book, Islam's standpoint concerning them has remained what it was from the first day.

Now we consider it appropriate here to present some comments of the Holy Qur'an concerning the beliefs and ideas of the People of the Book. Then we shall present their practical conduct towards Islam, as a result of which this final and definitive policy regarding them was determined.

In Makkah, there was no Jewish community, and there were not many Christians, nor did they hold any power. There were a few individual Christians. The Holy Qur'an has described that the Christians of Makkah accepted Islam with great joy. They entered Islam and testified to its truth, that this religion and this Messenger are true. These were the people among the Christians who were monotheists (ahl al-tawhid), and they still had with them the authentic teachings of the Gospel. Regarding them the Holy Qur'an has made these comments:

﴿Those to whom We gave the Book before it, they believe in it. And when it is recited to them, they say: "We believe in it; indeed it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed we were Muslims before it."﴾ (28:52–53)

﴿Say: "Believe in it or do not believe. Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall down prostrate upon their faces, and they say: 'Glory be to our Lord! Indeed the promise of our Lord was ever fulfilled.' And they fall down upon their faces weeping, and it increases them in humility."﴾ (17:107–109)

﴿Say: "Have you considered: if this is from Allah and you have disbelieved in it, and a witness from the Children of Israel has testified to the like of it and believed, while you were arrogant? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people."﴾ (46:10)

﴿And thus We have sent down to you the Book, so those to whom We gave the Book believe in it, and among these there are those who believe in it. And none rejects Our signs except the disbelievers.﴾ (29:47)

﴿"Shall I seek other than Allah as judge, while it is He who has sent down to you the Book explained in detail? And those to whom We gave the Book know that it is sent down from your Lord in truth, so be not among the doubters."﴾ (6:114)

﴿Those to whom We gave the Book rejoice in what has been sent down to you, and among the factions there are those who deny part of it. Say: "I have only been commanded to worship Allah and not associate anything with Him. To Him I invite, and to Him is my return."﴾ (13:36)

These were the Meccan Christians. In Madinah too, some Christians accepted the call of Islam, and the Medinan surahs have recorded their testimony. In some verses it is expressly stated that these were Christians, because in Madinah the Jews did not adopt the stance that some of their individuals had taken in Makkah, since in Madinah Islam had become a threat to their worldly interests.

﴿And indeed among the People of the Book are those who believe in Allah and in what has been sent down to you and what has been sent down to them, humbling themselves before Allah, not selling the signs of Allah for a small price. Those will have their reward with their Lord. Indeed, Allah is swift in account.﴾ (3:199)

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 9, verse 29 (part 2 of 3):

"You will find the most intense of people in enmity toward the believers to be the Jews and the polytheists, and you will find the nearest of them in affection toward the believers to be those who say, 'We are Christians.' That is because among them are priests and monks, and because they are not arrogant. And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of the truth they have recognized. They say, 'Our Lord, we have believed, so record us among the witnesses.' And they say, 'Why should we not believe in Allah and in the truth that has come to us, while we long that our Lord will admit us among the righteous people?' So Allah rewarded them, for what they said, with gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the reward of the good-doers." (82–85)

But this was the attitude of a few individuals, and it does not reflect the attitude of the majority of the People of the Book living in the Arabian Peninsula, especially the attitude of the Jews. When the Jews felt, within Madinah, that their interests and their religion were in danger, they launched a fierce assault against Islam, and they began to use all the base weapons whose details the Qur'an has given. Entering Islam was a very great matter for them. They even flatly denied the prophecies about the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that were present in their own scriptures, although the Qur'an was confirming the books that were in their possession. And this despite the fact that some of their own pure-natured people had acknowledged the truth of Islam, and had openly affirmed and proclaimed Islam before deniers and opponents. Thus Islam recorded this general attitude and conduct of theirs as well, and in several surahs it commented on how corrupt, how falsehood-loving, and how far they had deviated from their own religion. Indeed, the Makkan Qur'an also took up the general attitude of the People of the Book. Let us observe:

"And when Jesus came with clear proofs, he said, 'I have come to you with wisdom, and to make clear to you some of that about which you differ; so fear Allah and obey me. Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him; this is a straight path.' But the factions differed among themselves. So woe to those who did wrong, from the punishment of a painful day." (63–65)

"And when it was said to them, 'Dwell in this town and eat from it wherever you wish, and say, "Remission," and enter the gate prostrating; We will forgive you your sins and We will increase the good-doers [in reward].' But those among them who did wrong changed the word from what had been said to them, so We sent upon them a punishment from the heaven because they were wrongdoing. And ask them about the town that was by the sea, when they transgressed in the matter of the Sabbath, when their fish came to them openly on their Sabbath day, and did not come to them on the days other than their Sabbath. Thus did We test them because they were defiantly disobedient." (161–163)

"And [mention] when your Lord proclaimed that He would surely send against them, until the Day of Resurrection, those who would afflict them with the worst torment. Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful." (167)

"Then there succeeded them successors who inherited the Scripture, taking the goods of this lowly world and saying, 'It will be forgiven us.' And if similar goods come to them, they would take them. Was not the covenant of the Scripture taken from them, that they would not say about Allah except the truth, and they have studied what is in it? And the Last Abode is better for those who fear Allah. Will you not reason?" (169)

In the final surahs of the Madinan period, the final and decisive policy regarding the People of the Book was again stated. It was explained in detail how wicked and base weapons these people used in the war against Islam, and in these surahs detailed comments were made on their conduct. For example, in Surah al-Baqarah, Al 'Imran, Surah an-Nisa, al-Ma'idah and others, and their final and enduring policy was then stated in Surah at-Tawbah. The rulings and comments concerning them are these:

"Do you hope that they will believe in you, when a faction of them used to hear the words of Allah and then distort them after they had understood them, while they knew? And when they meet those who believe, they say, 'We believe'; but when they are alone with one another, they say, 'Do you tell them what Allah has disclosed to you, so that they may argue with you about it before your Lord? Will you not reason?' Do they not know that Allah knows what they conceal and what they declare? And among them are unlettered people who know not the Scripture except wishful thinking, and they merely assume. So woe to those who write the Scripture with their own hands and then say, 'This is from Allah,' to exchange it for a small price. So woe to them for what their hands have written, and woe to them for what they earn." (75–79)

"We gave Moses the Scripture, and We sent after him a succession of messengers, and We gave Jesus, son of Mary, clear proofs and supported him with the Holy Spirit. Is it that whenever a messenger came to you with what your souls did not desire, you acted arrogantly, so you denied one group and killed another? And they say, 'Our hearts are wrapped.' Rather, Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so little is it that they believe. And when there came to them a Book from Allah, confirming what was with them, although previously they had been seeking victory over those who disbelieved, yet when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers. Wretched is that for which they have sold themselves, that they disbelieve in what Allah has sent down, out of insolent envy that Allah should send down His bounty upon whom He wills of His servants. So they have returned bearing anger upon anger, and for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment. And when it is said to them, 'Believe in what Allah has sent down,' they say, 'We believe in what was sent down to us,' and they disbelieve in what is beyond it, while it is the truth confirming what is with them. Say, 'Then why did you kill the prophets of Allah before, if you were believers?'" (87–91)

"O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the signs of Allah while Allah is Witness over what you do?" (98)

"Say, 'O People of the Scripture, why do you avert from the way of Allah those who believe, seeking to make it crooked while you are witnesses? And Allah is not unaware of what you do.'" (99)

"Have you not considered those who were given a portion of the Scripture, who believe in Jibt and Taghut and say of those who disbelieve, 'These are better guided than those who believe, in way.' Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, and whoever Allah curses – you will not find for him a helper." (51–52)

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 9, verse 29 (part 3 of 3):

Surely they have disbelieved who said, "Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary." Yet the Messiah said, "O Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord." Indeed, whoever associates others with Allah, Allah has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire. And for the wrongdoers there are no helpers. (72) Surely they have disbelieved who said, "Indeed, Allah is the third of three," while there is no god except one God. And if they do not desist from what they say, a painful punishment will surely touch those among them who disbelieved. (73) Will they not then turn in repentance to Allah and seek His forgiveness? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. (74) The Messiah, son of Mary, was not but a messenger; messengers had passed before him. His mother was a truthful woman, and they both used to eat food. Look how We make the signs clear to them, then look how they are turned away. (75)

Other similar verses of the Qur'an, both Meccan and Medinan, are countless, and they clearly show that the People of the Book have deviated from their true religion. The stance of the Qur'an regarding the People of the Book, from the very first day, has not been changed by the surahs revealed last. Although the accusations of deviation, transgression, association (shirk) and disbelief that have been levelled against them are none of them new. As far as their beliefs and ideologies are concerned, the Qur'an has adopted this same position from the first day. Nevertheless, it is also a fact that the Qur'an has acknowledged that those among them who were good and righteous and firm upon correct beliefs. Consider for example the following verses:

"Among the people of Moses there was a group that guided by the truth and did justice by it." (Cf. 7:159)

"Among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him with a heap of wealth, will return it to you; and among them is one who, if you entrust him with a single dinar, will not return it to you unless you stand over him persistently. That is because they say, 'There is no blame upon us regarding the unlettered.' And they speak untruth about Allah while they know." (3:75)

"Upon them is abasement wherever they are found, except under a rope from Allah and a rope from the people. And they have returned with anger from Allah, and humiliation has been imposed upon them. That is because they used to disbelieve in the signs of Allah and kill the prophets without right. That is because they disobeyed and were transgressing. They are not all alike. Among the People of the Book is a steadfast community who recite the verses of Allah throughout the night while prostrating. They believe in Allah and the Last Day, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and hasten to good deeds. And those are among the righteous. And whatever good they do, it will not be denied them. And Allah is Knowing of the righteous." (3:112–115)

What has changed is the conduct and treatment that the Islamic state would adopt towards the People of the Book. This conduct and treatment have changed with circumstances. In various stages this has altered, and this alteration has come about due to the events that occurred on their part. Because the establishment of the religion of Islam took the form of a movement, and the Islamic state adopted its treatment of them in accordance with the practical attitude that the People of the Book adopted towards this movement.

There was a time when the treatment of the People of the Book was this:

"And do not dispute with the People of the Book except in a way that is best, except for those of them who commit injustice, and say: 'We believe in what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to you. And our God and your God is one, and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him.'" (29:46)

"Say: 'We believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Descendants, and what was given to Moses and Jesus and what was given to the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and we are Muslims to Him.' And if they believe in the like of what you have believed, then they have been guided; but if they turn away, they are only in dissension, and Allah will suffice you against them, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing." (2:136–137)

"Say: 'O People of the Book, come to a word that is equitable between us and you: that we will not worship except Allah and not associate anything with Him and not take one another as lords instead of Allah.' And if they turn away, then say, 'Bear witness that we are Muslims.'" (3:64)

"Many of the People of the Book wish they could return you to disbelief after your belief, out of envy from themselves, after the truth has become clear to them. So pardon and overlook until Allah brings His command. Indeed, Allah is Able to do all things." (2:109)

After these circumstances and policies came the injunctions with which Allah commanded the believers. Thus various events occurred. Because of these events the rulings regarding conduct kept changing, and the positive and movement-oriented work of Islam continued along its course, and the final rulings were revealed, concerning which we have given a detailed discussion in this surah.

Regarding the beliefs and ideologies of the People of the Book, the Qur'an's view has been one and the same from the very beginning: that these are disbelieving and polytheistic ideologies. The change that has occurred is only in how the Islamic state should treat the polytheists and disbelievers among the People of the Book. Please cast another glance at the analysis we presented in the introduction to this surah.

"This final change, which concerns merely the conduct and manner between the Islamic society and the People of the Book, can only be understood if it is viewed from the angle of international relations between the Islamic state and the People of the Book, and then it is seen that the establishment of the Islamic system came into existence as a result of a practical, movement-based process. And in it, modern means were adopted in the face of modern means, and in the various stages of the changing movement-related situation of society, various modes of conduct were adopted.."

Now we will explain in detail what the permanent doctrinal positions are between the Islamic society, the Islamic government and the People of the Book, and what conduct has been adopted historically at various occasions, and as a result of that, what final rulings Islam has given.

Whoever wishes to investigate the true position between the Islamic state and the People of the Book should conduct that research within the following limits. Firstly, that the explanations Allah has given on this matter are final, preserved, and true, and no falsehood is mixed into them. And since these explanations are from Allah, the Lord of the worlds, it cannot be said about them that, like human explanations, there may be some error in them, or that, as with human positions, any interpretation, deduction or reasoning may be applied to them. Secondly, that the conduct, treatment and regulations between them should be determined in the light of the history of Muslims concerning the People of the Book and in relation to them.
