Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 9, verse 30 (part 1 of 3):

(Continuation of the commentary on the preceding verse)

Islam is a true religion on this earth, and it has the right to remove unjust material obstacles from its path, and to leave all people free from all religions other than the true religion (Islam), so that they may come out of a state of compulsion and freely adopt whichever religion they wish. Every person should have the freedom to adopt whatever religion he wishes. There should be no obstacle in his path to adopting any religion.

The right that no person is compelled by any material obstacle, and that every person is free to accept Islam or any other religion, can only be realised when the power and might of jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance) is broken. All non-Islamic powers should be subordinate to the Islamic state and tributaries of the Islamic system.

Through the process of being tributaries, the freedom of man reaches its completion. Every individual adopts the religion he wishes; whoever is satisfied with Islam enters Islam, and whoever is not satisfied remains upon his own religion. But for this freedom he must pay its price in the form of jizyah (poll tax), and this will achieve the following objectives.

1. By paying jizyah, he declares that he will no longer raise any material force as an obstacle in the enmity against Islam, and will not be a barrier to the Islamic call.

2. In return for the defence of his wealth and honour, and the right to freedom which Islam guarantees him, he will pay his share of the expenses of the state. For those who pay jizyah, the Islamic system of government is the guardian of their wealth, life and honour, and defends them, whether the attack is external or whether it is internal security and order.

3. Furthermore, he will pay his share into the Bayt al-Mal (public treasury), from which the maintenance of both Muslims and non-Muslims is arranged. All such people who are unable to earn a living are given a stipend from the Bayt al-Mal, whether they are Muslims or non-Muslims, whereas zakat is not obligatory upon non-Muslims.

We do not go further into the juristic (fiqhi) disputes about which non-Muslims shall be charged jizyah, what the amount of jizyah shall be, and what the procedure for its collection shall be, because today we do not face any practical problem of this kind. In the era of the jurists this matter was a practical issue, so they issued rulings for their own age, gave verdicts, and engaged in ijtihadi discussion of these questions.

Today this matter is regarded as a historical question. It is not a real question, because today Muslims are not engaged in the practice of jihad, and this is because true Muslims are rare in our age. Today the real question before us is whether Islam exists in the world or not.

What is the Islamic system of life? As we have answered this question repeatedly, it is a serious and practical system. This system does not engage in mere idle talk and argument. Nor does it consider it necessary to exert the mind in juristic discussions which do not exist in practice, because in the reality of the world there is no society of Muslims in which the Islamic Shari'ah is implemented and Islamic fiqh governs its practical life. Islam looks with contempt upon those people who fabricate hypotheses and then raise debates upon them. In Islamic terminology they are called "ara'itis" (those who say "what if"), who ask in this manner: "Look, if the situation were to arise thus, what would be the ruling?"

Today we must begin the work of reviving Islam from the same point from which the Messenger (ﷺ) began, and that is: to bring into existence in the world a society which establishes the government of God and implements the religion of Islam within it. It must first bear witness that there is no ruler but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah and the Lawgiver. Therefore, in our society Allah is the Ruler and the Lawgiver, and we are going to implement the commands of Allah and His Messenger in this society; and then, carrying this vision, they should take up the cause of human freedom throughout the whole world. Then, when the government of God is established and is implemented and operative in some Islamic society, only then will the question arise of what the relations of that society shall be with other communities and religions, and at that time the need for these juristic investigations will arise, and at that time experts and people of thought and insight will decide, in the specific circumstances of that time, what our relations with the followers of other faiths and with their governments shall be.

We have, in principle, explained the meaning of this verse here, in a manner that accords with the principles of belief and the methodology of the Islamic system, and upon this we halt our discussion here. Today we do not consider it appropriate to begin discussing subsidiary matters here, because the Islamic system of life is a realistic and practical system.

﴿And the Jews say, "Ezra is the son of Allah," and the Christians say, "The Messiah is the son of Allah." That is their saying from their mouths. They imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before them. May Allah destroy them; how are they deluded?﴾ The Jews say that Uzair is the son of Allah. These are baseless words which they utter with their tongues, following the example of those who disbelieved before them. Curse of God upon them; from where are they being deceived?

When Allah commanded the Muslims to begin fighting the People of the Book and to continue this fighting until they, by their own hands, paying jizyah, demonstrate their humiliation, then the Islamic government of Madinah Munawwarah was facing certain practical circumstances, and at the beginning of this surah we have discussed them in detail. Then, in the general commentary on the first part of the surah, we also discussed them. Here it is necessary to fix these circumstances well in mind, and also to determine well the causes which gave rise to those circumstances, so that all the doubts and misgivings which arise in the minds of some people may be removed. The truth is that compliance with this command required that the Muslims go out against the Romans, who at that time occupied the borders of Syria. Even before Islam the Romans feared the Arab tribes, because these people had for a long time occupied the northern regions of Arabia. The Romans also had their friendships and relations among the Arab tribes. In the north, the Ghassanid government was their tributary. Therefore, the first encounter between the Muslims and the Romans was not the first. That is, when Allah honoured the Arabs through Islam and they came forward as a great nation against great powers such as Persia and Rome, whereas before this they had been scattered tribes, and the tales of their bravery and warlike spirit consisted only of stories of mutual killing, brigandage and plunder, nevertheless the fear of the Arabs still sat in the hearts of the Romans, especially the fear of those who had not yet fully adopted the Islamic colour. The last clash and skirmish with the Romans had taken place in the form of the Battle of Mu'tah, in which, according to reports, more than two hundred thousand Romans had gathered, and the outcome of that battle did not even turn out according to the aims of the Muslims.

On the one hand there were these circumstances, that the work of purifying thought had not yet been completed even within the Islamic society; on the other hand, there was a general fear of the Romans in the hearts of the Muslims; and then the Battle of Tabuk was facing them under circumstances which, both economically and in other respects, were a very time of hardship. For this reason it has been called the "Year of Hardship" (Ghazwa 'Usrah). Detailed circumstances will be explained later. Furthermore, the Muslims also had in their hearts the thought that the Romans and their agents among the Arabs were, after all, among the People of the Book. These were the reasons for which, here, the greatest possible clarifications were given on this matter, and a decisive and plain manner of expression was adopted, and all mental agitation and psychological confusion were removed. And the real causes and factors behind these rulings were also stated.

So, in the verse under discussion, the Holy Qur'an clarifies the intellectual misguidance of the People of the Book: that their doctrine and the doctrine of the misguided Arabs and the doctrine of the idolaters are false and mutually similar and of the same colour. There is no doctrinal difference between the Arab idolaters, the ancient Roman idolaters and those Christians. They have not remained steadfast upon the correct beliefs which Jesus (peace be upon him) had given them; therefore their status as People of the Book has remained only in name. The correct and true doctrines and beliefs which had been given to them in their scriptures, they have abandoned.

Here, the saying of the Jews is also mentioned, that they declare Uzair (peace be upon him) to be the son of Allah, although the direct address and the practical confrontation was only with the Romans, who were Christians and Nasara. Here the Jews have been brought in for two reasons:

1. The previous verse was general, because the term People of the Book applied to both Jews and Christians, and the command given in the preceding verse about fighting, and about taking jizyah and keeping them in subjection, was addressed to all the People of the Book. Therefore, in the mention of the intellectual and doctrinal misguidance of the People of the Book, both were included, so that in terms of doctrine both are equal.

2. Secondly, all the Jews of Arabia had migrated and settled around the borders of Syria. From the time the Messenger of Allah and the Muslims migrated to Madinah, the Jews had continued their war against Islam, as a result of which Banu Qaynuqa' and Banu Nadir were exiled towards the borders of Syria, and some individuals of Banu Qurayzah as well. Therefore the Jews were standing as an obstacle in the path of the expansion of the Islamic revolution towards Syria. Hence it was also necessary to include the Jews in this command.

The Christian saying that the Messiah is the son of Allah is well known and famous. And since Paul misled them, from that time until today they have remained upon this belief. Then, after Paul, their religious councils gave official form to Paul's beliefs and completely misguided them. But the Jewish belief that Uzair is the son of Allah is also very well known. In the Jewish holy books a person named Ezra is mentioned, and about him it is said that he was a skilled scribe of the Torah of Moses. That he turned his heart to seeking the divine Law. But from the belief which the Qur'an has related on their behalf, it becomes clear that some Jews held this view, especially those Jews who lived around Madinah. The Qur'an was in practical dialogue with the Jews of Madinah. It related this belief. If this belief did not exist among the Jews, they would have immediately said that the Qur'an has said something wrong, that this is not our belief. But there is complete silence from the Jews of Madinah on this subject. Therefore, at least at that time this belief was current among the Jews.

In Tafsir al-Manar, volume 10, the late Rashid Rida, on pages 385 to 387, has written a useful discussion on the views of the Jews concerning Ezra. Here we quote from it some passages which will prove most useful. He says:

"The Jewish Encyclopaedia, edition of 1903, states that the age of Ezra was the springtime of Jewish history, in which flowers bloomed everywhere; it could rightly be said of him that he set the chariot of the Law in motion, had Moses (peace be upon him) not received the Law. For after Moses the Law had been forgotten. Ezra presented the Law again and revived it. Had the Children of Israel not committed errors, they would have seen such miracles as they saw in the time of Moses. It is said that he wrote the Law in Assyrian script. Wherever he had doubts about words, he placed a sign upon them. His era is the source for the written history of the Jews."

George Lust, in the Dictionary of the Holy Book, writes: Ezra was a Jewish priest and a renowned writer who resided in Babylon during the reign of Artaxerxes Longimanus. In the seventh year of his accession, the king permitted Ezra to take a large number of his people to Jerusalem. This event took place around 457 BC. These people reached their homeland in four months.

He then writes that according to the beliefs of the Jews, the station of Ezra is equal to that of Moses and Elijah. They say that he established a very great academy, collected the various books of the Holy Book, and wrote them in Chaldean letters instead of ancient Hebrew letters. He composed the Books of Chronicles, and Ezra and Nehemiah.

Mazdi says that the language of "Ezra" at 6-8:4:19 is Chaldean, and similarly at 7:1-27. These people, after returning from captivity, understood the Chaldean language well compared with Hebrew.

"I say that it is well known among all nations, and especially among the People of the Book, that the Torah which Moses (peace be upon him) wrote, and which he kept in or beside the Ark, was lost from the time of Solomon. For in their time, when the Ark was opened, it contained only those two tablets on which the ten commandments were written, as is recorded in the Book of Kings. In fact, the Torah and related books were later written by Ezra, and this was written in Chaldean script after the period of the Babylonian captivity. The Chaldean language contained some Hebrew words as well, which the Jews had forgotten. The People of the Book say that Ezra wrote in such a manner as if it were revelation or inspiration from Allah, but outsiders do not accept it. Very great doubts and objections have been raised in this regard, which are mentioned in detail in the books written on this subject. Even in the books of the People of the Book themselves they are mentioned, for example in the Catholic religion, etc., which was written in French, in whose eleventh and twelfth chapters in particular these objections are mentioned in detail, namely whether the five books of Moses are among them or not."

The Scripture of Ezra (414, no. 21) states that all the sacred books were burnt in the fire, and this happened in the time of Nebuchadnezzar. In it: "The fire has nullified your Law, so no one has any means of knowing what you did" (I believe the Qur'an is the true word, and it has reported that the Tabut contained remnants). Furthermore, Ezra re-collected through revelation of the Holy Spirit the sacred books which the fire had burnt. And in their compilation, five scribes of his contemporaries assisted him. And for this reason, the priests Tertullian, the priest Irenaeus, Jerome and the priest John, the priest Basilius, and others say that Ezra is the reviser of the well-known sacred books. In the end they write:

"I believe this is sufficient here, but here we will state two points: first, that all these People of the Book are indebted to this Ezra, who established the foundation of their religion and compiled their sacred religious books. Second, that these their authentic books are not safe from forgetfulness and error, and this has been acknowledged by free European researchers."

(In Fi Zilal al-Quran we have repeatedly drawn attention to this manner of expression of the school of thought of Muhammad Abduh. These people give too much importance to the free thought of the West, which is alien to the Islamic way of thinking. Because of this way of thinking they give importance to the liberal thinkers of Europe. Likewise, these people look favourably upon the democratic institutions, fundamental rights and way of life of the West. We have many times warned readers in Fi Zilal al-Quran about the dangers of this method and conduct. We must examine Western thought with the most profound scrutiny.)

The British Encyclopaedia, in the biography of him and in the Book of Lamentations (Lahmiah), writes that he also wrote lost books and, in addition, wrote seventy forged books. After this the author wrote about him: "When the situation is such that the story of Ezra was written by some historians on their own account and not attributed to any other book, then modern writers will think that the narrator fabricated these books himself." (See vol. 9, p. 14)

In short, the Jews used to respect Uzair (Ezra) before and still do now, to the extent that some even called him the son of God. The question is: did they use the title "son of God" for him as an honorific in the same way they used it for Solomon and David, or did they use it in the meaning which they attribute to a philosopher (Philo), whose mention will come ahead, which is the original philosophy of the Indians and which is the foundation of the beliefs of the Christians? However, the commentators agree that not all Jews regarded Uzair as the son of God, but rather some people were such.

Which people held the belief that he was the son of God? Some Jews of Medina held this belief, as God Almighty explained about them clearly. And just as they also held this belief: "The hand of Allah is chained" and this belief: "Indeed Allah is poor and we are rich" (Qur'an 3:181). They said this in response to this verse of the Qur'an: "Who will lend Allah a goodly loan?" (2:245). And it is also possible that apart from the Jews of Medina some other sect considered him the son of God, but their belief has not reached us.

Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas that Sallam ibn Mishkam, Nu'man ibn Awfa, Abu Anas, Malik ibn al-Sayf, and Shas ibn Qays came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "How can we submit to you? You abandoned our qiblah, and you do not consider Uzair the son of God."

It is also known that some Christians who considered Messiah the son of God were of Jewish origin. Philo, the famous philosopher of Alexandria who was a contemporary of Messiah, held the belief that God has a son, and this son is that Word through which He created all things. Therefore it is not far from possibility that at the time of the advent of Muhammad there were some people among the Jews who had adopted the belief of sonship regarding Arabia, although in this sense...

From this it becomes known that what the Qur'an said about the Jews, that they consider Uzair the son of God, what is its background; and the context of the speech at this point also shows this. Therefore, the aspect in which the Qur'an spoke is that some Jews held this belief, and among them some people's belief became so corrupt that, with this belief of sonship, they could neither be called believers nor could it be said of them that they were upon the true religion. And the basic row and cause of the command to fight the People of the Book given here is also this corruption of belief. The purpose of fighting is not that they be compelled to abandon their religion and then be compelled to enter Islam. Rather, the sole purpose is to break their power and glory and to make them subject to a system of government in which every human being has complete freedom and liberty, and which does not become an obstacle in the path of the spread of the Islamic state, and that there be no obstacle before them in freely choosing belief, nor any pressure upon them from any direction as to what belief they should adopt.

As for the Christian belief that the Messiah is the son of God and that he is one of three, this is their well-known belief. Since Paul removed Christianity from the common monotheistic belief of the apostles and gave them polytheistic beliefs, and after him their various councils completed this distortion and entirely removed the belief in tawhid from the conceptual system of Christianity, since then they have been founded on the belief in the Trinity, and all their sects have adopted this belief.

Here again I will be content with extracts from the commentary of Ustadh Muhammad Rashid Rida. He writes about the Trinity:

"This term is used among Christians for the three hypostases (aqanim thalatha). In their theological discussions they are known by the names Father, Son and Holy Spirit. These are the beliefs of the Eastern Catholic Church, and generally all Protestants also subscribe to it. Only rare individuals will oppose it. Those who adhere to this belief say that the texts of the Holy Book bring this belief closest. Theological scholars have added extremely complex philosophical explanations regarding this belief, which were based on their ancient councils and the writings of great scholars. Most of the discussions relate to the methods of the birth of the second hypostasis and the process by which the third hypostasis emanates from it. Then there are discussions on the relationship between these three hypostases. Then there is discourse on the attributes and titles of each hypostasis. But the word 'third' is not present in the Gospel. Likewise, there is no verse in the Old Testament which explicitly states the Trinity. Early Christian writers have cited verses in which the collective form of this belief appears, but all these verses can be given a brief exegesis and explanation, so these verses cannot be presented as a definitive proof of the doctrine of the Trinity, but rather they are an indication of a clear revelation which, according to their belief, is present in the New Testament. Two great collections of New Testament verses have been cited as proof of this belief. One collection is of verses in which Father, Son and Holy Spirit are mentioned together. The other collection is of verses in which each is mentioned separately, and in which their important special attributes are mentioned, and their mutual relationship is mentioned."

"The dispute about the hypostases within the Divine Being arose in the age of the apostles. It arose as a result of Hellenistic and Gnostic philosophies. In the second century Theophilus, bishop of Antioch, used the Greek word triados. After this Tertullian used the word trinitas. This word was synonymous with thaluth. There was tremendous dispute about this belief before the first council of Nicaea, especially in the Eastern Church. And the Eastern Church declared all these opinions to be heretical. Among them were the views of the Ebionites, whose belief was that Messiah is merely a human being. Likewise, the Sabellians were also included, who held that Father, Son and Holy Spirit are three different attributes which God applied to His own being. Likewise there were the Arians, whose beliefs were that the Son is not eternal but a creation of the Father. But his creation took place before the creation of the world, and therefore his rank is lower than the Lord; rather he is subordinate and obedient to the Lord. Among them were also the Macedonians, whose belief was that the Holy Spirit is not a hypostasis at all."

The creed of the church today was formulated by the council of Nicaea in 325. After this, the conference of Constantinople in 381 CE ratified it. The decision was that the Son and the Holy Spirit are both equal to the Father in divinity and godhead, and that the Son was begotten from eternity together with the Father, while the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Lord. Then the council of Toledo in 589 decided that the Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son. Thereupon the entire Latin Church accepted this amendment. As for the Greek Church, it remained silent at first, but later it argued that this amendment is heretical.

The phrase (and from the Son) in the creed has always been a cause of disagreement between the Greek and Catholic Churches. Lutherans and other reformed churches continued the original beliefs of the Catholic Church, but in the thirteenth century the majority of the clergy opposed them, and some modern theologians and some modern sects, such as the Socinians, Germans, Mohammedans, Universalists and others, declared that these beliefs are incompatible with both the Holy Book and reason. Mr. Swedenborg applied the term Trinity to Christ as a sign; that is, instead of a trinity of different hypostases, he gave the theory of a trinity of one hypostasis. This meant that the Divinity in the person of Christ was the Lord, and the Son was the one connected to Christ's natural person, and that which proceeded from him was the Holy Spirit. Because of the ideas that spread for a long time in Lutheran churches, great instability arose in the beliefs of German theologians and remained so for a long time."

"Kant's theory was that the three attributes in the Divinity, namely Lord, Son and Holy Spirit, mean power, wisdom and love; or they mean three supreme acts, namely creation, preservation and control. Hegel and Schelling gave an imaginative basis, and many German theologians imitated them. They defended the doctrine of the Trinity on an imaginative foundation. Some theologians who rely on revelation do not consider the views of the church correct on the basis of research; that is, the views decided by the councils of Nicaea and Constantinople. In recent times many people have supported the Sabellians."

After this summary discussion it becomes known that not all sects and religions of the church community are upon the true religion. In none of them does the belief in tawhid exist in its proper sense, the essence of which is that there is none like Allah, and that Allah is the one who "begets not, nor is He begotten" (112:3).

The Arians often claim that they are monotheists, but this claim is misleading, because they are not monotheists in the way Muslims are monotheists; rather they have mixed their beliefs. On one hand they affirm that Messiah is not eternal like Allah, and this statement of theirs is indeed correct. But together with this they also hold to sonship and also hold that Messiah was a creature even before the world. Therefore this belief cannot be called the belief of tawhid.

Allah has explicitly called those people disbelievers who say that the Messiah is the son of God or that he is one of three. So how can the attribute of disbelief and the attribute of faith be combined in one belief, when these are contradictory attributes and contradictory matters?

The Qur'an's comment on the saying of the Jews (Uzair is the son of Allah) and the saying of the Christians (Isa is the son of Allah) establishes that their saying is equal to the conceptions and beliefs of other disbelievers:

"The Jews say, 'Uzair is the son of Allah,' and the Christians say, 'The Messiah is the son of Allah.' That is their saying from their mouths; they imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before them" (9:30).

From this it becomes known that this statement was actually issued by them, not merely attributed to them. And the word "from their mouths" (afwahihim) has not been brought without purpose; rather, it also intends to point to the physical state of their faces at the time they were saying it. Therefore it cannot be objected that the word afwahihim is superfluous and purposeless, since it does not befit Allah to speak without purpose. Nor is it prolixity, because the Qur'an's manner is to bring the real situation before the eye in its depiction. Furthermore, through this word it is also intended to indicate that this is merely an empty claim on their part; there is no reality behind it. It is merely a saying, with no meaning.

"They imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before them" (yudahi'una qawl alladhina kafaru min qabl). The commentators said that the sonship belief of these people is like the sonship belief of the polytheists regarding the angels, and the Arabs held the sonship of the angels. This is also correct in its place. But the meaning of the verse is broader than this, and it became clearer when the beliefs of Hindu idol-worshippers reached people. These beliefs resemble the beliefs of the ancient Egyptian idolaters and the Greeks. And these very beliefs penetrated into the People of the Book, especially into the beliefs of the Christians. The first to introduce these conceptions into the beliefs was "Paul the Apostle," and after that, having gained dominance in the doctrinal councils of the Christians, they spread widely.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 9, verse 30 (part 3 of 3):

The Egyptian trinity and the Osirian doctrine of Zoris (Lord), Isis and Horus (the son) is the fundamental principle of idol worship.

Even before the birth of Hazrat Masih (Jesus), the theology taught in Alexandria called the "Word" (Kalimah) a second god, and it was also called "the only begotten son of God."

The Hindus too believed in three hypostases, or they expressed them as three states of God in which Allah manifests Himself. In the state of creation and formation it is called Brahma; as preserver and sustainer it is Vishnu; and in the state of destruction and annihilation it is called Shiva. According to this belief, Vishnu is the son, and he issues from the divinity of Brahma.

The Assyrians too believed in the Word (Kalimah). They called it Marduk, and they called Marduk "the only begotten son of God."

The Greeks too believed in a triune divinity. When they slaughtered a sacrifice, they would sprinkle holy water on it three times, and in the same way they would take perfume from a perfume vessel with three fingers. Then they would sprinkle that perfume three times on the people standing around the sacrifice, and all of these gestures pointed toward the trinity. The Church derived these gestures and organized its rites and worship in such a way that they came to resemble the sayings of the other disbelievers.

At the time of the revelation of the Qur'an these beliefs of the ancient polytheists were not widespread, yet the All-Knowing, All-Aware declared: ﴿Yudahi'un qawl alladhina kafaru min qabl﴾ ("They imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before them"). Moreover, these beliefs also establish that the People of the Book are not upon the true religion, and their faith is not sound faith. Besides this, it also establishes that the Holy Qur'an is a miraculous speech from the All-Knowing, All-Aware, and its source is solely the Divine Essence.

After this judgment and clarification, at the end of the verse it is stated what position of shirk and disbelief the People of the Book hold: ﴿Qatalahumu Allah, anna yu'faknun﴾ ("May Allah destroy them; how are they deluded?"). May Allah destroy them; how do they turn away from the truth, when it is straightforward and clear, and in adopting idol worship, which is extremely intricate and convoluted, and which no wise and sensible person can even comprehend?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 9, verse 31:

Now the Qur'an turns to another page of the deviations and misguidance of the People of the Book. Here their misguidance is no longer limited to belief and utterances alone, but they are also astray and deviated in terms of the practical condition that results from these corrupt beliefs and conceptions.

...

This verse too continues the same theme, which is the main subject of this lesson: that these people are in reality not People of the Book. Therefore, in this respect they cannot be regarded as being upon the true religion. The truth is that these people are not upon the religion of Islam. Their practical life bears witness to this. Their conceptions bear witness to this. They were commanded only to worship Allah, the One, but they made their rabbis (ahbar) and monks (ruhban) into lords besides Allah, just as they made Hazrat Masih (Jesus) a lord, which is clear shirk on their part. Whereas Allah is free from every kind of shirk. The result is that, in terms of their beliefs and conceptions, and in terms of their deeds and actual life, they are not upon the true religion.

In what manner did these people make their rabbis and monks lords alongside Allah? Before explaining this, we wish to cite here the exegetical narrations reported from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning this verse, because the explanation of the Messenger himself is the decisive word.

Ahbar is the plural of hibr or habr (with the vowel of the ha being either kasra or fatha). It is the title of the scholars of the People of the Book, and it is applied more to the scholars of the Jews. Ruhban is the plural of rahib. Among Christians, this term is used for a person who dedicates himself to worship and cuts himself off from all other activities. Generally such a person does not marry, nor does he engage in any livelihood, and therefore he is free from economic burdens.

In Ad-Durr al-Manthur there is a narration of Imam Tirmidhi, which he called a hadith hasan. Also Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, Bayhaqi and others have narrated it. This narration is from Hazrat 'Adi ibn Hatim. He says that I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was reciting Surah Tawbah. He recited this verse: "They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah." Then the Messenger (ﷺ) said: "It is true that they did not worship their rabbis and monks, but the matter was that when they declared something lawful for them, they considered it lawful, and when they declared something unlawful, they considered it unlawful."

Ibn Kathir has cited this narration of Hazrat 'Adi ibn Hatim in his tafsir. He says that when the call of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) reached him, he fled towards Syria. He had become a Christian in the Age of Ignorance. His sister was taken captive along with her people, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) treated her with great generosity and gave her gifts. She returned to her brother and inspired him towards Islam and persuaded him to go to Madinah. So 'Adi went to Madinah. He was the chief of his people, Tayy, and his father Hatim al-Ta'i was famous for his generosity and magnanimity. People in Madinah talked about his arrival. He met the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). There was a golden cross around his neck. The Messenger was reciting this verse: "They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah." He says that I asked: "O Messenger of Allah, the Christians do not worship their rabbis and monks." The Messenger said: "It is true that they do not worship them, but they have fixed for them the limits of lawful and unlawful, and the people obey them in this matter. Therefore this is their worship of them by the people."

Imam al-Suddi says that they had made human beings their leaders and had cast the Book of Allah behind their backs. That is why Allah says: "And they were commanded only to worship One God" [wa ma umiru illa liya'budu ilahan wahidan], meaning that they were commanded only to worship Allah alone, that is, to consider lawful what Allah declares lawful and to consider unlawful what Allah declares unlawful. That is, the law made by Allah should be obeyed and what He commands should be enforced.

Imam Alusi, in his well-known tafsir, says: "The majority of the exegetes have said that this does not mean that they regarded their rabbis and monks as the gods of the universe, but rather that they obeyed them in their commands and prohibitions."

From this most clear verse, and then from the explanation of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), together with the interpretations of the earlier and later exegetes, the following conclusions emerge regarding the original concepts and beliefs of the religion of Islam. And these conclusions are extremely important and concise.

According to the text of the Qur'an and the explanations of the Messenger, the meaning of worship is that one follows someone. Because the Jews and Christians did not regard their rabbis and monks as gods in belief, nor did they perform acts of servitude before them, yet despite this fact Allah charged them with kufr. Merely because these people took their law from their religious leaders and then obeyed it. Therefore, if someone does not regard another as a god and does not perform acts of servitude before him, but takes law and legislation from him, this person is a mushrik and kafir, and the one from whom he takes the law stands in the position of a lord.

The Jews, who took law from their rabbis, and the Christians, who regarded Masih as god and also took law from their monks, Allah has placed both in one category and has not made any distinction between them, because both are equal in committing shirk and both are outside the fold of Islam.

As soon as a person grants the right of legislation to anyone other than Allah, he becomes a mushrik, even if he does not regard that person as a god or worshipped being and does not perform acts of servitude before him, as has become clear from the above explanations. But we wish to elaborate further on this point.

When these realities were presented to the Muslims, the ummah was facing particular circumstances. There was the issue of war with the Romans, and some Muslims had doubt and hesitation in their minds that the Romans are, after all, People of the Book. Therefore, to remove this doubt and misgiving, these verses were revealed and it was made clear that although the People of the Book are believers in Allah, and that their state of faith is this, nevertheless, despite being revealed in particular circumstances, these verses state the general principles and absolute realities of the religion of Islam.

According to Allah, the true religion is only Islam, and Allah does not accept from people any religion other than Islam. And the religion of Islam will be fully established in the world only when the Shari'ah of Allah is enforced on this earth, and even before the enforcement of that Shari'ah, that people regard Allah alone as God and perform acts of servitude before Him alone. So if people follow any law other than the Shari'ah of Allah, then in them the condition that existed among the Jews and Christians is present, and for this reason they were declared non-believers, although they repeatedly claimed to be believers. Because the moment they accept the Shari'ah of any human being other than Allah, they become mushrik. Except where there is a situation in which they are compelled to live under a non-Islamic legal system and are forced to follow it, while at the same time striving to remove that system.

The meaning of the word din has shrunk so much that people have come to regard it as synonymous only with religious belief, or at most extend it to acts of servitude and worship. To this limited extent the Jews too were adherents of their religion and called themselves religious in this restricted sense. But the explanation of the Messenger (ﷺ) shows that in true terms they were neither believers nor religious, because they had taken their rabbis and monks as lords besides Allah.

The first meaning of din is that one submits before someone, and this can be realised only when someone submits before the legal system of God. Therefore this matter is very serious, and this meaning does not recognise as people of religion those who follow legal systems other than the Shari'ah, except where they are compelled. Such people are not Muslims or believers in Islam merely because they regard Allah as the one God and worship Him. The latitude that has been given to the common people in our age is an extremely dangerous latitude for the religion of Islam. It is in fact a dangerous weapon that the enemies of Islam use for the eradication of Islam. They affix the label of Islam upon those situations and persons, and about such people, Allah clearly tells us that they are not people of religion, they are not believers, because they have made others lords besides Allah. When the enemies of religion insist on proving as religious those people who are in reality not religious, then it is also the duty of the supporters of Islam to demonstrate that such situations are non-Islamic situations, to show that such individuals and such societies are non-Islamic individuals and societies, and to explain clearly the reality of this issue, that such people have made others lords. Whereas they were commanded:

"They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah, and also the Messiah, son of Mary. Yet they were commanded only to worship One God; there is no god but Him. Glory be to Him above what they associate." [Qur'an 9:31]

Following this, the discourse continues thus:

"They wish to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths. But Allah refuses to do anything except perfect His light, even though the disbelievers may dislike it. It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, so that He may make it prevail over all religions, even though the polytheists may dislike it."

That is, the fault of the People of the Book is not only that they have deviated from their true religion, which was a true faith, and their crime is not only that they had made other personalities lords besides Allah and did not believe in the Hereafter as the correct meaning of the Hereafter requires; rather, besides this, they have another unpardonable crime. It is that they have declared war against the religion of truth, and they wish to extinguish with their own eyes the new light that Muhammad ﷺ is spreading in the form of the religion of truth, and they want to end the call that is spreading throughout the world, and they want to destroy the system of life that has been formed in accordance with this new call.

﴿They wish to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths﴾

Therefore, these people are enemies of the light of Allah. Through their lies, intrigue and mischief-making, they seek to extinguish this light, or they incite their followers, their groups, and their kin and allies to wage war against this religion and block its path. At the time these verses were being revealed this was the situation, and today it is the same situation.

The purpose of these verses at that time was that the Muslims should prepare to defend themselves with enthusiasm, but after those circumstances, to this day, the stance of the People of the Book regarding Islam has remained the same. They constantly strive to extinguish the light of Islam, but Allah's stance is this:

﴿But Allah refuses except to perfect His light, even though the disbelievers dislike it﴾

This is Allah's true promise, and this promise is based on Allah's unchangeable law, that although the disbelievers will dislike it, Allah will shine His light fully.

This promise is a source of reassurance for the believers and the workers of the Islamic revolution. They should advance further on their chosen path, press forward steadily, face the difficulties of the way with resolve, and confront the plots of the enemy and the enemy's continuous war. Initially the intended ones were the People of the Book, but the intended meaning now is the common enemy who wishes to block the way of Islam, by whatever title they block it and under whatever protection they do so.

Now, in the next verse, the same theme is further emphasized.

This verse shows that the "religion of truth" (din al-haqq) here means the same religion that is referred to as "din" in the verse of fighting:

"Fight those who do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day, and do not forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, and do not adopt the religion of truth from among those who were given the Book, until they pay the jizyah (poll-tax) willingly while they are humbled." (29) Fight against those among the People of the Book who do not believe in Allah and the Last Day, and who do not forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, and do not make the religion of truth their religion. (Fight them) until they give the jizyah with their own hand and remain subservient. And this religion of truth is the very one that was given to Muhammad (ﷺ). Fighting is obligatory against those who do not accept this religion of truth.

Whatever interpretation we adopt of this verse, the following point is correct, because religion means that a person completely obeys Allah, and accepts Allah's law both in matters of worship rituals and in legislation. This is the principle of entering the whole of religion. And the final form of this religion of truth is the one presented by Muhammad (ﷺ). Therefore, whoever does not accept Allah's religion, His acts of worship and His Shariah, the ruling applies to him that he does not accept the religion. And the verse of fighting mentioned above applies to him, but at the time of applying the verse of fighting, the stages of the movement-based and gradual nature of Islam must certainly be kept in view, because in Islam every step has a set time, the explanation of which we have repeatedly given.

This is the verse: "He it is who sent His Messenger with guidance..." It is an emphasis on the subject of the previous verse, in which it was said: "Allah refuses except to perfect His light, though the disbelievers dislike it." The meaning was that the light which Allah wishes to perfect is the establishment and dominance of the Islamic system of life, and indeed after its establishment, this light will be complete in the form of its dominance over all the systems established in the world. Now, what is the religion of truth? As we have said repeatedly before, the religion of truth is to hold belief in Allah alone, to worship and serve Allah alone, and to obey and implement the Shariah revealed by Allah. And these elements were part of all the religions that the truthful messengers presented to mankind at any time. Therefore, the religion of truth does not include those idolatrous, deviated religions whose original contained correct elements but whose present form is a distorted form, and which are in reality idolatrous religions, such as global Judaism and Christianity.

Moreover, the religion of truth also includes those religions and creeds which have put up the label of religion, but in reality in those systems people worship others besides Allah (arbaban min dun Allah), in that people obey laws made by human beings, and laws which Allah has not revealed.

Whereas Allah's clear command is that He has sent His Messenger with the religion of truth and guidance, so that he may make this religion of truth dominant over all religions. Therefore it is our duty to take religion in its broad meaning, so that we may know the breadth of Allah's covenant.

Religion is in fact a system of life. Therefore, whatever system people accept, obey, and consider their concepts to be correct, and whose following they pledge loyalty to, that is their religion.

Then it is Allah's decision that He wishes to make this religion dominant over all religions. Here too, the same broad meaning of religion is intended, namely a system of life. The system of life is only Allah's system of life, and all people have to obey it. And only this system is intended to be made dominant.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) demonstrated this once in practice. After him, his rightly-guided Caliphs maintained the dominance of the religion. In those periods the religion of truth remained dominant and distinguished, and all those religions in which obedience was not purely for Allah trembled before it. After this, the bearers of the religion of truth themselves abandoned this religion. Gradually they moved away from religion, and as a result of the continuous intrigues of the cross-worshipping and idolatrous religions against the Islamic system and Islamic society, and the joint operations of disbelievers and People of the Book, this system was brought to an end.

But the battle has not stopped. Allah's promise remains in place. Allah is watching the believers; He is waiting. Those believers who have raised the banners of Allah have begun their work from the starting point from which the Prophet (ﷺ) began his work, and this movement for the revival of the religion of truth is now advancing in the light of divine radiance.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 9, verse 34:

We have now reached the last unit of this lesson in the surah. It is explained how the People of the Book do not make unlawful what Allah has made unlawful. Previously it was said that they take their rabbis (aḥbār) and monks (ruhbān) as lords. They make them lords besides Allah. The Prophet ﷺ interpreted this by saying that these People of the Book consider lawful what the rabbis and monks declare lawful, and unlawful what they declare unlawful. Here it is stated that these rabbis and monks do not consider unlawful what Allah has made unlawful, and do not consider lawful what Allah has made lawful.

In the verse, the role of the rabbis and monks is described in such a way that the common people have made them lords besides Allah. As a consequence, these people frame laws of lawful and unlawful for the masses. In this way they have presented themselves to the people as lords, and the people have accepted this. The necessary result of this situation is that they consume the wealth of people unjustly, and they prevent people from coming onto the right path.

The ways of consuming people's wealth are various, and they are still prevalent. Among them is the fee that was taken in exchange for declaring the unlawful lawful or the lawful unlawful. Such decisions generally went in favour of the wealthy or were issued in favour of kings. Among them is also the fee that religious leaders used to take from a confessed sinner, and then forgive him. In the belief of these religious leaders, they held these powers under the Sharia, and in this regard the well-known issue has been that they used to declare it lawful.

Among them are also the amounts that they used to collect from people for opposition to the true religion. The rabbis, monks, bishops and other religious leaders have continued to collect millions of rupees for the Crusades, and now they collect billions for orientalists and missionaries and spend them in the Islamic world. Thus, by misguiding people, they block the way of Allah.

The following verse of the Holy Qur'an deserves deep reflection. In it, the matter is stated with such justice and fairness.

Inna kathīran min al-aḥbāri wa al-ruhbān: that is, most of the rabbis and monks. This excludes the small number of those who do not commit this error, because the presence of good people among the various sects and communities of the world is a natural matter. And the Divine Being, in any case, deals justly with everyone.

Most rabbis and monks used to accumulate the wealth taken from people. The history of the Jews and Christians bears witness that they gathered the wealth of people in their churches, and their cushions were filled with immense offerings. Sometimes the wealth accumulated with religious leaders exceeded even that of kings and rajas and maharajas.

Therefore, in this context, Allah has made the very wealth they accumulated a cause of punishment for them on the Day of Judgment, and this same punishment will be given to all those who do not spend their wealth in the way of Allah. This is depicted in an extremely frightening manner:

"And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend them in the way of Allah, give them the good news of a painful punishment. On a Day when it will be heated in the fire of Hell, and their foreheads, their sides and their backs will be branded with it. This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard."

Many details of this scene of punishment are given here, and the punishment is explained in detail from its early stages to its final stages, so that this scene settles firmly in the senses and imagination. Therefore, giving the details of the punishment is purposeful.

"Give the good news of a painful punishment to those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend them in the way of Allah." After this, the context falls silent, and after the general and ambiguous statement, the details are given in the next verse.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 9, verse 35 (part 1 of 2):

"On the Day when it shall be heated in the fire of Hell, and their foreheads, their sides and their backs shall be branded with it" — a day will come when fire of Hellfire will be kindled upon that very gold and silver. Now the listener sees how these metals are heated. In the next scene, attendants holding hot rods in their hands appear. The rods are ready and the painful punishment begins. Now the faces and hands of these criminals are branded, and when their faces have been thoroughly branded, their sides are then branded, and when their sides have been branded, the branding of their backs begins. And when this physical punishment ends, they are then reproached, so that their spiritual humiliation may be complete.

﴿This is what you hoarded for yourselves﴾ — "This is the treasure that you gathered for yourselves." You gathered it for pleasure, but now it has become for you an instrument of painful punishment.

﴿So taste what you used to hoard﴾ — "Now taste the wealth you had amassed." It is the very same wealth. Now see that mere contact of it with your faces, your sides and your backs is a cause of torment.

In short, this is an extremely frightening scene, and every single movement of it is described in detail, and the majority of the rabbis and monks will undergo these details. Then there are those who hoard wealth without necessity and do not spend it in the way of Allah. It should be kept in mind here that these verses were revealed on the occasion of the Battle of Tabuk, which is also called Ghazwat al-'Usrah.

I think we should pause here and re-examine this entire discussion afresh, and keep in mind the position which, according to these divine guidelines, the People of the Book truly hold: what are their beliefs? What are their successors? What is their conduct? Especially in the light of the indications we gave during the explanation of these verses.

Clarifying the image of the People of the Book, as to whether they are upon the true religion, was extremely necessary. Openly polytheistic people are, in any case, polytheists, and they are visible to everyone. They are seen by their beliefs, their deeds and their acts of worship, that they are polytheists. But by the name "People of the Book" there could have been doubt that perhaps they are religious. It was necessary to remove these doubts so that Muslims would be well prepared to confront that jahiliyyah (ignorance). As for the polytheists, everyone knows that they are followers of jahiliyyah, but the position regarding the People of the Book was not clear, because the People of the Book claimed that they, like the Muslims, were followers of a heavenly religion from earlier times. Just as the majority of today's so-called Muslims make the claim that they are Muslims.

From the very beginning of this surah, complete disavowal of the polytheists and complete confrontation with them has been the detailed subject of this surah, and the circumstances also required it, which we explained in the introduction of this surah, where Allah the Exalted said:

"How can there be a covenant with Allah and His Messenger for the polytheists, except those with whom you made a covenant at al-Masjid al-Haram? So as long as they are upright towards you, be upright towards them; indeed Allah loves the righteous. (7) How (can there be)? For if they gain the upper hand over you, they would not observe regarding you any tie of kinship or covenant. They please you with their mouths, but their hearts refuse, and most of them are defiantly disobedient. (8) They have exchanged the signs of Allah for a small price, and they have averted (people) from His way. Indeed, evil is what they have been doing. (9) They do not observe regarding a believer any tie of kinship or covenant, and it is those who are the transgressors. (10)"

How can the polytheists have a covenant with Allah and His Messenger? Except those with whom you made a covenant at al-Masjid al-Haram. So as long as they remain straight with you, you too remain straight with them, for Allah loves the righteous. But how can there be a covenant with the other polytheists, when their condition is that if they gain power over you, they would observe no kinship and no covenant regarding you? They try to please you with their mouths, but their hearts refuse, and most of them are defiantly disobedient. They have accepted a small price for the verses of Allah, and then they stood as barriers in the way of Allah. Evil were the deeds they kept doing. Regarding a believer they observe neither kinship nor covenant. And the transgression has always come from them.

"Will you not fight a people who broke their oaths, and who resolved to expel the Messenger, and who started the aggression against you first? Do you fear them? Allah has more right that you should fear Him, if you are believers. (13) Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands, and will disgrace them, and will help you against them, and will heal the breasts of a believing people (14), and will remove the rage of their hearts; and Allah turns in forgiveness to whom He wills, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise. (15)"

"It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah while they bear witness against themselves to disbelief. Those, their deeds have become worthless, and in the Fire they will abide eternally. (17)"

"O you who believe, do not take your fathers and your brothers as allies if they prefer disbelief over faith. And whoever among you takes them as allies, those are the wrongdoers. (23)" The necessary requirement of rising for jihad against the polytheists was that they be criticized, and their case was also straightforward, because at that time the Islamic community faced the kind of circumstances in which the polytheists were the opponents of the Islamic society. But to wage jihad against the People of the Book, perhaps even more than against the polytheists, a critical assault was needed, and it was necessary to strip them of the label of being People of the Book and People of Religion that they bore, and to reveal their true reality: that they are polytheists just like the polytheists, and that there is no difference between them and other polytheists. Like other disbelievers, they too are disbelievers, and just like both disbelievers and polytheists, they too are engaged day and night in war against the religion of Islam. They are misguided, and they consume the wealth of people by the most utterly false means. They bar people from the way of Allah. Accordingly, Allah the Exalted revealed a clear-cut position regarding them:

"Fight those who do not believe in Allah and the Last Day, and who do not forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, and who do not follow the religion of truth from among those who were given the Book, until they pay the jizyah willingly, while they are humbled. (29) The Jews say, 'Ezra is the son of Allah,' and the Christians say, 'The Messiah is the son of Allah.' That is their statement from their mouths; they imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before them. May Allah destroy them; how deluded they are! (30) They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah, and (also) the Messiah, son of Mary. And they were not commanded except to worship one God; there is no deity except Him. Exalted is He above what they associate with Him. (31) They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah refuses except to perfect His light, although the disbelievers dislike it. (32) It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, to make it prevail over all religion, although the polytheists dislike it. (33) O you who believe, indeed many of the rabbis and monks consume the wealth of people unjustly and bar from the way of Allah. And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah — give them tidings of a painful punishment. (34) On the Day when it shall be heated in the fire of Hell, and their foreheads, their sides and their backs shall be branded with it: 'This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard.' (35)"

The rulings that other Meccan and Medinan surahs give about these People of the Book are apart from these. In all the Meccan and Medinan surahs it is established regarding them that they have entered completely into disbelief and polytheism, and have fully gone out of the true religion. They have entirely abandoned the religion that their prophets brought to them. Moreover, they have not only failed to accept the present true religion, but are also determined to block its path. Therefore, on account of their stance regarding the new religion, they too are wholly disbelievers and polytheists.

Earlier verses have already passed in which the People of the Book were addressed with the statement that they have completely departed from the heavenly religion and the divine religion:

"Say, O People of the Book, you are not upon anything until you establish the Torah and the Gospel and what has been revealed to you from your Lord." It is certain that what has been revealed to you will increase many of them in rebellion and disbelief. So do not grieve over the disbelieving people. (68)

"Certainly those who say that Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary, have disbelieved." "Certainly those who say that Allah is the third of three have disbelieved." "Those who disbelieved among the People of the Book and the polytheists would not have ceased (from their disbelief) until there came to them clear evidence."

These and many other verses of this kind, which we cited earlier, are found in both the Meccan and the Medinan Qur'an, and they are numerous.

The situation was that the Qur'an had given the People of the Book a distinctive position in certain matters. For instance, their food was made lawful for Muslims, and marriage with their chaste women was declared permissible. But this distinctive position was not given to them because they adhered to some part of the true religion; rather, these concessions were given to them because they were in principle holders of the true religion, and historically they were part of the Islamic movement, although in fact they themselves did not even remain upon their own religion. Thus, in dialogue with them, it was possible to say that our and your original religion is indeed one. Accordingly, the Qur'an gave them this distinctive position over the idolaters and polytheists, whereas among the idolaters there was no principle in hand with which Islam could enter into dialogue with them. As for the question of what the reality of the leadership of the People of the Book itself is, what their beliefs are, and what their religious status is, the Qur'an left no ambiguity in this matter; rather, it spoke a clear-cut word: that they are outside the religion. They have abandoned their original religion of beliefs and practices, and now their beliefs and practices are those which their rabbis and monks have composed for them, and which have been formally settled in councils of belief and law. The divine word on this subject is decisive and clear.

At this point, the important matter is that we discuss the consequences of this decisive divine ruling: given the present beliefs and religious condition of the People of the Book, what will be the nature of relations with them?

The title and the board placed upon them are a cause of misunderstanding. There is no reality behind this board. Because of this board, the Islamic movement does not stand out against the jahiliyyah (ignorance) of these people. Therefore there is an urgent need to tear down this board, to thoroughly remove the misunderstanding caused by this address, and to make people aware of the true reality of these people and their real face.

Earlier we have pointed out that in the Islamic society at that time there were conditions in which some elements of the Islamic society held a soft corner for them, especially at the time of the Battle of Tabuk, where certain particular circumstances also existed. Moreover, at that time the awe of Rome also overshadowed the hearts of the Arabs. But, as we have given the details before, the real matter was that some Muslims could not comprehend such an all-encompassing war against the Romans merely because the Romans were, after all, People of the Book.

Today, the enemies of the religion who keep watch over the movements striving for the revival of Islam study these movements with great skill. These people put Islamic labels on modern conditions, new movements, new trends, and ideas and concepts, and with this Islamic label they work against the true Islamic movements in the Muslim world. These cunning enemies of Islam, who are among the People of the Book and also in the form of atheists and disbelievers, never unite among themselves; they unite only when they face a confrontation with Islam, and they carry out their hostilities in secret. Apart from the movement of Ataturk, all their other movements are still running under an Islamic label and an Islamic board. Through them they want to create and maintain such conditions, and to sustain these collective conditions they also provide economic and political aid. Those simple-minded people who call themselves Muslims are being thoroughly deceived by this title and label. Even some callers to Islam have been deceived by this label.
