**Lesson No. 89: At a Glance**

The context continues logically, removing the obstacles to preparations for war against the Romans and their Christian allies in northern Arabia. These preparations and the military campaign were apparently taking place in the month of Rajab. In reality, however, this was not so. The truth was that in that year the month of Rajab was not in its proper place. This was because of the system of *nasi'* (the intercalation practice by which the Arabs shifted sacred months, explained further below) that they had established for their calculations. According to that system, the month of Dhul-Hijjah was not in its place. It was in the place of Dhul-Qa'dah, and Rajab was coming in the place of Jumada al-Akhirah. The real secret of this confusion was that the system of jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic age of ignorance) did not even observe its own principles and rules. It respected laws and principles only as a matter of outward show. In every jahili system, since the limits of the lawful and the unlawful are fixed by human beings themselves, they carry out the duty of violating limits by making interpretations within the limits they have set.

The story is this. God had declared four months sacred. Of these, three were consecutive, namely Dhul-Qa'dah, Dhul-Hijjah and Muharram, and the fourth stood alone, namely Rajab. This sanctity was tied to the well-known months of the Hajj, and it dated from the time of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). Although the Arabs had greatly distorted the religion of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and had turned away from a religion that was true, they nevertheless continued to observe the sanctity of the four sacred months down to the time of the Messenger (ﷺ). This was because they were connected with the season of the Hajj, and the economic life of the Hijaz depended entirely upon these months, especially that of the people of Makkah. For the success of trade during the season of the Hajj depended on people being able to move about freely and on trade continuing uninterrupted.

After this, it happened that the personal needs of some Arab tribes came into conflict with this sanctity, and their desires also began to exert their influence. People arose who convinced them that the sacred months could be advanced or postponed according to their wishes, so that one month might be brought forward in one year and postponed in another. The number of months would remain four, but the names of the months would be changed. In this way they could both complete the number of months God had made sacred and make lawful what God had made sacred. Thus, when the year 9 AH arrived, the month of Rajab in it was not the true Rajab. Likewise, the month of Dhul-Hijjah was not the true Dhul-Hijjah. Rajab was in reality Jumada al-Akhirah, and Dhul-Hijjah was in reality Dhu al-Qa'dah. In fact, this military campaign was actually in Jumada al-Akhirah, but by name it was in Rajab, and this was because of the manipulations of those people through *nasi'*. Therefore God, by these commands, declared the practice of *nasi'* forbidden from then on. He also made clear that by this *nasi'* these people themselves were making months lawful or unlawful, and that this practice is contrary to the principles of the religion. The fundamental principle of the religion is that only God can determine the limits of the lawful and the unlawful. This is God's exclusive right, and to exercise this right and authority without God's permission is disbelief and polytheism. Indeed, this act is equivalent to going to the furthest limits of disbelief. In this way, through these verses, the doubts in people's hearts were removed, and at the same time the principle was made clear that in Islam the authority to determine the lawful and the unlawful in the system of life belongs solely and exclusively to God. This belief is connected with the great reality hidden within the order of this entire universe, which God has placed within this universe from the first day of creation. Thus, God's legislation for people is in fact based on the principle that God has placed in this universe. Therefore, for any person to undertake legislation for people is, in effect, to advance into disbelief and to lead others astray.

In this part of the verses, it is also intended to impress again the truth that was stated just before these verses: that the People of the Book are also polytheists, and that in terms of enmity and jihad (struggle in the way of God) they belong to the front of the polytheists. The command is that all of them be fought, that is, both the polytheists and the People of the Book. This is because all of them wage jihad and war against the people of Islam, and this conduct of theirs is established by the whole history of Islam. The words of the Qur'an are completely clear on this matter: the common goal of the People of the Book and the polytheists is that they are constantly engaged in battle against Islam and the Muslims. Whenever they face Islam and the Muslims, they forget the enmities among themselves, whether these differences concern mutual hostilities or beliefs and ideologies. Thus, to block the path of Islam, no obstacle remains before them, and they become united and agreed in order to uproot Islam.

The reality that the People of the Book are polytheists like the other polytheists, and that they fight against the Muslims just as the polytheists do, requires that the Muslims also fight against all these polytheists, whether they are from among the polytheist People of the Book or from among the polytheist Arabs. Furthermore, the practice of *nasi'* is an advanced form of disbelief, because, besides being a wrong act, it also involves an encroachment upon God's exclusive authority to legislate. Therefore, it is more than mere disbelief. This is the connection that links these verses with the preceding discussion, because the earlier verses mentioned the obstacles that stand in the way of going out for jihad, and it is clear that jihad was against both the People of the Book and the polytheists.

**Lesson No. 89: Explanation of the Verses**

**Verses 36 to 37**

﴿Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months in the Book of Allah since the day He created the heavens and the earth; of them four are sacred. That is the correct religion.﴾

This verse returns time to that standard and law, and the course of time is returned to the system according to which God created this universe. That is, the determination of time is in accordance with the creation of the universe. This verse also indicates that in this universe time operates by a most firm order, and that within this order the year has been divided into twelve months. No increase or decrease can be introduced into this firm order. This order of time and the cycle of the years is extremely precise, and it conforms to the law of nature according to which this universe was created. This system, order, or measure is so exact and firm that no increase or decrease can be made in it, because the course of time is carried out according to a most precise standard. It has been put into operation from the beginning of the creation of the universe, and it has never been suspended.

This firmness of the law of motion of time and space is brought in here so that people may be told that the determination of the limits of the lawful and the unlawful is based on this firm principle of the universe. Therefore, the determination of the lawful and the unlawful cannot be based merely on temporary desires and inclinations, nor can its movement be advanced or postponed, because this is an extremely serious matter.

*Dhalika al-din al-qayyim* ("That is the correct religion"). Therefore, this religion is in accordance with the firm order of the universe, and the firm order of the universe is that according to which this universe has been running since the first day, from the time God created it.

This is a short verse, yet within it God has placed an unending chain of meanings and implications. These meanings follow one another in succession. Some provide explanation and expansion for others, and some strengthen other meanings. All the scientific discoveries that modern humanity brings to light in this world through science, and which it continues to reveal through constant experimentation, are included within its meaning. In this way, there is a continuous confirmation of agreement between the principles of religion and the principles of the universe, and the principles of religion are firmly settling in minds in the modern age, and their foundations are being strengthened. All these implications have been comprehended within only twelve words, and these words, though apparently very ordinary and simple, are plain and easy to understand.

﴿So do not wrong yourselves during them.﴾ "Do not wrong yourselves during these four months."

During these four months, do not wrong one another, because this principle is linked to the principle upon which the universe has been organized. This principle is linked to the principle upon which the universe has been organized, and this great principle is that just as God is the Lawgiver of this universe, so too God is the one who sets the regulations for people. Therefore, violating these regulations is wrongdoing. So do not, by making these sacred months lawful for yourselves, take steps against peace and security. This would be opposition to God's will and purpose, and that opposition is wrongdoing. Do not, by committing such wrongdoing, make yourselves deserving of the punishment of this world and the Hereafter. Do not create anguish and turmoil within your society, and do not make this world the victim of a war that has no purpose and that contradicts peace and security.

﴿And fight against the polytheists all together, as they fight against you all together. And know that Allah is with those who are mindful of Him.﴾ "And fight the polytheists all together, just as they fight you all together, and know that God is with the God-conscious (*muttaqin*)."

This means that outside the sacred months, fighting is permitted, unless the polytheists attack you during the sacred months. If they commit aggression against you during the sacred months, you may defend yourselves in those months, because if a unilateral declaration of a ceasefire were made, then forces of good conduct would be left in a weak position, the forces of human virtue would be unable to confront the wicked, corruption and disorder would prevail in the world, and the world would fall under the dominance of anarchy. Therefore, resisting aggression during the sacred months is, in fact, also protecting the sanctity of those months, so that in the future they will be respected and no one will commit aggression against another.

﴿And fight the polytheists all together﴾ "Fight the polytheists all together, just as they fight you all together." This means that all of you fight against them, without exception, all of them without any exemption. No group is excluded from this command, because all of them fight against you, and none of them is excluded. Nor do they exempt any of you. Therefore, the battle of jihad is in reality a battle between the ideas of polytheism and monotheism (*tawhid*). It is a confrontation between faith and disbelief, and between guidance and misguidance. It is a clash between two blocs, between whom peace can never be established at any time, nor can complete agreement ever be reached between them, because this difference is not a temporary and partial difference, but a permanent and fundamental one. It is not a difference over interests that can be brought together in harmony, nor is it a dispute over a piece of land that could be divided and its boundaries fixed. If the Muslim community thinks that the war waged against it by disbelievers, People of the Book and idol-worshippers is a war over economics or a national war, that is its misunderstanding, or if someone explains it to it in that way, he is deceiving it. This struggle is not merely a struggle over homeland or policy; it is a comprehensive ideological struggle, and it is a struggle between the Islamic system and religion on one side and disbelief on the other. The outcome of this comprehensive struggle cannot be decided by justice or by the principle of give and take, nor can it be resolved through negotiations. Its solution lies only in the practice of jihad. It lies in continuous struggle and ceaseless action. This is the Sunnah (established way) of God, which cannot be averted in any way. It is the system and law upon which the order of the universe stands. The heavens and the earth are established and move on in accordance with this supreme order. The religions and ideologies of the world also move in accordance with this order. The system of the heart and the mind is also this same created order, and it has been established from the very day on which God created the heavens and the earth.

﴿And know that Allah is with those who are mindful of Him.﴾ "And know that God is with the God-conscious (*muttaqin*)." Therefore, success has been decreed for those God-conscious people who respect the limits of God, who declare unlawful what God has declared unlawful, and who do not deviate from God's laws. Thus, the law of nature is that the Muslims should not suspend, even for a moment, their practical jihad against the polytheists. They should not deviate from it, and in this continuous jihad they should not violate the limits of God, but should respect them, and they should continue the practice of jihad in accordance with all its rules and etiquette. In this jihad, their aim should be the pleasure of God, both in their hearts and openly. If they enter jihad in accordance with these principles, then victory will come to them, because in that case God will be with them, and when God is one's helper, there is no doubt about one's success.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 9, verse 37:

Hazrat Mujahid said: "A man from the tribe of Banu Kinanah would come every year during the Hajj season, mounted on his donkey, and make this announcement: 'O people! No one can find fault with me, and I am not thwarted. My word cannot be rejected. We have declared Muharram sacred and postponed Safar.' Then he would come the following year and say the same thing: 'We have declared Safar sacred and postponed Muharram.' And this is the meaning of: ﴿liyuwati'u 'iddata ma harrama Allah﴾ ('so that they may complete the number of the months Allah has made sacred'), that is, complete the number of the four months. In this way they would make the permitted months forbidden and the forbidden months permitted."

Abdul Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: this man was from Banu Kinanah, and this task was ... (?) for him. The custom of the Age of Ignorance (jahiliyyah) was that no tribe would raid another during the sacred months. Sometimes a person would come face to face with the killer of his father, yet would not lay a hand on him. If someone sought help from others for fighting during the sacred months, people would say, "Do you not see that it is a sacred month?" The one seeking help would then say, "In this very year we will postpone it." So in that year, instead of Muharram, there would be two Safars, and in the next year we would make two Muharrams. In this way they would act. And in the following year they would declare Safar sacred as well as Muharram. Thus two months would become sacred.

There are these two opinions in the interpretation of this verse, and these were the two forms of nasi' that were practised. In the first form, they would declare Safar sacred in place of Muharram and complete the number of four. But the four months that Allah had specifically designated as sacred would not be those exact months, because Muharram would not be among them. In the second form, one year three months would be sacred, and in another year five would be sacred, and thus the average of two years would come to the number eight. But even in this way, the sanctity of Muharram would be broken, and Safar would become sacred in its place.

In both of these forms, what is permitted would be made forbidden and what is forbidden would be made permitted, which was an act contrary to Islamic law. This was called ziyadah fi al-kufr (an increase in disbelief), because alongside doctrinal disbelief, they committed disbelief by independently legislating.

﴿yudallu bihi alladhina kafaru﴾ ("by which those who disbelieve are led astray"): they deceive, they make a game of the religion, and they engage in distortion and misinterpretation of the texts.

﴿zuyyina lahum su'u a'malihim﴾ ("their evil deeds have been made attractive to them"): the result is that they see evil as good, and they consider abusive speech to be ornament. In this way they do not even recognise misguidance as misguidance, and they keep advancing further in disbelieving deeds.

﴿wallahu la yahdi al-qawma al-kafirin﴾ ("and Allah does not guide the disbelieving people"): because they themselves have drawn veils over their hearts. They have abandoned reflecting upon the proofs of guidance. Therefore they have made themselves deserving that Allah leave them in the very state they are in.

Lesson No. 90: An Overview

This section apparently came down after the general call to mobilisation (hukm-e-nafeer-e-aam) on the occasion of the Battle of Tabuk. When the Messenger (ﷺ) learnt that the Romans had gathered on the borders of Syria, in the northern part of the Arabian Peninsula, and that Heraclius had provided his companions and soldiers with a year's rations, and that the tribes of Lakhm, Judhab, Amilah and Ghassan, who were northern Arab tribes, had joined these forces, and their vanguards had reached the place Balqa, then in these circumstances the Messenger (ﷺ) too ordered the Muslims to prepare for a general campaign. Whenever the Messenger (ﷺ) set out for a battle, he would, as a war stratagem, turn the preparations in another direction, so that no one knew where he would strike. But in the Battle of Tabuk he abandoned this principle, because it was a distant journey and the weather was extremely harsh. Therefore the Messenger (ﷺ) openly told them about this journey. The fierce heat was at its height, the shade was pleasant, the orchards were ripe, and staying at home was far more beloved to people than travelling. In these circumstances the weaknesses that we have described in detail in the introduction to this surah appeared in the Islamic society. In these circumstances the hypocrites too found an opportunity for their base conduct; they began a propaganda that the army should not be sent out in the heat. They began to describe the hardships of a long journey. They frightened people greatly with the might of the Romans. And the effect of this propaganda also fell upon the Islamic society. Accordingly, in this part of the verses, warning was given against all these matters.

Whether or not the Messenger (ﷺ) suffers any loss from your staying behind, you will in any case incur sin and commit a great failing.

﴿O you who believe, what is wrong with you that when you are told, "Go forth in the way of Allah," you cling heavily to the earth?﴾

All these are burdens of the earth: the greed of the earth, earthly notions, the fear of losing life, the fear of losing wealth, the fear of losing worldly pleasures and possessions, the fear of losing comfort, luxury, peace and tranquillity. They are the obstacles of attachment to perishable pleasures, to the transient and temporary aims of life, and to the brief life of this very earth. In short, all the obstacles relate to blood, flesh and dust. And all these obstacles are described by one extremely vivid word: "ithaqaltum". There is also a reading "thaqaltum" in it, but the common reading of Hafs is extremely effective. This word conveys the meaning of a body that is loosening to fall to the ground. People try with difficulty to lift it upwards, but it has become so heavy that it falls to the earth. "Ithaqaltum ila al-ard": through these words it is expressed that the earth is pulling it towards itself, whereas the demand of spiritual strength, impulse and longing is that it should rise upwards. The act of rising for jihad is in fact an act of freeing oneself from the gravitational pull of this earth. It is an act of freeing oneself from the defilements of flesh and skin found within the earth. It is an act of inspiring a person towards the spiritual world and the world of lofty aims. It is an act of freeing the human soul from the bondage of worldly confinement. It is an act of abandoning this temporary and brief life and entering into an everlasting and long life.

﴿Are you content with the life of this world instead of the Hereafter? But the enjoyment of the life of this world, compared with the Hereafter, is but little.﴾

If the followers of any creed or ideology hold back from jihad in the way of Allah, or do not fight for their ideology, there can be only one cause for this, and that is that there is a flaw and weakness in the ideology and belief of such people. This is why the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever dies without having fought, and without having even thought of fighting, dies upon a branch of hypocrisy." Whoever dies, having neither taken part in jihad nor ever had the thought of it cross his mind, dies upon one of the branches of hypocrisy. Thus, when hypocrisy enters a creed, it prevents it from elevation and perfection. It is hypocrisy that, by frightening a person with death and with poverty and hunger, holds him back from jihad, although death is in the hand of Allah and the provision of every person is in the hand of Allah. And it is also a reality that, compared with the Hereafter, the entire wealth and enjoyment of this life is but a little thing. This is why the following statement comes next.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 9, verse 39:

This address is directed to a specific group in a specific event. However, in its meaning it is general for every person of belief and ideology. The punishment with which they are being warned is not only the punishment of the Hereafter. It is also a worldly punishment. Those who shy away from struggle (jihad) and do not strive continuously for dominance and exaltation are deprived, and they are afflicted with the punishment of humiliation, because they are deprived of taking part in good works. And they leave this field empty for their enemies. It should be remembered that, as a consequence of abandoning the path of jihad fi sabilillah (struggle in the way of Allah) and the striving for Islam, the loss of life and property of ideological people occurs in the form of participation in jihad and fighting. The noble act of jihad demands a sacrifice from them, but in comparison, humiliation and a base existence demand from them a greater sacrifice. In short, whichever nation has abandoned the practice of jihad, humiliation is written into its destiny. It becomes a morsel for the enemy, and the enemy easily makes it a slave.

*Wa yastabdil qawman ghairakum* (﴿And He will replace you with another people﴾): "He will raise up another group in your place." This second group will be one that stands firmly upon its principles, will be a sacrifice for its honour and dignity, and will be one that achieves victory over the enemies of Allah.

*Wa la tadurruhu shay'a* (﴿And you will not harm Him at all﴾): "You will not harm Allah in the least." Then you will have no standing, neither in the first rank nor in the last rank.

*Wallahu 'ala kulli shay'in qadir* (﴿And Allah is over all things competent﴾): "Allah has power over all things." He is not incapable of destroying you, raising other nations in your place, and disregarding you and casting you into the corner of obscurity. The reality is that rising above worldly interests and overcoming the weaknesses of the human self is, in fact, attaining the station of nobility and honour. As a result, the highest life is bestowed, but to adopt humiliation and cling to the earth and to fear the enemy is a negation of dignity, nobility and the life of greatness. And according to Allah's standard, this is annihilation and humiliation, and the destruction of spiritual values.

Now Allah, the Exalted, mentions a historical event and presents it as an example. This example was within their knowledge. They knew how, at certain sensitive moments, the Hand of Power (Dast-e-Qadr) supported the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Islamic movement. In that, the individuals of the movement had no part. It was pure unseen assistance, and not a single person from among the Muhajirin and Ansar was present to render help at that time.

When the patience of the Quraysh with regard to the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) ran out. It is always the case that when rebellious powers do not attain success, their patience runs out and they resort to violence. Thus the Quraysh also began plotting violence against the Messenger (ﷺ). They decided to kill him and be rid of him. Allah informed the Messenger (ﷺ) of their secret plots and commanded him to leave Makkah now. Only Abu Bakr al-Siddiq was with him as a companion. He had neither an army nor military equipment. His enemies were spread everywhere and they were very powerful. Here, in the context of the discourse, this has been depicted in a most beautiful way.

ٳذْ هُمَا فِي الْغَارِ "When they were both in the cave," and the people were pursuing them. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq was extremely anxious. He was not worried about his own life; he was concerned for the Leader, lest they should find his traces and reach his beloved. It is said that if one of them had looked down from the place of his feet, we would have seen him beneath his feet. At that moment, the state of tranquility and steadfastness from Allah had descended upon the heart of the Messenger (ﷺ). He tried to reduce the fear of Siddiq Akbar and said: "Abu Bakr, what do you think of two men whose third companion is Allah?"

What was the result? The circumstances were such that on one side were all the material powers, while the Messenger and his lone companion were deprived of every kind of material power. Now the hosts of Allah came onto the field. No army or power of any kind was visible among them. In this plan the disbelievers were badly defeated and they were humiliated and left disgraced.

"And He made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest" (﴿وَجَعَلَ كَلِمَةَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا السُّفْلَىٰ﴾): and Allah brought down the word of the disbelievers, while the word of Allah remained exalted in its place, as it always remains exalted, strong, and has influence.

"And the word of Allah is the highest" (﴿وَكَلِمَةُ اللَّهِ هِيَ الْعُلْيَا﴾). According to some recitations, "wa kalimata Allah" is also read in the accusative (naṣb), but "wa kalimatu Allah" in the nominative (rafʻ) is stronger. In meaning, the statement becomes more forceful, because it carries the sense of emphasis and permanence. That is, the very nature and true position of the word of Allah is that it is exalted. Its exaltation is not confined to a single event or incident. Allah is Mighty, and His friends are never humiliated, and He is Most Forbearing. Therefore He devises a successful policy for His friends and has written success in their destiny.

This was an example of how Allah granted success to His Messenger and to His words, and Allah can repeat such examples; but this kind of help can only reach those who do not become lax and do not sit idle. If Muslims do not do so, Allah can bring other groups. This was a real and practical example, and to explain it there was no need for any great proof or logical argument.

In the atmosphere of this example and in the state of this profound impression, Allah now commands that all Muslims rise up in this campaign, not heeding any obstacle, and that no excuse stand in their way. Let them rise up, if they desire triumph and victory in this world and everlasting well-being in the Hereafter.

Go forth, whether light or heavy, and strive in the way of Allah with your wealth and your lives. That is better for you, if you knew. Go forth in every circumstance, give of your lives and your wealth, do not fabricate excuses or put forward pleas, and keep overcoming difficulties and obstacles.

﴿ذٰلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ اِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُوْنَ﴾: "That is better for you, if you know." Thus it happened: the sincere believers grasped these realities. They rose up despite all the obstacles and difficulties. They had excuses available, but they did not avail themselves of those excuses. So Allah opened the doors of the earth before them. Hearts of people also opened up to them, and through these sincere ones Allah raised high His word, and through the words of Allah He Himself elevated and distinguished them. And through their hands such feats came into being that even today they are a marvel of human history.

Abu Talhah (may Allah be pleased with him) was reciting Surah al-Tawbah, and when he reached this verse he said: "Our Lord has commanded us to go forth, whether we are old or young! Sons, prepare me." His sons said: "Father, may Allah have mercy on you, you fought alongside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until he passed away, you fought alongside Abu Bakr until he passed away, you fought alongside Umar until he passed away. Now we will fight on your behalf." But he paid no heed and went off on a naval vessel. At sea, death overtook him. The fleet could find no island on which to bury him. After nine days they found an island, and during those nine days his body had undergone no change. So they buried him on that island.

Ibn Jarir narrated with his chain of narrators from Abu Rashid al-Harrani, who said: "I met Miqdad ibn al-Aswad (may Allah be pleased with him), apart from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He was sitting on the coffin of a money-changer and intended to go for jihad. I said to him: 'Uncle, you are excused by Allah.' He replied: 'Surah al-Bu'uth (meaning al-Tawbah) has been revealed to us.'"

﴿اِنْفِرُوْا خِفَافًا وَّثِــقَالًا﴾ "Go forth, whether light or heavy." Habban ibn Zayd al-Shar'i narrated: "We went out on jihad with Safwan ibn Amr, who was the governor of Homs. We went towards the land of Jarajima. I saw an old man whose eyebrows had fallen over his eyes, who was from the people of Damascus, riding on a dung-heap. I turned to him and said: 'O uncle, you are excused by Allah.' That old man raised both his eyebrows and said: 'Nephew, Allah has required of us that we go forth in the way of Allah, whether light or heavy. Know this: whom Allah loves, He afflicts with hardships and then brings him back safe and sound; but Allah tests from among His servants only those who are patient, thankful, remember Him, and worship none other than Him.'"

This was the continuous struggle and jihad through which Allah spread Islam in the world, and through these servants of Allah all of humanity was brought out of servitude to other humans and entered into the worship of Allah alone. And in the ebb and flow of Islamic history there occurred a miracle for which there is no parallel in human history.

Lesson 91: Commentary on Verses 42 to 91

From this point the commentary turns to those who showed weakness and shortcoming on this occasion. This whole lesson also identifies the hypocrites who had entered the ranks of the Muslims in the name of Islam, especially after Islam had become dominant, and whose safety and worldly interests required that they submit before Islam and enter its ranks, plotting against it from within, since the apparent circumstances had become such that they could do nothing against Islam while standing outside it.

In this lesson, all the conditions that we indicated in the introduction to this surah will come before us, and the situation will be portrayed in the words of the Qur'an. In the light of the fundamental discussion we presented at the beginning of the surah, it will not be very difficult to understand these texts, as we have said earlier:

لَوْ كَانَ عَرَضًا قَرِيْبًا وَّسَفَرًا: If this matter had been one of worldly gain, and that gain had been easily attainable, or if it had been a short and profitable journey whose results were certain, these people would certainly have joined you. But this journey is a long one, laborious and discouraging. Weak resolve and feeble-willed people fail to muster the courage. This journey is towards a great and lofty goal, at the sight of which souls of weak spirit become frightened, the faint-hearted tremble, and the base-minded fall behind. This expedition was in fact an exemplary expedition, and such expeditions in the history of humanity have always held an exemplary status and provide proud narratives and traditions for any nation.

﴿Had it been a near advantage and a moderate journey, they would have followed you, but the distance seemed long to them﴾: O Prophet, if the benefit were easily obtainable and the journey light, they would certainly have been ready to follow you, but for them this path has become too arduous.

When the station of honour and high rank can be reached with ease, a great number of aspirants come forward. But when the road is rough and difficult, a large number of people turn away and, because of the hardships of the road, fall behind the army, having before them a most worthless and unreal aim of the world. In every era and every age such people are found in abundance and become well known. Such people are not rare or exceptional; rather, they are found in great numbers in every age. Yet these people, at the edge of life, are residents of a worthless station. Although in their own conceit they think that they have obtained their interests, that they have attained high worldly aims, and that they have escaped giving high sacrifices for any cause, they do not know that whoever pays a greater price will be given a station commensurate with that price. Even in this world, a person receives only that for which he pays.

﴿They will swear by Allah, "Had we been able, we would certainly have gone out with you"﴾: This is the false excuse that weak people always put forward. Those who present excuses are often liars. Although those who present excuses may appear strong and brave outwardly, in reality they are people of a weak kind. The brave is one who faces difficulties, and the weak is one who turns away. This is a principle admitting no exception, and it remains in force always.

﴿They destroy themselves﴾: By telling lies and swearing false oaths, they think they have become successful in the eyes of people, whereas the reality is known only to Allah, that they are not successful. Allah can also expose their reality before people. Therefore these people will be worthless in this world because of their false excuses, and in the Hereafter as well, since in the Hereafter no pretext will avail.

﴿And Allah knows that they are liars﴾.

May Allah pardon you, O Messenger! Why did you grant them permission before it became clear to you who were truthful and who were liars?

Allah the Exalted is so merciful to His Messenger that He announces the pardon even before the rebuke. When those people presented false excuses, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) accepted their excuses, and such people hid themselves behind those excuses. The Messenger (ﷺ) accepted the excuses of these people because at that time there was no occasion to investigate which excuses were true and which were false. It was also possible that some people would stay behind from the army without any excuse at all, and in this way their true condition would become evident, and they would have no pretext of the Messenger's permission either.

Since the Messenger (ﷺ) had not disclosed the hypocrisy of the hypocrites, Allah here set out principles and attributes through which the hypocrites could be well recognised. And these attributes are to be distinguishing marks between the believers and the hypocrites.

﴿لَا يَسْتَاْذِنُكَ الَّذِيْنَ يُؤْمِنُوْنَ﴾ etc.: Those who believe in Allah and the Last Day would never ask you to excuse them from striving with their wealth and their lives. Allah knows well the God-fearing.

﴿اِنَّمَا يَسْـتَاْذِنُكَ الَّذِيْنَ لَا يُؤْمِنُوْنَ﴾: Such requests are made only by those who do not believe in Allah and the Last Day, whose hearts harbour doubt, and who are wavering in their doubt.

This is a principle that never fails. Those who truly come to believe in Allah, and who are certain that one day they will have to stand before Allah, do not wait for permission to stay back from jihad. Whenever they are called to sacrifice their lives and wealth in the way of Allah, they do not hesitate even for a moment. Rather, whether the call is light or burdensome, they rush towards it, obey the commander, and are certain that they are going to meet Allah. They are certain that He will give them their full reward and be pleased with them. They are so eager for jihad that they rise up for this deed of their own accord, and there is no need for anyone to stir them up to it; presenting excuses to stay back from jihad is an even greater matter. It is only those whose hearts have become empty of the wealth of faith and certainty who present excuses. Such people hesitate, seek out pretexts, take leave, and say that there are obstacles in their path to fulfilling the demands of the creed they have professed. In reality, they are sick with doubt and wavering.

The path that leads to Allah is clear and perfectly straight. Only one who is deprived of the wealth of certainty can hesitate and waver in this matter, or one who knows well that the Messenger is true, yet, because of his personal weaknesses, is frightened by the difficulties of the path.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 9, verse 46:

Those who stayed behind on that occasion had the capacity to wage war. They had the means of travel and the equipment were also available.

﴿And if they had really intended to go forth, they would have made some preparation for it﴾: "If they had truly intended to set out, they would have made some preparation for it." The leaders of such people were Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, and Jadd ibn Qays was also among such people. They were among the notables of their tribes, influential and wealthy.

﴿But Allah disliked their being sent forth, so He held them back, and it was said, "Sit with those who sit"﴾: "But Allah did not like their rising up, so He made them sluggish, and it was said, 'Remain sitting with those who remain sitting.'"

Allah knew the temperament of these people and their hypocrisy, and the hatred and enmity they harboured against the Muslims in their hearts, the mention of which comes up later. Therefore Allah caused them to be kept back on that occasion and took away their very resolve. These people sat down with their homes and women. Together with the children and the destitute, they stayed behind, those who truly lacked the strength and means to go with that army. Therefore, it was better for those of low resolve and weak conviction to remain seated and be deprived of that honour. And in this there was good for the Islamic call.

Weak-hearted and cowardly commanders make the army weak-hearted and cowardly, and treacherous leaders make the entire society treacherous. Even if these hypocrites had joined the Muslims as companions, they would have created restlessness, discouragement and disorder within the ranks, and would have produced sedition, discord and desertion within the Islamic army. This is because there were also people among the Muslims who had social ties with those former leaders, and the Muslims still lent their ears to these people's words. But Allah Himself was the guardian of His own call, and He was overseeing the protection of the callers under His own watch. Allah protected the believers from sedition in such a way that the hypocrites and the base remained only as they were.

﴿وَاللّٰهُ عَلِيْمٌۢ بِالظّٰلِمِيْنَ﴾: "And Allah is All-Knowing of the wrongdoers." Here "the wrongdoers" refers to the polytheists. Allah has placed the people under discussion in the category of the polytheists as well. Their past is a witness to what is in their hearts, and their history bears testimony to their evil nature. It was these very people who blocked the way of the Messenger of Allah, and in opposition to the Islamic movement they did whatever was within their power. But when the Islamic movement prevailed, they submitted, though the disease of hypocrisy remained in their hearts.

This event took place when the Messenger ﷺ arrived in Madinah with the support of the public, and the situation was such that he had not yet gained a decisive victory over his enemies. In Madinah, as success continued to come to the Prophet ﷺ, these enemies also bowed their heads, but in their hearts they continued to dislike the new movement, and they waited for some hard time to befall Islam so that they would get an opportunity for their intrigues.

Now the Qur'an turns to the various categories of these people and addresses their fabricated excuses. It is explained what kinds of enmity and hatred lie in their hearts against the Messenger of Allah, and how much malice they harbour against the Muslims.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrates from al-Zuhri and others that one day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was busy in preparations for jihad (on the occasion of Tabuk), and he said to Jadd ibn Qays, a brother of Banu Salima: "Jadd, are you interested in fighting against Banu al-Asfar (the Romans)?" He replied: "O Messenger of Allah, grant me permission and do not put me to trial. By Allah, my people well know that there is no one more fond of women than me, and I fear that if I see the women of Banu al-Asfar (the Romans), I will not be able to restrain myself." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned away from him and said: "I have granted you permission." Then this verse was revealed concerning this Jadd ibn Qays.

All the hypocrites presented this same kind of excuse, and Allah gave them this same answer: ﴿And among them is one who says, "Grant me permission and do not put me into temptation." Unquestionably, into temptation they have fallen. And indeed, Hell encompasses the disbelievers.﴾ The depiction is as though Hell is a trial, and these people keep falling into it. Hell surrounds them from every side, and all the paths of escape for them have been closed; the only path left open is toward Hell, and these people keep going and falling into it. This manner of expression is a metaphor indicating that by remaining behind they have committed a great error, and now the punishment of Hell is certain for them. This recompense has been decreed for them because of their staying behind from jihad, adopting a base position, and presenting flimsy excuses. It also points to the fact that although these people outwardly profess Islam, in reality they are hypocrites and worse than the disbelievers.

The condition of these people is that they wish no good for the Messenger of Allah and the Muslims, and they are deeply distressed that the Messenger of Allah and the Muslims should attain any superiority. If a calamity befalls the Muslims, they rejoice, and they say: "We had already taken our precautions beforehand, so we escaped, and we were not made to suffer these difficulties," and they celebrate in their own place.

But these people are very lacking in understanding; their attention is fixed only on outward matters. They think that calamities are evil in every circumstance, and they think that by sitting in their houses and staying behind from jihad they have gained good. Yet in their hearts obedience to Allah has not remained, and they have lost the great aim of seeking the pleasure of Allah. In truth, their good lay in submission and contentment and in jihad. A true Muslim is one who strives in the way of Allah, moves forward, and does not fear, because his belief is that good and evil both come from Allah, and Allah alone is the Helper and the Supporter.

And God has decreed victory for the believers and has promised them ultimate triumph. Whatever difficulties they face, however severe the trials they meet, they should know that in the end victory will be theirs. These difficulties are a prelude to that victory, so that when the Muslims attain it, it will be evident that they deserve it. They also serve to purify their ranks, and this victory and support come through worldly means and resources, after hardships, so that the Muslims will feel its worth. This victory is attained through the great sacrifices of people of high resolve. It is achieved after trials, and people must have offered sacrifices for it.

Since the true Helper and Supporter is Allah, Muslims always place their trust in Him and not in their own sacrifices: ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾. However, belief in Allah's decree and trust in Him do not preclude a person from preparing for a task and gathering the necessary means. For this reason, God's explicit command regarding jihad is: ﴿Prepare against them whatever you can of power﴾, that is, prepare against the enemies as much strength as is within your capacity. Anyone who does not implement the commands of Allah cannot be considered to be a person of tawakkul (reliance on God). The saying goes: "Trust in God, but tie your camel." Whoever does not provide the means in accordance with the command of Allah fails to comprehend the sunnah (divine way) of Allah, which operates throughout this universe. This sunnah is immutable and makes no exceptions for anyone.

For the believer, every situation is a gain: if he is granted victory, he succeeds, and if he attains martyrdom, he also succeeds. As for the disbeliever, he fails in every way. If he is punished in this world at the hands of the Muslims and is then cast into Hell, he has failed; and if he dies a natural death and is then cast into Hell, he has failed as well.

Say (to them): "What are you awaiting concerning us except one of the two best things (ḥusnayayn)? And what we await concerning you is that Allah will afflict you with a punishment from Himself, or at our hands. So wait; indeed we are waiting along with you."

Why would the hypocrites await anything concerning the Muslims? The Muslims always hope for good and success. Either they will be victorious, and Allah's word will be raised high, and this triumph belongs to this world; or they will be granted martyrdom, and the martyr attains lofty ranks. Yes, let the believers certainly wait to see what the end of the hypocrites will be. They will be afflicted with punishment in the same way that all the deniers (mukadhdhibin) were afflicted with punishment, namely in the Hereafter; or it will happen that they will be seized in this very world, just as all the people of falsehood (ahl al-batil) are seized. Therefore, the end of both groups is well known and renowned.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 9, verses 53–54:

Among those who stayed behind and those who waited, there were some who offered their financial contribution, but who expressed inability to take part personally in jihad. They adopted this attitude so that they would neither be disgraced nor be counted fully on either side, neither with one party nor with the other. Therefore Allah commanded His Messenger ﷺ to reject the financial contributions of such people, because they offered their monetary support out of fear and for show. Their spending was not the result of the demands of faith or of trust in Allah. Whether they were doing this for show, deceiving the believers, or doing it out of fear of the polytheists, in both cases their act is rejected by Allah, and it has no reward with Allah.

The characteristics of the hypocrites are the same in every age. They are always in fear and turmoil. Their hearts are empty, and their conscience and thinking are devoid of composure. There is no spirit of reality in their outward displays, and their outward appearance is completely separate from their inner state.

Consider the manner of expression of the Qur'an: ﴿wa la ya'tunas-salata illa wahum kusala﴾ (they do not come to prayer except in a lazy and reluctant state). They perform prayer for show. Outwardly it is a prayer, but within them there is no spirit of prayer. They do not perform the prayer correctly and with steadfastness, because the feeling that compels one to pray is not in their hearts and inner selves; rather, they are driven towards it under the pressure of some external causes. Therefore they feel that they are being forced to do this act. In this way, whatever they spend in the way of Allah, they also spend only for the sake of show. This is why these are not accepted by Allah, since Allah does not accept any act of worship that does not result from sincere feeling and conscious faith. So the criterion is that the deed be good and be done with a good intention.

Therefore Allah commanded His Messenger ﷺ to reject the financial contributions of such people, because they offered their monetary support out of fear and for show. Their spending was not the result of the demands of faith or of trust in Allah. Whether they were doing this for show, deceiving the believers, or doing it out of fear of the polytheists, in both cases their act is rejected by Allah, and it has no reward with Allah.

The characteristics of the hypocrites are the same in every age. They are always in fear and turmoil. Their hearts are empty, and their conscience and thinking are devoid of composure. There is no spirit of reality in their outward displays, and their outward appearance is completely separate from their inner state.

Consider the manner of expression of the Qur'an: ﴿wa la ya'tunas-salata illa wahum kusala﴾ (they do not come to prayer except in a lazy and reluctant state). They perform prayer for show. Outwardly it is a prayer, but within them there is no spirit of prayer. They do not perform the prayer correctly and with steadfastness, because the feeling that compels one to pray is not in their hearts and inner selves; rather, they are driven towards it under the pressure of some external causes. Therefore they feel that they are being forced to do this act. In this way, whatever they spend in the way of Allah, they also spend only for the sake of show. This is why these are not accepted by Allah, since Allah does not accept any act of worship that does not result from sincere feeling and conscious faith. So the criterion is that the deed be good and be done with a good intention.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 9, verse 55:

These hypocrites were people of wealth and children, yet they disliked jihad and were influential people. But in the sight of Allah, wealth and riches and status have no value. Therefore, in the sight of the Messenger and the believers too, wealth and riches and status should have no importance. For these things are not such blessings from Allah that they enjoy through them and face no accountability; rather, they are a trial and a test. For this they will be held to account and will be punished.

Wealth and children are sometimes a blessing, with which Allah bestows favour upon some of His servants, and then grants them the ability to give thanks for it, and to use this power for the reform of the earth. Through it they turn towards Allah, and thus their conscience is at peace. There is tranquillity and contentment in their soul, and they have full and complete certainty of their end, a good end. Their conduct is such that they spend in the way of Allah with utmost sincerity, gather provision for the Hereafter, and when they suffer a loss of wealth or life, they still regard it as coming from Allah and hope for the mercy of Allah. And these same wealth and children are sometimes a punishment from Allah, and Allah gives this punishment to some of His servants in this very world. So these possessions and children become a cause of anguish and torment for them, and because of this anguish and distress, they are in hell, and in order to increase their wealth further, their nights' sleep is ended and they become nervously paralysed. Now the spending of wealth appears to them to be equal to its destruction. If their child is ill, they still fret, and if the child is healthy, even then it is a cause of torment for them. There are countless such people for whom their own children become a burden to their lives.

People of this kind existed in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They still exist now and will always exist. They will have wealth, they will have children, and people will be impressed by their outward position, but in reality all of this will be a punishment for them: a punishment in this world, and because Allah is well aware of their inner state and their end, they are poised for hell. Thus, their death is delayed only until they die in a state of disbelief. As soon as they give up their life, they are cast into hell.

The Qur'anic expression "wa tazhaq anfusuhum" (and their souls will depart while they are disbelievers) gives the impression that these people are, psychologically, in a state of ruin and destruction. Their condition is such that they are deprived of the wealth of tranquillity, composure and contentment. Therefore, just as they will be in severe punishment in the Hereafter, so too this world is no less than hell for them. Thus, in effect, they will be in punishment in both this world and the Hereafter. And of such wealth and such children, it is clear that no sensible person would desire one in which there is nothing but punishment hidden.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 9, verses 56–57:

Such hypocrites were creating a place for themselves within the ranks of the Muslims. They were not sitting in the Muslim ranks because of their beliefs and their faith; rather, they were afflicted with the disease of hypocrisy, and out of fear they would also echo the words of the Muslims. They expressed faith for the sake of some of their interests and views. But this Surah has exposed their inner selves. For this reason it is also called "al-Kashifah" (the Revealer) and "al-Fadihah" (the Disgracer). It has torn away the veil from the hypocrites and thoroughly humiliated them.

﴿And they swear by Allah that they are surely of you; but they are not of you, but they are a people who are frightened.﴾ "They swear by Allah that they are surely of you, while in truth they are by no means of you. Rather, they are people who fear you. These are utter cowards, and the manner of expression is such that these people appear before us as visibly fleeing and cowering. Flight is in their souls and hearts. Flight and fear are in their demeanour.

﴿If they could find a refuge, or caves, or a place to enter, they would turn towards it at full speed﴾ "If they find a place of refuge, or a cave, or a hiding place, they would run off and hide in it." They are always searching for a place to hide and for a place of safety: a fortified place, a cave, or a cellar. They are in a state of fear and flight, as though some unseen force or sudden calamity were pursuing them. They are spiritually defeated and cowardly.

﴿And they swear by Allah that they are surely of you; but they are not of you﴾ "They swear by Allah that they are surely of you." They take oaths with great emphasis so that they may conceal the matters that are in their hearts, so that these do not become revealed, and so that their lives and property remain safe. Their condition is most pitiable. They are immersed in cowardice, hypocrisy and flattery, and the Qur'an employs such methods to describe them. It is a remarkable portrayal through which their secret mysteries are, as it were, X-rayed, and this in an extremely effective manner.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 9, verses 56–57:

Such hypocrites were creating a place for themselves within the ranks of the Muslims. They were not sitting in the Muslim ranks because of their beliefs and their faith; rather, they were afflicted with the disease of hypocrisy, and out of fear they would also echo the words of the Muslims. They take oaths with great emphasis so that they may conceal the matters that are in their hearts, so that these do not become revealed, and so that their lives and property remain safe.
