The first group are those whose excuses are genuine. Therefore they were granted permission, and they remained behind out of compulsion. As for the second group, they remained without any excuse, because they presented false excuses to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Among them, those who committed disbelief will be afflicted with a painful punishment. However, regarding those who repented, there is no mention here of what their end will be.

In the end it is explained that the order to march out with this army was not a blind, arbitrary command; rather, the weak and the disabled were taken into account. For Islam is a reasonable religion of ease. In it no one is required to do more than his capacity allows. Therefore the disabled will not be held to account.

Those who are weak, elderly, and disabled, and who remain behind, are not held to account. The sick who, for a temporary reason, could not take part in this expedition are not worthy of blame. Those too who have no mount and no provisions for the journey are regarded as excused. If such people remained away from the field of battle, what fault is it of theirs? But their hearts, their consciences and their feelings are with Allah and His Messenger. These people have concealed nothing and do not deceive; while remaining in Madinah they carry out guarding, sentry duty, and the other services of the Abode of Islam that are beneficial and necessary for the Islamic state. Such people, though excused, are also doers of good; they will not be held to account, nor will they be worthy of blame.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 9, verse 92:

In this way, those who had fighting strength but no mount will also be excused, those who could not set out on that long journey on foot. Such people were left behind out of compulsion, yet their hearts were breaking and tears were flowing from their eyes, because they were being deprived of this honour out of necessity.

How fine a portrayal this is of the true longing for jihad. In what beautiful words has the inner grief and sorrow been expressed. This verse depicts some practical incidents from the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Various narrations mention various devoted companions of Islam, but all of them are the correct referents of this verse.

﴿Nor is there blame upon those who came to you that you might provide them with mounts; you said, "I cannot find anything to mount you on." They turned back while their eyes overflowed with tears out of grief that they could not find anything to spend.﴾ Translation: "Likewise, there is no cause for objection against those people who themselves came to you asking that mounts be arranged for them, and when you said that you could not arrange mounts for you, they returned out of compulsion, and their condition was that tears were flowing from their eyes, and they were greatly grieved that they lacked the means to take part in jihad at their own expense."

Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas: "The Messenger of Allah ordered that people should rise up to go with him for jihad. A group came to him, among whom was Abdullah ibn Mughaffal ibn Muqarrin al-Muzani. They demanded, 'O Messenger of God, grant us mounts,' and the Messenger replied, 'By God, I have nothing with which I can arrange mounts for you.' These people returned, and tears were flowing from their eyes. It was very burdensome for them that they should be left behind from jihad, but they had no provision and no mount. When Allah saw how much love they had for Allah and His Messenger, this verse was revealed in their honour."

Mujahid says that it was revealed concerning the Banu Muqarrin of Muzaynah. Muhammad ibn Ka'b says that it was revealed concerning seven men: Salim ibn Awf from Banu Amr ibn Awf, Hirmi ibn Amr from Banu Waqif, from Banu Mazin ibn Najjar, Abdul Rahman ibn Ka'b, whose kunya was Abu Ya'la, from Banu Mu'alla Fadl Allah, from Banu Salamah Amr ibn Attamah, and Abdullah ibn Amr al-Muzani.

Ibn Ishaq, in relating the events of the Battle of Tabuk, said: "After this, some of the Muslims came to the Messenger of Allah. These people were among the Ansar and others. From Banu Amr ibn Awf: Salim ibn Umayr and Ulba ibn Zayd, brother of Banu Harithah, and Abu Ya'la Abdul Rahman ibn Ka'b, brother of Banu Mazin, and Amr ibn Hammam ibn Jamuh, brother of Banu Salamah, Abdullah ibn Mughall al-Muzani; some have identified him as Abdullah ibn Amr al-Muzani. Hirmi ibn Abdullah, brother of Banu Waqif, and Iyad ibn Sariyah al-Fazari. These people asked the Messenger of Allah for a mount, and since they were in fact poor, he said that he had nothing with which he could arrange mounts for them. They returned, and their condition was that tears were flowing from their eyes. On not receiving a mount, these people were grieved."

This was the spirit and passion because of which Islam prevailed, and through these sacrifices the banner of Islam was raised high. We should reflect on how our condition compares with these people. We should examine our own zeal for Islam. If we find any weakness in ourselves, we should raise our hands in supplication before Allah that He remove this weakness, and fill us with the spirit of Islamic jihad in the manner in which the Companions of the Messenger of Allah were. And Allah is the One whose help is sought.

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb, *Fi Zilal al-Quran* (Urdu translation), on Surah 9, verses 93–96 (Part 1 of 3)**

**Verses 93 to 96, Juz' 11 (Para 11) at a Glance**

This juz' (one of the thirty parts of the Qur'an) consists of the remaining portion of Surah al-Tawbah and the beginning of Surah Yunus. Most of Surah al-Tawbah was covered in juz' 10. Here we will comment on the remaining portion of Surah al-Tawbah, and the commentary on Surah Yunus will begin at its start, God willing.

When we discussed Surah al-Tawbah, we made a few key points: its subject and the nature of its themes; the circumstances in which it was revealed; its significance in determining the nature of the international relations of the Islamic society and state with other societies and states; and the method of revolutionary movement for establishing the Islamic system that can be understood from this Surah. Therefore, repeating these important points here will not be without benefit.

This is a Madinan surah, and it contains glimpses of the final period of the Qur'an's revelation. Although it cannot be called the last Qur'an, it contains final glimpses because in it the rules of international relations between the Muslim community and the other nations of the world are given their final form. Moreover, within it, the formation of the Islamic society itself, the determination of its values, the determination of the worth of its various classes, and, in general, the basic features of an Islamic society are described. It presents a very deep portrayal of all the classes that exist in it and their qualities.

From this perspective, this Surah al-Tawbah is of great importance, because in it the features of the revolutionary process of the method for establishing the Islamic system, and all its stages, are described in great detail and with precision. On this subject, final and definitive rulings are given in this Surah. This review shows how solid and how decisive this method is. Without this overall review, the true picture of the commands and principles of the Shari'ah does not emerge. If the verses are viewed in isolation from their context without this overall review, the rulings that were revealed for an interim period will appear as permanent and final rulings. Then whoever wishes may interpret these final verses and instructions so that they conform to and align with the rulings meant for the interim period. Especially on the subject of jihad, such efforts have been made in practice, and the same attitude was adopted regarding the relations between the Islamic society and other jahili (pre-Islamic ignorance-based) societies.

In the introduction to this Surah, we pointed out that although the subject of this Surah is one and it was revealed in similar circumstances, it has several parts, and in each part final and definitive rulings are stated.

The first part of it sets the boundaries of the international relations between a Muslim society and other jahili societies and states, while the second part sets the boundaries of relations between the Muslims and the People of the Book. The third part comments on the situation of those who were invited to take part in the Battle of Tabuk and who showed negligence and laziness in fulfilling this duty. That battle was against the People of the Book who lived on the western edge of the Arabian Peninsula and who were preparing to strike a decisive blow against the new Islamic state. In the fourth part, the conspiracies and misdeeds of the hypocrites living in the Islamic society were exposed. Their psychology and practical conditions are portrayed. Moreover, by recording their attitude before the Battle of Tabuk, during it, and after it, their true intentions, their deceptions, and the weak excuses they presented for not taking part in the Battle of Tabuk were unveiled. Furthermore, the mischief they spread within the Islamic ranks, the corruption they caused, the discord they sowed, and the torment they inflicted upon the Messenger (ﷺ) and the sincere believers are all recorded in it. Along with this, the believers were warned about their conduct, the nature of social relations between the believers and the hypocrites was defined, and it was stated that they should be socially boycotted, so that each group would be distinguished by its own qualities.

…

These four parts, with their subjects, have already passed in juz' 10. However, some subjects from the last part, concerning those who were left behind from the battle, and the punishment and fate of those who stayed behind from jihad, have come into this section.

The last verse of the tenth juz' was this:

﴿There is no blame upon the weak, nor upon the sick, nor upon those who find nothing to spend, if they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger. There is no cause for censure upon the good-doers. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. Nor is there blame upon those who came to you asking to be provided with mounts, and you said, "I cannot find anything to mount you on." They turned away while their eyes overflowed with tears out of grief that they could not find the means to spend.﴾

The supplement with which this juz' begins is this:

﴿The blame is only upon those who ask your permission while they are rich. They have consented to be with those left behind, and Allah has sealed their hearts, so they do not know. They will make excuses to you when you return to them. Say, "Do not make excuses; we will not believe you. Allah has already informed us of your news. Allah will see your deeds, and so will His Messenger. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do." They will swear by Allah to you when you return to them, so that you may turn away from them. So turn away from them; indeed they are filth, and their refuge is Hell, as recompense for what they used to earn. They swear to you so that you may be pleased with them. But even if you are pleased with them, indeed Allah is not pleased with a defiant people.﴾

These were the reports from Allah that He gave to the Prophet (ﷺ) about the excuses that those left behind would present upon the return to Madinah. It is made clear here what you should do with those who stayed behind when you return safe and sound.

…

After this, the fifth part of the Surah comes. It explains what elements were present in the formation of the Islamic society, that is, what kinds of elements had gathered into the Islamic ranks from the conquest of Makkah until the Battle of Tabuk. As we clarified in the initial commentary on this Surah, there were, on the one hand, those who were the foremost early Muslims (al-sabiqun al-awwalun), who were the backbone of the Islamic society, and upon whom the collective system of Islam was founded. However, alongside them, other groups had also gathered into the Islamic ranks. There were the a'rab (Bedouin Arabs), among whom were both sincere people and self-interested hypocrites. Among the people of Madinah too, there was a large group of hypocrites. There were some people whose actions were good, but some of whose statements were contrary to the Shari'ah. These people had not yet fully taken the shape of the Islamic mould, nor were they completely colored by the Islamic hue. And there were some people about whom it could not be said what kind of people they were; their matter was left to Allah. Some were secret conspirators who did everything under the cover of Islam, who prepared plots, and who had contacts with the external enemies of Islam.

The Qur'anic verses have alluded to these people with great brevity, and it has been stated how all these various kinds of people are to be treated in the Islamic system of government. In this section, Allah has given instructions to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and to the sincere Muslims about what they should do with these classes and how they should deal with them. Let us consider some verses:

﴿The Bedouins are most severe in disbelief and hypocrisy and most likely not to know the limits of what Allah has revealed to His Messenger. And Allah is Knowing and Wise. Among the Bedouins are those who consider what they spend as a fine, and they wait for misfortunes to befall you. Upon them is the misfortune of evil. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing. But among the Bedouins are those who believe in Allah and the Last Day and consider what they spend as means of nearness to Allah and as prayers of the Messenger. Unquestionably, it is a means of nearness for them. Allah will admit them into His mercy. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

These Bedouins are more severe in disbelief and hypocrisy, and there is a greater likelihood that they will remain ignorant of the limits of this religion that Allah has revealed to His Messenger. Allah is All-Knowing and All-Wise. Among these Bedouins are people who, when they spend, consider it a forced penalty upon themselves. They await the turns of fortune against you, although the cycle of evil is itself upon them. Allah hears and knows everything. And among these same Bedouins are some who believe in Allah and the Last Day and who regard what they spend as a means of nearness to Allah and as the prayers of the Messenger. Indeed, it is certainly a means of nearness for them. Allah will certainly admit them into His mercy. Surely, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.

﴿As for the foremost, the first of the Emigrants and the Helpers, and those who followed them with good conduct, Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. And He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great success.﴾

Those Emigrants and Helpers who were first to respond to the call of faith, and also those who afterwards followed them in righteousness, Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. Allah has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, and they will abide therein forever. This is the great achievement.

﴿Among those around you of the Bedouins are hypocrites, and among the people of Madinah are those who have become adept at hypocrisy. You do not know them; We know them. We will punish them twice; then they will be returned to a great punishment.﴾

Among the Bedouins who live around you are many hypocrites, and among the residents of Madinah too there are hypocrites who have become masters of hypocrisy. You do not know them; We know them. The time is near when We will punish them twice. Then they will be returned to a great punishment.

﴿And others have acknowledged their sins; they had mixed a righteous deed with another that was bad. Perhaps Allah will accept their repentance. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow, and invoke blessings upon them. Indeed, your invocation is a comfort for them, and Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾

And there are others who have confessed their sins. They have mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil. It is not far that Allah will again turn towards them with mercy, for He is Forgiving and Merciful. O Prophet, take from their wealth a charity to purify and cleanse them, and pray for them, for your prayer is a source of tranquility for them. Allah is Hearing and Knowing.

﴿And there are others whose matter is held in abeyance until the command of Allah: He will either punish them or turn to them in forgiveness. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.﴾

And there are other people whose matter has been left pending by the command of Allah. Either He will punish them or He will turn to them again. Allah is All-Knowing and All-Wise.

Now, after this brief explanation, we come to the detailed explanation of the verses.

**Lesson No. 92: Explanation of the Verses**

**Verses 93 to 96:**

There is no blame upon the weak, the sick and the poor, nor should they feel any shortcoming in their hearts. As for those who have neither provisions for the journey nor a mount, the Holy Prophet (ﷺ) or the Islamic state also cannot provide them with what is needed to reach the battlefield. The blame falls upon those who ask the Prophet (ﷺ) for leave while they are able to eat and drink, are strong and robust, and have no genuine excuse. These people are deserving of severe blame, because although they had the ability to participate in jihad, they preferred to sit with the women who stayed behind and to indulge in comfort in their homes.

Why are these people being held to account? Because they remained behind from the army of Islam, because they sought leave on false excuses, because they broke their covenant, and because Allah had made them wealthy but they did not fulfill the rights of that wealth. Allah granted them the Islamic system, but they did not discharge their duty toward the Islamic system. Islam gave them protection and honour, yet they did not discharge their duty toward that society, even though that society had also honoured them and granted them dignity. For this reason, Allah employed against them this shameful group:

﴿They were content to be with those who stay behind.﴾ That is, they chose to be among the women who remain at home. This is the utmost in low aspiration and weakness, and it is the acceptance of a humiliating position, in which a person in a place of courage and manhood sits down without excuse with the weak, the women and the children, remains at home, and joins the ranks of the unjustly excused, while it is plainly evident that he is not disabled.

﴿And Allah has sealed their hearts, so they do not know.﴾ That is, they do not understand what the outcome of their conduct will be before Allah.

This position they adopted because Allah closed the doors of knowledge and awareness upon them, and the faculties of their understanding and perception were rendered inoperative. This is because they themselves chose dullness, dimness of mind and humiliation for themselves. They deprived themselves of being alive, dynamic and active, and within them the spirit of advancing, of daring and of being assertive disappeared. Whenever a person in this world becomes comfort-seeking, ease-loving and dull-witted, he is deprived of the desire for discovery, the desire for experience and the desire for knowledge, and he becomes like a useless limb in his society, which can neither influence anyone nor accept any good influence from another, and is also deprived of self-expression.

Luxury, ease and the love of safety are a disease that closes the doors of consciousness and awareness upon a person. The power of human understanding and perception dies, whereas movement and advancement are the sign of life. Movement is the primary cause of life. By challenging difficulties, certain aspects of the human soul and human intellect are brought to light. A person's nerves become strong, and those hidden powers emerge which always come into being at times of danger and defend, and which motivate human powers toward action and toward answering a call. All these aspects are different dimensions of knowledge and perception, and those who choose humiliation and safety, and become lovers of comfort, are deprived of them. Every person seeks well-being, but there is a humiliating well-being and there is a dignified well-being; the former is not the latter.

The discussion continues concerning those wealthy men who were able to participate in jihad but who chose to remain with the women. Beyond comfort-seeking, low-spiritedness, cowardice and flight from hardship, consider how base they are and what they say: ﴿When you return to them, they will offer you excuses.﴾ This is being communicated by Allah to the Messenger of Allah in advance, and the sincere believers are being warned of how these people will behave toward them when they return from this campaign. From this it appears that these verses were revealed before reaching Medina, or even earlier during the journey.

It is said that these people will begin presenting excuses as soon as you arrive, because they will sense that their conduct is a naked hypocrisy. The causes of their conduct were also clear: their faith was weak. They sought comfort and were daunted by the difficulties of jihad.

﴿Say: Do not make excuses; we will never believe you. Allah has already informed us about your affairs.﴾ That is, say to them plainly: do not offer excuses; we will not accept anything you say, for Allah has informed us of your circumstances.

You cannot offer any excuse that would make us trust you again; we will not believe you. The relationship we maintained with the hypocrites on the basis of their outward Islam can no longer continue with you, because Allah, in His grace, has disclosed your circumstances to us. The filth that is in your hearts has also been revealed by Allah, and so has the motive behind your actions. Allah has laid all your affairs bare. Now you cannot hide yourselves, whatever form you may adopt.

The words in which the Qur'an has commanded that they should not be trusted, that their side should be met with dissatisfaction, and that their excuses should not be accepted are these: "Lan nu'mina lakum" ("We will never believe you"). This expression has a particular meaning: the verb of faith (iman) has been used for affirmation, trust, confidence and satisfaction. It becomes clear that the reality of faith (iman) is that the heart has certainty and trust in the Lord, and human consciousness is content with it. Faith is expressed by the tongue, while affirmation, acceptance, intellect and conscience confirm it. The Qur'an has always contained such allusive meanings in its expressions.

O Prophet, tell them that there is no need now for excuses. Now this matter cannot be decided by words alone. Now what is needed is action. If your deeds confirm your words, then the matter will be settled. Empty talk is now useless.

"Wa-sayara Allahu 'amalakum wa-rasuluhu" ("Allah and His Messenger will now see your conduct"). Allah is such that nothing of His servants' actions is hidden from Him, nor the motive that lies behind those actions. The Messenger will weigh your words on the scale of your deeds. On this principle, the Islamic society will now deal with you. But remember that all your affairs are not settled in this world alone. Here only a very short part of life passes. Real and lasting life, and reward and punishment, are yet to come, where every matter will be decided on the record prepared by Allah.

"Thumma turaddūna ilā ʿālim al-ghaybi wa-l-shahādati fa-yunabbi'ukum bi-mā kuntum taʿmalūn" ("Then you will be returned to the One who knows the unseen and the seen, and He will inform you of what you used to do").

What is the unseen (al-ghayb)? It is that which lies beyond the means of human perception. The seen (al-shahadah) is that which man can know and perceive. In this sense Allah is both the Knower of the unseen and the Knower of the seen. The meaning is that, from your point of view, He is the Knower of the seen and the unseen; He has knowledge of both, as stated here.

"Fa-yunabbi'ukum bi-mā kuntum taʿmalūn" ("He will inform you of what you used to do"). Here there is apparently nothing to be told, since they themselves knew their deeds. But the indication is that Allah has greater knowledge of your deeds than you do. He will tell you the reality of them. For some causes and reasons behind a person's deeds are not evident even to the doer himself, and Allah's knowledge of them is greater than man's. Furthermore, some effects of a person's deeds are so far-reaching that man himself has no knowledge of them, but Allah has knowledge of them. Therefore the real purpose is that, as a result of this knowledge and information, the reckoning of your deeds will take place, and it will be a most truthful reckoning. But here there is no mention of reward and punishment; the verse simply concludes by saying that Allah will inform you of the true state of affairs.

"Sa-yahlifūna billāhi lakum idhā ankalabtum ilayhim li-tuʿ-riḍū ʿanhum. Fa-aʿ-riḍū ʿanhum. Innahum rijsun wa-maʾwāhum Jahannamu, jazāʾan bi-mā kānū yaksibūn" ("They will swear to you by Allah when you return to them, so that you may overlook them. So indeed overlook them, for they are filth, and their abode is Hell, as a recompense for what they used to earn").

This is the second advance notice which Allah is giving to His Messenger: that when you and your companions, the sincere believers, return safe and sound to Madinah, the hypocrites, who were one hundred percent certain that not one of them would return after an encounter with the Romans, will swear oaths.

Allah informs the Messenger of Allah that these people will give solemn oaths to strengthen their excuses, so that the Muslims overlook their evil deeds. In this way, through pardon and forbearance, these people will escape accountability and their affairs will be passed over. The command is given: turn away from them in practice, but not as forgiveness and pardon; leave them to their condition and keep away from them, just as a person keeps away from filth and protects himself.

"Fa-aʿ-riḍū ʿanhum, innahum rijs" ("So overlook them, for they are filth"). That is, these people are themselves embodied filth. Although their physical bodies may be fragrant, not foul or smelly, their reality, their deeds and their souls are filthy. Yet by calling their bodies filth, an impression is being created that these people are hateful and contemptible, and that keeping away from them is the very nature of things.

A movement established for the Islamic revolution, whose workers keep themselves away from jihad, fighting and practical struggle merely for fear that they might be destroyed, are filth. There is no doubt about this reality. This filth has encompassed their souls. Their consciousness and their concepts are filthy, just as a single filthy fish makes the whole pond foul; this is their example.

"Wa-maʾwāhum Jahannamu jazāʾan bi-mā kānū yaksibūn" ("Their abode is Hell, a recompense for what they used to earn"). They thought that by remaining behind they were earning, were profiting, were in comfort, safety and well-being, and had escaped financial penalty. But the reality is that in this world they are filth, and in the Hereafter the reward they receive will be regretful, because in every way and measure it will be a loss. This is Allah's word, and who can be more truthful than Allah?

What will be the conduct of those who sit behind when you return?

"Yahlifūna lakum li-tarḍaw ʿanhum. Fa-in tarḍaw ʿanhum fa-inna Allaha lā yarḍā ʿani al-qawmi al-fāsiqīn" ("They will swear to you so that you may be pleased with them. Yet even if you are pleased with them, Allah is certainly not pleased with a people who are defiantly disobedient").

Their scheme is that first these people will wish that the Muslims pardon their offence and overlook it, and afterwards they will try to obtain the pleasure of the Muslims, so that the Muslims continue to treat them in the Islamic society as they did before, on the basis of their outward profession. And these people will escape the consequences set out in this surah for the Muslims: to fight against both the disbelievers and the hypocrites and to be harsh with them. Thus the relations between the believers and non-believers were settled in this way, namely by including the hypocrites among the non-believers.

But here it is made clear that these people, by remaining behind from this jihad, have become defiantly disobedient, and Allah is never pleased with such defiant people, even if they swear many times and strive to please the Muslims. Therefore Allah's command concerning them is the correct command, and even if the whole world, including the Muslims, were pleased with them, it would not benefit them in the least in Allah's sight. The only way to please Allah, His Messenger and the Muslims is for these people to turn away from this defiance, repent, take part in the action of jihad, and enter fully into the religion of Islam.

In this way Allah, without any excuse, exposed the reality of those who stayed behind from jihad, distanced them from the Muslim community, and decided the relationship between the Muslims and the hypocrites, just as previously the relationship between the Muslims and the polytheists had been regulated, or the relationship between the Muslims and the People of the Book had been organised. These were the final and conclusive commands on this subject.

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb, *Fi Zilal al-Quran* (Urdu translation), on Surah 9, verses 93–96 (Part 1 of 3)**

**Verses 93 to 96, Juz' 11 (Para 11) at a Glance**

This juz' (one of the thirty parts of the Qur'an) consists of the remaining portion of Surah al-Tawbah and the beginning of Surah Yunus. Most of Surah al-Tawbah was covered in juz' 10. Here we will comment on the remaining portion of Surah al-Tawbah, and the commentary on Surah Yunus will begin at its start, God willing.

When we discussed Surah al-Tawbah, we made a few key points: its subject and the nature of its themes; the circumstances in which it was revealed; its significance in determining the nature of the international relations of the Islamic society and state with other societies and states; and the method of revolutionary movement for establishing the Islamic system that can be understood from this Surah. Therefore, repeating these important points here will not be without benefit.

This is a Madinan surah, and it contains glimpses of the final period of the Qur'an's revelation. Although it cannot be called the last Qur'an, it contains final glimpses because in it the rules of international relations between the Muslim community and the other nations of the world are given their final form. Moreover, within it, the formation of the Islamic society itself, the determination of its values, the determination of the worth of its various classes, and, in general, the basic features of an Islamic society are described. It presents a very deep portrayal of all the classes that exist in it and their qualities.

From this perspective, this Surah al-Tawbah is of great importance, because in it the features of the revolutionary process of the method for establishing the Islamic system, and all its stages, are described in great detail and with precision. On this subject, final and definitive rulings are given in this Surah. This review shows how solid and how decisive this method is. Without this overall review, the true picture of the commands and principles of the Shari'ah does not emerge. If the verses are viewed in isolation from their context without this overall review, the rulings that were revealed for an interim period will appear as permanent and final rulings. Then whoever wishes may interpret these final verses and instructions so that they conform to and align with the rulings meant for the interim period. Especially on the subject of jihad, such efforts have been made in practice, and the same attitude was adopted regarding the relations between the Islamic society and other jahili (pre-Islamic ignorance-based) societies.

In the introduction to this Surah, we pointed out that although the subject of this Surah is one and it was revealed in similar circumstances, it has several parts, and in each part final and definitive rulings are stated.

The first part of it sets the boundaries of the international relations between a Muslim society and other jahili societies and states, while the second part sets the boundaries of relations between the Muslims and the People of the Book. The third part comments on the situation of those who were invited to take part in the Battle of Tabuk and who showed negligence and laziness in fulfilling this duty. That battle was against the People of the Book who lived on the western edge of the Arabian Peninsula and who were preparing to strike a decisive blow against the new Islamic state. In the fourth part, the conspiracies and misdeeds of the hypocrites living in the Islamic society were exposed. Their psychology and practical conditions are portrayed. Moreover, by recording their attitude before the Battle of Tabuk, during it, and after it, their true intentions, their deceptions, and the weak excuses they presented for not taking part in the Battle of Tabuk were unveiled. Furthermore, the mischief they spread within the Islamic ranks, the corruption they caused, the discord they sowed, and the torment they inflicted upon the Messenger (ﷺ) and the sincere believers are all recorded in it. Along with this, the believers were warned about their conduct, the nature of social relations between the believers and the hypocrites was defined, and it was stated that they should be socially boycotted, so that each group would be distinguished by its own qualities.

…

These four parts, with their subjects, have already passed in juz' 10. However, some subjects from the last part, concerning those who were left behind from the battle, and the punishment and fate of those who stayed behind from jihad, have come into this section.

The last verse of the tenth juz' was this:

﴿There is no blame upon the weak, nor upon the sick, nor upon those who find nothing to spend, if they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger. There is no cause for censure upon the good-doers. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. Nor is there blame upon those who came to you asking to be provided with mounts, and you said, "I cannot find anything to mount you on." They turned away while their eyes overflowed with tears out of grief that they could not find the means to spend.﴾

The supplement with which this juz' begins is this:

﴿The blame is only upon those who ask your permission while they are rich. They have consented to be with those left behind, and Allah has sealed their hearts, so they do not know. They will make excuses to you when you return to them. Say, "Do not make excuses; we will not believe you. Allah has already informed us of your news. Allah will see your deeds, and so will His Messenger. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do." They will swear by Allah to you when you return to them, so that you may turn away from them. So turn away from them; indeed they are filth, and their refuge is Hell, as recompense for what they used to earn. They swear to you so that you may be pleased with them. But even if you are pleased with them, indeed Allah is not pleased with a defiant people.﴾

These were the reports from Allah that He gave to the Prophet (ﷺ) about the excuses that those left behind would present upon the return to Madinah. It is made clear here what you should do with those who stayed behind when you return safe and sound.

…

After this, the fifth part of the Surah comes. It explains what elements were present in the formation of the Islamic society, that is, what kinds of elements had gathered into the Islamic ranks from the conquest of Makkah until the Battle of Tabuk. As we clarified in the initial commentary on this Surah, there were, on the one hand, those who were the foremost early Muslims (al-sabiqun al-awwalun), who were the backbone of the Islamic society, and upon whom the collective system of Islam was founded. However, alongside them, other groups had also gathered into the Islamic ranks. There were the a'rab (Bedouin Arabs), among whom were both sincere people and self-interested hypocrites. Among the people of Madinah too, there was a large group of hypocrites. There were some people whose actions were good, but some of whose statements were contrary to the Shari'ah. These people had not yet fully taken the shape of the Islamic mould, nor were they completely colored by the Islamic hue. And there were some people about whom it could not be said what kind of people they were; their matter was left to Allah. Some were secret conspirators who did everything under the cover of Islam, who prepared plots, and who had contacts with the external enemies of Islam.

The Qur'anic verses have alluded to these people with great brevity, and it has been stated how all these various kinds of people are to be treated in the Islamic system of government. In this section, Allah has given instructions to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and to the sincere Muslims about what they should do with these classes and how they should deal with them. Let us consider some verses:

﴿The Bedouins are most severe in disbelief and hypocrisy and most likely not to know the limits of what Allah has revealed to His Messenger. And Allah is Knowing and Wise. Among the Bedouins are those who consider what they spend as a fine, and they wait for misfortunes to befall you. Upon them is the misfortune of evil. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing. But among the Bedouins are those who believe in Allah and the Last Day and consider what they spend as means of nearness to Allah and as prayers of the Messenger. Unquestionably, it is a means of nearness for them. Allah will admit them into His mercy. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

These Bedouins are more severe in disbelief and hypocrisy, and there is a greater likelihood that they will remain ignorant of the limits of this religion that Allah has revealed to His Messenger. Allah is All-Knowing and All-Wise. Among these Bedouins are people who, when they spend, consider it a forced penalty upon themselves. They await the turns of fortune against you, although the cycle of evil is itself upon them. Allah hears and knows everything. And among these same Bedouins are some who believe in Allah and the Last Day and who regard what they spend as a means of nearness to Allah and as the prayers of the Messenger. Indeed, it is certainly a means of nearness for them. Allah will certainly admit them into His mercy. Surely, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.

﴿As for the foremost, the first of the Emigrants and the Helpers, and those who followed them with good conduct, Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. And He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great success.﴾

Those Emigrants and Helpers who were first to respond to the call of faith, and also those who afterwards followed them in righteousness, Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. Allah has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, and they will abide therein forever. This is the great achievement.

﴿Among those around you of the Bedouins are hypocrites, and among the people of Madinah are those who have become adept at hypocrisy. You do not know them; We know them. We will punish them twice; then they will be returned to a great punishment.﴾

Among the Bedouins who live around you are many hypocrites, and among the residents of Madinah too there are hypocrites who have become masters of hypocrisy. You do not know them; We know them. The time is near when We will punish them twice. Then they will be returned to a great punishment.

﴿And others have acknowledged their sins; they had mixed a righteous deed with another that was bad. Perhaps Allah will accept their repentance. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow, and invoke blessings upon them. Indeed, your invocation is a comfort for them, and Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾

And there are others who have confessed their sins. They have mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil. It is not far that Allah will again turn towards them with mercy, for He is Forgiving and Merciful. O Prophet, take from their wealth a charity to purify and cleanse them, and pray for them, for your prayer is a source of tranquility for them. Allah is Hearing and Knowing.

﴿And there are others whose matter is held in abeyance until the command of Allah: He will either punish them or turn to them in forgiveness. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.﴾

And there are other people whose matter has been left pending by the command of Allah. Either He will punish them or He will turn to them again. Allah is All-Knowing and All-Wise.

The conclusion of this Surah is praise of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he is instructed to rely only upon his Lord and turn his attention to Him alone.

But if they turn away, say: 'Allah is sufficient for me. There is no deity but Him. In Him I have placed my trust, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne.'" (128–129)

**Lesson No. 92: Explanation of the Verses**

**Verses 93 to 96:**

There is no blame upon the weak, the sick and the poor, nor should they feel any shortcoming in their hearts. As for those who have neither provisions for the journey nor a mount, the Holy Prophet (ﷺ) or the Islamic state also cannot provide them with what is needed to reach the battlefield. The blame falls upon those who ask the Prophet (ﷺ) for leave while they are able to eat and drink, are strong and robust, and have no genuine excuse. These people are deserving of severe blame, because although they had the ability to participate in jihad, they preferred to sit with the women who stayed behind and to indulge in comfort in their homes.

Why are these people being held to account? Because they remained behind from the army of Islam, because they sought leave on false excuses, because they broke their covenant, and because Allah had made them wealthy but they did not fulfill the rights of that wealth. Allah granted them the Islamic system, but they did not discharge their duty toward the Islamic system. Islam gave them protection and honour, yet they did not discharge their duty toward that society, even though that society had also honoured them and granted them dignity. For this reason, Allah employed against them this shameful group:

﴿They were content to be with those who stay behind.﴾ That is, they chose to be among the women who remain at home. This is the utmost in low aspiration and weakness, and it is the acceptance of a humiliating position, in which a person in a place of courage and manhood sits down without excuse with the weak, the women and the children, remains at home, and joins the ranks of the unjustly excused, while it is plainly evident that he is not disabled.

﴿And Allah has sealed their hearts, so they do not know.﴾ That is, they do not understand what the outcome of their conduct will be before Allah.

This position they adopted because Allah closed the doors of knowledge and awareness upon them, and the faculties of their understanding and perception were rendered inoperative. This is because they themselves chose dullness, dimness of mind and humiliation for themselves. They deprived themselves of being alive, dynamic and active, and within them the spirit of advancing, of daring and of being assertive disappeared. Whenever a person in this world becomes comfort-seeking, ease-loving and dull-witted, he is deprived of the desire for discovery, the desire for experience and the desire for knowledge, and he becomes like a useless limb in his society, which can neither influence anyone nor accept any good influence from another, and is also deprived of self-expression.

Luxury, ease and the love of safety are a disease that closes the doors of consciousness and awareness upon a person. The power of human understanding and perception dies, whereas movement and advancement are the sign of life. Movement is the primary cause of life. By challenging difficulties, certain aspects of the human soul and human intellect are brought to light. A person's nerves become strong, and those hidden powers emerge which always come into being at times of danger and defend, and which motivate human powers toward action and toward answering a call. All these aspects are different dimensions of knowledge and perception, and those who choose humiliation and safety, and become lovers of comfort, are deprived of them. Every person seeks well-being, but there is a humiliating well-being and there is a dignified well-being; the former is not the latter.

The discussion continues concerning those wealthy men who were able to participate in jihad but who chose to remain with the women. Beyond comfort-seeking, low-spiritedness, cowardice and flight from hardship, consider how base they are and what they say: ﴿When you return to them, they will offer you excuses.﴾ This is being communicated by Allah to the Messenger of Allah in advance, and the sincere believers are being warned of how these people will behave toward them when they return from this campaign. From this it appears that these verses were revealed before reaching Medina, or even earlier during the journey.

It is said that these people will begin presenting excuses as soon as you arrive, because they will sense that their conduct is a naked hypocrisy. The causes of their conduct were also clear: their faith was weak. They sought comfort and were daunted by the difficulties of jihad.

﴿Say: Do not make excuses; we will never believe you. Allah has already informed us about your affairs.﴾ That is, say to them plainly: do not offer excuses; we will not accept anything you say, for Allah has informed us of your circumstances.

You cannot offer any excuse that would make us trust you again; we will not believe you. The relationship we maintained with the hypocrites on the basis of their outward Islam can no longer continue with you, because Allah, in His grace, has disclosed your circumstances to us. The filth that is in your hearts has also been revealed by Allah, and so has the motive behind your actions. Allah has laid all your affairs bare. Now you cannot hide yourselves, whatever form you may adopt.

The words in which the Qur'an has commanded that they should not be trusted, that their side should be met with dissatisfaction, and that their excuses should not be accepted are these: "Lan nu'mina lakum" ("We will never believe you"). This expression has a particular meaning: the verb of faith (iman) has been used for affirmation, trust, confidence and satisfaction. It becomes clear that the reality of faith (iman) is that the heart has certainty and trust in the Lord, and human consciousness is content with it. Faith is expressed by the tongue, while affirmation, acceptance, intellect and conscience confirm it. The Qur'an has always contained such allusive meanings in its expressions.

O Prophet, tell them that there is no need now for excuses. Now this matter cannot be decided by words alone. Now what is needed is action. If your deeds confirm your words, then the matter will be settled. Empty talk is now useless.

"Wa-sayara Allahu 'amalakum wa-rasuluhu" ("Allah and His Messenger will now see your conduct"). Allah is such that nothing of His servants' actions is hidden from Him, nor the motive that lies behind those actions. The Messenger will weigh your words on the scale of your deeds. On this principle, the Islamic society will now deal with you. But remember that all your affairs are not settled in this world alone. Here only a very short part of life passes. Real and lasting life, and reward and punishment, are yet to come, where every matter will be decided on the record prepared by Allah.

"Thumma turaddūna ilā ʿālim al-ghaybi wa-l-shahādati fa-yunabbi'ukum bi-mā kuntum taʿmalūn" ("Then you will be returned to the One who knows the unseen and the seen, and He will inform you of what you used to do").

What is the unseen (al-ghayb)? It is that which lies beyond the means of human perception. The seen (al-shahadah) is that which man can know and perceive. In this sense Allah is both the Knower of the unseen and the Knower of the seen. The meaning is that, from your point of view, He is the Knower of the seen and the unseen; He has knowledge of both, as stated here.

"Fa-yunabbi'ukum bi-mā kuntum taʿmalūn" ("He will inform you of what you used to do"). Here there is apparently nothing to be told, since they themselves knew their deeds. But the indication is that Allah has greater knowledge of your deeds than you do. He will tell you the reality of them. For some causes and reasons behind a person's deeds are not evident even to the doer himself, and Allah's knowledge of them is greater than man's. Furthermore, some effects of a person's deeds are so far-reaching that man himself has no knowledge of them, but Allah has knowledge of them. Therefore the real purpose is that, as a result of this knowledge and information, the reckoning of your deeds will take place, and it will be a most truthful reckoning. But here there is no mention of reward and punishment; the verse simply concludes by saying that Allah will inform you of the true state of affairs.

"Sa-yahlifūna billāhi lakum idhā ankalabtum ilayhim li-tuʿ-riḍū ʿanhum. Fa-aʿ-riḍū ʿanhum. Innahum rijsun wa-maʾwāhum Jahannamu, jazāʾan bi-mā kānū yaksibūn" ("They will swear to you by Allah when you return to them, so that you may overlook them. So indeed overlook them, for they are filth, and their abode is Hell, as a recompense for what they used to earn").

In this way, through pardon and forbearance, these people will escape accountability and their affairs will be passed over. The command is given: turn away from them in practice, but not as forgiveness and pardon; leave them to their condition and keep away from them, just as a person keeps away from filth and protects himself.

"Fa-aʿ-riḍū ʿanhum, innahum rijs" ("So overlook them, for they are filth"). That is, these people are themselves embodied filth. Although their physical bodies may be fragrant, not foul or smelly, their reality, their deeds and their souls are filthy. Yet by calling their bodies filth, an impression is being created that these people are hateful and contemptible, and that keeping away from them is the very nature of things.

A movement established for the Islamic revolution, whose workers keep themselves away from jihad, fighting and practical struggle merely for fear that they might be destroyed, are filth. There is no doubt about this reality. This filth has encompassed their souls. Their consciousness and their concepts are filthy, just as a single filthy fish makes the whole pond foul; this is their example.

"Wa-maʾwāhum Jahannamu jazāʾan bi-mā kānū yaksibūn" ("Their abode is Hell, a recompense for what they used to earn"). They thought that by remaining behind they were earning, were profiting, were in comfort, safety and well-being, and had escaped financial penalty. But the reality is that in this world they are filth, and in the Hereafter the reward they receive will be regretful, because in every way and measure it will be a loss. This is Allah's word, and who can be more truthful than Allah?

What will be the conduct of those who sit behind when you return?

"Yahlifūna lakum li-tarḍaw ʿanhum. Fa-in tarḍaw ʿanhum fa-inna Allaha lā yarḍā ʿani al-qawmi al-fāsiqīn" ("They will swear to you so that you may be pleased with them. Yet even if you are pleased with them, Allah is certainly not pleased with a people who are defiantly disobedient").

But here it is made clear that these people, by remaining behind from this jihad, have become defiantly disobedient, and Allah is never pleased with such defiant people, even if they swear many times and strive to please the Muslims. Therefore Allah's command concerning them is the correct command, and even if the whole world, including the Muslims, were pleased with them, it would not benefit them in the least in Allah's sight. **Verses 93 to 96, Juz' 11 (Para 11) at a Glance**

This juz' (one of the thirty parts of the Qur'an) consists of the remaining portion of Surah al-Tawbah and the beginning of Surah Yunus. Most of Surah al-Tawbah was covered in juz' 10. Here we will comment on the remaining portion of Surah al-Tawbah, and the commentary on Surah Yunus will begin at its start, God willing.

When we discussed Surah al-Tawbah, we made a few key points: its subject and the nature of its themes; the circumstances in which it was revealed; its significance in determining the nature of the international relations of the Islamic society and state with other societies and states; and the method of revolutionary movement for establishing the Islamic system that can be understood from this Surah. Therefore, repeating these important points here will not be without benefit.

This is a Madinan surah, and it contains glimpses of the final period of the Qur'an's revelation. Although it cannot be called the last Qur'an, it contains final glimpses because in it the rules of international relations between the Muslim community and the other nations of the world are given their final form. Moreover, within it, the formation of the Islamic society itself, the determination of its values, the determination of the worth of its various classes, and, in general, the basic features of an Islamic society are described. It presents a very deep portrayal of all the classes that exist in it and their qualities.

From this perspective, this Surah al-Tawbah is of great importance, because in it the features of the revolutionary process of the method for establishing the Islamic system, and all its stages, are described in great detail and with precision. On this subject, final and definitive rulings are given in this Surah. This review shows how solid and how decisive this method is. Without this overall review, the true picture of the commands and principles of the Shari'ah does not emerge. If the verses are viewed in isolation from their context without this overall review, the rulings that were revealed for an interim period will appear as permanent and final rulings. Then whoever wishes may interpret these final verses and instructions so that they conform to and align with the rulings meant for the interim period. Especially on the subject of jihad, such efforts have been made in practice, and the same attitude was adopted regarding the relations between the Islamic society and other jahili (pre-Islamic ignorance-based) societies.

In the introduction to this Surah, we pointed out that although the subject of this Surah is one and it was revealed in similar circumstances, it has several parts, and in each part final and definitive rulings are stated.

The first part of it sets the boundaries of the international relations between a Muslim society and other jahili societies and states, while the second part sets the boundaries of relations between the Muslims and the People of the Book. The third part comments on the situation of those who were invited to take part in the Battle of Tabuk and who showed negligence and laziness in fulfilling this duty. That battle was against the People of the Book who lived on the western edge of the Arabian Peninsula and who were preparing to strike a decisive blow against the new Islamic state. In the fourth part, the conspiracies and misdeeds of the hypocrites living in the Islamic society were exposed. Their psychology and practical conditions are portrayed. Moreover, by recording their attitude before the Battle of Tabuk, during it, and after it, their true intentions, their deceptions, and the weak excuses they presented for not taking part in the Battle of Tabuk were unveiled. Furthermore, the mischief they spread within the Islamic ranks, the corruption they caused, the discord they sowed, and the torment they inflicted upon the Messenger (ﷺ) and the sincere believers are all recorded in it. Along with this, the believers were warned about their conduct, the nature of social relations between the believers and the hypocrites was defined, and it was stated that they should be socially boycotted, so that each group would be distinguished by its own qualities.

…

These four parts, with their subjects, have already passed in juz' 10. However, some subjects from the last part, concerning those who were left behind from the battle, and the punishment and fate of those who stayed behind from jihad, have come into this section.

The last verse of the tenth juz' was this:

﴿There is no blame upon the weak, nor upon the sick, nor upon those who find nothing to spend, if they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger. There is no cause for censure upon the good-doers. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. Nor is there blame upon those who came to you asking to be provided with mounts, and you said, "I cannot find anything to mount you on." They turned away while their eyes overflowed with tears out of grief that they could not find the means to spend.﴾

The supplement with which this juz' begins is this:

﴿The blame is only upon those who ask your permission while they are rich. They have consented to be with those left behind, and Allah has sealed their hearts, so they do not know. They will make excuses to you when you return to them. Say, "Do not make excuses; we will not believe you. Allah has already informed us of your news. Allah will see your deeds, and so will His Messenger. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do." They will swear by Allah to you when you return to them, so that you may turn away from them. So turn away from them; indeed they are filth, and their refuge is Hell, as recompense for what they used to earn. They swear to you so that you may be pleased with them. But even if you are pleased with them, indeed Allah is not pleased with a defiant people.﴾

These were the reports from Allah that He gave to the Prophet (ﷺ) about the excuses that those left behind would present upon the return to Madinah. It is made clear here what you should do with those who stayed behind when you return safe and sound.

…

After this, the fifth part of the Surah comes. It explains what elements were present in the formation of the Islamic society, that is, what kinds of elements had gathered into the Islamic ranks from the conquest of Makkah until the Battle of Tabuk. As we clarified in the initial commentary on this Surah, there were, on the one hand, those who were the foremost early Muslims (al-sabiqun al-awwalun), who were the backbone of the Islamic society, and upon whom the collective system of Islam was founded. However, alongside them, other groups had also gathered into the Islamic ranks. There were the a'rab (Bedouin Arabs), among whom were both sincere people and self-interested hypocrites. Among the people of Madinah too, there was a large group of hypocrites. There were some people whose actions were good, but some of whose statements were contrary to the Shari'ah. These people had not yet fully taken the shape of the Islamic mould, nor were they completely colored by the Islamic hue. And there were some people about whom it could not be said what kind of people they were; their matter was left to Allah. Some were secret conspirators who did everything under the cover of Islam, who prepared plots, and who had contacts with the external enemies of Islam.

The Qur'anic verses have alluded to these people with great brevity, and it has been stated how all these various kinds of people are to be treated in the Islamic system of government. In this section, Allah has given instructions to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and to the sincere Muslims about what they should do with these classes and how they should deal with them. Let us consider some verses:

﴿The Bedouins are most severe in disbelief and hypocrisy and most likely not to know the limits of what Allah has revealed to His Messenger. And Allah is Knowing and Wise. Among the Bedouins are those who consider what they spend as a fine, and they wait for misfortunes to befall you. Upon them is the misfortune of evil. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing. But among the Bedouins are those who believe in Allah and the Last Day and consider what they spend as means of nearness to Allah and as prayers of the Messenger. Unquestionably, it is a means of nearness for them. Allah will admit them into His mercy. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

These Bedouins are more severe in disbelief and hypocrisy, and there is a greater likelihood that they will remain ignorant of the limits of this religion that Allah has revealed to His Messenger. Allah is All-Knowing and All-Wise. Among these Bedouins are people who, when they spend, consider it a forced penalty upon themselves. They await the turns of fortune against you, although the cycle of evil is itself upon them. Allah hears and knows everything. And among these same Bedouins are some who believe in Allah and the Last Day and who regard what they spend as a means of nearness to Allah and as the prayers of the Messenger. Indeed, it is certainly a means of nearness for them. Allah will certainly admit them into His mercy. Surely, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.

﴿As for the foremost, the first of the Emigrants and the Helpers, and those who followed them with good conduct, Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. And He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great success.﴾

Those Emigrants and Helpers who were first to respond to the call of faith, and also those who afterwards followed them in righteousness, Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. Allah has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, and they will abide therein forever. This is the great achievement.

﴿Among those around you of the Bedouins are hypocrites, and among the people of Madinah are those who have become adept at hypocrisy. You do not know them; We know them. We will punish them twice; then they will be returned to a great punishment.﴾

Among the Bedouins who live around you are many hypocrites, and among the residents of Madinah too there are hypocrites who have become masters of hypocrisy. You do not know them; We know them. The time is near when We will punish them twice. Then they will be returned to a great punishment.

﴿And others have acknowledged their sins; they had mixed a righteous deed with another that was bad. Perhaps Allah will accept their repentance. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow, and invoke blessings upon them. Indeed, your invocation is a comfort for them, and Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾

And there are others who have confessed their sins. They have mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil. It is not far that Allah will again turn towards them with mercy, for He is Forgiving and Merciful. O Prophet, take from their wealth a charity to purify and cleanse them, and pray for them, for your prayer is a source of tranquility for them. Allah is Hearing and Knowing.

﴿And there are others whose matter is held in abeyance until the command of Allah: He will either punish them or turn to them in forgiveness. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.﴾

And there are other people whose matter has been left pending by the command of Allah. Either He will punish them or He will turn to them again. Allah is All-Knowing and All-Wise.

**Lesson No. 92: Explanation of the Verses**

**Verses 93 to 96:**

There is no blame upon the weak, the sick and the poor, nor should they feel any shortcoming in their hearts. As for those who have neither provisions for the journey nor a mount, the Holy Prophet (ﷺ) or the Islamic state also cannot provide them with what is needed to reach the battlefield. The blame falls upon those who ask the Prophet (ﷺ) for leave while they are able to eat and drink, are strong and robust, and have no genuine excuse. These people are deserving of severe blame, because although they had the ability to participate in jihad, they preferred to sit with the women who stayed behind and to indulge in comfort in their homes.

Why are these people being held to account? Because they remained behind from the army of Islam, because they sought leave on false excuses, because they broke their covenant, and because Allah had made them wealthy but they did not fulfill the rights of that wealth. Allah granted them the Islamic system, but they did not discharge their duty toward the Islamic system. Islam gave them protection and honour, yet they did not discharge their duty toward that society, even though that society had also honoured them and granted them dignity. For this reason, Allah employed against them this shameful group:

﴿They were content to be with those who stay behind.﴾ That is, they chose to be among the women who remain at home. This is the utmost in low aspiration and weakness, and it is the acceptance of a humiliating position, in which a person in a place of courage and manhood sits down without excuse with the weak, the women and the children, remains at home, and joins the ranks of the unjustly excused, while it is plainly evident that he is not disabled.

﴿And Allah has sealed their hearts, so they do not know.﴾ That is, they do not understand what the outcome of their conduct will be before Allah.

This position they adopted because Allah closed the doors of knowledge and awareness upon them, and the faculties of their understanding and perception were rendered inoperative. This is because they themselves chose dullness, dimness of mind and humiliation for themselves. They deprived themselves of being alive, dynamic and active, and within them the spirit of advancing, of daring and of being assertive disappeared. Whenever a person in this world becomes comfort-seeking, ease-loving and dull-witted, he is deprived of the desire for discovery, the desire for experience and the desire for knowledge, and he becomes like a useless limb in his society, which can neither influence anyone nor accept any good influence from another, and is also deprived of self-expression.

Luxury, ease and the love of safety are a disease that closes the doors of consciousness and awareness upon a person. The power of human understanding and perception dies, whereas movement and advancement are the sign of life. Movement is the primary cause of life. By challenging difficulties, certain aspects of the human soul and human intellect are brought to light. A person's nerves become strong, and those hidden powers emerge which always come into being at times of danger and defend, and which motivate human powers toward action and toward answering a call. All these aspects are different dimensions of knowledge and perception, and those who choose humiliation and safety, and become lovers of comfort, are deprived of them. Every person seeks well-being, but there is a humiliating well-being and there is a dignified well-being; the former is not the latter.

The discussion continues concerning those wealthy men who were able to participate in jihad but who chose to remain with the women. Beyond comfort-seeking, low-spiritedness, cowardice and flight from hardship, consider how base they are and what they say: ﴿When you return to them, they will offer you excuses.﴾ This is being communicated by Allah to the Messenger of Allah in advance, and the sincere believers are being warned of how these people will behave toward them when they return from this campaign. From this it appears that these verses were revealed before reaching Medina, or even earlier during the journey.

It is said that these people will begin presenting excuses as soon as you arrive, because they will sense that their conduct is a naked hypocrisy. The causes of their conduct were also clear: their faith was weak. They sought comfort and were daunted by the difficulties of jihad.

﴿Say: Do not make excuses; we will never believe you. Allah has already informed us about your affairs.﴾ That is, say to them plainly: do not offer excuses; we will not accept anything you say, for Allah has informed us of your circumstances.

You cannot offer any excuse that would make us trust you again; we will not believe you. The relationship we maintained with the hypocrites on the basis of their outward Islam can no longer continue with you, because Allah, in His grace, has disclosed your circumstances to us. The filth that is in your hearts has also been revealed by Allah, and so has the motive behind your actions. Allah has laid all your affairs bare. Now you cannot hide yourselves, whatever form you may adopt.

The words in which the Qur'an has commanded that they should not be trusted, that their side should be met with dissatisfaction, and that their excuses should not be accepted are these: "Lan nu'mina lakum" ("We will never believe you"). This expression has a particular meaning: the verb of faith (iman) has been used for affirmation, trust, confidence and satisfaction. It becomes clear that the reality of faith (iman) is that the heart has certainty and trust in the Lord, and human consciousness is content with it. Faith is expressed by the tongue, while affirmation, acceptance, intellect and conscience confirm it. The Qur'an has always contained such allusive meanings in its expressions.

O Prophet, tell them that there is no need now for excuses. Now this matter cannot be decided by words alone. Now what is needed is action. If your deeds confirm your words, then the matter will be settled. Empty talk is now useless.

"Wa-sayara Allahu 'amalakum wa-rasuluhu" ("Allah and His Messenger will now see your conduct"). Allah is such that nothing of His servants' actions is hidden from Him, nor the motive that lies behind those actions. The Messenger will weigh your words on the scale of your deeds. On this principle, the Islamic society will now deal with you. But remember that all your affairs are not settled in this world alone. Here only a very short part of life passes. Real and lasting life, and reward and punishment, are yet to come, where every matter will be decided on the record prepared by Allah.

"Thumma turaddūna ilā ʿālim al-ghaybi wa-l-shahādati fa-yunabbi'ukum bi-mā kuntum taʿmalūn" ("Then you will be returned to the One who knows the unseen and the seen, and He will inform you of what you used to do").

What is the unseen (al-ghayb)? It is that which lies beyond the means of human perception. The seen (al-shahadah) is that which man can know and perceive. In this sense Allah is both the Knower of the unseen and the Knower of the seen. The meaning is that, from your point of view, He is the Knower of the seen and the unseen; He has knowledge of both, as stated here.

"Fa-yunabbi'ukum bi-mā kuntum taʿmalūn" ("He will inform you of what you used to do"). Here there is apparently nothing to be told, since they themselves knew their deeds. But the indication is that Allah has greater knowledge of your deeds than you do. He will tell you the reality of them. For some causes and reasons behind a person's deeds are not evident even to the doer himself, and Allah's knowledge of them is greater than man's. Furthermore, some effects of a person's deeds are so far-reaching that man himself has no knowledge of them, but Allah has knowledge of them. Therefore the real purpose is that, as a result of this knowledge and information, the reckoning of your deeds will take place, and it will be a most truthful reckoning. But here there is no mention of reward and punishment; the verse simply concludes by saying that Allah will inform you of the true state of affairs.

"Sa-yahlifūna billāhi lakum idhā ankalabtum ilayhim li-tuʿ-riḍū ʿanhum. Fa-aʿ-riḍū ʿanhum. Innahum rijsun wa-maʾwāhum Jahannamu, jazāʾan bi-mā kānū yaksibūn" ("They will swear to you by Allah when you return to them, so that you may overlook them. So indeed overlook them, for they are filth, and their abode is Hell, as a recompense for what they used to earn").

This is the second advance notice which Allah is giving to His Messenger: that when you and your companions, the sincere believers, return safe and sound to Madinah, the hypocrites, who were one hundred percent certain that not one of them would return after an encounter with the Romans, will swear oaths.

Allah informs the Messenger of Allah that these people will give solemn oaths to strengthen their excuses, so that the Muslims overlook their evil deeds. In this way, through pardon and forbearance, these people will escape accountability and their affairs will be passed over. The command is given: turn away from them in practice, but not as forgiveness and pardon; leave them to their condition and keep away from them, just as a person keeps away from filth and protects himself.

"Fa-aʿ-riḍū ʿanhum, innahum rijs" ("So overlook them, for they are filth"). That is, these people are themselves embodied filth. Although their physical bodies may be fragrant, not foul or smelly, their reality, their deeds and their souls are filthy. Yet by calling their bodies filth, an impression is being created that these people are hateful and contemptible, and that keeping away from them is the very nature of things.

A movement established for the Islamic revolution, whose workers keep themselves away from jihad, fighting and practical struggle merely for fear that they might be destroyed, are filth. There is no doubt about this reality. This filth has encompassed their souls. Their consciousness and their concepts are filthy, just as a single filthy fish makes the whole pond foul; this is their example.

"Wa-maʾwāhum Jahannamu jazāʾan bi-mā kānū yaksibūn" ("Their abode is Hell, a recompense for what they used to earn"). They thought that by remaining behind they were earning, were profiting, were in comfort, safety and well-being, and had escaped financial penalty. But the reality is that in this world they are filth, and in the Hereafter the reward they receive will be regretful, because in every way and measure it will be a loss. This is Allah's word, and who can be more truthful than Allah?

What will be the conduct of those who sit behind when you return?

"Yahlifūna lakum li-tarḍaw ʿanhum. Fa-in tarḍaw ʿanhum fa-inna Allaha lā yarḍā ʿani al-qawmi al-fāsiqīn" ("They will swear to you so that you may be pleased with them. Yet even if you are pleased with them, Allah is certainly not pleased with a people who are defiantly disobedient").

Their scheme is that first these people will wish that the Muslims pardon their offence and overlook it, and afterwards they will try to obtain the pleasure of the Muslims, so that the Muslims continue to treat them in the Islamic society as they did before, on the basis of their outward profession. And these people will escape the consequences set out in this surah for the Muslims: to fight against both the disbelievers and the hypocrites and to be harsh with them. Thus the relations between the believers and non-believers were settled in this way, namely by including the hypocrites among the non-believers.

But here it is made clear that these people, by remaining behind from this jihad, have become defiantly disobedient, and Allah is never pleased with such defiant people, even if they swear many times and strive to please the Muslims. Therefore Allah's command concerning them is the correct command, and even if the whole world, including the Muslims, were pleased with them, it would not benefit them in the least in Allah's sight. The only way to please Allah, His Messenger and the Muslims is for these people to turn away from this defiance, repent, take part in the action of jihad, and enter fully into the religion of Islam.

In this way Allah, without any excuse, exposed the reality of those who stayed behind from jihad, distanced them from the Muslim community, and decided the relationship between the Muslims and the hypocrites, just as previously the relationship between the Muslims and the polytheists had been regulated, or the relationship between the Muslims and the People of the Book had been organised. These were the final and conclusive commands on this subject.

After this, the fifth part of the Surah comes. It explains what elements were present in the formation of the Islamic society, that is, what kinds of elements had gathered into the Islamic ranks from the conquest of Makkah until the Battle of Tabuk. As we clarified in the initial commentary on this Surah, there were, on the one hand, those who were the foremost early Muslims (al-sabiqun al-awwalun), who were the backbone of the Islamic society, and upon whom the collective system of Islam was founded. However, alongside them, other groups had also gathered into the Islamic ranks. There were the a'rab (Bedouin Arabs), among whom were both sincere people and self-interested hypocrites. Among the people of Madinah too, there was a large group of hypocrites. There were some people whose actions were good, but some of whose statements were contrary to the Shari'ah. These people had not yet fully taken the shape of the Islamic mould, nor were they completely colored by the Islamic hue. And there were some people about whom it could not be said what kind of people they were; their matter was left to Allah. Some were secret conspirators who did everything under the cover of Islam, who prepared plots, and who had contacts with the external enemies of Islam.

The Qur'anic verses have alluded to these people with great brevity, and it has been stated how all these various kinds of people are to be treated in the Islamic system of government. In this section, Allah has given instructions to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and to the sincere Muslims about what they should do with these classes and how they should deal with them. Let us consider some verses:

﴿The Bedouins are most severe in disbelief and hypocrisy and most likely not to know the limits of what Allah has revealed to His Messenger. And Allah is Knowing and Wise. Among the Bedouins are those who consider what they spend as a fine, and they wait for misfortunes to befall you. Upon them is the misfortune of evil. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing. But among the Bedouins are those who believe in Allah and the Last Day and consider what they spend as means of nearness to Allah and as prayers of the Messenger. Unquestionably, it is a means of nearness for them. Allah will admit them into His mercy. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

These Bedouins are more severe in disbelief and hypocrisy, and there is a greater likelihood that they will remain ignorant of the limits of this religion that Allah has revealed to His Messenger.
