Allah is All-Knowing and All-Wise. Among these Bedouins are people who, when they spend, consider it a forced penalty upon themselves. They await the turns of fortune against you, although the cycle of evil is itself upon them. Allah hears and knows everything. And among these same Bedouins are some who believe in Allah and the Last Day and who regard what they spend as a means of nearness to Allah and as the prayers of the Messenger. Indeed, it is certainly a means of nearness for them. Allah will certainly admit them into His mercy. Surely, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.

﴿As for the foremost, the first of the Emigrants and the Helpers, and those who followed them with good conduct, Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. And He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great success.﴾

Those Emigrants and Helpers who were first to respond to the call of faith, and also those who afterwards followed them in righteousness, Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. Allah has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, and they will abide therein forever. This is the great achievement.

﴿Among those around you of the Bedouins are hypocrites, and among the people of Madinah are those who have become adept at hypocrisy. You do not know them; We know them. We will punish them twice; then they will be returned to a great punishment.﴾

Among the Bedouins who live around you are many hypocrites, and among the residents of Madinah too there are hypocrites who have become masters of hypocrisy. You do not know them; We know them. The time is near when We will punish them twice. Then they will be returned to a great punishment.

﴿And others have acknowledged their sins; they had mixed a righteous deed with another that was bad. Perhaps Allah will accept their repentance. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow, and invoke blessings upon them. Indeed, your invocation is a comfort for them, and Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾

And there are others who have confessed their sins. They have mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil. It is not far that Allah will again turn towards them with mercy, for He is Forgiving and Merciful. O Prophet, take from their wealth a charity to purify and cleanse them, and pray for them, for your prayer is a source of tranquility for them. Allah is Hearing and Knowing.

﴿And there are others whose matter is held in abeyance until the command of Allah: He will either punish them or turn to them in forgiveness. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.﴾

And there are other people whose matter has been left pending by the command of Allah. Either He will punish them or He will turn to them again. Allah is All-Knowing and All-Wise.

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 9, Verses 93–96 (Part 2 of 3)**

"Some others have built a mosque for the purpose of causing harm (to the call to truth), for disbelief, for dividing the believers, and as a place of ambush for the one who had already waged war against Allah and His Messenger. They will surely swear, 'We intended nothing but good.' But Allah bears witness that they are indeed liars. Never stand in that building. A mosque founded on righteousness from the first day is more deserving that you stand in it (for worship). In it are men who love to purify themselves, and Allah loves those who purify themselves." (107–108)

"Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their wealth, in return for Paradise. They fight in the way of Allah, so they kill and are killed. It is a true promise binding upon Him in the Torah, the Gospel and the Qur'an. And who fulfills his covenant more than Allah? So rejoice in the bargain you have made with Him. That is the great success." (111)

"It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to seek forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were near relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of the Blazing Fire." (113)

"And Abraham's seeking forgiveness for his father was only due to a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disassociated himself from him. Indeed, Abraham was tender-hearted and forbearing." (114)

"Allah has indeed forgiven the Prophet and the Emigrants and the Helpers who followed him in the hour of hardship, after the hearts of a group of them had nearly swerved. Then He relented toward them. Indeed, He is Kind and Merciful to them." (117)

"And (He forgave) the three who were left behind, until when the earth, despite its vastness, became confining for them, and their own souls became a burden to them, and they perceived that there is no refuge from Allah except in Him. Then He turned to them so that they might repent. Indeed, Allah is the Accepter of Repentance, the Merciful." (118)

"It was not befitting for the people of Medina and the Bedouins around them to remain behind from the Messenger of Allah, or to prefer their own selves over his self. That is because they will not suffer thirst, fatigue or hunger in the way of Allah, nor tread a path that angers the disbelievers, nor gain anything from an enemy, but a righteous deed is recorded for them thereby. Indeed, Allah does not waste the reward of the good-doers." (120)

"Nor do they spend any expenditure, small or large, nor cross a valley, but it is recorded for them, so that Allah may reward them with the best of what they used to do." (121)

"It is not for the believers to go forth all together. Why should not a party from every section of them go forth, so that they may gain understanding of the religion and warn their people when they return to them, that they may beware?" (122)

"O you who believe, fight those disbelievers who are near to you, and let them find harshness in you. And know that Allah is with the righteous." (123)

"Whenever a Surah is revealed, some of them glance at others, (saying), 'Does anyone see you?' Then they slip away. Allah has turned their hearts away, because they are a people who do not understand." (127)

The conclusion of this Surah is praise of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he is instructed to rely only upon his Lord and turn his attention to Him alone.

"There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; your suffering distresses him, he is anxious over you, and toward the believers he is kind and merciful. But if they turn away, say: 'Allah is sufficient for me. There is no deity but Him. In Him I have placed my trust, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne.'" (128–129)

Now, after this brief explanation, we come to the detailed explanation of the verses.

**Lesson No. 92: Explanation of the Verses**

**Verses 93 to 96:**

There is no blame upon the weak, the sick and the poor, nor should they feel any shortcoming in their hearts. As for those who have neither provisions for the journey nor a mount, the Holy Prophet (ﷺ) or the Islamic state also cannot provide them with what is needed to reach the battlefield. The blame falls upon those who ask the Prophet (ﷺ) for leave while they are able to eat and drink, are strong and robust, and have no genuine excuse. These people are deserving of severe blame, because although they had the ability to participate in jihad, they preferred to sit with the women who stayed behind and to indulge in comfort in their homes.

Why are these people being held to account? Because they remained behind from the army of Islam, because they sought leave on false excuses, because they broke their covenant, and because Allah had made them wealthy but they did not fulfill the rights of that wealth. Allah granted them the Islamic system, but they did not discharge their duty toward the Islamic system. Islam gave them protection and honour, yet they did not discharge their duty toward that society, even though that society had also honoured them and granted them dignity. For this reason, Allah employed against them this shameful group:

﴿They were content to be with those who stay behind.﴾ That is, they chose to be among the women who remain at home. This is the utmost in low aspiration and weakness, and it is the acceptance of a humiliating position, in which a person in a place of courage and manhood sits down without excuse with the weak, the women and the children, remains at home, and joins the ranks of the unjustly excused, while it is plainly evident that he is not disabled.

﴿And Allah has sealed their hearts, so they do not know.﴾ That is, they do not understand what the outcome of their conduct will be before Allah.

This position they adopted because Allah closed the doors of knowledge and awareness upon them, and the faculties of their understanding and perception were rendered inoperative. This is because they themselves chose dullness, dimness of mind and humiliation for themselves. They deprived themselves of being alive, dynamic and active, and within them the spirit of advancing, of daring and of being assertive disappeared. Whenever a person in this world becomes comfort-seeking, ease-loving and dull-witted, he is deprived of the desire for discovery, the desire for experience and the desire for knowledge, and he becomes like a useless limb in his society, which can neither influence anyone nor accept any good influence from another, and is also deprived of self-expression.

Luxury, ease and the love of safety are a disease that closes the doors of consciousness and awareness upon a person. The power of human understanding and perception dies, whereas movement and advancement are the sign of life. Movement is the primary cause of life. By challenging difficulties, certain aspects of the human soul and human intellect are brought to light. A person's nerves become strong, and those hidden powers emerge which always come into being at times of danger and defend, and which motivate human powers toward action and toward answering a call. All these aspects are different dimensions of knowledge and perception, and those who choose humiliation and safety, and become lovers of comfort, are deprived of them. Every person seeks well-being, but there is a humiliating well-being and there is a dignified well-being; the former is not the latter.

The discussion continues concerning those wealthy men who were able to participate in jihad but who chose to remain with the women. Beyond comfort-seeking, low-spiritedness, cowardice and flight from hardship, consider how base they are and what they say: ﴿When you return to them, they will offer you excuses.﴾ This is being communicated by Allah to the Messenger of Allah in advance, and the sincere believers are being warned of how these people will behave toward them when they return from this campaign. From this it appears that these verses were revealed before reaching Medina, or even earlier during the journey.

It is said that these people will begin presenting excuses as soon as you arrive, because they will sense that their conduct is a naked hypocrisy. The causes of their conduct were also clear: their faith was weak. They sought comfort and were daunted by the difficulties of jihad.

﴿Say: Do not make excuses; we will never believe you. Allah has already informed us about your affairs.﴾ That is, say to them plainly: do not offer excuses; we will not accept anything you say, for Allah has informed us of your circumstances.

You cannot offer any excuse that would make us trust you again; we will not believe you. The relationship we maintained with the hypocrites on the basis of their outward Islam can no longer continue with you, because Allah, in His grace, has disclosed your circumstances to us. The filth that is in your hearts has also been revealed by Allah, and so has the motive behind your actions. Allah has laid all your affairs bare. Now you cannot hide yourselves, whatever form you may adopt.

The words in which the Qur'an has commanded that they should not be trusted, that their side should be met with dissatisfaction, and that their excuses should not be accepted are these: "Lan nu'mina lakum" ("We will never believe you"). This expression has a particular meaning: the verb of faith (iman) has been used for affirmation, trust, confidence and satisfaction. It becomes clear that the reality of faith (iman) is that the heart has certainty and trust in the Lord, and human consciousness is content with it. Faith is expressed by the tongue, while affirmation, acceptance, intellect and conscience confirm it. The Qur'an has always contained such allusive meanings in its expressions.

O Prophet, tell them that there is no need now for excuses. Now this matter cannot be decided by words alone. Now what is needed is action. If your deeds confirm your words, then the matter will be settled. Empty talk is now useless.

"Wa-sayara Allahu 'amalakum wa-rasuluhu" ("Allah and His Messenger will now see your conduct"). Allah is such that nothing of His servants' actions is hidden from Him, nor the motive that lies behind those actions. The Messenger will weigh your words on the scale of your deeds. On this principle, the Islamic society will now deal with you. But remember that all your affairs are not settled in this world alone. Here only a very short part of life passes. Real and lasting life, and reward and punishment, are yet to come, where every matter will be decided on the record prepared by Allah.

"Thumma turaddūna ilā ʿālim al-ghaybi wa-l-shahādati fa-yunabbi'ukum bi-mā kuntum taʿmalūn" ("Then you will be returned to the One who knows the unseen and the seen, and He will inform you of what you used to do").

What is the unseen (al-ghayb)? It is that which lies beyond the means of human perception. The seen (al-shahadah) is that which man can know and perceive. In this sense Allah is both the Knower of the unseen and the Knower of the seen. The meaning is that, from your point of view, He is the Knower of the seen and the unseen; He has knowledge of both, as stated here.

"Fa-yunabbi'ukum bi-mā kuntum taʿmalūn" ("He will inform you of what you used to do"). Here there is apparently nothing to be told, since they themselves knew their deeds. But the indication is that Allah has greater knowledge of your deeds than you do. He will tell you the reality of them. For some causes and reasons behind a person's deeds are not evident even to the doer himself, and Allah's knowledge of them is greater than man's. Furthermore, some effects of a person's deeds are so far-reaching that man himself has no knowledge of them, but Allah has knowledge of them. Therefore the real purpose is that, as a result of this knowledge and information, the reckoning of your deeds will take place, and it will be a most truthful reckoning. But here there is no mention of reward and punishment; the verse simply concludes by saying that Allah will inform you of the true state of affairs.

"Sa-yahlifūna billāhi lakum idhā ankalabtum ilayhim li-tuʿ-riḍū ʿanhum. Fa-aʿ-riḍū ʿanhum. Innahum rijsun wa-maʾwāhum Jahannamu, jazāʾan bi-mā kānū yaksibūn" ("They will swear to you by Allah when you return to them, so that you may overlook them. So indeed overlook them, for they are filth, and their abode is Hell, as a recompense for what they used to earn").

This is the second advance notice which Allah is giving to His Messenger: that when you and your companions, the sincere believers, return safe and sound to Madinah, the hypocrites, who were one hundred percent certain that not one of them would return after an encounter with the Romans, will swear oaths.

Allah informs the Messenger of Allah that these people will give solemn oaths to strengthen their excuses, so that the Muslims overlook their evil deeds. In this way, through pardon and forbearance, these people will escape accountability and their affairs will be passed over. The command is given: turn away from them in practice, but not as forgiveness and pardon; leave them to their condition and keep away from them, just as a person keeps away from filth and protects himself.

"Fa-aʿ-riḍū ʿanhum, innahum rijs" ("So overlook them, for they are filth"). That is, these people are themselves embodied filth. Although their physical bodies may be fragrant, not foul or smelly, their reality, their deeds and their souls are filthy. Yet by calling their bodies filth, an impression is being created that these people are hateful and contemptible, and that keeping away from them is the very nature of things.

A movement established for the Islamic revolution, whose workers keep themselves away from jihad, fighting and practical struggle merely for fear that they might be destroyed, are filth. There is no doubt about this reality. This filth has encompassed their souls. Their consciousness and their concepts are filthy, just as a single filthy fish makes the whole pond foul; this is their example.

"Wa-maʾwāhum Jahannamu jazāʾan bi-mā kānū yaksibūn" ("Their abode is Hell, a recompense for what they used to earn"). They thought that by remaining behind they were earning, were profiting, were in comfort, safety and well-being, and had escaped financial penalty. But the reality is that in this world they are filth, and in the Hereafter the reward they receive will be regretful, because in every way and measure it will be a loss. This is Allah's word, and who can be more truthful than Allah?

What will be the conduct of those who sit behind when you return?

"Yahlifūna lakum li-tarḍaw ʿanhum. Fa-in tarḍaw ʿanhum fa-inna Allaha lā yarḍā ʿani al-qawmi al-fāsiqīn" ("They will swear to you so that you may be pleased with them. Yet even if you are pleased with them, Allah is certainly not pleased with a people who are defiantly disobedient").

Their scheme is that first these people will wish that the Muslims pardon their offence and overlook it, and afterwards they will try to obtain the pleasure of the Muslims, so that the Muslims continue to treat them in the Islamic society as they did before, on the basis of their outward profession. And these people will escape the consequences set out in this surah for the Muslims: to fight against both the disbelievers and the hypocrites and to be harsh with them. Thus the relations between the believers and non-believers were settled in this way, namely by including the hypocrites among the non-believers.

But here it is made clear that these people, by remaining behind from this jihad, have become defiantly disobedient, and Allah is never pleased with such defiant people, even if they swear many times and strive to please the Muslims. Therefore Allah's command concerning them is the correct command, and even if the whole world, including the Muslims, were pleased with them, it would not benefit them in the least in Allah's sight. The only way to please Allah, His Messenger and the Muslims is for these people to turn away from this defiance, repent, take part in the action of jihad, and enter fully into the religion of Islam.

In this way Allah, without any excuse, exposed the reality of those who stayed behind from jihad, distanced them from the Muslim community, and decided the relationship between the Muslims and the hypocrites, just as previously the relationship between the Muslims and the polytheists had been regulated, or the relationship between the Muslims and the People of the Book had been organised. These were the final and conclusive commands on this subject.

Lesson No. 93 — At a Glance

This lesson discusses the constituent elements of the Islamic society before the Battle of Tabuk. It also details the various groups of believers that were included in the Islamic society at that time, and it deals with the organic formation of the Islamic society. The activities of the different groups are examined and their characteristics are described.

At the beginning of this surah we explained in detail the historical causes that had brought together people of such different temperaments into the Islamic society. It is appropriate here to reproduce a few paragraphs again, so that the circumstances through which the Islamic society was then passing come back to mind. In the Arabian Peninsula, the Quraysh stood like a wall and a dam in the path of the spread of Islam, because the Quraysh held a great position in both religious and worldly affairs. Furthermore, in literary, cultural, scholarly and economic respects they were also worthy of emulation for the other Arabs. For this reason, their taking up opposition and blocking the path of this religion caused all of Arabia to turn away from this religion and not enter Islam; or, if they did not ignore it, the situation was at least such that the people remained in doubt and decided to wait, so that the struggle between the Muslims and the Quraysh would be decided. When the Quraysh were brought low after the Conquest of Makkah, the Hawazin and Thaqif also were brought low. The powerful Jewish tribes of Madinah had already been broken before this. The Banu Qaynuqa and the Banu Nadir were exiled to Syria. The Banu Qurayza also came to an end, and the matter of Khaybar was also settled. Because of these events, Islam now spread throughout the whole Arabian Peninsula, and people began to enter the religion of Islam in multitudes, and within the span of only one year people entered the religion of Islam.

Because the graph of Islam rose horizontally, the weaknesses that had crept into the Islamic ranks as a result of the astonishing victory of the Battle of Badr also entered. Now these weaknesses were on a very large scale. The weak elements that had entered the Islamic ranks after the Major Battle of Badr were purified through education and training to such an extent that, in the seven years from the Major Battle of Badr until the Conquest of Makkah, the Madinan society was close to being free of all weaknesses, and the people of Madinah were about to become a strong base and firm foundation for the Islamic revolution. Here, the body of the foremost Muhajirun and Ansar was so prepared that it was at all times a trustee for the Islamic system. Had this body not existed, it would have been difficult to manage that great revolution. But after the Major Battle of Badr, this body, consisting of the foremost of the Muhajirun and Ansar, continuously guarded that great revolutionary trust. During these seven years, Allah the Exalted prepared and trained this body of Madinah for this task, so that these people could control the flood of human beings who would enter Islam after the great victory. Allah knew well to whom He should entrust the protection of His Message and His revolutionary Message.

The first appearance of these weaknesses occurred on the day of Hunayn. Its mention in Surah al-Tawbah is in these words:

"Allah has already helped you on many occasions, and on the day of Hunayn, when your large numbers made you conceited, but they availed you nothing, and the earth, spacious as it is, became too narrow for you, and you turned back retreating. Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down hosts that you did not see, and punished those who disbelieved; and that is the recompense of the disbelievers." (9:25-26)

The first cause of the initial defeat in this battle was that among the ten thousand Islamic army, two thousand were from the Tulaqa'. These had accepted faith at the time of the Conquest of Makkah and had come out with the Islamic army for jihad. Thus, the presence of these other individuals along with the Islamic army also became a cause of this disorder. The second cause was that Hawazin attacked quite suddenly, and since the army of Islam was not composed solely of the truly trained army of Madinah, whose training had been completed over the previous seven years and who were the real foundation and capital of this movement, disorder arose.

The weaknesses that appeared in the Battle of Hunayn were due to the sudden vertical rise in the numerical strength of Islam. New people entered Islam in multitudes, who were of different degrees in faith and sincerity. There was a difference of ranks among them. In Surah al-Tawbah these weaknesses are discussed, and then from various angles and various aspects severe criticism is made, excerpts of which we have already given earlier.

Now we proceed to explain the verses in detail, to elaborate on this summary.

ٱلْأَعْرَابُ أَشَدُّ كُفْرًا وَنِفَاقًا وَأَجْدَرُ أَلَّا يَعْلَمُوا حُدُودَ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ رَسُولِهِ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ

"The desert Arabs are more severe in disbelief and hypocrisy and more likely not to know the limits of what Allah has revealed to His Messenger. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise." 

Here begins a general comment on the varieties of the desert Arabs. These desert Arabs used to reside around Madinah. Before accepting Islam, these people took the most active part in every action against Islam, and after accepting Islam they were generally of two kinds, which are mentioned in these verses. Before the explanation of these two kinds, there is a general comment on these desert people.

By describing them in these general words, it becomes known what the qualities of bedouinism are; therefore every bedouin's quality is that they are severe disbelievers and extreme hypocrites, and their circumstances are such that they are more ignorant and unaware of the limits of Allah, and they remain distant from the teachings that Allah has sent down upon His Messenger.

That is, the real cause of their lack of knowledge and unawareness is their very circumstances. Living constantly in difficult conditions, these people remain hardened, uncouth and unfamiliar with the ways of religion. Since their contact is always with sensory and material things, they give more importance to material things than to higher values and moral principles. Although faith brings about a change in their temperament, raises their values and priorities, and lifts them from the sensory horizon to focus their gaze upon the spiritual horizons.

Countless incidents of the harshness of the bedouins have been related in hadith and narrations. Allama Ibn Kathir has related most of these incidents.

...

A'mash related from Ibrahim, who said: a bedouin came and sat with Zayd ibn Sawhan. He was talking with his companions. It should be remembered that his hand had been injured in the Battle of Nahawand. The bedouin said, "Your talk seems strange to me, but your hand, I suspect, is stolen." Zayd said, "Why do you doubt because of my hand? Do you not see that it is the left one?" Upon this the bedouin said, "By God, I do not know whether the hand of criminals is cut off on the left or the right." Zayd ibn Sawhan then said:

"The desert Arabs are more severe in disbelief and hypocrisy and more likely not to know the limits of what Allah has revealed to His Messenger." Imam Ahmad narrates from Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Sufyan, from Abu Musa, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, from Ibn Abbas, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said that whoever lives in the countryside becomes harsh, whoever pursues game becomes heedless, and whoever visits rulers falls into trial. Since harshness and oppression are found in great measure among the bedouin people, Allah the Exalted has never sent a Messenger from among the bedouins. All the Messengers were sent from towns and cities.

"And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed, from the people of the towns." (12:109) Once when a bedouin presented a gift to the Messenger of Allah, the Messenger of Allah gave in return several times its value, so he was pleased. The Prophet said that he had intended to accept gifts only from a Qurayshi, a Thaqafi, an Ansari, and a Dawsi, because these people lived in cities, that is, in Makkah, Ta'if, Madinah and Yemen. These people were very gentle in temperament, whereas the bedouins have harshness in their temperament.

Imam Muslim narrates from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and from Abu Kurayb, from Abu Usamah and from Ibn Numayr, from Hisham, from his father, from A'isha, who said: some villagers came to visit the Messenger and said, "Do you kiss your children?" The people said, "Yes." They said, "By God, we do not kiss them." Upon this the Messenger of Allah said, "What can I do if Allah has removed compassion from your hearts?"

In short, countless narrations relate incidents of the harshness and hard-heartedness of the Arab villagers. And some of these incidents relate to events from the period after Islam. Therefore it is quite possible, after Islam too, that some bedouins are more intense in disbelief and hypocrisy, and that there is a greater likelihood that they are ignorant of the limits of Allah which were sent down upon the Messenger of Allah, because they spent their whole lives in villages in an environment of harshness and severity, in which they kept others under control, and when they were weak and subordinate they resorted to hypocrisy and cunning in expressing their hatred. Since these people were not acquainted with the ways of the new religion, they often transgressed the limits.

"And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise." That is, He has full knowledge of the circumstances of His servants. He fully knows their qualities and their temperaments, and He is Wise and Knowing. He has endowed different people with different characteristics, qualities and capacities, and He has divided people into different races, sexes, families and nations.

After the description of the general qualities of the bedouin people, the details are now being given of the differences that have arisen among them, from the angle of the changes that occurred through Islamic training in the Islamic movement. Some hearts, in any case, were such that true faith had entered them, and others were such that they still remained in their former condition, and the state of disbelief and hypocrisy still existed within them.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 9, verse 98:

Since the entire preceding lesson was about the hypocrites of Madinah, the hypocrites are mentioned here before the believers, so that the Bedouin hypocrites and the hypocrites of Madinah are mentioned in one place.

﴿Among the Bedouins there are those who regard what they spend (in the way of Allah) as a forced fine.﴾ Because of their outward declaration of faith, these people are compelled to pay zakat and to give financial support for the military campaigns of the Muslims, for without this outward conformity they could not enjoy the fruits of peaceful life in the Islamic society. Moreover, since the Islamic government was established in Madinah, they had to go along with its word as well. But in reality they regarded all these expenses as a forced fine; they did not spend with a willing heart, because they had no interest in the victory and support of the Muslims.

﴿And they wait for misfortunes to befall you.﴾ They waited for the Muslims to get caught in some trap, to suffer defeat, and for their warriors not to return safe and sound.

Here, a curse from Allah comes upon them. The meaning of a curse from Allah is that the content of the curse practically comes to pass upon them.

﴿Upon them is a circle of evil.﴾ It is as though evil is a circle that has encircled them, and from which they cannot escape in any way. They are completely surrounded. Here the meaning has been presented in a concrete form. This is a figurative embodiment (tajsim) through which the meaning appears more forceful and vivid.

﴿And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.﴾ Here the attributes of Allah, sami' (All-Hearing) and 'alim (All-Knowing), have been brought, which are highly suitable and appropriate to the situation under discussion. These people keep hidden desires in their hearts and conceal them, that some calamity should fall upon the Muslims; moreover, they were concealing disbelief while displaying faith. Therefore Allah hears their secret talk and knows the hidden secrets and the disbelief they conceal.

And the other group, in whose hearts the light of faith has arisen:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 9, verse 99:

They spend (in the way of Allah) out of faith in Allah and hope for the reward of the Last Day, not out of fear of the common people, nor to please those in authority. Their concern is not the profit or loss of this world. Rather, this group has firm faith in Allah and the Last Day, and whatever it spends, it spends purely for the pleasure of Allah. It also desires that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) pray good for them, and the Messenger (ﷺ) prays for someone only when he is pleased with them. And when he prays for someone, it is certain that such a person has attained the true meaning of the prayer, because the prayer of the Messenger (ﷺ) is itself the guarantee of their faith, of their belief in the Last Day, of their seeking the pleasure of Allah, and of their sincerity.

That is why it is immediately announced that the effort of such people has been accepted.

﴿Indeed, it is surely a means of nearness for them﴾, and at the same time it is declared that these people have attained their goal.

﴿Allah will surely admit them into His mercy﴾. Here the Qur'an presents the mercy of Allah in a tangible form, as though it were a palace into which these people will enter, just as earlier it had depicted the hardship surrounding those hypocrites and disbelievers of the opposing party, who harbored malice against the Muslims in their hearts, by portraying it as a circle encompassing them.

﴿Indeed, Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful﴾. He accepts repentance, He accepts charity, He pardons the shortcomings that occurred in the path of Islam, and He does not disappoint whoever seeks His mercy.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 9, verse 100 (part 1 of 2):

After this analysis of the Bedouin society, the following verses now examine the position of the entire Islamic society of that time. It is clearly evident that the Islamic society at that time had four categories. First, the foremost early Muslims among the Emigrants (Muhajirin) and the Helpers (Ansar), and those who truly followed them. Second, the hypocrites (munafiqun), who were both among the people of Madinah and were spread across the settlements around Madinah, and had become highly skilled in the practice of hypocrisy. Third, those whose deeds were a mixture of good and bad. And fourth, those concerning whom Allah had reserved His decision, and they were awaiting that decision.

The first group: ﴿And the foremost, the first of the Emigrants and the Helpers, and those who followed them in goodness — Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him, and He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great achievement.﴾ The Emigrants and Helpers who took the lead in responding to the call of faith, along with those who came afterwards following them with uprightness: Allah was pleased with them, and they were pleased with Allah; He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. This is the supreme success.

The second group: ﴿And among those around you of the Bedouins are hypocrites, and among the people of Madinah as well; they have persisted in hypocrisy. You do not know them; We know them. We will punish them twice, then they will be returned to a great punishment.﴾ Among the Bedouins who live around you there are many hypocrites, and likewise among the residents of Madinah too there are hypocrites who have become adept in hypocrisy. You do not know them, We know them. The time is near when We will punish them doubly, and then they will be brought back to a greater punishment.

The third group: ﴿And others have acknowledged their sins; they mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil. Perhaps Allah will turn to them in forgiveness; indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ There are also others who have confessed their sins; their deeds are mixed, some good and some bad. It is not unlikely that Allah will again turn mercifully towards them, for He is Forgiving and Merciful. O Prophet, take from their wealth a charity to purify them and to elevate them (in the path of goodness), and pray for them, for your prayer is a source of tranquility for them; Allah hears and knows all. Do they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants and accepts their charities, and that Allah is Most Forgiving and Merciful? And say to them, O Prophet: work, and Allah, His Messenger, and the believers will see your conduct, and then you will be returned to the One who knows the hidden and the manifest, and He will inform you of what you used to do.

The fourth group: ﴿And others are held in suspense for the command of Allah: either He will punish them or He will turn to them in forgiveness. Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾ There are some others whose matter is still pending the command of Allah; whether He punishes them or again turns mercifully to them. Allah knows all and is Wise.

Apparently, this commentary on the constituent elements of the Islamic society of that time was revealed after the return from Tabuk and after hearing the excuses of the people. These excuses were presented both by the hypocrites who remained behind despite the emphatic command of that campaign, and by some sincere believers. Among them, some presented genuine excuses; some tied themselves to a pillar of the Prophet's Mosque and insisted on remaining bound until the Messenger of Allah untied them; and some had presented no excuse at all and hoped that Allah would forgive them. These were the three individuals who had remained behind, concerning whom the Prophet had not issued any ruling, until Allah revealed forgiveness for them and accepted their repentance, as the details about them will come shortly. These people belonged to the various categories of those who had joined the Islamic movement at that time, and after the Tabuk campaign all kinds of people were within the Islamic ranks. Allah, the Exalted, was informing the Prophet ﷺ well about the ranks of the movement at that time, what the days and nights of the Islamic movement were, and at the conclusion of this first stage of the Islamic movement, namely at the completion of the revolution in the Arabian Peninsula and at the beginning of the stage of global revolution, he was being told who the people of the next stage would be, so that the Islamic movement could, with them, establish the system of worship of One Allah on a global level, and thus free every human being across the entire earth from the servitude of any human being, so that no human on earth would remain the slave of another in any way.

The Islamic movement had an urgent need to know clearly on what ground it was to play, what it had to do at every stage and every step. This knowledge was necessary so that people could know what their position was and what measures it had to take for the next stage.

﴿And the foremost, the first of the Emigrants and the Helpers, and those who followed them in goodness — Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him, and He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great achievement.﴾
The Emigrants and Helpers who took the lead in responding to the call of faith, along with those who came afterwards following them with uprightness: Allah was pleased with them, and they were pleased with Allah; He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. This is the supreme success.

This group of Muslims, consisting of three elements — the foremost early Emigrants, the foremost early Helpers, and those who came after them with uprightness — these three categories were the backbone of the Islamic movement of that time, and after the conquest of Makkah in the Arabian Peninsula these were the true bearers of the call. In the tenth juz' we have given details of this surah while commenting on it. In short, it was these people who held firmly to this call and who had full control over that society. It was they who sustained that society in every good and every bad condition, and every movement should well understand that trials of hardship are much easier compared with the trial of prosperity and victory.

Who are the foremost early Emigrants? In our opinion, they are those who migrated before Badr. Likewise, the foremost early Helpers are those who believed before the Battle of Badr. As for those who followed them with uprightness, they are those who passed the test of the Tabuk campaign. These were the people who adopted the Islamic way of life, believed fully, and then fulfilled the demands of faith, and reached a high standard of faith, although those who embraced Islam in the most severe circumstances are ahead of them.

Narrations differ concerning who the foremost early Emigrants and Helpers are. One view is that they are those who migrated and gave support before Badr. One view is that they are those who prayed facing both qiblahs. Some have said that they are the People of Badr. Some people say that they are those who prayed facing both qiblahs. Some have said that they are the People of Badr. Some people say that they are those who migrated and gave support before the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. Some have said that they are the People of the Pledge of Ridwan. Our view is the one we have mentioned above, and we have arrived at this view after a deep study of the stages of the formation of Islamic society and the stages of the believers and the formation of the different classes of believers. And Allah knows best.

It would be good to quote here a few sentences from the tenth juz' which we wrote there about the formation of Islamic society and the determination of the ranks of the believers within it, so that those points are refreshed in the minds of readers, and they need not turn back to the tenth part again. And in the light of these points, readers can well understand the class classification of Islamic society. This was the final classification of Islamic society, because the verses under discussion are among the verses of the last period of the Holy Qur'an.

"The Islamic movement arose in Makkah in extremely severe circumstances; its opposition was the jahili society of the Quraysh. The call of the Islamic movement, the word 'There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah', was seen by the jahili society of the Quraysh as a threat to itself, because this word was in reality a declaration of a kind of rebellion against all those societies and their sovereignty whose sovereignty was not derived from the sovereignty of Allah and the rule of Allah. This word was, as it were, an announcement that the one who utters it has declared rebellion against all the powers of tyranny and is loyal only to the rule and authority of Allah. Then the jahili society of the Quraysh immediately sensed that this new call was rising in the form of a distinct movement under a new leadership, the leadership of Muhammad ﷺ. And the motto of this new movement from the first day has been that obedience be rendered to Allah and His Messenger, and the jahili, arrogant and oppressive leadership of the Quraysh be refused obedience.

As soon as the Quraysh sensed the above danger, that the existing system, its interests and principles were threatened, that jahili society raised a storm of violence and oppression against the individuals of the Islamic movement. They began to use all the methods within their power against this new movement, this new society and this new leadership, including persecution, conspiracies, base weapons and mischief-making, all of these.

The jahili society of the Quraysh suddenly rose up and began to defend itself, and that society began to protect itself in exactly the same way as a living person wishes to save himself from the dangers of death. This reaction of the Quraysh's jahili society was entirely natural, and whenever any call begins to invite people only to the worship of the Lord of the worlds, to His lordship and sovereignty, the reaction of the jahili society established at that time is exactly like this, because in jahili society human beings are slaves of human beings, whereas the Islamic call is only towards the worship of the Lord of the worlds. Whenever the Islamic call arises in the form of an organic movement, jahiliyyah will rise up against it, just as an opposite stands against its opposite. And every worker of such a movement comes into the grip of jahili society and has to face every kind of trial and hardship. And sometimes, as a result of this violence, the blood of the workers is also shed. When such circumstances arise, the ones who bear witness to the truth in the ranks of the Islamic movement are only those who have decided that they will offer even their lives in the path of Allah. Membership of this call, this movement and this new society is adopted only by such devoted people who have resolved to bear torment, trials, hunger, poverty and hardships. Sometimes they even have to be prepared for imprisonment and death."

Among the Arab society of Makkah, it was precisely such strong, powerful and high-minded people who became the foundation of Islamic leadership. Those who had entered the movement in droves without bearing hardships and without facing trials later apostatized and returned to jahiliyyah. These high-minded people were very few in number, and this is well known and evident, because apart from the chosen, distinguished and selected people who had been prepared for this purpose, nobody was ready to adopt the difficult and perilous path of Islam in place of jahiliyyah.

The foremost Emigrants were among such people, who were unmatched in their time; they were the fundamental asset and firm foundation of this religion, and they responded in the early Makkan period. These very people, when they reached Madinah, were the driving force of this movement and the central pillars of the religion. Alongside them in Madinah, similarly high-minded individuals from among the Helpers joined them. Although these people did not bear the hardships the Emigrants bore, yet, since they had pledged allegiance to the Prophet at Aqabah in extremely difficult circumstances, these people too were pure-hearted and of original disposition, and they possessed the basic qualities required of the first bearers of this religion. Allama Ibn Kathir, in his tafsir, says: Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi narrates that at the time of the Pledge of Aqabah, Abdullah ibn Rawahah said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Set down for yourself and for your Lord whatever conditions you wish to impose upon us." The Prophet said: "For my Lord, I impose the condition that you worship Him and associate nothing with Him; and for myself, I impose the condition that you will defend me just as you defend your own lives and property." The people said: "If we do this, what reward will we have?" The Prophet said: "Paradise." They said: "This is a very good bargain; we will neither seek its cancellation nor demand that the other party seek its cancellation."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 9, verse 100 (part 2 of 2):

These people who were pledging allegiance at the hand of the Messenger ﷺ wanted nothing but Paradise. With great certainty they also declared that they would neither revoke this bargain nor permit the other party to put off this bargain. And they knew that this pledge was no ordinary pledge. They knew that now Quraysh would turn against them, and not only Quraysh but all of Arabia would fall upon them, and that they would no longer be able to live in peace alongside the jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance), which had pitched its tents around them and held sway over the Arabian Peninsula and the surroundings of Madinah.

From this narration it becomes known that the Ansar had knowledge of this, and it was certain knowledge, of what the consequences of this pledge would be. They had also clearly understood that the Messenger ﷺ had not promised them any worldly reward or recompense. Indeed, the Messenger ﷺ did not even promise them that they would succeed in this aim in this world, apart from Paradise. No other promise was made to them. This was the extent of their understanding of the religion, and this was the depth of their love for this religion. Therefore these people attained the lofty station of the foremost (al-sabiqun al-awwalun), and they were counted among the first companions of the Muhajirin, who took part in laying the foundations of the building of the religion and constructed that edifice. These people were the backbone of Madinan society.

But the society and community of Madinah did not remain equally sincere and pure. Islam appeared from Madinah, spread far and wide, and many people, especially among those of rank and leadership, began to echo the words of their people so that their leadership would remain intact. When the great event of the Battle of Badr took place, the leader of such people, Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, commented on it that the matter had now gone far ahead, and therefore he accepted Islam as hypocrisy. It is necessary to note that some people were swept away by the flood of Islam, and they accepted Islam in imitation of others. Although these imitative people were not hypocrites, they had not yet understood Islam well, nor had they fully taken on the Islamic mould, and because of this there was disorder in the Islamic society of Madinah, since different people stood at different levels of faith.

The Qur'an began to train such people under the leadership of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Since people of various levels of faith and moral conduct had entered this society, it was necessary that balance, harmony and concord be created among these different elements, so that the new society would be established on firm foundations.

When we study the Madani surahs in order of revelation (although this order is known only approximately), we find that the Qur'an continuously carried on its struggle to train and purify the new elements that kept entering the Islamic society, because the people who came were of different families and temperaments and kept coming continuously. Although Quraysh prevented people from entering the religion of Islam and incited all the Arab tribes to war against this religion, the Jews likewise were an obstacle in the path of this religion, and they too were busy night and day so that all nations would attack this new religion and uproot it. Therefore there was great need for the training of the newly arriving people.

Despite this continuous struggle of training and purification, at times, especially in difficult and severe moments, weaknesses would appear in the ranks of the Muslims. In some quarters hypocrisy would arise, in others hesitation and uncertainty. Some people would be stingy in spending wealth in the path of the new religion. Some would fear facing dangers. Sometimes people could not understand what the Islamic bond and relationship among them was, and what the status now was of their former jahili ties of kinship and association. They did not understand the Islamic brotherhood well. From the verses of this surah we clearly come to know how the Qur'anic verses train such people in various ways and from various angles, and what methods they adopt for this purpose. We present some of these verses as examples.

But the basic structure of the Muslim society in Madinah was sound, because in this structure the primary importance belonged only to those among the Muhajirin and Ansar who were the foremost (al-sabiqun al-awwalun) and were extremely firm people. Moreover, in the building and training of this society there was such unity, concord and firmness in its structure that it overcame those weaknesses, ailments and disunity, and the collective social system also supported those elements who were affected by fear and anxiety, who had not yet been fully trained, who had not yet blended into this new society, and in whom full harmony had not yet been produced.

In any case, gradually these new elements were being trained. They were blending into this society, their purification was continuously taking place, and they kept joining the real strength of the Islamic society. And the number of the weak-hearted, the disobedient and the wavering in certainty was decreasing day by day, as were those who feared their interests and those people in whose hearts the Islamic worldview had not yet fully settled, so that they would base their social relations also upon this worldview.

To the point that before the Conquest of Makkah the situation had become such that the Islamic society had come close to the level of perfection in education, training and its outward form, and most people from among the Muhajirin and Ansar had begun to follow in the footsteps of the foremost (al-sabiqun al-awwalun). And this society had become so pure and trained that it was closer to the standard required by the Islamic system of life.

It is correct that by then there had developed in this society values directly connected with Islamic principles. Because of these values, some people within the movement were more distinguished, more steadfast, and ahead of others in the ranks of the movement. For example, among the Muhajirin and Ansar, the foremost (al-sabiqun al-awwalun), the people of Badr, and those who gave the Pledge of Ridwan at Hudaybiyah. Then those who took part in jihad, spending and fighting before the Conquest of Makkah, and those who did so afterwards. From the texts of the Book of Allah, the hadith of the Prophet, and certain practical steps of the movement, the evidence of this differentiation of ranks and values is found. These Islamic values and this differentiation were determined from the standpoint of advancing the Islamic worldview.

From the above excerpts it is well known how the foremost (al-sabiqun al-awwalun) among the Ansar and Muhajirin were raised to that lofty station by their faith standard and their movement's trials, and from this we come to know well how important and factually grounded the role of the Companions (ṣaḥābah) is in the whole of human history in building Islam and in the practical establishment of the Islamic system. And from this we also come to know what the true meaning is of Allah's saying (raḍiyallāhu ʿanhum wa raḍū ʿanh).

Allah was pleased with them, and the outcome of Allah's pleasure is reward from Allah. Allah's pleasure is itself a great blessing. And the meaning of people being pleased with Allah is that they are content with Allah, they accept Allah's decrees, and they think well of Allah's judgments. They thank Allah for the blessings He has given them, and if a trial comes upon them from Allah, they bear it patiently. But from the words and the manner in which the pleasure is mentioned here, it appears that between this chosen group and the Divine Being there will be a general, deep, mutual, far-reaching exchange of pleasure from both sides, and Allah has granted this chosen group the station that they became capable of being pleased with Allah, although Allah is the Lord and Ruler and they are His creatures and servants. The relationship between the two parties is so deep and so magnificent that it cannot be described in human words. However, this status of the Companions opens up only to the person who has spiritual longing, whose heart is open to the meanings of the Qur'an, and whose perception and consciousness are joined to the higher world, between the lines of the Qur'anic texts.

This is their lasting and special relationship with their Lord: that they became pleased with Allah and Allah became pleased with them. What is the sign of this pleasure? That: "He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great achievement" (9:100).

This is one standard, and in contrast there are also people of a second level.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 9, verse 101:

Earlier, a general discussion of the hypocrites (munafiqun) has taken place, and their conditions have been revealed. Their connection was with the people of Madinah as well as with the Bedouin hypocrites spread around Madinah. Here a particular category of the hypocrites is being mentioned. These are the people who have become adept in the art of hypocrisy (hunar-e-nifaq), and they have acquired very great skill in this art. They have become so immersed in the practice of hypocrisy, and have become such masters of it, that even the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), despite his prophetic insight, could not recognize them, although by that period he had gathered a good deal of information about them and had passed through a long phase of experience.

Allah says that these kinds of hypocrites still exist in Madinah and in the population surrounding it. The Prophet and the believers have been reassured regarding the plots and the sharp attacks of this kind of hypocrite. Allah, on the one hand, tells the Messenger that their intrigues are not within his knowledge, and at the same time they are severely warned that they cannot escape from this. Their deceit, cunning and crafty schemes are not effective against Allah; Allah will humiliate and disgrace them in this world and in the Hereafter, and in the Hereafter they will be given a double punishment.

﴿You do not know them; We know them. We will punish them twice; then they will be returned to a great punishment.﴾ (Qur'an 9:101)

The question arises: will they be punished twice in this world? The meaning that is easiest to grasp is this: first, they will be severely distressed by the fact that, despite their cunning schemes within the Islamic society, their reality was made clear to the people; and second, a punishment at the time of death, when their souls will be seized harshly and, while their souls are being seized, blows will be struck upon their faces and backs; or the punishment of seeing the Muslims receiving victory after victory while they burn inwardly with envy; and another punishment, that these people live constantly in fear that their condition will be revealed to the Muslims and that they will become the target of the act of jihad.

These were the two extreme standards, and between them there are some people who are in an intermediate position.

1: Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi (may Allah have mercy on them) narrated in al-Dala'il from Ibn 'Abbas (raḍiyallahu 'anhu) that, concerning the verse ﴿And others who have acknowledged their sins: they mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil﴾, he said: They were ten men who remained behind from the Battle of Tabuk from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned, seven of them tied themselves to the pillars of the mosque. When the Prophet (ﷺ) passed by them in the mosque and saw them, he said: "Who are these people who have tied themselves up?" The Companions said: "They are Abu Lubabah and his companions, who remained behind from you, O Messenger of Allah. They tied themselves up and swore that no one would release them until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) releases them and accepts their excuse." He said: "I also swear by Allah that I will not release them, nor will I accept their excuse, until Allah Himself releases them, because they turned away from me and remained behind from fighting alongside the Muslims." When this reached them, they said: "We will not release ourselves until Allah Himself is the One who releases us." Then Allah revealed this verse: ﴿And others who have acknowledged their sins: they mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil. Perhaps Allah will accept their repentance﴾, and that it is likely that Allah will accept their repentance, for He is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful. When this verse was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) conveyed it to them, released them and accepted their excuse. They brought their wealth and said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is our wealth; accept it on our behalf as charity and seek forgiveness for us." He said: "I have not been commanded to take your wealth." Then Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow, and pray for them﴾. He said: seek forgiveness for them. Then (He said): ﴿Indeed, your prayer is a comfort for them﴾, meaning your supplication will be a mercy for them. The Prophet (ﷺ) took the charity from them and sought forgiveness for them. Three of them did not tie themselves to the pillars; their matter was deferred for one year. They did not know whether they would be punished or whether their repentance would be accepted. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿Certainly Allah has turned in mercy to the Prophet and the Emigrants and the Helpers who followed him in the hour of difficulty﴾ up to the end of the verse, then ﴿and to the three who were left behind﴾ up to ﴿then He turned to them in mercy that they might repent; indeed Allah is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful﴾ (9:118), meaning: "provided they remained upon the straight path."

2: Abu al-Shaykh (raḥimahullah) narrated from al-Dahhak (raḥimahullah) a report in the same manner, without a chain of differences.

3: Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il narrated from Mujahid (raḥimahullah) that, concerning ﴿they acknowledged their sins﴾, he said: They were Abu Lubabah. When he said something to the Qurayzah, he simultaneously gestured toward his throat, meaning: Muhammad will slaughter you if you come down to his judgment.

The tying of Abu Lubabah (raḍiyallahu 'anhu) to the pillar:

4: Al-Bayhaqi (raḥimahullah) narrated in al-Dala'il from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab (raḥimahullah) that the Banu Qurayzah (Jews) were allies of Abu Lubabah. They looked down at him from above and began calling him to the judgment of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They said: "O Abu Lubabah, do you order us to come down?" He gestured with his hand toward his throat, saying: "You will be slaughtered." When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was informed of this, he said to him: "Do you think that Allah is unaware of your hand, when you gestured with it toward your throat?" Then they remained for a while until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out for the expedition of Tabuk, which was a difficult jihad. Among those who remained behind from the expedition of Tabuk was Abu Lubabah. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned from the expedition, Abu Lubabah came, greeted him, and the Prophet (ﷺ) turned his face away from him. Abu Lubabah became distressed and tied himself to the pillar of repentance, which is near the door of Umm Salamah, for seven days and nights in intense heat, remaining in that state. During those days he ate nothing and did not drink even a drop, and he said: "I will remain in this place until I depart this world, or until Allah accepts my repentance." He remained in this condition until, from weakness, he could no longer hear anyone's voice, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would look at him morning and evening. Then Allah accepted his repentance. A call came: "Allah has accepted your repentance." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent a man to him to release him from his rope, but he refused, saying that no one should release him except the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came and released him with his own blessed hand. When he regained his health, Abu Lubabah said: "O Messenger of Allah, I will give up the house of my people in which this mistake occurred, and I wish to migrate to you. Grant me a dwelling, and I wish to give from my wealth as charity to Allah and His Messenger." He said: "A third of your wealth is sufficient for you." Abu Lubabah migrated from the house of his people and took up residence with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he gave a third of his wealth as charity. Then he repented, and after that nothing was seen from him in Islam except righteous deeds and goodness, until he departed this world.

5: Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh (raḥimahumullah) narrated from Ibn 'Abbas (raḍiyallahu 'anhu) that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out for the expedition of Tabuk, Abu Lubabah and two men with him remained behind from the Prophet (ﷺ) (from jihad). Then Abu Lubabah and the two men reflected, became remorseful, and became certain of their destruction. They said: "We were living at ease and comfort with our neighbours and women, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the believers are engaged in jihad with him. By Allah, we will certainly tie ourselves to the pillars and will not release ourselves until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) releases us and accepts our excuse." Abu Lubabah went and tied himself, and two men with him also tied themselves to the pillars of the mosque, while three men remained who did not tie themselves. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned from jihad, he went straight to the mosque, and passing by them he said: "Who are these people tied to the pillars?" One man said: "They are Abu Lubabah and his two companions, who remained behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They made a covenant with Allah that they would not release themselves until you release them and are pleased with them, and they have acknowledged their sins." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Allah, I will not release them until I am commanded to release them, and I will not accept their excuse until Allah accepts their excuse, because they remained behind from the Muslims and turned away from fighting with them." Then Allah revealed this verse: ﴿And others who have acknowledged their sins﴾, and it is likely that Allah will do so. When the verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) released them and accepted their excuse. Abu Lubabah and his companions came with their wealth and said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Take our wealth and give it on our behalf as charity, and pray for mercy for us." They began to say: "Seek forgiveness for us and purify us." He said: "I will not take anything from it until I am commanded." Then Allah revealed this verse: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity﴾. The narrator said: Three men remained who had opposed Abu Lubabah; they had not repented and had not mentioned anything, and no verse was revealed concerning their excuse. The earth became constricted for them despite its vastness, and concerning them Allah said: ﴿And others are deferred to the command of Allah﴾. Some people began to say: "They are destroyed, since no excuse was revealed for them," and others said: "It is likely that Allah will accept their repentance." They waited for the command of Allah, until this verse was revealed: ﴿Certainly Allah has turned in mercy to the Prophet﴾ up to ﴿and to the three who were left behind﴾, meaning they were awaiting Allah's command; then the command of repentance was revealed concerning them, and they acted upon it.

6: Ibn Abi Hatim (raḥimahullah) narrated from Ibn Zayd (raḥimahullah) that, concerning ﴿And others who have acknowledged their sins﴾, he said: They were eight men who tied themselves to the pillars. Among them were Kurdam, Mirdas, and Abu Lubabah.

7: Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah (raḥimahullah), concerning ﴿And others who have acknowledged their sins: they mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil﴾, that it was mentioned to us that they were seven men who remained behind from the expedition of Tabuk. Four of them were those who had mixed good deeds with bad deeds. (Their names were:) Jadd ibn Qays, Abu Lubabah, Haram and Aws. All of them were from the Ansar. Their repentance was accepted, and these are the ones concerning whom it was said: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity﴾.

8: Ibn Abi Hatim (raḥimahullah) narrated from al-Suddi (raḥimahullah) that, concerning ﴿mixed a righteous deed﴾ and ﴿another that was evil﴾, he said: They are people of righteous deeds who fought alongside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and ﴿another that was evil﴾ refers to those who remained behind.

9: Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn al-Dunya in al-Tawbah, and Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Abu al-Shaykh and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, narrated from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi (raḥimahullah) that he said: There is no verse in the Qur'an that, in my view, gives greater hope to this ummah than this verse: ﴿And others who have acknowledged their sins: they mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil﴾.

Repenting from evil deeds:

10: Abu al-Shaykh and al-Bayhaqi (raḥimahullah) narrated from Mutarrif (raḥimahullah) that he said: I was lying on my bed at night reflecting upon the Qur'an, and I presented my deeds against the deeds of the people of Paradise. Suddenly their deeds were intense and severe, such as ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾ (51:17), and ﴿who spend the night before their Lord prostrating and standing﴾ (25:64), and ﴿Is one who is devoutly obedient during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing﴾ (39:9). So I did not consider myself among them. Then I presented myself against the verses: ﴿What led you into Saqar?﴾ (74:42), and ﴿They said: We were not of those who prayed﴾ (74:43), up to ﴿and we used to deny the Day of Judgment﴾ (74:46). So I reflected upon the people who denied, and I did not consider myself among them. Then this verse was given as a command: ﴿And others who have acknowledged their sins: they mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil﴾. So I hoped that I would be among them, and O my brothers, you too will be among them.

11: Abu al-Shaykh, Abu al-Mundhir, Abu Nu'aym in al-Ma'rifah, and Ibn 'Asakir with a strong chain narrated from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah (raḍiyallahu 'anhu) that six men remained behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the expedition of Tabuk. They were: Abu Lubabah Aws ibn Jizam, Tha'labah ibn Wadi'ah, Ka'b ibn Malik, Murarah ibn Rabi' and Hilal ibn Umayyah. Of them, Abu Lubabah Aws ibn Jizam and Tha'labah came, tied themselves to the pillars, and brought their wealth, saying: "O Messenger of Allah, accept the wealth which we have left behind from you." They were deferred for forty days. They went out and pitched their tents, and the Prophet (ﷺ) separated them from their women. No Muslim was their friend, and no one drew near to them. Then this verse was revealed concerning them: ﴿and those three who were left behind﴾ up to ﴿the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful﴾. Umm Salamah sent a man to Ka'b and gave him the good news.

12: Ibn Abi Hatim (raḥimahullah) narrated from Ibn Shawdhab (raḥimahullah) that al-Ahnaf ibn Qays said: I presented myself to the Qur'an, and I found no verse more resembling this verse in my view, namely: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity, and others who have acknowledged their sins: they mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil﴾.

13: Abu al-Shaykh (raḥimahullah) narrated from Malik ibn Dinar (raḥimahullah) that he asked al-Hasan al-Basri concerning Allah's saying: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity, and others who have acknowledged their sins: they mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil﴾. He said: "O Malik, they repented; it is hoped that Allah will accept their repentance, and that hope is binding from Allah" (i.e., it is established).

Asking the Companions about dreams:

14: Bukhari, Muslim, Tirmidhi, Nasa'i and Ibn Mardawayh (may Allah have mercy on them) narrated from Samurah ibn Jundub (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would often ask his Companions, "Has anyone of you seen a dream?" One morning he said to us, "Last night two comers came to me, said, 'Let us go,' and I went with them. They took me to a holy land, and we came upon a man lying down while another man stood over him with a stone, suddenly striking him on the head so that his head was crushed and the stone rolled away. He went after the stone, picked it up, and returned to him, and his head was restored just as it was. Then he did to him the same thing again." I said, "Subhan Allah! Who are these two?" My companions said to me, "Go on." So we went on and came upon a man lying on his back, while another man stood over him with an iron hook. Suddenly he came to one side of his face and tore open his cheek down to his nape, and likewise his nostril down to his nape and his eye down to his nape. Then he came to the other side and did to it the same as he had done to the first side. When he had finished with that side, the first side would be restored just as it was, and then he returned and did to it as he had done the first time. I said, "Subhan Allah! Who are these two?" My companions said to me, "Go on." So we went on and came upon something like a furnace, with noise and voices in it. We looked into it, and suddenly in it were men and women, naked, with a flame of fire rising up from beneath them. Whenever the flame reached them, they screamed and wailed. I said, "Who are these?" The two said to me, "Go on." So we went on and came upon a red river, like blood, in which a man was swimming, while on the bank of the river was another man with many stones before him. When the swimmer came near the man who had gathered stones, the latter would open his mouth and the other would throw a stone into it. Then the swimmer would go off swimming, and would return to him, and whenever he returned, he would open his mouth and the other would throw a stone into it. I said to the two, "Who are these two?" My two companions said, "Go on." So we went on and came upon a man of extremely ugly appearance, the ugliest of men you have ever seen, and beside him was a fire which he was kindling and running around. I said to him, "Who is this?" They said to me, "Go on." So we went on and came upon a dark green garden, with every kind of spring splendour in it, and suddenly in the midst of the garden's paths was a man of tall stature, so tall that his head seemed to reach the sky, and around him were many children, more than I had ever seen. I asked them, "Who is this?" They said to me, "Go on." So we went on and reached a great garden, larger and better than I had ever seen. They said to me, "Climb up in it." We climbed up and reached a city built of gold and silver bricks. We came to the gate of the city and asked for it to be opened, and it was opened for us. We entered it and met many people in it, some of whom were so handsome that you have never seen more handsome, and some so ugly that you have never seen more ugly. The two said to them, "Go and bathe in that river," which was wide and flowing, and its water was white like milk. They went and plunged into it, then returned to us, and all their ugliness had left them, and they had become extremely handsome. The two said to me, "This is your mansion and your abode." I said to them, "May Allah bless you both. Leave me to enter it." They said, "Not now, but you will certainly enter it."

Seeing Hell in a dream:
I said to the two, "Tonight I have seen amazing sights. What was it that I saw?" They said to me: The first man, whose head was crushed by a man with a stone, is the one who learned the Qur'an but then abandoned it and slept through the obligatory prayer (i.e., did not perform the prayer). This will be done to him until the Day of Resurrection. The man whose cheek was torn to his nape, his nostril to his nape and his eye to his nape is one who would go out in the morning and tell lies, and his lie would spread throughout the horizons; this will be done to him until the Day of Resurrection. The naked men and women in the furnace are adulterous men and adulterous women. The man who came to the one swimming in the river and pelted him with stones is one who consumed interest. That ugly man beside the fire, kindling it, is the keeper of Hell, Malik. The tall man in the garden is Ibrahim (peace be upon him). The children around him are newborns who died upon the fitrah. The people who were half handsome and half ugly are those who mixed righteous and wicked deeds together; Allah has overlooked them. And I am Jibril, and this is Mika'il.

15: Al-Khatib (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated in his History from Abu Musa (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: I saw some men whose skins were being cut with fire scissors. I said, "Who are these?" It was said, "They are those who adorned themselves with things that were not lawful for them." And I saw a foul-smelling tent from which came screaming. I said, "What is this?" It was said, "These are the women who beautified themselves for them with what was not lawful for them." And I saw a people bathing in water of major impurity (janabah). I said, "Who are these?" It was said, "They are the people who mixed the good and the bad together."

16: Ibn Sa'd (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from Aswad ibn Qays al-Adwi (may Allah have mercy on him) that Hasan ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) met Habib ibn Maslamah one day and said, "O Habib! You have a Lord for matters other than the obedience of Allah." He said, "But my reach extends only to your door, and they are not like that." He said, "Of course they are not. But you obeyed Mu'awiyah on the condition of the small, fleeting worldly life. If they stand with you in your worldly affairs, they will surely sit with you in your religion. And if what you did was your own deed, it is a matter of goodness and benefit, as Allah said: ﴿They have mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil﴾. But you are like what Allah said: ﴿No! Rather, what they used to earn has covered over their hearts﴾."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 9, verse 103:

﴿Take alms from their wealth﴾. That is, take from the wealth they are giving as an expiation for their sins. According to some, the alms (sadaqah) here means zakah.

﴿To purify them﴾ — the alms will purify them from sins, or by taking the alms you will purify them. In the first case, the feminine third-person pronoun of tatahhurahum refers back to sadaqah. In the second case the address is in the second person and is directed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

﴿And cleanse them thereby﴾. That is, you will make them pure and clean through the alms: you will increase their good deeds and raise them to the ranks of sincere believers.

Ibn Jarir has transmitted this statement of Hadrat Ibn Abbas through the chain of Ali ibn Abi Talhah, and has transmitted the same meaning from the statements of Hadrat Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Dahhak and Zayd ibn Aslam. However, al-Baghawi has written that according to the narration of Ata', in the statement of Hadrat Ibn Abbas, the number of those who tied themselves to the pillars is given as only five, among whom was Abu Lubabah. In the statements of Hadrat Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Zayd ibn Aslam it is given as eight, and in the statements of Qatadah and Dahhak as seven. Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Abi Hatim have transmitted, through the narration of Awfi, the account of Hadrat Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out on a (certain) expedition, but Abu Lubabah and five other men remained behind (and could not go on the jihad). Then Abu Lubabah and two of the five men reflected, repented, and became certain of their own destruction (that is, the ruin of their religion).
