The Messenger (ﷺ) said: May Allah have mercy on Abu Dharr; he walks alone, will die alone and will be raised alone. Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Salihi said: And so it happened. When he reached the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and related his account, the Messenger (ﷺ) said: Abu Dharr! The step you took to reach me, Allah has forgiven you one of your sins in exchange for it.

Abu Khaythamah was reported by Tabarani on the authority of Abu Khaythamah himself, and Ibn Ishaq and Muhammad ibn Umar related on the authority of their shaykhs, that when some days had passed since the departure of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Abu Khaythamah (one day) reached his home; the day was hot. Upon reaching home he saw that within the garden his two wives had built two separate arbours, and each had sprinkled water to cool her hut, had cooled water for Abu Khaythamah and had prepared food. On reaching the doorway of the hut, he observed this condition and inspected what his wives had done, and he said: Subhan Allah! Allah has forgiven the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) his earlier and later lapses, yet he sets out at the height of midday, in hot wind and heat, carrying his weapons on his shoulder (in the way of Allah), and Abu Khaythamah is sitting in the cool shade with a beautiful wife, with prepared food, in his own property. This is not just. By Allah, I will not enter the hut of either of you, but will join the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from behind. Prepare provisions for me, both of you. The wives prepared the provisions. Then he mounted his camel and set out in search of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), until he joined the Messenger (ﷺ). On the way, Abu Khaythamah had been joined by Umayr ibn Wahb al-Jumahi, who was also searching for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the two went together. When Abu Khaythamah approached near the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) near Tabuk (that is, at a distance where people could see him), the people said: A rider is coming. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: It will be Abu Khaythamah. The Companions said: By Allah, it is Abu Khaythamah. The Messenger (ﷺ) said to Abu Khaythamah: Abu Khaythamah! May you be ruined. Abu Khaythamah related the event to him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke some words of goodness on his behalf and offered a prayer of goodness.

﴿Then He turned to them in mercy﴾: the repetition of "taba" is for emphasis. In the previous verse, the acceptance of repentance was expressed concerning the permission given to the hypocrites not to take part in the jihad; and in this verse there is an announcement of forgiveness for the inclination of hearts that had begun to arise from friendship with the hypocrites. Or, in the previous verse was expressed the granting of the ability to repent, and in this verse the acceptance of repentance. Or, in this verse the forgiveness is expressed in contrast to the severity and affliction that people had endured on that journey.

﴿Indeed, He is Kind and Merciful to them﴾: Indeed Allah is very compassionate and merciful towards them. Al-Baghawi wrote that Ibn Abbas said: Those upon whom Allah has shown mercy, He will never punish them for that sin.

And [He also turned in mercy to] the three who were left behind. [Verse 118]

ʿAlā al-thalāthati (وعلی الثلثۃ) is in the conjunctive relation (ʿaṭf) to ʿalayhim (عَلَیْھِمْ). Khulifū (خُلِفُوْا) means that they stayed behind from the expedition of Tabuk and did not go with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It has also been stated that the meaning is: those whose matter was left in suspense (multawi rakha gaya) until the acceptance of the repentance of Abu Lubabah and his companions. These three were Kaʿb ibn Mālik, the poet Mararah ibn Rabiʿ, and Hilal ibn Umayyah. They were Ansar.

Al-Shaykhan in the Sahihayn, and Imam Ahmad, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Ishaq and ʿAbd al-Razzaq, have related the account of Kaʿb ibn Mālik, who said: "In whichever expedition the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out, I was never absent with him in any expedition except the expedition of Tabuk. However, I did not take part in the expedition of Badr, though no one was rebuked by Allah for not going to Badr. The reason was that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had set out intending the caravan of Quraysh (he had no intention of fighting), but without any appointed promise, the enemy met them by the decree of Allah. I was also present on the night of ʿAqabah (that is, at the third ʿAqabah occasion, when the Ansar pledged allegiance; I too was present there), where we all made a firm covenant upon Islam. Although among people the fame of Badr is greater, in my view, my presence at the night of ʿAqabah is not superior to participation in Badr."

The account of my own situation is this: at the time of the expedition of Tabuk I was very strong and well-off; never before had I been so prosperous and strong. At that time, for the first time, I had two riding camels; never before had I had two mounts. It was the custom of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that when he intended a campaign, he would mention another campaign by way of concealment (tawriyah), and would say: "War is a secret stratagem." When the time of the Tabuk expedition came, the heat was severe, the journey was long, the way lay through deserts, and the enemies were numerous; therefore the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) openly declared to the Muslims and gave them accurate information about his destination, so that they might prepare for their jihad. The number of Muslims with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was very large. According to Muslim, ten thousand Muslims were with him. Al-Hakim, in al-Iklil, has written on the authority of Mu'adh that at the time of setting out for the expedition of Tabuk, our number was more than thirty thousand. Abu Zurʿah said: their names were not preserved in any book. Al-Zuhri said: by "book" is meant the register. Whoever wished to remain absent thought that, as long as no revelation came from Allah concerning him, his matter remained hidden (no one would come to know). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) resolved upon the expedition of Tabuk at a time when the fruits and the shade of the trees had become pleasant. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims with him made their preparations and set out on Thursday. He preferred to set out on a Thursday, whether for jihad or for any other purpose.

I too used to leave home in the morning intending to prepare, but I would return without having done anything, and I would say to myself: "I am able; whenever I wish, I shall do it at once." Thus time kept passing, until the heat became severe, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out with the Muslims, and I had made no preparations at all. I resolved in my heart that after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) I would complete my preparations within a day or two and catch up with them from behind. After the Muslims had departed, I went out in the morning to make preparations, but I returned without doing anything. Then on the next day I went out in the morning and again did nothing. In this way the delay kept increasing, until the people went far away and advanced swiftly toward jihad, and I kept only intending that I would set out and overtake them from behind. Would that I had done so, but it was not decreed for me. After the departure of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when I went out and looked at the people, I would see either only those who were called hypocrites, or weak people whom Allah had made excused; and no one else was visible. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not mention me until he reached Tabuk. At Tabuk, one day, while he was sitting among the companions, he asked: "What has happened to Kaʿb ibn Mālik?" A man from Banu Salamah, or from my own people (whose name, according to the report of Muhammad ibn ʿUmar, was ʿAbd Allah ibn Unays al-Salami), said: "O Messenger of Allah, his two garments and his looking at his own sides with pride have kept him from coming" (that is, nowadays he is prosperous; he wears one cloak and wraps another, and he turns his neck from side to side looking at his shoulders, and for this reason he could not come). Muʿadh ibn Jabal or Abu Qatadah said: "You have spoken evil; (it is not so), O Messenger of Allah! By Allah, we have found in him nothing but good." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fell silent.

Kaʿb ibn Mālik reports: When I was informed that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had set out to return, I became greatly anxious, and I began to devise excuses to present before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and I prepared such a statement that I might be able to escape his displeasure tomorrow. I also sought help in this matter from various people of judgement and from my household. Then, when I was told that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had come very near, all false thoughts left my heart, and I understood that with any statement mixed with falsehood I could never be safe from his displeasure. So I firmly resolved to speak the truth, and I became certain that only truthfulness would save me. In the morning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived.

Ibn Saʿd said: (They returned) in Ramadan. Kaʿb said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned from a journey, he would arrive in Madinah after the sun had risen; and first of all he would go to the mosque and offer two rak'ahs of prayer, then sit there; then from there he would go to Fatimah, and after that he would go to the homes of the Mothers of the Believers. As was his custom, he first went to the mosque, offered two rak'ahs, then sat there for the people (to hear their matters). Now those who had stayed behind from the Tabuk expedition began to come and present their excuses and swear oaths. They were about eighty men. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) accepted their outward excuses, took their pledge, asked forgiveness for them, and left their inner state to Allah. When I came into his presence and gave salam, he smiled, but it was an angry smile, and he said: "Come." I walked until I reached and sat in front of him. In the narration of Ibn ʿAbid it is related that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned his face away from Kaʿb. Kaʿb said: "O Messenger of Allah, why have you turned your face away from me? By Allah, I am not a hypocrite, nor is there any doubt in me (about the truth of Islam), nor have I changed my faith." He said: "Then why did you stay behind? Had you not bought a mount?" I said: "Indeed (I had bought a mount), O Messenger of Allah! If I were sitting before some other worldly person at this time, by Allah, I would escape his displeasure by making some excuse, for I possess the power of speech (and strength of argument). But I know that if I were to fabricate a lie before you and you were pleased, still soon Allah would make you displeased with me; and if I tell you the truth, though you will be displeased, I hope that Allah will forgive me. By Allah, I had no excuse; nor before this had I ever been so strong and so well-off." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "He has spoken the truth. Now get up, and Allah will decide concerning you."

Because I spoke the truth, some people of Banu Salamah became agitated and began to say: "Before this you had committed no offence, nor were you so weak that, like the others who did not take part, you could not have offered an excuse (and escaped reproach). The prayer for forgiveness of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would have been sufficient to pardon your sin." In short, they kept rebuking and reproaching me continually, to such an extent that I resolved to return to the presence of the Messenger of Allah and deny my first statement; but I said to myself: "Two sins cannot be combined in me: I did not go with the Messenger of Allah in jihad, and now I should also lie to the Messenger of Allah."

Then I asked the people: "Is there anyone else with me who did not go to Tabuk (and who also made no excuse)?" They said: "Yes, two other men said the same thing you said, and they were given the same instruction that you were given." I asked: "Who are those two?" They said: "Murarah ibn Rabiʿ al-ʿAmri and Hilal ibn Umayyah al-Waqifi."

Ibn Abi Hatim has related, on the authority of the mursal narration of Hasan al-Basri, that the reason the first of these did not go was that he had an orchard which had ripened (i.e., its clusters were hanging), and he said to himself: "I have already fought many jihads before; what harm if I remain at home this year?" But when he became aware of his offence, he said: "O Allah, I call You to witness that I give it in charity in Your path" (it was this that had kept me from going). As for the second man, his household had been scattered somewhere on a journey; when they returned he said: "Do not go this year; stay with us (there is no harm)." When he too became aware of his offence, he (made a covenant with Allah and) said: "O Allah, it is binding upon me that I shall not return to my household and my property (until You issue a new command)."

Kaʿb says: The people mentioned to me two righteous men who had taken part in Badr and whose example could be followed. When I heard their names, I remained firm upon my former position. Of those who had not gone to Tabuk, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade the Muslims to speak with only the three of us. After that command, people changed toward us entirely. In the narration of Ibn Abi Shaybah it is stated: "We would go out among the people in the morning, but no one would speak or greet us, nor would anyone return our greeting." In the narration of ʿAbd al-Razzaq: "People changed so much that it was as if they did not know us. The walls and the houses became strange; they were no longer the walls and houses we had known." The most painful thought for me was this: if I died in this state, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would not perform the funeral prayer over me; and if the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed away during this period, my condition would remain the same, no one would speak to me, nor would anyone pray the funeral prayer over me. To such an extent did matters reach that that land itself became strange to me; the town was no longer the town I had known. This condition continued for fifty nights. My two companions remained weak and sat in their houses, weeping, but I was strong and young; I would leave home and join the Muslims in prayer and walk in the markets, yet no one would speak or greet me. After the prayer, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sat in the gathering of the companions, I would come and greet him and say in my heart: "Did the Messenger of Allah move his blessed lips to return the greeting or not?" Then I would go near the Messenger of Allah and pray (deliberately), and watch him from the corner of my eye (to see whether his attention had turned to me or not). When I turned toward the prayer, the Messenger of Allah would face me; but when I glanced at him, he would turn away. When people had kept distant from me for a long period, one day I climbed over a wall and reached Abu Qatadah in his orchard. Abu Qatadah was my paternal cousin; that is, he was from the clan of Banu Salamah, and was not the son of my father's brother. I had great affection for him. I greeted him, but by Allah, he did not return my greeting. I said: "Abu Qatadah, you know well that I love Allah and His Messenger." Abu Qatadah remained silent. I repeated my words, but he remained silent and said nothing. After I said it for the third or fourth time, he said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." Hearing this, tears flowed from my eyes, and I returned, climbing over the wall. One day, as I was walking in the market, I saw a farmer from the land of Syria who had come to Madinah to sell grain. He asked someone: "Tell me where Kaʿb ibn Mālik is." People pointed to me. He came to me and handed me a letter which was from the King of Ghassan (that is, from the ruler of Syria). In the narration of Ibn Abi Shaybah it is found that a man of my tribe was in Syria, and he had sent it. The letter was wrapped in a piece of silk cloth, and in it was written: "We have received news that your companion has cut you off and thrown you away, and Allah has not made you such that you should remain in a place of disgrace and your right be wasted; so if you wish to move your residence, come to us, and we shall help you." Having read the letter, I said: "This too is a trial (from Allah): even the unbelievers have begun to covet me" (my person became the arena of the unbelievers' greed). Then I threw the letter into the oven. In the narration of Ibn ʿAbid it is related that Kaʿb complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about his condition and said: "Your turning away from me has reached such a point that even the polytheists have begun to covet me."

When forty of the fifty nights had passed, a messenger of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) suddenly came to me. Muhammad ibn Umar has said that the name of this messenger was Khuzaymah ibn Thabit. This same messenger also went to Murarah and Hilal. The messenger said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has commanded you to separate yourself from your wife." I said: "Should I divorce her, or do something else?" He said: "There is no command for divorce. Keep away from her and do not approach her." The same command reached my two companions. In compliance with the command, I said to my wife: "Go to your family's house and remain there until Allah decides this matter."

Hilal ibn Umayyah's wife, Khawlah bint Asim, came into the presence of the Messenger (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)! Hilal ibn Umayyah is an old man. He cannot do his work himself, and he has no servant. If I do his work for him, will it be displeasing to you?" In the narration of Ibn Abi Shaybah, these words appear: "He is old, and his eyesight is very weak." The Messenger (ﷺ) said: "No (there is no prohibition on doing his work), but he must not approach you." The woman said: "By Allah! He has no sense of anything at all. Since this incident happened, he has continued to weep until today."

Ka'b said: Someone from my own household also said to me: "If you too, like Hilal ibn Umayyah's wife, were to seek permission from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that your wife may serve you, it would be appropriate." I said: "By Allah! I will not ask permission from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Who knows what he may say, and I am a young man (I have no need to make use of another's service)." In this condition, ten more nights passed, and the fifty nights were completed.

In the narration of Abd al-Razzaq, Ka'b's statement appears: "Our repentance was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the time of one-third of the night." Umm Salamah said: "O Messenger of Allah! Should we give Ka'b ibn Malik the good news?" He said: "(At that time, you would inform him of the acceptance of repentance,) then people would pounce upon you and would not let you sleep for the rest of the night (so inform him at Fajr)."

Ka'b said: On the morning of the fiftieth night, after I had prayed the Fajr prayer, I was sitting on the roof of my house, and my condition was that described by Allah: "the earth, spacious as it was, became narrow for them" (wa daqat 'alayhim al-ardu bima rahubat). The earth had become narrow for me despite its vastness. Suddenly I heard the voice of a caller who had climbed Mount Sal' and called out with a very loud voice: "O Ka'b ibn Malik! Rejoice, good news for you!" Muhammad ibn Umar's narration is that the one who climbed Mount Sal' was Abu Bakr, and it was he who called out: "Allah has had mercy upon Ka'b. O Ka'b! Rejoice."

Uqbah's narration is that two men ran to give Ka'b the good news; one went ahead, and the one who remained behind climbed Mount Sal' and from there called out: "O Ka'b! Good news of the acceptance of your repentance. Allah has revealed the Qur'an concerning you people."

Historians are of the view that the two men who ran to give the good news were Abu Bakr and Umar.

Ka'b said: As soon as I heard the voice, I fell into prostration and began to weep with joy, and I understood that the time of ease had come. After the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had performed the Fajr prayer, he announced the acceptance of our repentance. People came to give us the good news. Some other people went to give the good news to my two companions. A man came to me riding a horse. Muhammad ibn Umar said: "This was Zubayr ibn Awwam." Another man of the tribe of Aslam also ran, but before the horse reached me, I had already heard the voice, so when the man whose voice I had heard came, that is, Hamzah al-Aslami, I took off my two garments and put them on him. By Allah! I had no other clothes apart from those two. I borrowed two garments from Abu Qatadah (according to Muhammad ibn Umar's narration) and wore them.

Hilal ibn Umayyah was given the good news of the acceptance of his repentance by Sa'id ibn Zayd. Hilal had given up eating and drinking, kept continuous fasts, and was constantly occupied with weeping. I thought he would not even be able to raise his head, and that his life would depart. Murarah ibn Rabi' was given the good news by Salkan ibn Salamah. He was the father of Salamah ibn Waqsh.

Ka'b ibn Malik said: I set out to go into the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). On the way, groups of people kept meeting me to congratulate me. Finally I entered the mosque. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting, and people were around him. Talhah ibn Ubaydullah rose on seeing me, hurried toward me, shook my hand, and congratulated me. Apart from Talhah, no one among the Muhajirin rose. I will never forget Talhah's gesture. The blessed face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was shining with joy. I greeted him with salam. The Messenger (ﷺ) said: "Be given good news of the best day that has come upon you since the day your mother bore you until today." I said: "O Messenger of Allah! Is this from you, or from Allah?" He said: "No, it is from Allah. You people dealt truthfully with Allah, and Allah also declared you truthful." It was the habit of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that when he was happy, his face would shine, appearing like a piece of the moon. We would recognize this by looking (that the Messenger (ﷺ) was pleased at that time). When I sat in front of him, I said: "O Messenger of Allah! As the completion of my repentance, I wish to relinquish all my wealth and present it as charity to Allah and His Messenger." He said: "Keep some of your wealth for yourself; that is better for you." I said: "Very well, I will give up half of it." He said: "No." I said: "Then one-third (accept it)." He said: "Very well." I said: "Then I will keep my share in Khaybar." Then I said: "O Messenger of Allah! Allah has saved me because of truthfulness, so as the completion of my repentance, I also pledge that as long as I live, I will speak only the truth. By Allah! I do not know that anyone has been shown a greater favor by Allah than the favor He showed me in speaking the truth. From that pledge until today, I have never told a lie, and I hope that as long as I live, Allah will protect me from lying."

Allah revealed verses concerning the acceptance of repentance: "Indeed Allah has forgiven the Prophet and the Muhajirin and the Ansar..." up to "...and be with the truthful" (Surah al-Tawbah 9:117–119). By Allah! Since Allah guided me to Islam, no greater blessing has been bestowed upon me than my speaking truthfully before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Had I told a lie, I would have been destroyed like those who lied, about whom Allah spoke in the worst terms. He said: "They will swear to you by Allah when you return to them..." up to "...indeed Allah is not pleased with the defiant people" (Surah al-Tawbah 9:95–96).

Ka'b said: Those who had sworn oaths and whose excuses the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had accepted, from whom he had taken the pledge of allegiance and for whom he had made supplication for forgiveness, had their matter deferred compared to ours; the three of us had our matter held back. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had postponed our matter until Allah's decision. The phrase in the verse "and to the three who were left behind" (wa 'ala al-thalathati alladhina khullifu) does not mean being left behind from jihad, but rather that our matter was set aside from the matter of those who made excuses, and our decision was held in suspense.

Hatta idha daqat 'alayhim al-ardu bima rahubat: until, when the earth, despite being wide and vast, became narrow for them (because of the aloofness of their companions). The expression "the earth became narrow for someone" is an idiom that depicts extreme bewilderment; that is, they were so confused and distressed about their situation that there was no place in the vast earth where they could find relief from their restlessness and anguish.

Wa daqat 'alayhim anfusuhum: and their own souls became straitened to them. That is, their hearts became so constricted from intense loneliness and grief that there was no room left in them for comfort and joy.

Wa zannu an la malja'a min Allahi illa ilayh: and they understood that there is no refuge from Allah (from His wrath and displeasure) except in Him, that is, that they should only seek forgiveness from Him.

Thumma taba 'alayhim: then He turned to them in forgiveness.

Liyatubu: that they might remain steadfast in repentance. Here, repentance means remaining steadfast in repentance, because they had already repented earlier (there is no sense in repentance after repentance). Or the meaning is that Allah accepted their repentance so that they would be included among the group of those who repent.

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: Sincere and true repentance is this: that if a sin is committed, the vast earth becomes narrow for the person, and a severe restlessness and anxiety arise in the heart, as was the repentance of those three.

Inna Allaha huwa al-Tawwab al-Rahim: Indeed Allah is the Oft-Returning, the Most Merciful.

Abu Musa al-Ash'ari narrates that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah extends His hand at night (to accept repentance) so that one who sinned by day may repent at night, and He extends His hand by day so that one who sinned by night may repent by day. This continues until the sun rises from the west" (that is, the door of repentance remains open until the Day of Resurrection; when the sun rises from the west, the door of repentance will close). Narrated by Muslim.

Anas narrates that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If one of you loses his riding camel in a desert wilderness (while traveling), and the camel carried all his food and drink, and he searches for it and, despairing, lies down under the shade of a tree and falls asleep, then suddenly wakes up to find the camel standing beside him, and he immediately seizes its halter, and out of extreme joy his tongue slips and he says: 'O Allah! You are my servant and I am your Lord'—the traveler's joy at finding his camel is greater than Allah's joy at a servant's repentance when the servant repents before Him." Narrated by Muslim.

Many hadiths about repentance and the acceptance of repentance have been narrated.

O you who believe! Fear Allah (from disobedience and punishment) and be with the truthful. That is, those who are true in faith and in their promises. Or, those who are truthful in Islam, in sincerity of intention, truthfulness of speech and integrity of action (so that, in the first sense, "truthful" means truth of faith and of promise, and in the second sense it means sincerity of intention and truth of speech and action). The meaning is: adopt truthfulness in everything and be steadfast in observing it.

Hadrat Ibn Abbas and Hadrat Ibn Umar said: that is, be with Muhammad (ﷺ) and his Companions, whose intentions are pure, whose hearts are sincere and whose deeds are sincere. They went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to Tabuk with sincerity and a true resolve. Do not be like the hypocrites who did not support the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Hadrat Sa'id ibn Jubayr interpreted "al-Sadiqin" as Abu Bakr and Umar; that is, be with Abu Bakr and Umar.

Dahhak said: Muslims have been commanded to be with Hadrat Abu Bakr, Hadrat Umar and their companions.

In one narration, a statement of Hadrat Ibn Abbas has come that it means: be with Hadrat Ali ibn Abi Talib.

Sufyan al-Thawri said: this is a difference of interpretation (on the part of the commentators), and the verse includes all these interpretations. This is meant, and that is meant too (no single one is specified).

Ibn Juraij said: "al-Sadiqin" refers to the Muhajirun. Allah has said: "For the poor emigrants... it is they who are the truthful" (in this verse the Muhajirun are described as the truthful).

Some said: "al-Sadiqin" refers to those who sincerely acknowledged their sin with a true heart and did not present false excuses.

Hadrat Ibn Mas'ud said: Lying is in no way permissible, neither in jest nor in serious speech. No one should make a promise to his child (to pacify him) that he does not fulfil. If you want confirmation of this statement, recite this verse. Then he recited the verse mentioned above:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 9, verse 120:

It was not fitting for the people of Madinah and for the Bedouins around them to hold back from the Messenger of Allah, nor to prefer their own selves over his self. (Translation of the Urdu rendering of the verse: مدینہ کے رہنے والوں کو اور جو دیہاتی ان کے گرد و پیش رہتے ہیں ‘ ان کو یہ زیبا نہ تھا کہ رسول اللہ (ﷺ) کا ساتھ نہ دیں اور نہ یہ زیبا تھا کہ اپنی جانوں کو ان کی جانوں سے زیادہ عزیز سمجھیں۔)

Although the words of this statement appear to be a report, in reality they are a prohibition and a restraint, as in the other verse: ﴿It was not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah﴾ (9:120 is preceded by this context). The "Bedouins" here means the tribes of Muzaynah, Juhaynah, Ashja', Aslam and Ghifar, who lived in the desert (they did not live inside Madinah).

The meaning of ﴿from the Messenger of Allah﴾ is that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) himself goes out in person on jihad, it is not permissible to abandon his company and not to accompany him. The meaning of ﴿nor prefer their own selves﴾ is that people should not keep their own lives apart from a jihad from which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has not kept his own self apart.

﴿That is because﴾ (the need to accompany him) is due to the following cause: ﴿they are not afflicted with thirst, nor fatigue, nor hunger in the way of Allah, nor do they tread upon any ground that enrages the disbelievers, nor do they gain any gain from an enemy except that a good deed is written for them thereby. Indeed Allah does not waste the reward of the doers of good.﴾ (Urdu rendering: یہ (ساتھ جانے کی ضرورت) اس سبب سے ہے کہ اللہ کی راہ میں جو پیاس لگی اور جو ماندگی پہنچی اور جو بھوک لگی اور جو چلنا چلے جو کفار کیلئے موجب غیظ ہوا اور دشمنوں کی جو کچھ خبر لی ‘ ان کے نام اس کی وجہ سے ایک ایک نیک کام لکھا گیا۔ یقیناً اللہ مخلصوں کا اجر ضائع نہیں کرتا۔)

﴿That﴾ refers to the command of prohibition understood from the preceding statement. In ﴿بِاَنَّھُمْ﴾, the bāʾ is causal, meaning "because of." ﴿ẓamaʾ﴾ means a small amount of thirst. ﴿naṣab﴾ means tiredness. ﴿makhmaṣah﴾ means hunger. ﴿mawṭiʾan﴾ is a verbal noun (for emphasis of the verb) or a adverb of place, meaning that they will not go over any ground. ﴿nayلan﴾ means so that they gain some kind of advantage, whether by killing, capturing, plundering, or acquiring spoils of war. ﴿Illā kutiba﴾ means that they become deserving of reward because of it, and this promise requires that they go with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and not turn away from accompanying him. ﴿Inna Allāha lā yuḍīʿu ajra al-muḥsinīn﴾: this sentence is the cause of the preceding command and shows that jihad is a good (for all humanity). That jihad is good for the disbelievers is because it is the ultimate effort to free them from the Fire and to perfect their humanity, like striking a madman (which at times is a treatment for him), and beating a child to teach him manners (which is good for him). The good of jihad for the believers is that, through jihad itself, the believers are protected from the aggression, dominance and control of the disbelievers.

Abu ʿAbs narrated that he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: whoever's feet become dusty in the way of Allah, Allah has made the Fire forbidden for him. Related by al-Bukhari in al-Sahih, Ahmad in al-Musnad, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i.

Abu Hurairah narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: The one who fights in the way of Allah, as long as he does not return from jihad, is in a state like one who fasts (every day), one who prays (at night), and one who recites the verses of Allah and does not slacken in fasting or prayer (he remains constantly engaged with vigour). Al-Baghawi wrote: The scholars differ in their opinions regarding the ruling of this verse (whether it is general or specific, urgent or perpetual).

Qatadah said: This command relates to the case of going with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) (it is not general). When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) himself went out on jihad, it was not permissible for anyone to stay behind without a (legitimate) excuse. The obligatory command to accompany other caliphs and rulers is not in this verse. If Muslims have no need to fight, it is permissible for Muslims not to go on jihad with the caliph or ruler.

Walid ibn Muslim reported that he heard from al-Awza'i, ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, Ibn Jabir and Saʿid ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz that the ruling of this verse applied at the beginning of this ummah and also applies to its last era (i.e., the ruling is perpetual, and supporting every caliph is obligatory in every age).

Ibn Zayd said: This ruling applied when Muslims were few. When they became many, Allah abrogated this ruling and made it permissible for one who did not wish to go on jihad not to go, and said: ﴿It is not for the believers to go forth all together﴾.

I say: All the imams agree that jihad is a collective obligation (fard kifayah). If a group of Muslims performs jihad to the extent necessary, the obligation is lifted from the remaining Muslims. Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib held that jihad is an individual obligation (fard ʿayn), because the rulings on jihad are general, and harsh rulings were revealed concerning those who did not go to the expedition of Tabuk. We say: when the call to jihad is general, by the consensus of the scholars it becomes obligatory upon every person, as occurred on the occasion of the Battle of Tabuk; otherwise it is a collective obligation, because Allah has said: ﴿Those who sit back among the believers are not equal...﴾ etc. At the end of this verse is: ﴿And to each Allah has promised the best﴾ (each group has been promised good by Allah, though the degrees of good differ and are not equal). Another verse is: ﴿It is not for the believers to go forth all together﴾.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 9, verse 121:

And [those who] do not spend any expenditure, small or large, and do not cross any valley, [it is] also recorded for them, [whatever] small or large they spent in the way of Allah, such as when Hazrat Uthman ibn Affan and Hazrat Abdur Rahman ibn Auf spent wealth at the time of preparation for Jaish al-Usrah (the Army of Hardship).

Every valley that they had to traverse, all of it was also written in their good deeds. That is, every valley they cross while coming and going is recorded. Wadi (valley) is a watercourse through which flood water flows (coming down from the mountains). Wadi is in the form of the active participle; wadiya (past tense) means it flowed, it ran off. Figuratively, it denotes land, and this meaning is in common use.

﴿So that Allah may reward them with the best of what they used to do﴾, that is, Allah may give them the best possible reward for their good deeds.

That is, the good deeds are rewarded with a good deed, meaning jihad; or the good reward for their deeds. Hazrat Abu Mas'ud Ansari narrates that a man came with a camel having a nose-rope and said: "This is in the way of Allah." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "On the Day of Resurrection, you will receive seven hundred camels with nose-ropes in return for it." (Narrated by Muslim)

Hazrat Zayd ibn Khalid narrates that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever provides equipment for a person fighting in the way of Allah has himself fought, and whoever looks after the wife and children of a mujahid after him has himself fought." (Narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim in their Sahihs.) And Allah knows best.

Al-Kalbi has mentioned that the tribes of Bani Asad ibn Khuzaymah, afflicted by famine, came to Madinah with their children (having left their homes); because of them the roads of Madinah became unclean and the prices of goods rose. Upon this, the following verse was revealed:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 9, verse 122:

{Wa ma kana al-mu'minuna liyanfiru kaffah} And (it is not befitting for the believers to go forth all together). This negation carries the meaning of a prohibition, that is, all Muslims should not go forth from their homelands in pursuit of knowledge; this would bring about the corruption of society and the disruption of livelihoods.

{Falau la nafara min kulli firqatin minhum taifah liyatafaqqahu} So why should not a party from every large group among them go forth, so that the remaining people may keep acquiring understanding of the religion? That is, why does not a small group from every large community, such as a tribe, a city or a settlement, go forth in pursuit of knowledge, so that by enduring hardships and difficulties it may acquire religious understanding and comprehend the matters of the religion? The author of al-Nihayah (Ibn al-Athir) has written: the original linguistic meaning of fiqh (understanding, comprehension) is to comprehend, and its derivation is from the sense of splitting (shaqq) and opening (fath). Firqah refers to a large group, and taifah to a small group. In the Qamus it is written: fiqh, with a kasra on the fa, means to know and understand something. Since, among all sciences, the science of religion holds excellence, the word fiqh has been specifically reserved (in terminology) for the science of religion. Some have said: acquiring the unknown through the known is fiqh, that is, the word is specific to inferential knowledge; in this case the word 'ilm is general and the word fiqh is specific. God says: {Fa-mali ha'ulai al-qawmi la yakadoona yafqahuna hadithan} What has happened to these people that they cannot even understand a statement? That is, they do not derive the content of the statement (they do not grasp the essence of the statement).

Imam Abu Hanifah said: fiqh is knowing those matters that are harmful and beneficial to the self (whether in respect of thought and belief or of speech and action; whether it is knowledge of principles or of branches). The specific use of the term fiqh for knowledge of the branches of religion is a later terminological development (it was not so specific in the first century).

It is evident that the word fiqh includes the knowledge of the muqallid (one who follows); acquiring knowledge from a mujtahid, or from a book of a mujtahid, fulfils the obligation which is commanded in the aforementioned verse.

{Wa liyundhiru qawmahum idha raja'u ilayhim la'allahum yahdharun} And that (those who went forth) may warn their people when they return to them, so that they may be cautious (of evil deeds, by learning the religion from them).

That is, when they return to their homeland, they should warn those who did not go out to seek knowledge and remained at home (against opposing the commands of Allah) and should inform them of the commands. Mujahid said: some people went out to preach and call to guidance in the villages and deserts. The people said to them: you have come to us (for preaching) and have left behind your companion (that is, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ). On hearing this, these men felt something in their hearts; they immediately returned from the villages and presented themselves in the service of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Upon this, the aforementioned verse was revealed. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: you will find people as mines, like the mines of gold and silver (they are diverse sources of good and evil, and different people are the products of different sources). So those who were (by nature) better in the Days of Ignorance will also be better in Islam, provided they acquire understanding. Narrated by al-Shafi'i; similarly, al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim) in their Sahihs and Ahmad narrated it from Abu Hurairah. Al-Tabarani narrated from Ibn Mas'ud that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: there are only two kinds of men: the scholar and the seeker of knowledge; there is no good in any others.

The verse indicates that a single report (khabar ahad) is a valid proof in the Shariah (that is, to know a matter, a single report, provided it has come through a trustworthy narration, must be accepted), because in the verse the word "kulli firqah" is general, which shows that if there are only three people in a settlement, it is necessary for one of them to go out to acquire knowledge and, upon returning, to inform the others after learning. If no report were acceptable without tawatur, then the expression "kulli firqatin" would have no meaning.

Some fiqh is fard 'ayn (individual obligation) and some is fard kifayah (collective obligation). Correct beliefs and essential actions, such as purity, prayer, fasting, zakat, hajj, and knowledge of all obligatory duties, are fard 'ayn. Apart from acts of worship, knowing those transactions which continually come before a person and with which he is regularly concerned is also fard 'ayn; for example, traders must know the rules of valid sale, invalid sale, interest, and so on. Those connected with contracts, wages or employment must acquire their rulings as necessary. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: seeking knowledge is obligatory upon every Muslim man. This hadith has been narrated by Ibn 'Adi and al-Bayhaqi from the report of Anas, by al-Khatib from the report of Imam Hasan ibn 'Ali, by al-Tabarani in al-Saghir, also by al-Tabarani in al-Awsat from the report of Ibn 'Abbas, in al-Kabir from the report of Ibn Mas'ud, by al-Khatib from the report of 'Ali, and by al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, as well as by al-Bayhaqi, from the report of Abu Sa'id. In the report of Anas, as cited by Ibn 'Abd al-Barr, there is this additional wording: every thing seeks forgiveness for the seeker of knowledge, even the fish in the depths of the sea. In one report these words also occur: and Allah loves to respond to the cry of the afflicted.

Fard kifayah means acquiring knowledge of the issues of every subject until one reaches the rank of giving fatwa. If no person in a city attains this level of scholarship and all remain idle, all will be sinful; and if even one prepares himself for complete scholarly attainment, the obligation is removed from all, and it becomes obligatory upon all to follow him. Whatever circumstances arise, those who seek resolution should refer to that scholar.

Acquiring knowledge is superior to every voluntary act of worship. Through the narration of Ibn 'Abbas, the author of Musnad al-Firdaws has reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: seeking knowledge is, in the sight of Allah, superior to prayer, fasting, hajj and jihad in the path of Allah. It has also come in a narration of Ibn 'Abbas that an hour spent acquiring knowledge is superior to a night spent in standing (prayer), and a day spent seeking knowledge is superior to fasting three days. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: the excellence of the scholar over the worshipper is like my excellence over the least of you. Indeed Allah (shows mercy), and His angels, and the dwellers of the heavens and the earth, even the ants in their holes and the fish in the water, invoke blessings upon the one who teaches people good. Narrated by al-Tirmidhi with a sahih chain from Abu Umamah. Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: one scholar is heavier upon Satan than a thousand worshippers. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ also said: when a man dies, his deeds come to an end except three (whose benefit continues): ongoing charity, or knowledge from which people benefit, or a righteous child who prays for him.

Ladunni knowledge, whose bearers are the Sufis, is fard 'ayn, because this inner knowledge has two aims:

(1) To remove from the heart the inclination towards everything other than Allah, and to regard oneself always as present before Allah. To keep the self purified from self-admiration, pride, envy, love of the world, laziness in worship, desires of the self, showing off, seeking fame, and other inward moral defects.

(2) To repent from sins, be content with divine decree, be patient in calamities, be grateful for blessings, and adorn the self with other good qualities and noble character. And it is evident that for every person, abstaining from prohibitions of this kind and adhering to obligations is more important and necessary than those related to the bodily organs. If sincerity and the correctness of intention are absent, then prayer, fasting and other acts of worship are unacceptable. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Allah accepts only that deed which is sincere and done purely to seek the pleasure of Allah. Narrated by al-Nasa'i from Abu Umamah. Muslim narrated from Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Allah does not look at your forms or your wealth, but He looks at your hearts.

And it is clear that whatever the fard 'ayn depends upon is itself fard 'ayn; therefore Ladunni knowledge, whose bearers are the Sufis, is fard 'ayn.

Another cause of the revelation of this verse has also been mentioned. Al-Baghawi, through the narration of al-Kalbi, and Ibn Abi Hatim, through the narration of 'Ikrimah and 'Abdullah ibn 'Umair, have related the statement of Ibn 'Abbas that when, in connection with the Battle of Tabuk, Allah had disclosed the faults of the hypocrites and the verse {In la tanfiru yu'adhdhibkum 'adhaban alima} (If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment) was revealed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began sending military detachments in various directions, then all the Muslims began to go forth to jihad and to leave the Messenger of Allah ﷺ alone. In the narration of 'Ikrimah it has come that some Bedouin dwellers of the desert did not go for jihad. The hypocrites began to say: these Bedouins have been ruined (they did not observe the command of jihad). Upon this, the verse {Ma kana al-mu'minuna liyanfiru} (that is, to the expedition) {kaffah} {Falau la nafara min kulli firqatin} (that is, a great group) {taifah} (that is, a part went to the expedition and a part remained with the Prophet) {liyatafaqqahu} (that is, those who sat behind) {fi al-din} (that is, in the Qur'an, the Sunnah, the obligations and the rulings) was revealed. The meaning is that not all Muslims should go forth to jihad, but from a large group it is obligatory that a small party goes for jihad, and one group should remain in the service of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to learn the Qur'an, the Sunnah, the obligations and the rulings, so that when the military detachments return, these people can tell them what commands were revealed after their departure. Accordingly (after the revelation of this verse) it began to happen so. Some groups would remain with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and some detachments would go, so the chain of religious instruction would not be broken. Religious understanding is the greater jihad. The very purpose of the prophetic mission is to present the Islamic rulings with proofs (the rank of jihad by the sword is defensive, while the rank of propagative jihad is higher). For this reason the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said that the scholars are the heirs of the prophets. In the light of this occasion of revelation and this explanation, the pronouns in liyatafaqqahu and liyundhiru refer to those who remained present in the service of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for acquiring knowledge after the departure of the military detachments, and the pronoun in raja'u refers to the detachments that went forth for jihad.

Suyuti has written that Ibn 'Abbas said: the ruling of this verse is restricted to the case when Muslim detachments go for jihad without the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the prohibition of abandoning jihad applies when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ himself goes forth.

Hasan's statement is that the pronouns in liyatafaqqahu and liyundhiru refer to the detachments of Muslims who went for jihad. The meaning of the verse is: why is it not that a party (from every group) goes for jihad and personally witnesses and understands the support of the religion and the dominance over the polytheists, and then, after returning from jihad, informs the disbelievers of their people that Allah granted victory to His Messenger and the believers, and the purpose of this information is that the disbelievers of their people refrain from confronting the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, fearing that, just as others fared, they too would meet the same fate by waging war against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

From this explanation it is understood that jihad is a fard kifayah: if one group discharges this obligation, the obligation is removed from all. However, if a general call to jihad is proclaimed and everyone is ordered to come for jihad, then jihad becomes fard 'ayn upon every individual.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 9, verse 123:

﴿Yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū qātilū alladhīna yalūnakum mina al-kuffār﴾ O you who believe! Fight those of the disbelievers who are near to you.

This verse commands that jihad against the disbelievers be begun according to the principle of al-aqrab fa al-aqrab (the nearest first). Beginning the jihad should be with those disbelievers who are nearest in terms of residence and kinship. The nearest disbelievers have the greatest right to reform and compassion; for this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was first commanded to convey the message to his closest family members, and after the Hijrah the command to fight the Jews of Banu Qurayzah, Banu Nadir and Khaybar was given first. When the jihad in Arabia was finished and there was no longer a need, the command to fight the Romans was given. This verse indeed commands fighting the Romans. The Romans lived in Syria (and the Persians in Iraq), and Syria was nearer to Madinah than Iraq. After the revelation of this verse, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out towards Tabuk to fight the Romans, as narrated by Ibn Mardawayh on the authority of Ibn Abbas, by Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn al-Mundhir on the saying of Mujahid, and by Ibn Jarir on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

Taking into account the requirement of this verse, the jurists (ulama al-fiqh) have stated explicitly that it is obligatory upon the Muslims who live near the border of the disbelievers to fight the disbelievers of the border. If they are not sufficient, or more strength is needed, or they are negligent and do not heed the command of jihad, then it becomes obligatory upon the Muslims who live adjacent to these border Muslims to fight the border disbelievers. And if even among them there is not enough strength as needed, or they abandon jihad out of negligence, then the duty of those behind them becomes the same as the duty of those who were negligent. In this same order, the obligation of jihad falls upon all Muslims of East and West. The same ruling applies to providing the means for the shroud and burial of the deceased, and to performing the funeral prayer for the deceased.

﴿Wa-l-yajidū fīkum ghilẓah﴾ And let them find harshness in you.

Ghilẓah means severity and zeal for Islam. According to Hasan (al-Basri), ghilzah means steadfastness in jihad. Apparently the form "liyajidū" is in the imperative sense, whose pronoun refers to the disbelievers, and the disbelievers are the ones addressed; but in reality the command is directed to the Muslims, and the meaning is: O Muslims, adopt severity and firmness against the disbelievers (let them not perceive any softness or cowardice in you).

﴿Wa-'lamū anna Allāha ma'a al-muttaqīn﴾ And know that Allah is with the God-fearing. Allah's help and support are with the God-fearing, not with the disbelievers; therefore do not be concerned about their war (do not be afraid).

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 9, verse 124:

﴿وَإِذَا مَا أُنزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ فَمِنْهُم مَّن يَقُولُ أَيُّكُمْ زَادَتْهُ هَٰذِهِ إِيمَانًا ۚ فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا فَزَادَتْهُمْ إِيمَانًا﴾

And when a (new) surah is revealed, among them are some who say: "Which of you has this increased in faith?" As for those who believe, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice.

Meaning: When a surah is revealed, some of the hypocrites say to their companions, mockingly, "Which of you has had his faith and certainty increased by this surah?" God answered them: the revealed surah increases the faith of the believers. The inimitability (i'jaz) expressed within the surah increases the knowledge of the believers, and they become certain of the revealed surah, so the measure of their earlier faith increases. (Previously their faith was in that part which had already been revealed; then their faith extends to the new surah as well, and whatever scientific and inimitable content the surah contains is also attained by them. In this way faith grows.)

﴿وَهُمْ يَسْتَبْشِرُونَ﴾

And they rejoice at the revelation of the surah, because through the surah their knowledge and perfection increase and their ranks are raised.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 9, verse 125:

﴿And as for those in whose hearts is a disease, it adds filth to their filth, and they die while they are disbelievers.﴾

Disease (marad) means doubt and hypocrisy. Filth (rijs) means disbelief. That is, they were already rejecting the earlier revealed verses and surahs, and now they also reject this new surah. In this way disbelief is piled upon disbelief.

The explicit mention of dying in a state of disbelief is made because faith is a gift from God. The function of verses is not to bestow faith. If Allah does not grant faith, the verses are of no benefit.

Mujahid said: this verse proves that faith increases and decreases (that is, faith is composite, and its components vary in amount). Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), holding the hand of one or two of his companions, would say: "Come, let us increase our faith" (that is, if a new verse or surah has been revealed, let us go and listen to it so that our faith may grow).

Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Faith appears in the heart in the form of a white point; as faith increases, the whiteness grows, until the whole heart becomes white. Hypocrisy appears in the heart in the form of a black point; as hypocrisy increases, the blackness grows, until the whole heart becomes black. By God, if you were to split open the heart of a believer you would find it white, and if you were to split open the heart of a hypocrite you would find it black.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 9, verse 126:

Do they not see that they are tested once or twice every year? Yet they do not repent, nor do they take heed.

That is, they are tested by being sent various kinds of illnesses and calamities. Mujahid said: they are tested by being afflicted with famine and hardship. Qatadah said: they go out to jihad in the company of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and witness the signs of truth that become manifest. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: their hypocrisy is exposed, and because of this they are disgraced. Ikrimah said: they practise hypocrisy, then they accept faith, then they become hypocrites again. Yaman said: they break their covenants.

"Yet they do not repent" means: they do not repent of breaking covenants, of sins, and of hypocrisy, which is the cause of the calamities and disgraces that befall them.

"Nor do they take heed" means: they do not take a lesson from the way Allah fulfilled His promise of help to His Messenger and of victory to the Muslims.

And when a surah is revealed, they look at one another. That is, they signal to each other with their eyes in denial or mockery, or express anger through eye gestures, because this surah exposes their faults and disgraces them. Intending to rise from the gathering and flee, they say to one another by eye signals:

"Does anyone see you?" That is, is any (Muslim) watching you? If you get up from this gathering, will anyone notice? Then, if no Muslim was watching, they would slip away from the mosque; but if they were sure of being seen, they would remain seated.

"Then they turn away." That is, they turn away (from believing in this newly revealed surah). According to some exegetes, the meaning is that they turn away from the place where they were sitting and listening to the surah, that is, they turn away from the gathering of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Remaining seated involved for them the fear of disgrace.

"Allah has turned their hearts away." Allah has turned their hearts away (from faith). Abu Ishaq said: Allah misguided them as a punishment for their deeds. This sentence may also be understood as a supplication rather than a statement (meaning: may Allah turn their hearts away from faith, so that whatever trace of faith remains in their hearts also departs).

"Because they are a people who do not understand." Because they are such people who do not comprehend the truth, due to their lack of understanding and faulty reflection.
